title: Kintsugi Pottery Class for Beginners
description:
Learn the Philosophy

Discover the meaning behind the ancient Japanese art of kintsugi.




Break Your Pottery

Gently break your ceramic piece — each crack becomes part of your artwork’s story.




Mix Your Gold

Create your golden resin — the key to transforming broken pieces into art.




Repair with Care

Rejoin the pieces using your golden resin, embracing each imperfection with intention.




Take Home Your Piece

Leave with a one-of-a-kind display piece — handmade, meaningful, and uniquely yours.



Discover the Japanese art of kintsugi at this London pottery class and create a beautiful ceramic piece to take home.
Kintsugi is an ancient art form that celebrates the Japanese philosophy of the beauty of imperfection. It involves putting broken pieces of pottery back together with gold and embracing the cracks to produce a beautiful piece of art, showing how the obstacles that we overcome in life can become an important and powerful part of our identity.
In this kintsugi class, your experienced tutor will tell you all about the history and philosophy of kintsugi whilst taking you through the process of making your own kintsugi piece.
Kintsugi is a perfect solution for a mistakenly broken treasured item, but to practice this art form you'll learn how to safely break pottery to practice mending it in the kintsugi way, without overdoing the cracks.
The gold of kintsugi is what makes it so beautiful and in the next stage of your craft class, you'll learn to use a micro metal mix with epoxy resin to create your gold solution. You'll then use this solution to fix together your broken pottery pieces, creating a wonderful piece of perfectly imperfect art.
You'll finish this London kintsugi class with lots of new knowledge on kintsugi pottery and the ability to mend broken ceramic pieces. You'll also take away your own handmade piece of kintsugi art. Kintsugi is a therapeutic process and you'll feel a sense of calm and accomplishment as you finish this special workshop.
Your finished piece is only for display not for food use, microwaves, ovens or the dishwasher.
What you'll get
One beautiful piece of kintsugi pottery made by you to take home.
All materials and equipment provided.

title: Pottery Mug Workshop - Making and Painting
description:
Ready to get your hands dirty (in the best way)? In this pottery class in London, you’ll dive into the relaxing and playful world of hand-building - a pottery technique that lets you shape clay entirely by hand. It’s a slower, more sculptural process that’s perfect for beginners and lets you get really creative with shapes and designs.
You’ll get to design and build your very own pottery piece from scratch - whether that’s a mug for your morning coffee, a vase for your favourite flowers, a bowl for snacks (or your dog’s dinner), or something totally unexpected. There’s no right or wrong - just your creative flair, a bit of guidance, and plenty of laughs along the way. No experience needed. Just show up, relax, and see where your ideas take you.
Easy, creative and beginner-friendly
We’ll teach you the key hand-building techniques: coiling, pinching and slab-building. These are the foundations of traditional pottery and are surprisingly easy to pick up. Once your shape is formed, the fun really begins - painting and decorating with a full range of colours, patterns, and finishes. Go bold or go minimal. Either way, it’s totally your style.
Learn as you go
As you’re creating, we’ll talk you through the whole process - how clay behaves, how pieces are fired in the kiln at a sizzling 1300°C, and how glazing gives your creation a glossy, food-safe finish. It’s hands-on, informative and super satisfying seeing how a lump of clay transforms into something beautiful and lasting.
Want to keep it forever?
For £6-10 (depending on size), we’ll fire and glaze your piece so it’s microwave, dishwasher and life-proof. You’ll get a proper, usable item you made with your own hands.

title: 3.5 Hour Introductory Watercolour Workshop for Beginners
description:
Personalised Guidance in Small Group

To ensure a high-quality experience, our workshops are limited to just six students. This allows our instructor to dedicate one-on-one time to each participant, offering tailored advice and feedback to help you grow as an artist.




A Guided Path to a Beautiful Painting

Choose one of four beautiful landscapes, each thoughtfully designed as the perfect project for a beginner. This is far more than just copying. Our focus is on the 'why' behind every step, ensuring you understand the process and leave with foundational skills, not just a pretty picture




Start for the Line Work

From blank page to bold lines. We guide you step-by-step through the inking process. Pro tools provided, plus my secret weapon for unique textures: a chopstick! Ready to get creative




Controlling the Magic of Watercolour

Watercolour's magic lies in the dance of water and pigment. Our methodical approach is designed to demystify this process. You'll learn precisely how to handle the water and master core techniques, gaining the skills to unlock your creative freedom.




The Final Touch

At the end of the class, we will professionally mount your work, transforming it into a beautiful piece that’s ready to be framed and displayed with pride. It's the perfect way to celebrate your artistic achievement.




Paintting in a Real Artist Studio

This is more than just a classroom; it’s the personal, working studio of an award-winning illustrator. You'll be surrounded by original art, professional tools, and a truly creative atmosphere—the very space where daily artistic practice happens. Learn and create, feeling the inspiration that fills the room.



Always wanted to try watercolour but found it hard to start on your own? This is the systematic foundation for those serious about learning authentic techniques.
This 3.5-hour workshop is a comprehensive deep dive, not just a simple trial. Led by an award-winning illustrator in a professional studio dedicated solely to watercolour, you will receive all the guidance needed to start your journey with confidence. You'll leave not only with a beautiful painting but with the skills to continue learning independently.
Many of our students progress directly from this foundational workshop into our advanced classes to create their own original art. See their incredible progress on our Instagram: @venchoartstudio.
————————————————————————————————————
What we do Learn：
In this 3.5-hour art class in London, you will explore and learn professional watercolour techniques, including wet-on-wet, and dry-on-dry, using the highest quality painting materials available on the market. By the end of your first class, you will complete a full watercolor landscape painting.
Throughout the session, we'll guide you in recreating a painting, ensuring you grasp each step from sketching to inking, and ultimately to applying watercolour. We provide four landscape watercolour painting samples, allowing you to choose your preferred subject matter. Each sample focuses on specific techniques for practice.
Additionally, we'll show you how to select various watercolour tools from the art shop. This includes selecting suitable watercolor paper, mounting techniques, choosing pigments, and matching them with your brushes. We will also provide tips on using all the materials, so you don't need to prepare any tools in advance.
————————————————————————————————————
The Material We Use: Professional Quality for Beginners
We believe that using the finest tools is the secret to falling in love with watercolour. We provide everything you need, so you can enjoy a professional experience without the high cost of buying your own gear:
· Premium "Mistake-Proof" Palette: You’ll use my personally curated palette, combining the best pigments from Daniel Smith, Winsor & Newton, Sennelier, and Schmincke. These professional colours stay vibrant and won't turn "muddy, " making it easy for you to mix beautiful tones.
· The Gold-Standard Paper (Arches 300g): We use 100% cotton professional paper. It absorbs water beautifully and stays flat, ensuring your painting looks clean and high-end even if it's your first time.
· Professional Squirrel Hair Brushes: These soft, high-quality brushes hold more paint, allowing for smooth, fluid strokes that synthetic brushes just can't match.
### Our Secret Preparation: The Perfect Surface
· To ensure you have a flawless experience, I personally "Wet-Mount" your paper before you arrive. This is a professional, time-consuming technique where the paper is soaked and stretched onto a board.
· Why this matters to you: It means your paper will remain perfectly flat like a drum, no matter how much water you use. You can focus entirely on your creativity without worrying about the paper buckling or puddling—a luxury usually reserved for professional studios.
——————————————————————————————————
Meet your Tutor ：
Vencho Wang is an award-winning illustrator whose talent is endorsed by Arts Council England—a prestigious recognition reserved for artists demonstrating exceptional potential on a global stage. As a professional specialising in the medium, her studio focuses exclusively on watercolour. Vencho’s mission is to share the sophisticated techniques and creative mindset of professional illustration, helping aspiring artists bridge the gap between hobby and artistry.
——————————————————————————————————
More of our students painting：
Our studio doors open every Saturday for both our foundational workshops for beginners and our advanced sessions. It is a dedicated day for creativity, learning, and community. To see the beautiful results and incredible progress of our students, we invite you to visit our Instagram gallery: @venchoartstudio

title: Woodcut Printing Workshop
description:
Getting to Know the Tools

We begin the session with a 15 minute introduction to the set of 5 Japanese tools: how they carve and how best to safely use them. Each blade is unique in it's shape and cutting style - we'll run through each blade by making individual cuts and finish by carving out the drawn up circle.




Carving the Circle

This exercise is key in showing how best to use the most important tool in the set: the Hangito (flat knife). Scoring the line of the circle enables a safe guide to carve the shape using the V blade with precision and definition.




Printing the Starter Circle and Cuts

Now the circle and cuts will be printed by hand using the bamboo barens (burnishing discs), onto newsprint using inked rollers.

Two prints from the block will be pulled after being inked only once: the 1st print is always the fullest/darkest image (ink wise) and the 2nd print showing less ink as the 'ghost print'. This is a good moment to show the difference between both prints - whether it's ink, tone, wood grain or faint marks coming through onto the paper.




Print Selection to Show the Numerous Fun Ways to Make Woodcut Prints

Examples of experimental prints and traditional techniques, which are key to the history of woodcut printing: multi layered prints, reduction cuts, jigsaw prints, abstract cuts and German Expressionist inspired portraits.



The workshop is about learning the use of traditional Japanese hand tools, the process of inking Japanese Shina wood blocks, printing on different types of handmade printing paper and developing a new understanding of various techniques in woodcut art. All of these enable you to make numerous fine art prints to take away at the end of the session!
Printing Class Structure
Intro - Cups of tea, coffee or soft drinks followed by some words from me on my printmaking career and a round-the-table 'meet and greet' from everyone to begin the workshop.
Stage one - We will cover the use of hand tools to design, draw and cut woodblocks and explore the process of hand printing using traditional Japanese barens (circular discs wrapped in bamboo) and rollers on three types of paper.
Stage two - Delve a little deeper, showing you how to use multiple blocks and reduction-cutting techniques to create more complex multi-colour prints.
Stage three - This a perfect opportunity to make multiple prints through editions, ending the final part of the session by experimenting with your favourite design or playing with various colours.
Stage four - I'll be collecting everyone's individual prints and rolling them up into tubes for safe passage home.
I'll hand out a materials list from my favourite suppliers I use for the studio - a great resource to encourage more printing in the future!
My studio is on floor 6 at Regent Studios: if you’re not taking the stairs please take the right hand lift and depart on floor 6 for studio 64B. For all evening workshops there will be plenty of snacks available, especially for those who've come straight from work. The day sessions include a light plant-based lunch: homemade soup with sourdough. Please do let me know if you have any dietary requirements or allergies.
Thanks, Alex

If you have always loved the principles and aesthetic of Kintsugi repair but haven't had the time to learn or haven't known where to begin, this workshop is for you! Kintsugi, the art of 'golden joinery', originated in Japan and has since been practised and taught for over 600 years. Embracing the tradition of highlighting imperfection instead of disguising it, traditional Kintsugi uses gold and lacquer to mend broken ceramic objects.
This specially designed two-hour taster session, taught in the heart of Stoke Newington, will have you better understanding Kintsugi fundamentals. After this session, you will come away with a beautiful mended object (or two!) which will make a gorgeous keepsake for yourself or a gift for someone you love.

All materials will be supplied, including one piece of reclaimed stoneware or Japanese tea bowl. You can also bring along your own broken piece which we will assess together and then repair if time allows. Time to pull out Grandma's teacup and saucer that you accidentally broke 2 years ago and have been hiding ever since!
For this course, modern repair materials will be used in combination with historic materials for a stunning result. Kintsugi Repair kits will also be available for purchase so that you can continue the practise at home.

title: Charcuterie Board Woodworking Workshop
description:
Design Your Board Shape

Choose your wood blank from a couple of varieties of timber and design your own board shape. Mark it out onto the wood. Let your creativity flow!




Cut on the Bandsaw

Using a bandsaw, carefully cut out your shape! Bandsaws are a safe and satisfying tool to use - see your design come to life!




Edge Sanding

Using table top sanding machines, you’ll sand the edge of the boards to refine the shape. We’ve been told by our students this step is very therapeutic!




Drill the Handle

Using the drill press, you’ll drill out the handle hole for your board. The wood shavings from this step are beautifully tactile.




Orbital Sanding

Using an orbital sander and a bit of hand sanding as well, you’ll get your board super smooth and ready for some oil!




Oiling

Using our non toxic and food safe oil, you’ll finish your boards and watch the wood grain come to life! This step is the most exciting because of the dramatic change in the wood!




Finish

Revel in the knowledge that you made this beautiful object with your own two hands! Take it home and let it dry over night before using it to serve yourself a feast of charcuterie to celebrate!



Looking for hands-on woodworking classes in London? Join Harry and Johanna from Variegate and learn how to design and make a sustainable charcuterie board for your home using offcuts from their furniture projects!
First of all, ensuring everyone's safety is paramount, so we'll conduct a comprehensive safety briefing, familiarising you with the tools we'll be using.
Next, it's time to unleash your creativity! You'll handpick a piece of wood sourced from the offcuts of our furniture business. Whether you wish to design a custom board shape or use one of our stencils, the choice is entirely yours.
Under our expert guidance, you'll bring your design to life using a bandsaw and then refine and perfect it with a variety of tools at your disposal; hand sandpaper, an orbital sander, and a disc/belt sander. You'll achieve a smooth and polished finish that showcases the natural beauty of the wood.
To protect and enhance your charcuterie board, you'll learn how to apply mineral oil and get a quick rundown on how to properly care for your board.
Our practical woodworking classes are comprehensive and designed for complete beginners, so no prior knowledge or experience with woodworking is needed. Give the gift of creativity and craft to yourself or a loved one!

title: Mosaic Making Class
description:
Discover Your Creative Retreat

Step into our London studio, a creative space stacked with treasures. You'll meet your passionate teachers, who bring over 25 years of mosaic-making experience to guide and inspire you on your creative journey.




Choose Your Perfect Pieces

Explore shelves full of vibrant tiles to find the perfect colours and textures for your design. Don't worry if you're new to mosaics; we'll help you gather everything you need!




Plan Your Pattern

Begin arranging your chosen tiles on your base (a selection to choose from: tiles or shapes). This is your chance to play with different layouts and patterns to get a feel for your design. Your friendly teachers will be on hand to offer tips and tricks.




Cut, Shape, and Stick

Learn how to use professional tools to snip and shape your tiles to fit your vision. Then, start fixing your pieces into place, watching as your unique design comes together one tile at a time.




Add the Finishing Touch

Once your tiles are all set, you'll learn the important step of how to apply grout to fill the gaps and make your design pop. A final polish will make your creation shine!




Take Home Your Handmade Tile

Enjoy your finished mosaic. You can leave your mosaic ungrouted if you prefer, or take it home ready to grout (the pieces need to fully set within 12 hours). We provide a bag of grout, clear instructions and a glove so you can finish it at home. We wrap it for you to carry home.

title: Taster Pottery Making Workshop - Deptford
description:
Are you searching for relaxed and calming activities in London, away from a hectic city lifestyle? Unwind and release your creativity by joining a pottery making workshop in Deptford!
Beginners are welcome to this London pottery class. You'll receive plenty of support from your teacher as you transform clay into handmade pottery pieces. Your local teacher will guide you through hand-building techniques using coils and slabs. You'll also get to try wheel throwing!
No matter your experience level, whether you're a novice or an experienced clay artist, this workshop provides an excellent opportunity to relax in a beautiful London pottery studio and explore your creative side.
After the session, your pottery will be taken to be fired and glazed and will be available for collection after three weeks. You can then showcase your beautiful pieces at home or gift them to your loved ones!
Please note:
Please note: This is an adult pottery class. Participants aged 11 years and over are welcome, provided they are able to work independently in an adult-paced group class. This is not a children's class.
Your finished pieces will be fired and glazed, ready to collect 4 weeks after the class.
A materials fee of £5 per piece of pottery kept is NOT included in the class and is payable on the day of your workshop.
Pieces are ready around 4-5 weeks after the class. We will send you an email when they are ready to be collected. Please check you email and spam folder. We will keep your pots in the studio for a month. If not collected in time they may be disposed of.
It is your responsibility to arrive on time for the class. Upon arriving to your class 30 minutes or later, we have the right to reject you joining the class without any refund or rescheduling.
No cancellations or reschedules allowed.
During summer, there is no air conditioning in the studio, so please bring water and dress for the heat!
During winter, it would be a bit cold in the studio. Whilst we try our best to keep the studio warm, please prepare an extra coat or clothes to keep yourself warm during class.
Please enter and leave the studio quietly - the studio is in the middle of the neighbourhood!
** Please note that due to the nature of ceramics, final results may vary and cannot be guaranteed. This includes, but is not limited to:
Glaze colours and finishes may vary from samples and are for reference only.
Textures and fine details may appear differently after firing.
Finished pieces will shrink by approximately 15% during the drying and firing process.
Minor imperfections, such as small clay marks or uneven surfaces, may be present.
Pieces may crack, warp or break during drying or firing.
We take every care throughout the making and firing process; however, these are natural characteristics and risks of working with clay and cannot always be prevented.
If a piece is damaged beyond use during the firing process, we will reimburse the £5 materials and firing fee paid for that piece. Class fees are non-refundable.
What you'll get
Clay, aprons and tools will be provided during the class.
If you would like to keep your finished pieces, a materials and firing fee of £5 per piece is payable on the day of the class.
Finished pieces are usually ready for collection 4–5 weeks after the class. We will notify you by email when they are ready. Please check your inbox and spam/junk folder.
We will store finished pieces for one month from the date of our collection email. Pieces not collected within this period may be disposed of due to limited storage space.
Please note that ceramics are fragile. While every care is taken, cracking, warping or breakage can occur during the drying and firing process. These are natural risks of ceramics, and we cannot guarantee that every piece will be successfully fired.

title: Pottery Wheel Throwing and Hand Building Taster Workshop
description:
Welcome & Introduction

Escape the city and step into our tranquil canalside studio in Alperton, NW London . A calm, plant-filled space overlooking the Grand Union Canal. We'll welcome you with a warm hello, show you around, and get you settled in. From the moment you walk in, the city quiets down.




Introduction to Pottery

Your tutor walks you through the journey ahead: how clay behaves, what wheel throwing and hand building actually feel like, the materials you'll work with, and the glaze options waiting for you at the end. No prior knowledge needed ,you'll leave knowing more about ceramics than 99% of people.




Wheel-Throwing Session

Now the fun begins. Sit at the wheel, plant your hands in cool, wet clay, and learn to centre, open and pull your first pot. Your tutor will be right beside you, guiding, correcting, encouraging. Most people are shocked at how quickly the wheel starts to feel intuitive.




Hand-Building Session

Step away from the wheel and explore pottery's older, slower art. Through pinching, slab-building and coiling, you'll shape clay entirely with your hands, no spinning, no rush. It's where pottery feels most meditative.




Decorating Your Pieces

Time to make it yours. Add texture with carving tools, brush on colour with underglaze, or experiment with patterns and personal touches. Whatever you make, it will be unmistakably yours.




Finishing & Glazing Option

Choose any pieces you'd like to keep and we'll glaze and kiln-fire them for £6 each. You'll be notified when they're ready , usually about 4 weeks later at which point you'll have a beautiful, finished, functional piece of pottery that you made with your own hands.



Join this beginner-friendly pottery taster class in North West London and find a calm, plant-filled retreat away from the rush of the city. Set right on the Grand Union Canal at The Slightly Curious Studio, this workshop is the perfect way to spend a few hours whether you're planning a unique date, celebrating a birthday, or finally ticking "learn to throw a pot" off your bucket list.
Over three hours, you'll get hands-on with the full pottery experience. You'll move through three distinct areas of the craft:
Wheel throwing – Master the basics of shaping clay on the potter's wheel with expert guidance.
Hand building – Learn how to pinch and coil your way to a unique creation.
Decoration – Add those final personal touches to your work before it's ready for the kiln.
There's no need to feel any creative anxiety; our tutors have been teaching for years and keep groups small so you'll get plenty of personal attention. We'll have everything set up for you – including the clay, tools, and aprons – so you can simply show up and enjoy the friendly, low-pressure atmosphere.
You'll finish your London pottery session with a newfound sense of confidence and a piece or two of your own work to collect once they've been fired and glazed. It's a wonderful opportunity to switch off and enjoy the rewarding feeling of creating something beautiful from scratch.
What you'll get
3 hours of hands-on tuition with an experienced ceramics tutor.
All materials provided: clay, tools, aprons.
Wheel throwing instruction (centering, opening, pulling).
Hand-building instruction (pinching, coiling, slab work).
Decoration time with underglaze, carving tools and surface techniques.
Friendly small-group setting (max 12 students).
Optional kiln firing and glazing for £6 per piece.
Pieces ready to collect approximately 4 weeks after class.

title: Authentic Chinese Hand-Pulled Biang Biang Noodles Masterclass
description:
A Warm Welcome

Welcome to our fun, friendly London kitchen, where you'll discover the secrets of authentic Biang Biang noodles. Your expert teacher will introduce you to this famous Xi'an dish, explaining its tradition of bringing long life—perfect for a celebration!




Create the Signature Sauce

Next, you’ll create the amazing sauce to top your noodles. Learn to make either the aromatic Chilli Sauce or a delicious non-spicy Spring Onion Oil. Best of all, you get to take the rest of the jar home with you!




Prepare the Perfect Dough

Get hands-on with the most important first step: making the noodle dough. You'll learn how to mix and knead your dough from scratch using all-natural ingredients to create the perfect texture, ready for pulling.




Hand Pull Your Noodles

This is the moment you’ve been waiting for! Experience the incredible fun of stretching and pulling your dough into one long, continuous noodle. With expert guidance, you’ll master the technique – why not try and beat our 5.1-metre record?




Your Finished Bowl

Assemble your masterpiece and dig in! You'll enjoy a steaming, delicious bowl of your very own hand-pulled noodles, coated in the sauce you made. You'll leave with a full belly and the skills to recreate this amazing vegan-friendly dish at home.




Add-on Recipe Collection Booklet

This is your journey of cooking adventure.
You can get beautifully designed and printed recipe from each class once you bought the booklet (Two colours to choose).
You also will get Polaroid-style photo sticker from your class, showing your highlight in the class you attended.
Your chef tutor also will give you a stamp. It is your certificate of success.



Did you know that in China, a long strand of noodles symbolises long life? That’s why Biang Biang noodles are often enjoyed at birthdays and celebrations. If you’re looking for a unique birthday gift experience in London — this is it.
Inspired by the bold flavours of Xi’an street food, this hands-on cooking class teaches you how to make authentic Hand-Pulled Biang Biang Noodles (La Mian) completely from scratch — no additives, no shortcuts, just proper technique.
Love spicy food? You’ll adore the aromatic chilli oil topping. Prefer something milder? We also offer a beautifully fragrant spring onion oil version — equally delicious and fully vegan.
Best of all, the class is thoughtfully designed to be vegan-friendly. If you’re a meat lover, you can explore our dedicated Beef Biang Biang Noodle Class separately, https://classbento.co.uk/w/tmkn.
Whether you're a complete beginner or a confident home cook, your friendly tutor will guide you step by step in a small, spacious, air-conditioned studio. Weekday bookings often feel like a private class.
In this class, you will learn to:
Prepare and knead noodle dough to achieve perfect elasticity
Hand-pull Biang Biang noodles from scratch (challenge our 5.1 metre record!)
Make authentic Xi’an-style chilli sauce and take the remaining jar home. Alternatively, prepare a non-spicy spring onion oil (please mention preference at booking)
Cook, assemble, and plate your noodles beautifully
By the end of the workshop, you’ll sit down to enjoy your handmade noodles — chewy, glossy, and proudly created by you. You’ll leave not only with a full belly, but with a skill that genuinely impresses.

title: Kintsugi Workshop
description:
Discover the beautiful Japanese art of Kintsugi by repairing a handmade ceramic pot created by one of our studio potters. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn traditional-inspired repair techniques and leave with your own unique piece to take home.
Guided by our experienced ceramicists, you'll restore a broken pot using the principles of Kintsugi, celebrating cracks and imperfections rather than hiding them. No previous experience is required, making this a relaxing and rewarding introduction to this timeless craft.
About Kintsugi
Kintsugi (金継ぎ, meaning "golden joinery") is the Japanese art of repairing broken pottery by highlighting rather than concealing the cracks. Traditionally, broken pieces are rejoined using lacquer mixed or dusted with precious metals such as gold, silver or platinum.
Beyond its technique, Kintsugi embraces the Japanese philosophy of wabi-sabi—finding beauty in imperfection—and reflects the idea that damage and repair become part of an object's history rather than something to hide.
Important Information
Repaired pieces created during this workshop are not food safe and should be used for decorative purposes only.

title: Beef Hand Pulled Biang Biang Noodle Class
description:
Welcome and Prep

Arrive at a bright, welcoming kitchen where your instructor greets you with a smile. Start by prepping your ingredients and learning some Chinese knife skills.




Beef Short Ribs

Practise your Chinese knife skills as you prepare the beef that will top your hand-pulled noodles, learning tips to get perfect slices every time.




Knead the Dough

Learn to knead the dough -- a key step to ensure your noodles stretch long, smooth, and ready for hand-pulling.




Make Your Noodles

The most fun part of the class -- hand-pull your noodles! See how long you can stretch them and maybe even beat the class record.




Taste the Success

Sit down to enjoy your hand-pulled noodles, proud of your efforts. Take home new skills, recipes, and the joy of making noodles by hand.




Add-on Crispy Chilli Sauce

Learn to make the popular crispy chilli sauce to serve with your noodle and take the rest home.




Add-on Knife Sharpening

Learn more Chinese knife skills in this pre-class add-on.




Add-on Recipe Collection Booklet

This is your journey of cooking adventure.
You can get beautifully designed and printed recipe from each class once you bought the booklet (Two colours to choose).
You also will get Polaroid-style photo sticker from your class, showing your highlight in the class you attended.
Your chef tutor also will give you a stamp. It is your certificate of success.



For years, guests have asked:
“Simon, what’s your favourite dish?”
This is the one.
Wide, hand-pulled Biang Biang noodles served with tender oven-baked beef and served with homemade chilli sauce — comforting, generous and full of flavour. It’s the kind of dish that feels like home.
This class is created especially for meat lovers who want to learn something truly hands-on and satisfying.
(If you prefer a plant-based option, you can book our vegan-friendly Biang Biang Hand-Pulled Noodle Class here, https://classbento.co.uk/w/j9dn)
A Comforting, Hands-On Cooking Experience in London
In this relaxed and welcoming class, you’ll learn how to make authentic Biang Biang noodles (La Mian) completely from scratch — just flour, water and technique.
No additives. No shortcuts. Just traditional skills passed down properly.
You’ll gently build confidence as you knead, stretch and pull your dough into long, beautiful noodles. Don’t worry if you’re new to cooking — we guide you step by step.
Classes are small and held in our spacious, air-conditioned studio. Weekday sessions are often very quiet, sometimes even private, giving you plenty of time to ask questions and enjoy the process.
In This Class, You Will Learn To:
Make authentic hand-pulled Biang Biang noodles from scratch
Strengthen and stretch dough using traditional pulling techniques
Slice and prepare beef using a Chinese kitchen knife
Season and bake the beef for maximum flavour
Plate your dish beautifully and enjoy it fresh
If you enjoy a little heat, you can also add our Crispy Chilli Sauce experience — you’ll make a jar to share and take home.
There is something incredibly satisfying about sitting down to eat noodles you stretched with your own hands.
Why Guests Love This Class
It feels relaxed and personal, never rushed
The hand-pulling technique is fun, impressive and deeply satisfying
You learn real traditional skills — not shortcuts
The flavour combination is comforting and bold
You leave with a dish you’re genuinely proud of
Many guests say it’s both calming and energising at the same time — especially when they finally stretch that long noodle successfully!
Allergy Information
Gluten (essential)
Soy used in sauce
Sesame, peanut and celery may be used in sauce (can be avoided upon request at booking stage)
Please let us know about any dietary requirements after booking and we will do our best to accommodate.
Add-On Experiences
All add-ons take place within the same session to make your visit even more enjoyable. Please allow an additional 30–60 minutes depending on your selection.
Popular options include:
Crispy Chilli Sauce – Our signature homemade sauce to elevate your noodles
Smashed Cucumber Salad – A refreshing, vegan-friendly classic
Bubble Cocktail or Drinks – Perfect for celebrations or date nights
Knife Sharpening – Learn more about the traditional Chinese kitchen knife (you may bring one from home if safe to do so)
Apron with logo to wear at home cooking in the future
Recipe Collection Booklet to collect beautifully designed and printed recipes
If you’ve travelled to join us, it’s a lovely way to make the most of your experience.
Come and enjoy a calm, welcoming cooking space in London. You’ll leave with a full belly, flour on your apron, and a new skill that stays with you long after the class ends.

Your Dim Sum Feast

title: Cheeky Rug Tufting Workshop
description:
Send Your Design Before the Class

Send us your design before the workshop and we’ll prepare it on your canvas in advance. If your idea needs adjusting for the best tufting result, our team can guide you before the session.




Choose from 115 Yarn Colours

When you arrive, you’ll choose your colours from our own cheekyarn range, made with GRS-certified recycled yarn. With over 115 colours available, you can make your rug feel truly personal.




Learn the Tufting Basics

Never used a tufting gun before? No problem. We’ll show you how the equipment works, how to move with control and how to start building your design with confidence.




Tuft with Close Guidance

Our team stays nearby throughout the session to help with technique, rethreading, colour changes and tricky parts of your design. You’ll never be left wondering what to do next.




We Professionally Finish Your Rug

After the tufting is complete, our team handles the trimming, glueing, backing and shaping. This final process helps your rug look polished, neat and ready for home.




Leave with Something Worth Keeping

You’ll receive a custom rug made from your own design and colours. It’s more than a fun afternoon in London — it’s something personal you’ll actually want to display at home.




Complimentary Drink

Enjoy a complimentary Sonic Tonics drink during your workshop. Pick a flavour, settle in, and sip while you tuft, chill, and create your own rug!



Spend three creative hours turning your own design into a custom 40 × 40 cm tufted rug at Cheeky Studio, our premium tufting studio in Hackney Wick, East London.
This workshop is designed for complete beginners, but the result is made to feel polished, personal and worth keeping. You do not need any previous tufting experience or drawing skills. Send us your design before the class and we’ll prepare it on your canvas in advance, so you can arrive, choose your colours and start tufting with confidence.
To make the experience even more relaxed, each guest will also receive one complimentary Sonic Tonics drink to enjoy during the workshop. Pick a flavour, settle in, sip while you tuft, and enjoy a playful creative session in our cosy London studio.

description:
If you're keen to explore your creativity and want to feel more at home with yourself, come along to this mandala drawing workshop and enjoy a meditative, purposeful art experience.
In the ancient Sanskrit language of Hinduism and Buddhism, mandala means “circle.”
Traditionally, a mandala is a geometric design or pattern that represents the cosmos or deities in various heavenly worlds. Creating a mandala is a form of ‘artistic meditation’, which involves a careful, quiet, prayerful kind of attention, helping you:
Feel more balanced and centred in yourself
Be a bridge between your conscious and unconscious self
Improve concentration and develop mindfulness
Enhance your sense of awareness and perception of shapes and patterns
In this beginner-friendly drawing workshop, you'll learn how to create a mandala design using geometry, with the traditional tools of a compass, straight-edge, pencil and pen.
In your journey of creating beautiful art, you extend your curiosity outwards from the centre and inwards within yourself. The process is in itself a wonderful metaphor for Life's journey: How we navigate pathways and intersections, follow lines of interest, pause to step back and contemplate the whole, and trust the gradual unfolding without knowing the end result.
So come join in for a surreal experience, which is fun and engaging over a cup of coffee!
This workshop is held in a beautiful cafe, where you can purchase coffee or tea of your choice at additional cost! (Optional)
Additionally, you can purchase my Mandala Journey Workbook, specially designed and curated with 100+ patterns to practice your art and 20 mandala grid templates for you to create your own stunning Mandala artwork at home. The workbook can be purchased alongside the workshop. (Optional).
In this workbook, you’ll find a thoughtful blend of guided exercises and open spaces to help you build confidence, consistency, and calm through art.

100+ curated mandala patterns to practise line work, detailing, rhythm, and flow
20 mandala grids & guided templates to help you create balanced designs with ease
Inspiring quote pages and mindful pauses throughout
Space for free exploration and your own creative expression

Build your own personal “keep book” of patterns, ideas, and progress

title: Italian Cooking Class and Prosecco Tasting Experience
description:
Welcome & Introduction

Guests are greeted with a warm welcome, while sipping a glass of bubbly and nibbling on a a few classic Italian antipasti.




Pasta Dough Explanation

Introduction of the different pasta flours used, pasta history explanation, step-by-step demonstration of core pasta kneading techniques.




Pasta Shaping

Learn how to roll out the pasta dough and make shapes with it.




Tagliatelle Pasta Cutting

Everyone follows along cutting the Tagliatelle with personalized tips from the instructor.




Time for Enjoying the Meal and Socialising

Celebrate the hard work by eating the pasta dish, pairing it with a lovely prosecco, while socialising with the other attendees.



Begin your evening with a warm Italian welcome. As you arrive, you’ll be greeted with a glass of premium sparkling wine and a selection of traditional antipasti, setting the perfect mood for a relaxed and friendly pasta workshop.
To start, you’ll enjoy a tasting of different sparkling wines while learning how to recognise their aromas, flavours, and textures. You’ll also discover how beautifully bubbles pair with Italian cuisine.
Once everyone is feeling inspired, it’s time to roll up your sleeves and dive into pasta making. You’ll begin by preparing fresh pasta dough from scratch, learning simple kneading techniques while hearing fascinating stories about pasta’s history and traditions. With guidance, you’ll transform your dough into delicate strands of tagliatelle — one of Italy’s most beloved pasta shapes.
Next comes the cooking. Your freshly made tagliatelle will be served with a rich, traditional meat ragù. A vegetarian option will also be available, and special dietary requirements can be accommodated with advance notice.
When everything is ready, you’ll sit down to enjoy the fruits of your work. More sparkling wine will be poured as the room fills with lively conversation, laughter, and the joy of sharing food together.
At the end of the experience, you’ll receive a PDF recipe so you can recreate your handmade pasta at home and impress friends and family. You’ll leave with new skills, great memories, and a refreshed spirit. There’s nothing quite like the pride of creating something with your own hands — and, of course, the pleasure of enjoying the delicious dish you’ve made.
Location
The workshop takes place in a private flat near Victoria Station. The aim is to create a cosy and welcoming atmosphere, just like being in a real Italian family home. You’ll feel comfortable the moment you step inside.
For larger groups (over 10 people), such as corporate events, birthday celebrations, hen parties, or team-building experiences, a professional kitchen will be required. These venues are located in different areas of London, including Victoria, Old Street, Borough, and Covent Garden. Venue hire is subject to availability and an additional fee will apply. Please get in touch for more details.
Get ready for a delicious and joyful handmade pasta experience.
Sip, cook, and socialise in true Italian style!

title: Calligraphy Workshop
description:
Settle in and Embrace the Flow

Find your spot, relax, and take in the calm, creative atmosphere. Discover the beauty and mystery of calligraphy — where every stroke becomes a mindful expression.




Get Ready and Give It a Try

Everything you need is provided — brushes, ink, paper, and more — so you can dive straight into the art of beautiful writing.




Master the Strokes

Learn foundational brush techniques step by step. With guidance and practice, you’ll start to feel the rhythm and precision behind each elegant line.




Create Your Calligraphy Masterpiece

Bring your learning together to design your own expressive artwork — a reflection of your creativity and personal touch.




Admire and Take It Home

Once your piece is complete, take it home with pride — a unique creation and a beautiful reminder of your special experience.



Immerse yourself in an inspiring calligraphy and brush lettering class in London, where you will delve into the world of brush and ink creations in a tranquil setting. During this workshop, you will discover how to create stunning calligraphy pieces using traditional materials with the guidance of expert instructors in a small-group setting. By the end of the session, you can proudly take home your own masterpiece as a tangible memento of your newfound skills.
Beginners are embraced in this enriching activity, providing a nurturing environment for you to learn and grow at your own pace.
Specially tailored guidance will help you hone your skills and unleash your creativity in each brushstroke.
You may feel inspired and serene as you embark on this artistic journey, discovering the joy of calligraphy and brush lettering.
This class promises a transformative experience, equipping you with the knowledge and confidence to create beautiful pieces of art. Take home not just your artwork, but also a newfound passion for the timeless art of calligraphy and brush lettering.
What you'll get
Create their own beautiful calligraphy artwork to take home or gift to a loved one.

title: Handmade Ravioli Pasta Making Workshop
description:
Welcome & Introduction

Guests are greeted with a warm welcome, while sipping a glass of bubbly and nibbling on a few classic Italian antipasti.




Pasta Dough Explanation

title: Kintsugi Workshop
description:
Discover the beautiful Japanese art of Kintsugi by repairing a handmade ceramic pot created by one of our studio potters. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn traditional-inspired repair techniques and leave with your own unique piece to take home.
Guided by our experienced ceramicists, you'll restore a broken pot using the principles of Kintsugi, celebrating cracks and imperfections rather than hiding them. No previous experience is required, making this a relaxing and rewarding introduction to this timeless craft.
About Kintsugi
Kintsugi (金継ぎ, meaning "golden joinery") is the Japanese art of repairing broken pottery by highlighting rather than concealing the cracks. Traditionally, broken pieces are rejoined using lacquer mixed or dusted with precious metals such as gold, silver or platinum.
Beyond its technique, Kintsugi embraces the Japanese philosophy of wabi-sabi—finding beauty in imperfection—and reflects the idea that damage and repair become part of an object's history rather than something to hide.
Important Information
Repaired pieces created during this workshop are not food safe and should be used for decorative purposes only.
What you'll get
* One handmade ceramic pot to repair and take home
* All tools and materials provided
* Step-by-step guidance from our experienced tutors

Bring Your Own Piece (Optional)

Please note:
* All broken pieces must be present. Unfortunately, we cannot repair ceramics with missing fragments.
* This workshop is designed as a hands-on learning experience, not a professional restoration service. Participants will repair their own pieces under the guidance of our tutors.
* If your ceramic is particularly valuable or has significant sentimental importance, we recommend consulting a professional ceramic conservator or restorer instead.

Master the difference between spring rolls and summer rolls

Prepare a beautifully balanced dipping sauce to elevate every bite

Small, intimate class sizes
Personal attention from expert instructors
A calm, welcoming environment
Often available as a private weekday experience

the crispness, the freshness, the warmth of something crafted entirely by your own hands.
You may also take your creations home—
a beautiful reminder of the experience, ready to be shared with those you love.

Fresh, thoughtfully selected ingredients
Authentic techniques passed down through culinary tradition
Vegan-friendly options for spring rolls
A balance of taste, texture, and visual beauty

Connection

Important Booking Information
Price is per person. Each attendee must hold a valid ticket.

If you need to reschedule your booking, a £50 fee per person applies. Reschedule requests must be made at least 7 days before your scheduled class date.
Arrival & Punctuality
Classes begin promptly. A 15-minute grace period is provided. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the scheduled start time, we may not be able to admit you and your booking will be forfeited.

title: Ring Making Workshop
description:
Sift Through Inspiration

The workshop will begin with an introduction to the rich history of the lost wax casting process and how it is done in our studio. We will then spend some time looking through a selection of rings in all styles, shapes and textures to begin brainstorming your idea. There will also be books, gemstones and plenty to draw inspiration from!




Discuss Your Idea (s) and Design

Natasha will individually discuss the ideas and designs you have in mind, and give you right jewellers wax to create it. In addition to the typically hard wax for carving there is also soft wax, sheet wax and wax wire to help create your specific design!




Sketching Your Unique Design

You'll start by determining your ring size and thinking about the depth and width of your ring design. From there you will sketch out a rough blueprint to follow when carving your design.




Carve, Sculpt, Melt and Shape Your Custom Design

You’ll be guided step-by-step through the wax carving process. First by sizing your wax accordingly, then by applying your design to the wax. I do tailer a portion of the workshop to each individual's design, but will also cover all the different methods and techniques used in wax carving for lost wax casting.




Add the Finishing Touches

In the last stage of the workshop, you can smooth out any imperfections, add engraving, discuss the finish (matte, shiny or in between) and add any gemstones or oxidisation to your ring!




Ring Casting After Class

Once the workshop is complete your wax ring model will be prepared for casting and cast in our studio. The full casting process takes around 15 hours, and is documented and shared on our instagram stories! You can watch the journey of your ring from the casting investment to the final polishing finishes! The turnaround time is usually 2-3 weeks for silver pieces. Solid gold requires extra time for hallmarking and gold vermeil requires up to two additional weeks for plating in Hatton Garden.



In this 2.5 hour hands-on workshop you will learn all the skills required to design and create your own bespoke ring using ancient wax carving techniques!
This workshop is the perfect opportunity to free your mind, get creative and connect with other like-minded people whilst making a special heirloom.
You'll be guided each step of the way by jeweller, Natasha Kutrovacz of Anonoma Jewellery. Natasha trained in NYC and creates custom jewellery for film and TV, alongside her own designs. The workshop is kept small so you will also receive 1:1 guidance on how to create your specific design.
No need to come with a design in mind, the creative process will allow some time to brainstorm with inspiring materials to help you come up with your very own and unique piece of jewellery.
All materials will be provided, and no prior experience is necessary. However, if you would like to deepen your existing skill set, that is possible too. The techniques in wax carving and what you can create in wax are endless! I will tailer a portion of the workshop to each individual's design, but will also cover all the different methods and techniques used in wax carving for lost wax casting.
There will be some exciting optional upgrades available in-class, including gemstone setting, gold plating or engraving to make your ring even more special (available for pre-purchase or to add on the day).
By the end of the class, your piece will be completed, ready for casting. The casting, finishing and polishing takes about 2-3 weeks. If you have opted for gold plating this will take an additional 5-7 working days.
PRICING:
[[ Please read carefully before booking, as the workshop ticket does not include the casting of your ring. ]]
Workshop ticket - £55
This includes your 2.5-hour experience, all tools and materials to make the perfect signet. You will receive 1:1 guidance and a step-by-step demonstration of how to design and carve your own unique ring of choice.
Silver Ring Casting / Polishing fee - £50 + cost of silver at the current rate.
22ct Gold Vermeil Casting / Polishing fee - £95 + cost of silver at the current rate.
This will be charged at the end of class once your wax has been weighed and includes preparing your wax for casting, casting in recycled sterling silver, and polishing your ring to your desired finish. The cost of silver usually starts at £8 and depends on the size/thickness and size of your ring.
CASTING IN SOLID GOLD - You can choose to upgrade your ring to recycled gold in 9, 14 or 18 carats. We will weigh the wax model to determine the cost of gold, and there is an additional £20 added to the casting fee. Hallmarking at the London Assay Office is £25
Gemstones and settings - from £20
I have over 60 different gemstones to choose from and they vary by shape, size, colour and type.
We hold a lot of sentiment in the jewellery we wear. It has the power to transport us, to bring back memories of loved ones and experiences. Hand-making a special heirloom only amplifies this. You can use this time to make the perfect present for a loved one or make a special ring to celebrate yourself.

Plus, a variety of jewellers waxes from ring blanks, to sheet, wire, and soft, mouldable wax.

description:
A Warm Welcome

Step into a cosy, creative space where everything you need is ready and waiting. Meet your friendly teacher and get inspired by beautiful examples of Kokedama on display.




Shape & Wrap

Wrap and bind your kokedama with natural string, creating a design that’s as unique as you are. Guidance is always on hand to help perfect your technique.




Style & Display

Add the finishing touches and learn how to style your kokedama at home—whether hung in the air or displayed in a decorative dish.




Take Home Your Creation

Leave with your handmade kokedama, new skills, and the joy of nurturing your plant at home. Each one is a little piece of living art you’ve made yourself.



Join us for an exciting Kokedama Workshop in collaboration with in-residence lifestyle store, hosted by Hana Flowers London!
Kokedama, which means moss ball in Japanese, is a beautiful and meditative form of plant art where the roots of a plant are wrapped in a ball of soil and moss, transforming it into a living sculpture.
In this hands-on workshop, you will learn the traditional technique of creating your own Kokedama to take home, along with care tips to keep it thriving. No experience needed - just bring your creativity and love for plants!
You will work with a variety of natural materials such as plants, moss, and twine. Crafting with these elements is deeply therapeutic, offering a calming sense of connection to nature.

title: Epoxy Resin Flower Masterclass
description:
Unleash your creativity and discover the beauty of combining natural elements with modern art in our Resin Flowers course at The Rivershop. In this immersive, hands-on workshop, you'll learn how to craft a unique wooden trinket tray using flowers and resin. Whether you're a complete beginner or a seasoned crafter, this course offers an enjoyable, creative journey that will leave you with a stunning handmade piece to cherish or gift.
The course centers around the popular art of resin flowers - an exciting technique that involves embedding natural flowers in resin to create beautiful, long-lasting designs. In addition to crafting your trinket tray, you'll also have the option to upgrade to create a larger tray or wall art if you're feeling adventurous. This is the perfect opportunity to develop a new skill, express your artistic side, and create something uniquely yours.
What You’ll Learn:
Introduction to Resin Art:
We’ll kick off the course by introducing you to the world of resin art. You’ll learn about the different types of resin, their properties, and safety tips to ensure you handle the material properly. Our instructors will demonstrate how to measure and mix resin, how long it takes to cure, and common mistakes to avoid. With a special focus on using resin flowers, you’ll be able to bring vibrant colors and natural elements into your artwork.
Preserving Flowers in Resin:
In this section, you’ll dive into the process of selecting, preparing, and preserving flowers to use in your resin projects. Not all flowers work well with resin, so we’ll guide you through the best choices and show you how to preserve them to maintain their beauty over time. Once your flowers are ready, you’ll learn how to arrange them on your wooden trinket tray to create a captivating, artistic design. The fusion of nature with resin will give your piece a timeless, elegant look that highlights the charm of resin flowers.
Crafting Your Wooden Trinket Tray:
The main project for this course is a wooden trinket tray, which you’ll customise with your own resin flowers design. We will guide you through each step of the process—from preparing your tray to pouring the resin and embedding your floral elements. This project is designed to give you the foundational skills you need to work with resin, while also allowing plenty of room for your own creative expression. You'll leave with a personalised trinket tray that's both functional and decorative.
Advanced Techniques and Optional Upgrades:
Once you’ve mastered the basics, you’ll have the option to take your skills a step further by upgrading your project. If you want to go beyond the trinket tray, you can choose to create a larger wooden tray or even wall art featuring resin flowers. These upgrades allow you to explore more complex designs and work on a bigger canvas, giving you more space to experiment with your artistic ideas. Our instructors will be on hand to help you navigate these larger projects and ensure your final piece is beautifully executed.
Course Details:
What’s Included:
All materials needed to create your wooden trinket tray, including flowers, resin, and finishing supplies, are provided. You’ll also have access to a range of decorative elements to further personalise your piece, such as additional flowers, glitter, and pigments.
Optional Upgrades:
On the day of the course, you’ll have the option to upgrade your project to a larger tray or wall art featuring resin flowers. This is ideal if you want to challenge yourself or create a more prominent piece of art. These upgrades are offered at an additional cost, and you can decide whether to opt for them during the class.
Takeaway:
Your wooden trinket tray will not be ready to take home on the same day due to the resin’s curing time. We will arrange a collection date for your finished piece or offer postage, depending on your preference. Once the resin has fully cured, your resin flowers creation will be ready to adorn your home.

These skills are perfect for home cooking, hosting dinner parties, or surprising friends with something they probably haven’t seen before.
Why Guests Love This Class
Unique buns rarely found in the UK
Fully vegan-friendly by design
Hands-on and beginner-friendly
Small class sizes with expert guidance
Instagram-worthy shapes and textures
Perfect foodie gift experience
Allergy & Diet Information
Please inform us of any dietary requirements via ClassBento message after booking:
Designed to be vegan-friendly
Gluten is essential for dough structure
Add-On Options
All add-ons take place within the same session, allowing you to maximise your visit and experience. Please allow extra time depending on your selection.
Learn additional bun varieties
Drinks pairing options — relax and sip while your buns steam
Jajang Add-On – our chef’s family signature dish (highly recommended)

Apron with logo to wear at home cooking in the future
Recipe Collection Booklet to collect beautifully designed and printed recipes
Important Booking Information
Price is per person. Each attendee must hold a valid ticket.
This is an adult-only class (18+). Don't worry, we have a family class for you and your children. Please visit this link, https://classbento.co.uk/w/9cz5.
Outside food and drinks are not permitted.
Class duration is an estimate and may vary depending on group size.
No Refund Policy
All bookings are non-refundable. If you are unable to attend, you are welcome to transfer your ticket to another adult (18+). Please notify us in advance with the new attendee’s name.
Rescheduling
If you need to reschedule your booking, a £50 fee per person applies. Reschedule requests must be made at least 7 days before your scheduled class date.
Arrival & Punctuality
Classes begin promptly. A 15-minute grace period is provided. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the scheduled start time, we may not be able to admit you and your booking will be forfeited.
Health & Safety Policy
For the safety of all guests and in line with UK food hygiene guidance, anyone experiencing vomiting, diarrhoea, or similar symptoms must be symptom-free for at least 48 hours before attending the class
Guests may be asked to confirm this upon arrival
We reserve the right to refuse entry if this requirement is not met
We appreciate your understanding, as our small-group classes require advance preparation and planning.

title: Chinese Vegan Cooking Class with Tofu
description:
Master Ma Po Tofu

First, you'll learn to make one of China's most famous and flavourful dishes. We’ll show you how to prepare the tofu and create the authentic, aromatic Ma Po sauce, balancing the spices perfectly for that signature taste.




Try More Tofu

Next, explore the gentler side of tofu. To complete your meal, you’ll learn how to create a delicious non-spicy tofu dish, showcasing just how adaptable this wonderful ingredient can be.




Create a Tofu Feast

With expert guidance, you’ll bring all the elements together, cooking and presenting your dishes like a pro. It’s a wonderfully rewarding experience to see your ingredients transform into a complete and beautiful three-course meal.




Admire Your Dishes

It’s time to eat! You can sit down and enjoy the amazing tofu feast you’ve just cooked, or pack it up to take home. You’ll leave with a set of fantastic new recipes and the confidence to cook them again.



Think tofu is bland?
This class may completely change your mind.
If you're looking for a unique gift experience in London, planning something different for a party, or simply curious about plant-based Chinese cooking — this tofu-focused class is a wonderful choice.
Tofu is one of the most versatile and celebrated ingredients in Chinese cuisine. When treated properly, it’s comforting, bold, delicate and deeply satisfying — all at once.
A Relaxed & Flavour-Focused Vegan Cooking Experience
In this welcoming small-group class, your experienced chef teacher will guide you step by step through creating two completely different tofu dishes — proving just how versatile this ingredient can be.

This class is calm, hands-on and full of flavour.

How to prepare tofu and vegetables properly for maximum flavour

How to create the famous Ma Po sauce and balance spice and savoury depth

How to bring everything together into a satisfying two-course meal

It completely changes how they see tofu

You leave with two different dishes from one core ingredient
It’s perfect for plant-based food lovers and curious beginners alike

title: Introductory Printmaking Class
description:
Looking for a new hobby to indulge in this summer? Get your print on with this fun art class in London!
This introductory workshop is a great way to kick start your printmaking journey. Your friendly teacher (and printmaking expert!) will teach you two techniques: lino and drypoint. After that, it'll be up to you which one you will explore for the rest of the workshop.
What is drypoint printmaking?
Drypoint is a fun form of printmaking that involves scratching an image into a thin plastic or metal sheet using a variety of tools. The lines made are then filled with ink and finally, transferred onto paper.
What is lino printmaking?
Lino, also known by those in the business as 'relief' printing, works in the opposite way to drypoint. With lino printing, you start by cutting away everything but the image, then ink the outlying surface and then finally print onto paper.
This adventurous arty class perfect for creative enthusiasts, beginners or someone who's simply looking for a new hobby or fun things to do in London.
By the end of your introductory printmaking workshop, you'll not only have a whole host of newfound knowledge and skills but also your very own prints to take home and admire.

title: Gelli Printing - an Exploratory Monoprinting Workshop
description:
Settle In

Arrive in the space, grab a chair, pop in your tea and coffee order or a drink from the bar, and chat whilst everyone arrives. Get ready to be creative!




Demonstration

After some intros, you'll receive demos on how to use the gelli prints. We'll be using acrylic paint and fresh flowers to create quick-drying prints.




Your Turn to Print

You'll be invited to start printing, with continued support. Experiment as much as you wish! We have collage supplies and papers to explore colour combinations and different approaches.




Choose Your Cards

If you'd like to mount your prints onto greeting cards, we'll have blanks available and the guillotine to chop prints down to size, so you can stick them on in the class and create finished cards!



Discover the joy of playful printmaking at our Gelli Printing Workshop, a relaxed creative session where you’ll experiment with colour, texture, and layered mark-making to create your own unique artworks.
We’ll explore a range of gelli printing techniques, including printing with natural textures, painting directly onto the plate, and building abstract geometric patterns. You’ll create a beautiful stack of experimental prints as you go and then choose how to finish your favourites.
You can turn your final pieces into a set of six greeting cards or bind a mini concertina to document your creative journey, a lovely keepsake of your time in the studio.
With a variety of papers and acrylic paints to explore, you’ll have plenty of time to play, test ideas, and surprise yourself along the way.
All materials, tea and coffee are included, just bring your curiosity and a love for handmade things.
We also have a fully stocked bar with craft beers, cocktails, soft drinks and snacks, so you can sip, snack, and settle in. Any dietary preferences? Just let us know, we’ve got you.
Can’t make the listed time? We’re happy to help arrange an alternative slot, whether you’d like a private session or a new group workshop time for others to join too.

title: Kintsugi Workshop - Deptford
description:
Discover the beautiful Japanese art of Kintsugi by repairing a handmade ceramic pot created by one of our studio potters. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn traditional-inspired repair techniques and leave with your own unique piece to take home.
Guided by our experienced ceramicists, you'll restore a broken pot using the principles of Kintsugi, celebrating cracks and imperfections rather than hiding them. No previous experience is required, making this a relaxing and rewarding introduction to this timeless craft.
About Kintsugi
Kintsugi (金継ぎ, meaning "golden joinery") is the Japanese art of repairing broken pottery by highlighting rather than concealing the cracks. Traditionally, broken pieces are rejoined using lacquer mixed or dusted with precious metals such as gold, silver or platinum.
Beyond its technique, Kintsugi embraces the Japanese philosophy of wabi-sabi—finding beauty in imperfection—and reflects the idea that damage and repair become part of an object's history rather than something to hide.
Important Information
Repaired pieces created during this workshop are not food safe and should be used for decorative purposes only.

Drinks to enjoy while baking
Other dessert or DimSum add-ons to extend the fun

Price is per person. Each attendee must hold a valid ticket.
This is an adult-only class (18+).
Outside food and drinks are not permitted.
Class duration is an estimate and may vary depending on group size.

Rescheduling

Arrival & Punctuality
Classes begin promptly. A 15-minute grace period is provided. Late arrivals may forfeit their booking.
Health & Safety Policy
For the safety of all guests and in line with UK food hygiene guidance, anyone experiencing vomiting, diarrhoea, or similar symptoms must be symptom-free for at least 48 hours before attending the class

title: Scone Baking Workshop for Beginners
description:
In this delightful workshop, you will learn the art of creating mouth-watering scones from scratch to impress your friends and family. You will discover how to master the perfect scone – golden on the outside, light and fluffy on the inside.
If you're a novice baker, fear not! Our experienced instructor will guide you through each step with patience and encouragement. You will be working with simple ingredients and basic techniques, making the process enjoyable and stress-free.
During the workshop, you can look forward to a hands-on activity that will leave you feeling accomplished and inspired in the kitchen. By the end of the class, you will have a batch of delicious scones to take home and enjoy those that you don't eat before you leave. We have jam, clotted cream, and butter, and we'll serve a big pot of tea!
Join us for a fun and tasty experience of learning the secrets to creating perfect tasty scones – you won't be disappointed!

title: Hand Tool Workshop - Make a Sushi Platter
description:
A day with hand tools. A piece to take home. No experience needed.
Over a full day, you’ll make a solid wood sushi platter and a pair (or more!) of chopsticks — choosing your timber from various species (walnut, beech, ash, oak), marking and cutting your own platter shape, and working the whole piece with hand tools. Use a jigsaw to rough out the form. Hand planes, rasps, spokeshaves, and sandpaper will bring it to a finished surface worth eating from!
This course is designed for people who’ve never picked up a hand plane — and for those who have and want a relaxed, enjoyable day to practice. You work at your own pace, make your own decisions about shape and edge treatment, and leave with something made by hand that you can use at home. Your teacher will guide you in how to properly use and get the best results from woodworking hand tools.
Across the day you’ll learn to:
Choose and read timber: understanding how walnut, beech, ash, and oak differ in grain, density, and working character
Mark out a platter shape: laying out your chosen profile on a wood blank — freehand or from a template; the shape is yours
Cut and refine a profile: sawing to the line with a jigsaw, then sanding and spokeshaving the edges smooth
Taper chopsticks with a hand plane: reading a taper, setting a plane, and working a fine section from a square blank
Apply edge treatments with hand tools: chamfer, roundover, or combination — your decision, made with planes, rasps, chisels, and spokeshaves
Add personal details: using the tools to bring your own character to the platter or chopsticks
Drill a soy sauce bowl recess (optional): marking and boring a recess into the platter surface at the drill press to fit a small ceramic bowl
Finish with food-safe oil: two coats across the platter and chopsticks, leaving the grain open and the surface ready for the table

title: Picassiette Mosaic Workshop - Upcycled Crockery
description:
As seen on ITV's Katie Piper's Breakfast show; Picassiette is a term used to describe a style of mosaic art where broken ceramics are pieced together to create something new and beautiful. Recycling is intrinsic to Picassiette, as the broken pieces can no longer be used as a plate or a vase but are repurposed to make something new and interesting. This philosophy is at the heart of what we do at Art4Space as we are always looking for ways to make art and crafts sustainable, while retaining creativity and beauty.
With over 25 years' experience running mosaic workshops, we believe mosaic art can be accessible to anyone, whether you see yourself as a creative person or not. Maybe this is why you often find works of mosaic in outsider or naive art, such as the French artist Raymond Isidore and his "La Maison Picassiette". It is often thought that his mosaics were the first to be coined with the term Picassiette.
In the 1930s, Isidore began obsessively covering his entire property with decorative mosaics of salvaged crockery. Translated from French, the term picassiette means “stolen plate” or “broken plate” but also a “scrounger” or “sponger". So when Isidore was given the nickname “Picassiette” it suggests that his neighbours were not originally enthusiastic about his artworks, however these days La Maison Picassiette gets over 30, 000 visitors a year, all keen to catch a glimpse of his original creations!
In our Picassiette class, you will be given different templates to choose from including a cat, bee, beetle or flower. Our experienced and friendly Art4Space tutor will guide you every step of the way, whether you are a beginner or have mosaic experience, so that everyone will leave with a unique Picassiette mosaic to treasure. This is a great hands-on experience with all the materials provided. You are, of course, welcome to bring your own broken crockery pieces to use in your artwork, but we also have boxes full of broken plates, cups and vases for you to rummage in.
Join us at our stunning centre, or we can come to your space: community venue, workplace, or home. Priced per person plus travel. We can vary class timings. Day, evening, or weekend bookings. We can host up to 50 people across our centre, with our large studio accommodating up to 30. If we come to you and the venue has capacity, the numbers are unlimited! We have full insurance, risk assessments, safeguarding and all required procedures in place to safely deliver outreach sessions.
Proceeds go towards our community art projects, providing mental well-being and creative health, especially for those facing barriers.
What you'll get
Boxes full of broken plates, cups, and vases for you to rummage in to create your Picassiette to take home.
Snacks and unlimited tea or coffee, plus a glass of wine/bottle of beer if desired.
