title: Foundational Fermentation and Microbiome Masterclass
description:
Lynn’s Living Kitchen – Foundational Fermentation & Microbiome Masterclass
Step into the world of wild lactic acid fermentation with a Raw Vegan Chef and Hippocrates Wellness Lifestyle Medicine Coach. This intimate masterclass offers direct access to decades of expertise, guiding you through both the craft of fermentation and the deeper science of the human microbiome.
This is far more than a hands-on workshop. It is a strategic exploration of how microbial ecosystems govern human vitality. You will understand what fermentation truly is, why it matters biologically, and how to execute it with precision at home. Alongside creating your own ferments, we will examine the microbiome not only within the gut, but also on the skin and in the environments you inhabit.
The Microbiome: Your Unseen Performance Partner
In a focused presentation, we will explore:
The Gut Microbiome:
The vast ecosystem of bacteria and microorganisms within your digestive tract that regulates digestion, nutrient assimilation, immune intelligence, inflammatory balance, neurotransmitter production, mood stability, cognition, and stress resilience.
The Skin Microbiome:
The microbial shield living on your skin that governs barrier integrity, immune defence, inflammation control, and visible ageing.
The Environmental Microbiome:
The microbial communities present in your home, kitchen, soil, and air, and how these ecosystems interact continuously with your biology.
Why This Matters?
These microbiomes do not function in isolation. They communicate constantly. When diversified and nourished, they enhance metabolic efficiency, immune sophistication, mental clarity, and long-term resilience.
How to support the microbiome:
You will learn practical, evidence-informed strategies to cultivate microbial diversity through fermented foods, raw living nutrition, and intelligent environmental exposure.
Why a High-Vibrational Raw Diet Amplifies the Microbiome:
A high-vibrational raw diet is not a trend; it is a biologically intelligent framework. Living plant foods deliver intact enzymes, diverse fibres, resistant starches, polyphenols, and naturally occurring microbes that feed keystone bacterial species. These compounds increase short-chain fatty acid production — particularly butyrate — which strengthens the gut lining, regulates inflammation, and enhances metabolic signalling.
Raw, plant-based diversity also increases microbial richness — a core biomarker associated with longevity, cognitive robustness, and reduced inflammatory disease risk. Fermented foods act as both probiotic and prebiotic agents: they introduce beneficial organisms while simultaneously feeding the ones already residing within you.
In short, a high-vibrational raw diet creates terrain where beneficial microbes dominate. When the terrain shifts, physiology follows.
This masterclass connects theory to practice, showing how daily dietary choices shape microbial architecture and, by extension, performance, energy, and long-term health trajectory.
Hands-On Fermentation Practice:
After understanding the science, we move into execution.
You will create three distinct wild lactic ferments, each selected for both flavour and functional diversity:
Sauerkraut – A foundational ferment that teaches the core mechanics of wild lacto-fermentation.
Spicy Kimchi – A dynamic ferment delivering complex flavour and microbial diversity.
Carrot & Cumin Retinol Kraut – A vibrant, nutrient-dense ferment rich in carotenoids and supportive phytonutrients.
You will not only learn the mechanics, but the diagnostics: how to observe microbial activity, regulate variables, correct imbalances, and refine flavour development. This builds fermentation fluency rather than simple recipe replication.
You will leave with three jars of your own creations and the confidence to continue independently.
Course Highlights:
Microbiome Mastery: Understand the Gut, Skin, and Environmental Microbiomes and how to actively optimise them.
High-Vibrational Nutrition Strategy: Learn how raw living foods enhance microbial diversity and metabolic resilience.
Hands-On Fermentation: Craft three wild lactic ferments with technical guidance.
Process Intelligence: Master preparation, salinity control, anaerobic conditions, and storage.
Recipe and Reference Guide: Detailed instructions, variations, and culinary applications.
Tasting Experience: Enjoy your creations alongside fermented flax crackers and cultured cashew cheese or sunflower seed pate.
Who This Class Is For:
This masterclass is designed for those who value depth, precision, and long-term health intelligence.
It is ideal for plant-based individuals, performance-driven professionals, discerning food enthusiasts, or anyone seeking to strategically enhance gut, skin, and environmental health. It also works exceptionally well as a refined private experience, executive team session, or elevated gift.
Class Guidelines
Arrive on time so we can start together and make the most of our session.
Enjoy refreshments, snacks, and sample tastings provided—no need to bring anything.
Classes are small, with a maximum of 8 participants, so everyone gets a focused, high-quality experience. Sessions may run a little over if we get caught up in discussion or activities—your flexibility is appreciated!
Questions are always welcome. Bring a notebook if you like to jot down tips and ideas.
Children are welcome when accompanied by an adult.
Hands-on or standing-intensive workshops aren’t suitable during pregnancy or for very young children.
Class Cancellations
We understand that plans can change. Here’s our policy:
More than 2 weeks’ notice: You can choose a full refund or move your booking to the next available class.
1–2 weeks’ notice: You can receive a 50% refund or transfer your booking to the next available class.
Less than 1 week’s notice: While we can’t offer a refund, you are welcome to transfer your ticket to someone else.
Ticket transfers are always welcome.
By the end of this masterclass, you will have three jars of probiotic-rich ferments, a full understanding of the fermentation process, and a clear appreciation for the microbiome in your body and environment. You will leave with the skills, confidence, and knowledge to continue experimenting at home while understanding the wider impact of microbes on your health.
Let’s get fermenting and supporting your microbiome from the inside out and all around you.
What you'll get

A Warm Welcome

Step into our warm and friendly workshop, where your pancake adventure begins! Your expert instructor will welcome you and introduce the secrets to creating those famously wobbly, cloud-like soufflé pancakes everyone loves.




Whip the Perfect Batter

Discover the most important step for ultimate fluffiness! We’ll guide you as you learn to whisk your egg whites into a perfect, glossy meringue. Mastering this key technique is your first step to pancake perfection.




Fold with Care

Learn the gentle art of folding your airy meringue into the batter to create a light, luscious mixture. This is a wonderfully mindful moment where you'll see your batter transform, ready to become the fluffiest pancakes imaginable.




Cook Your Pancakes

Time to hit the pan! We'll show you how to pipe and cook your pancakes low and slow, watching with pride as they puff up to incredible heights. We'll share all the tips for getting a brilliant result with simple home cooking equipment.




Taste Your Delicious Creations

Step back and admire your stack of warm, jiggly, and delicious soufflé pancakes! You'll leave the class with your amazing creations to take home, plus the confidence and skills to whip them up in your own kitchen anytime.



Love soft, fluffy Japanese pancakes? Join this fun soufflé pancake cooking class in London and learn how to make these light and airy desserts yourself. This hands-on Japanese dessert workshop is perfect for beginners who want to explore modern Asian sweets.

title: Shanghai Street Food Cooking Class - Rice Cake and Pork Chop
description:
Warm Welcome and Prep Your Ingredients

Get settled into our welcoming London kitchen as we introduce you to Chinese rice cakes and pork chops -- get ready to cook!




Fry the Pork Chop

Learn how to deep fry the pork chop and keep it juicy and tender. Don't worry if you're new to this style of cooking -- our expert chefs will be on hand to help you.




Make Shanghai Style Rice Cake

Learn about the unique style of the Shanghai rice cake, a very common food in China! With our guidance, you'll make your own delicious rice cake.




Cook with Special Shanghai Sauce

Level up your Chinese rice cake with a special Shanghai sauce, which you'll use to cook your rice cake. You'll be taught how to make this unique sauce to recreate at home!




Taste the Success

Reflect on your newfound skills and sit back, relax, and enjoy your handmade dishes. The fun doesn't stop when the class ends -- any leftovers can be taken away to share with loved ones or eaten later!




Add-on Bao Buns

Learn to make the plain Bao Buns to serve with your dish.




Add-on Crispy Chilli Sauce

Learn to make the delicious crispy chilli sauce to serve with your dish.



Discover a delicious and lesser-known Chinese street food in this Shanghai cooking class in London. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how to make Shanghai rice cakes (Nian Gao) and crispy pork chop — a classic comfort food combination loved by locals.
Rice cakes are one of the oldest staple foods in China. In the UK, many people recognise a sweet version like mochi, but in Shanghai we often enjoy rice cakes as a savoury dish. These rice cakes are chewy, satisfying and perfect for absorbing rich sauces.
In this friendly cooking class, your teachers will guide you step-by-step through the techniques needed to prepare authentic rice cakes and cook them into a delicious street food dish. Classes take place in a spacious, air-conditioned London studio with small groups, so you’ll receive plenty of personal guidance. On quieter weekdays, you may even enjoy a private class experience.
If you're looking for unique things to do in London, a memorable food experience, or a cooking class beyond the usual dumplings and noodles, this Shanghai street food workshop is a fantastic choice.
What you will learn in this class
During this hands-on workshop, you will learn how to:
Make Shanghai rice cakes (Nian Gao) from scratch
Cook rice cakes to achieve the perfect chewy texture
Prepare an authentic savoury sauce
Cook crispy pork chop, the classic partner to rice cakes in Shanghai
By the end of the class, you’ll enjoy the delicious dish you created and gain the confidence to recreate this authentic Shanghai recipe at home.
Why Guests Love This Class
Learn an authentic Shanghai street food dish rarely taught in London
Small classes with plenty of personal guidance
Discover the history and culture behind Chinese rice cakes
Beginner-friendly and suitable for home cooks
A fun activity for dates, gifts, or food-loving friends
By the end of the class, you'll be sitting down to enjoy your freshly cooked dish — crispy pork chop served with chewy rice cakes — and leaving with a unique recipe to recreate at home.
Add-on Classes
All add-ons take place within the same class session, saving travel time and making the experience even more enjoyable. Please allow 30 minutes to 1 hour extra depending on your selections.
Popular add-ons include:
Smashed Cucumber Salad – a refreshing and very popular vegan dish
Crispy Chilli Sauce – learn to make this flavourful condiment to serve with your rice cakes
Drinks Add-On – add cocktails, bubble tea or other drinks to make the class even more fun
Knife Sharpening Session – bring a knife if safe to do so and learn how to sharpen it properly
Feel free to contact us before booking if you would like more details about the available add-ons.
Apron with logo to wear at home cooking in the future
Recipe Collection Booklet to collect beautifully designed and printed recipes
Allergy Information
Please let us know about any dietary requirements via ClassBento message after booking and we will do our best to accommodate.
Gluten is used in sauces and some ingredients
Soy is essential in the sauce
Pork is the traditional ingredient for this dish.
Alternative options available on request:
Halal chicken can replace pork.
Tempura tofu can be used for a vegan version
Please mention any requests in the booking notes.
Come along and enjoy a relaxed cooking experience in London, discover a beloved Shanghai street food, and leave with new Chinese cooking skills and a delicious meal you created yourself.
Important Booking Information
Price is per person. Each attendee must hold a valid ticket.
This is an adult-only class (18+).
Outside food and drinks are not permitted.
Class duration is an estimate and may vary depending on group size.
No Refund Policy
All bookings are non-refundable. If you are unable to attend, you are welcome to transfer your ticket to another adult (18+). Please notify us in advance with the new attendee’s name.
Rescheduling
If you need to reschedule your booking, a £50 fee per person applies. Requests must be made at least 7 days before your scheduled class date.
Arrival & Punctuality
Classes begin promptly. A 15-minute grace period is provided. If you arrive more than 15 minutes late, your booking may be forfeited.
Health & Safety Policy
For the safety of all guests and in line with UK food hygiene guidance, anyone experiencing vomiting, diarrhoea, or similar symptoms must be symptom-free for at least 48 hours before attending the class
Guests may be asked to confirm this upon arrival
We reserve the right to refuse entry if this requirement is not met
We appreciate your understanding as our small-group classes require preparation and precise timing.
What you'll get
Your delicious food to eat and enjoy!
Complimentary tea to enjoy.

title: BYOB Handbuilding Class for Beginners
description:
During this two-hour session, you will utilise the traditional techniques of handbuilding like coiling, slabbing, and pinch pot to create beautiful pieces and develop a practise that embraces organic forms. This course is great for beginners or anyone who'd like to rekindle their love for handbuilding.
By the end of the two hours, you'll have your very own creation with the option to fire and glaze it (an additional £5). For more information about our cancellation policy, please see our FAQ section.
This session is BYOB, so please feel free to bring your own drinks and snacks and enjoy your Friday evening with us!
Please wear old clothing and have trimmed nails as you will be getting stuck in!
Please note:
Please note: This is an adult pottery class. Participants aged 11 years and over are welcome, provided they are able to work independently in an adult-paced group class. This is not a children's class.
Your finished pieces will be fired and glazed, ready to collect 4 weeks after the class.
A materials fee of £5 per piece of pottery kept is NOT included in the class and is payable on the day of your workshop.
Pieces are ready around 4-5 weeks after the class. We will send you an email when they are ready to be collected. Please check you email and spam folder. We will keep your pots in the studio for a month. If not collected in time they may be disposed of.
It is your responsibility to arrive on time for the class. Upon arriving to your class 30 minutes or later, we have the right to reject you joining the class without any refund or rescheduling.
No cancellations or reschedules allowed.
During summer, there is no air conditioning in the studio, so please bring water and dress for the heat!
During winter, it would be a bit cold in the studio. Whilst we try our best to keep the studio warm, please prepare an extra coat or clothes to keep yourself warm during class.
Please enter and leave the studio quietly - the studio is in the middle of the neighbourhood!
** Please note that due to the nature of ceramics, final results may vary and cannot be guaranteed. This includes, but is not limited to:
Glaze colours and finishes may vary from samples and are for reference only.
Textures and fine details may appear differently after firing.
Finished pieces will shrink by approximately 15% during the drying and firing process.
Minor imperfections, such as small clay marks or uneven surfaces, may be present.
Pieces may crack, warp or break during drying or firing.
We take every care throughout the making and firing process; however, these are natural characteristics and risks of working with clay and cannot always be prevented.
If a piece is damaged beyond use during the firing process, we will reimburse the £5 materials and firing fee paid for that piece. Class fees are non-refundable.
What you'll get
Clay, aprons and tools will be provided during the class.
If you would like to keep your finished pieces, a materials and firing fee of £5 per piece is payable on the day of the class.
Finished pieces are usually ready for collection 4–5 weeks after the class. We will notify you by email when they are ready. Please check your inbox and spam/junk folder.
We will store finished pieces for one month from the date of our collection email. Pieces not collected within this period may be disposed of due to limited storage space.
Please note that ceramics are fragile. While every care is taken, cracking, warping or breakage can occur during the drying and firing process. These are natural risks of ceramics, and we cannot guarantee that every piece will be successfully fired.

title: Gintsugi - Japanese Silver Repair Workshop
description:
This ancient Japanese technique not only mends pottery but also enhances its beauty. Gintsugi, the silver counterpart to Kintsugi, uses silver instead of gold to repair broken pottery, creating a unique and striking aesthetic.
In our Gintsugi technique, heat lamps are used with lacquer adhesive and silver mica powder. Led by an experienced instructor, you'll receive step-by-step guidance to create your own unique Gintsugi pieces. No previous experience is required; this class is designed for beginners. You’ll be amazed at how your broken ceramics can transform into beautiful artworks. We offer a vast selection of vintage crockery and Japanese bowls, or you can bring your own piece from home to repair. Throughout the workshop, you'll also gain an appreciation for the beauty of imperfections through the philosophy of wabi-sabi. (Kintsugi and Gintsugi are related to the Japanese philosophy of mushin (無心, "no mind"), which encompasses concepts of non-attachment and the acceptance of change.
Don’t miss this chance to learn a fascinating skill. Plus all served with a gintsugi gin and tonic (no-alcohol gin an option).
By the end, you’ll take home silver-seamed pottery and a deeper appreciation for life’s beautiful imperfections.
Join us at our stunning centre, or we can come to your space: community venue, workplace, or home. Priced per person plus travel. We can vary class timings. Day, evening, or weekend bookings. We can host up to 50 people across our centre, with our large studio accommodating up to 30. If we come to you and the venue has capacity, the numbers are unlimited! We have full insurance, risk assessments, safeguarding and all required procedures in place to safely deliver outreach sessions.
Proceeds go towards our community art projects, providing mental well-being and creative health, especially for those facing barriers.

All the materials you need to make two Gintsugi products.
Snacks.

description:
A Warm Welcome

Welcome to our fun, friendly London kitchen, where you'll discover the secrets of authentic 3-Cup Chicken. Your expert teacher will introduce you to this famous Taiwan dish, explaining its tradition and meaning behind the dish name!

title: Carpentry Course: Wildwood Bench Crafting
description:
Experience the RiverShop’s one-of-a-kind carpentry course and learn how to create a stunning, rustic wooden bench with tree trunk legs.
This carpentry course is more than just a workshop—it’s a journey that connects you to the land, the materials, and the process of woodworking.
Each bench features legs cut from tree trunks we hand-selected and harvested ourselves from a beautiful farm in Suffolk. We then bring this responsibly sourced wood to our London studio, where students like you can turn it into a functional, artful piece of furniture.
Our carpentry course is designed to immerse you in every step, from raw material to finished bench, with guidance from our passionate instructors who love sharing their knowledge of woodworking techniques and craftsmanship.
About the Course:
In this carpentry course, you’ll learn how to build a unique tree trunk bench, blending the charm of Suffolk’s natural wood with skilled craftsmanship. The bench’s tree trunk legs give it a grounded, rustic beauty, making each piece uniquely yours. Our carpentry course instructors are seasoned woodworkers who will teach you each stage of the project, ensuring you learn not only to make a bench, but also to understand the tools, materials, and techniques that go into crafting it.
This carpentry course uses tree trunks that have been carefully chosen and harvested to promote the growth of new woodlands in Suffolk. From our hand-selection and cutting of the wood to bringing it to London for our students, each step is an intentional part of creating a sustainable and meaningful piece. We are deeply committed to this process, and you’ll feel this passion throughout the carpentry course as you gain insight into the origins of your materials and the impact of responsible sourcing.
What You Will Learn:
This carpentry course is designed to teach you every aspect of woodworking needed to create a durable, beautiful bench that will last for years to come.
Learn to select, clean, and prepare tree trunks that provide both stability and beauty. You’ll understand how to assess wood grain, density, and structural integrity, ensuring that your bench has a strong foundation.
This carpentry course covers all essential techniques, including sanding, cutting, and joining, so you’ll feel confident working with the wood’s natural, uneven qualities. Whether you’re a beginner or looking to refine your craft, we’ll teach you the foundational skills for success.
Our instructors will guide you in creating solid joinery connections that will ensure the stability of your bench. We focus on simple yet strong methods, including mortise and tenon joints, to make sure your bench is both functional and beautiful.
Learn to finish your bench with professional-quality techniques that highlight the wood’s unique character. From sanding to sealing, you’ll understand how to preserve the natural beauty of your materials and protect your bench for years to come.
This carpentry course is open to anyone who loves hands-on work and wants to create a unique, rustic piece of furniture. No prior experience is necessary—our experienced instructors will provide step-by-step guidance tailored to your level, making this carpentry course ideal for beginners as well as those looking to expand their woodworking skills.
Whether you’re an aspiring woodworker, a nature enthusiast, or simply looking to build something with your own hands, this carpentry course will leave you with newfound skills, a deeper appreciation for sustainable woodworking, and a bench that’s uniquely yours.
By the end of this carpentry course, you’ll leave with a bench that captures the beauty of the Suffolk countryside, a deeper connection to sustainable woodworking, and skills you can use for future projects.
Join us to create a bench that’s truly special, from source to finished product, with the guidance of skilled instructors and the joy of working with nature’s material.

title: Leather Crafting Workshop: Create a Small Pouch
description:
Discover the art of leather crafting in our workshops, where you can create unique, handcrafted cardholders and personalise them to your liking. No prior experience is required, as you’ll receive full guidance from the instructor every step of the way.
This session lasts between three and four hours. This is a great introductory session to leather crafting and you have 2 designs to choose from. Participants are welcome to bring their own snacks and drinks to enjoy during the workshop.
Throughout the workshop, you will learn essential leather-working techniques, including punching, cutting, edging, burnishing, stitching, finishing, and embossing. These skills will empower you to create beautiful, durable items with confidence and precision.
The workshops are conveniently located within a 10-minute walk from Eltham train station and a 15-minute walk from Mottingham train station.
We take pride in using only the finest quality full-grain, vegetable-tanned leather sourced ethically and sustainably. Our materials include cow leather from Derbyshire, UK, which is environmentally friendly and ages beautifully; goat leather imported from France, renowned for its durability and elegance; and kangaroo leather from a Derbyshire tannery, which is exceptionally lightweight yet strong.
Join us to explore the art of leather crafting and leave with a unique masterpiece made by your own hands. All tools, leather, patterns, and guidance are provided to help you bring your creative vision to life.

title: Mosaic Making Class - Themed
description:
Want to get creative? Come along and unleash your inner artist at this fun mosaic-making class in London!
During this craft workshop, your friendly teacher will guide you through an array of mosaic techniques before you're let loose on an extensive range of materials.
Each of these workshops have specific themes or you can learn the basics
- Sun 6th September 10 am - 12.30 pm: Picassiette Mosaic. You will use broken ceramics to piece together to create something new and beautiful. In our, you will be given different templates to choose from including a cat, bee, beetle or flower. Our experienced and friendly Art4Space tutor will guide you every step of the way, whether you are a beginner or have mosaic experience, so that everyone will leave with a unique Picassiette mosaic to treasure.
- Sun 20th September 1.30pm-4 pm: Picassiette Mosaic. You will use broken ceramics to piece together to create something new and beautiful. In our, you will be given different templates to choose from including a cat, bee, beetle or flower. Our experienced and friendly Art4Space tutor will guide you every step of the way, whether you are a beginner or have mosaic experience, so that everyone will leave with a unique Picassiette mosaic to treasure.
- Fri 30th Oct 6.30 pm - 9 pm: Halloween Mosaic Candy Skull: Create a mosaic inspired by Day of the Dead candy skulls. Learn mosaic techniques in a relaxed, supportive environment.

title: Preserving Flowers in Resin Class: Bouquet Preservation Skills
description:
Join this hands-on resin art workshop in Woolwich and discover the calming craft of preserving flowers in clear resin. Designed for beginners and curious creatives, this session invites you to slow down and learn how to capture natural beauty in a lasting, tactile form.
You’ll be guided through the full resin layering process from preparing dried blooms to pouring and understanding cure stages using professional techniques that prioritise clarity, colour retention and care.
All botanical materials used in this workshop have a special story. They’ve been grown and harvested on a family farm in Suffolk before being carefully dried for your use. You’ll explore the connection between land and studio, learning which flowers preserve best and how to protect their colour and structure inside resin.
What You’ll Learn
This session is designed to teach you the complete, start-to-finish process of creating a layered resin flower piece.
During the workshop you will:
Learn how to preserve flowers using silica and why drying technique matters
Clean and prepare delicate blooms for professional clarity
Mix and pour resin confidently, understanding ratios, temperature and bubble control
Design a balanced floral composition within a mould
Learn how resin layering works, including timing between pours
Understand how and when to pour a second (top) layer
You will be taught the entire Part 2 process (the second layer pour) during this first session, demonstrated and completed using a pre-cured piece so you can fully see and understand the full workflow.
What You’ll Take Home
Because resin requires curing time between layers:
You will complete and finish a pre-cured resin piece during the session, you will not take home your own work. This course has been built so you will learn all the steps you need to know in one session and to then practice this at home and create your own work.
What you'll get
Hands-on experience placing flowers into silica gel and learning the flower-drying process
Guidance working with professionally pre-dried flowers for resin casting
Step-by-step tuition in casting a floral resin cube
The opportunity to design and create a botanical resin cube
Insight into resin curing & demoulding
A pre finished resin cube cured, demoulded, and posted after the workshop
All materials, tools, and PPE

Discover the beauty of sea glass and sea pottery jewellery making in our hands-on Bezel Setting Sea Glass Pendant Workshop. Naturally tumbled by the ebbs and flows of the sea, each piece has been shaped by the waves before washing ashore as a timeless treasure for lucky beachcombers to find.
In this beginner-friendly silver jewellery workshop, you will transform these unique seaside finds into your own handcrafted jewellery. Using traditional silversmithing techniques, you’ll choose from a beautiful collection of sea glass or pottery and learn how to bezel set it in fine silver to create a one-of-a-kind pendant.
As every piece of sea glass and pottery are completely unique, every design created in the workshop will be truly one of a kind.
This workshop is ideal for beginners and is a perfect introduction to essential jewellery making skills and techniques.
Skills taught :: Sawing straight and curved edges, forming bezel wire, soldering, measuring, setting, filing, sanding, and polishing.
Create your own beautiful sea glass jewellery and leave with a handmade keepsake inspired by the coast.

All equipment, tools and materials included

title: Tetrapak Printmaking Workshop
description:
Settle In

Come in, grab a complimentary drink from the bar and choose your seat for the session




Create a Texture Sample Plate

After introductions, we'll talk through what tetrapak printing and collagraph is. How the think about it, what it's limitations are, and then create a sample plate of different textures




Learn to Ink and Print

We'll the ink up, wipe and print your sample plates so you'll have tried the process end to end using soaked paper and our little printing press




Design and Print

Now you understand the textures and elements you have to play with, you have the rest of the session to design, develop and print your own prints.



Discover the magic of printmaking with an unexpected material, Tetrapak! In this hands-on three-hour London printing workshop, you’ll learn how to design, carve, and ink recycled Tetrapak cartons to create a unique series of prints.
You’ll be introduced to collagraph printmaking using Tetrapak (a type of drypoint etching), and guided through:
How to prepare and carve Tetrapak plates
Creating tone and texture
Designing modular image components
Planning compositions
Inking, wiping and printing using a printing press
Expect a relaxed and experimental session in a small group setting, so there’s time for 1:1 help and no waiting around at the press.
This is a brilliant introduction to sustainable printmaking techniques and a fun way to explore storytelling, composition, and visual rhythm.
At Something Good Workshops, we have a licensed bar that's always open during workshops. Whether it's tea, coffee, nibbles or a good glass of wine or cold cocktail, we've got you covered!

All Tetrapak, mountboard, inks, tools, paper and press access

title: Chinese Street Food Cooking Class: Rou Jia Mo (Chinese Burger)
description:
Welcome and Get Cooking

Settle into our welcoming kitchen and get familiar with your ingredients. With guidance, you'll cook the dish to go inside the burger.




Prepare the Dough

With help along the way, we'll work through the steps to prepare the dough with expert precision!

Bake It

Cook in a Pan

You'll also have the chance to cook the burger in a pan so you can try both cooking methods -- see which results you like the best!




Taste the Success

Sit down to enjoy your Chinese crispy burger.




Add-on Shanghai Scallion Pancake

Learn another type popular pancake with spring onions.




Add-on Crispy Chilli Sauce

Learn to make the delicious crispy chilli sauce to serve with the pancakes. Take the rest home.




Add-on Recipe Collection Booklet

This is your journey of cooking adventure.
You can get beautifully designed and printed recipe from each class once you bought the booklet (Two colours to choose).
You also will get Polaroid-style photo sticker from your class, showing your highlight in the class you attended.
Your chef tutor also will give you a stamp. It is your certificate of success.



Discover one of China’s most legendary street foods in this hands-on Chinese cooking class in London.
In this workshop you’ll learn how to make Rou Jia Mo, often called the “Chinese Burger.” This iconic street food comes from the historic city of Xi’an and is loved across China for its combination of crispy flatbread and rich braised meat filling.
Despite the playful nickname, Rou Jia Mo has a history stretching back thousands of years, making it one of the world’s oldest street food sandwiches.
Guided by your chef, you’ll learn how this famous dish evolved and why it remains a favourite across China today.
Classes take place in a spacious, air-conditioned cooking studio with small group sizes, ensuring plenty of individual guidance. Weekday sessions are often quieter and may even become private classes.
What You’ll Cook
During this hands-on workshop you will prepare an authentic Rou Jia Mo meal from scratch, including:
Traditional Chinese Crispy Flatbread (Mo) – preparing the dough and cooking the bread
Braised Pork Belly Filling – rich, slow-cooked and packed with flavour
Learning essential techniques from knife skills to dough preparation
Assembling your Rou Jia Mo “Chinese burger” just like street vendors in Xi’an
You will then enjoy your freshly made dishes during the class or take them home.
Dietary Options
The traditional version uses pork and pork lard to create the signature crispy bread and filling.
Alternative options are available:
Vegan version with shiitake mushroom filling
Non-pork option with soft bread instead of crispy lard pastry
Please inform your teacher when booking if you would prefer the vegan option.

title: Pottery Making Taster Workshop - Elephant and Castle
description:
Looking for chilled-out London activities to help you escape the hustle and bustle of the city? Sit back, relax, and get creative with clay at this pottery-making workshop in Stoke Newington!
During this beginner-friendly class, you'll learn all the tips and tricks needed to transform handmade clay into bespoke pottery pieces. Your expert guide will demonstrate hand-building techniques using coils and slabs before covering wheel throwing as you prepare to get hands-on with your clay!
Whether you're a complete beginner or a more experienced clay crafter, this workshop is a great chance to unwind in a London pottery studio as you let your creative side take over.
At the end of the class, your beautiful pottery pieces will be taken away to be biscuit fired and glazed, ready to collect after 4 weeks to display at home or give away as handmade gifts!
Please note:
Please note: This is an adult pottery class. Participants aged 11 years and over are welcome, provided they are able to work independently in an adult-paced group class. This is not a children's class.
Your finished pieces will be fired and glazed, ready to collect 4 weeks after the class.
A materials fee of £5 per piece of pottery kept is NOT included in the class and is payable on the day of your workshop.
Pieces are ready around 4-5 weeks after the class. We will send you an email when they are ready to be collected. Please check you email and spam folder. We will keep your pots in the studio for a month. If not collected in time they may be disposed of.
It is your responsibility to arrive on time for the class. Upon arriving to your class 30 minutes or later, we have the right to reject you joining the class without any refund or rescheduling.
No cancellations or reschedules allowed.
During summer, there is no air conditioning in the studio, so please bring water and dress for the heat!
During winter, it would be a bit cold in the studio. Whilst we try our best to keep the studio warm, please prepare an extra coat or clothes to keep yourself warm during class.
Please enter and leave the studio quietly - the studio is in the middle of the neighbourhood!
** Please note that due to the nature of ceramics, final results may vary and cannot be guaranteed. This includes, but is not limited to:
Glaze colours and finishes may vary from samples and are for reference only.
Textures and fine details may appear differently after firing.
Finished pieces will shrink by approximately 15% during the drying and firing process.
Minor imperfections, such as small clay marks or uneven surfaces, may be present.
Pieces may crack, warp or break during drying or firing.
We take every care throughout the making and firing process; however, these are natural characteristics and risks of working with clay and cannot always be prevented.
If a piece is damaged beyond use during the firing process, we will reimburse the £5 materials and firing fee paid for that piece. Class fees are non-refundable.

title: Double-Sided Knitting Workshop
description:
Learn to knit reversible colourwork with clean edges and no "wrong" side in this workshop, where you'll master the double-sided knitting technique and watch it come together in front of you, stitch by stitch.
Double-sided knitting (also known as double knitting) is a wonderfully clever structural technique that produces two layers of fabric at once, each showing a mirrored version of the same design in reverse colours. The result is a beautifully dense, double-thickness fabric with genuinely no "wrong" side – flip it over and you'll find just as polished a finish looking back at you. It's a technique that rewards patience and precision, and one that opens up a whole new way of thinking about colour, pattern and structure in your knitting.
You'll be guided step by step through the full process, building your skills and confidence as you go:
Cast on and set up correctly for double-sided knitting, so your fabric grows evenly from the very first row
Work two colours together in a mirrored, fully reversible design, developing the rhythm and coordination the technique relies on
Keep your edges tidy and your tension even throughout – the details that separate a good result from a great one
Bind off with a neat, matching finish that does justice to all the careful work that's come before it
Along the way, you'll build an understanding of why this technique works the way it does, so you're equipped to adapt it to your own future projects, whether that's a cosy scarf, a snuggly blanket, or anything else that calls for a fabric with two beautiful sides.
This workshop is designed for confident knitters who are comfortable with the basics and ready to take on a more structured, technical challenge. You'll leave with a new skill in your toolkit, a stronger grasp of colourwork construction, and the confidence to bring double-sided knitting into your own projects long after the class ends.
What you'll get
In-person tuition with hands-on help.
A printed double-sided knitting pattern to practise.
All materials and tools for your sample project.
Tea, biscuits, and plenty of encouragement.

title: Majolica Painting on Ceramic Class
description:
In this class, students discover the traditional art of painting on smalto, the classic Mediterranean method for creating vivid ceramic artworks. Each piece begins as biscotto, clay that has been fired once and is ready to be transformed. We apply a layer of white glaze (smalto) onto the biscotto, creating a soft, absorbent surface that acts like a luminous canvas.
Before the glaze is fired, you paint directly on top of it using ceramic pigments. This unfired smalto allows the colours to spread, blend, and sink gently into the surface—an expressive technique that produces beautifully fluid lines and rich tones.
During the final kiln firing, the smalto melts and absorbs the pigments, sealing your artwork beneath a glossy, glass-like finish. The result is a shining, vibrant ceramic piece where the colours appear bright, deep, and permanent.
This class is perfect for anyone who wants to explore a traditional yet artistic method of ceramic painting, creating pieces that are both timeless and full of colour.
In a small group, you'll be guided by our Waldorf teacher, with her unique method tailored to your needs. The Waldorf system emphasises the uniqueness of each individual, giving them the opportunity to express themselves freely and encouraging the beauty of diversity and creativity.

title: Watchmaking Taster Day Workshop
description:
Discover first-hand what it takes to be a professional watchmaker and dive into the micro-mechanical world of watchmaking.
Throughout the class, you will gain invaluable knowledge of the inner workings of a watch movement and begin to master the delicate skill of using watchmaker’s tools. Gain an understanding of the craftsmanship involved in creating a watch as you embark on an extraordinary journey guided by an experienced professional watchmaker.
With years of experience as watchmakers and teaching students watchmaking, one of our team will lead you through the process of disassembling a watch movement and then reassembling it. Detailed PowerPoint presentations, videos and hands-on demonstrations will aid your learning and understanding how a watch works.
You will be working on an ST36 watch movement, a type of movement that is used in modern-day wristwatches and used in watchmaking training centres throughout the world.
This is a very big watch movement, which helps when using tweezers, fine screwdrivers, and a loupe, which magnifies the work, especially for those using these tools for the first time. There are also high-powered trinocular stereo microscopes on each workbench to help with seeing and understanding what you will be working on.
You will disassemble the ST36 movement and reassemble it again, until it is fully working and ticking away.
You will also lubricate the movement using a fine tipped watchmaker's oiler,  which tests your steady hand, oiling what is in effect the size of a head of a pin!
You'll end the class by regulating (timing) the movement to within a few seconds per day using a timegrapher and if you have your own watch, see how that is keeping time using the same equipment.
No need to worry if you're new to watchmaking! This workshop is designed to alleviate any fears and cater to beginners. You'll be working with state-of-the-art equipment and height-adjustable workbenches, and one of our watchmakers will be there every step of the way to offer guidance, making the experience enjoyable and enriching.
At the end of the workshop, you'll leave with newfound knowledge and a sense of accomplishment. This unique experience offers a transformative journey into the world of horology, allowing you to fuel your passion for watches and gain hands-on experience of how they work.
Whether you're a complete novice, an enthusiast, or have always wanted to learn how to make your own watch, this workshop is the perfect activity to nurture your curiosity and expand your horizons.
You will also have cloud storage access to the 175 pages PowerPoint presentation that aided the watchmaking taster day, including two extra lessons to help understand more in depth the keyless and motion work, as well as a comprehensive watchmaking tools list to help navigate the pitfalls of buying watchmaking tools and equipment.
You'll have the opportunity to buy a brand new ST36 watch movement to take home for an extra £45, payable at the end of the lesson, if you choose.
With the movement and presentations you will be able to perform the same disassembly and assembly as you did in the taster day with some basic tools.
This is an amazing opportunity to experience what a watchmaker does every day in a small class of up to eight students.
If you are driving, there is free parking around Hewlett House, but don’t rely on parking being available, as spaces fill up quickly.
There is paid parking in Battersea Park and Battersea Power Station and on Sunday free parking in the surrounding streets and roads.

title: Metal Clay Jewellery Making Workshop
description:
Join us for a unique jewellery making class in London where you will discover the amazing world of Silver clay. In this workshop, you'll learn the essential techniques to transform a soft, squidgy material into stunning 99.9% pure silver creations.
Don't worry if you're new to this medium, our experienced instructors will guide you every step of the way, ensuring a fun and supportive environment for all. You'll be amazed at how quickly you can create beautiful pieces with silver clay.
During the class, you'll learn how to roll and texture the clay, allowing you to add your own personal touch to your creations.
After shaping your designs, you'll learn how to dry, sand, and refine them, bringing out their true beauty. And don't worry, we'll teach you how to safely use a blow torch to fire the clay, resulting in the remarkable transformation to pure silver.
Imagine the joy of taking home your own unique pieces, made from this precious metal. Whether you want to create stunning jewellery or unique decorative items, this class will provide you with the skills and confidence to do so.
So come and join us for an unforgettable class in London, where you'll learn all the techniques needed to create beautiful silver pieces with silver clay. Get ready to unleash your creativity and walk away with creations that will be cherished for years to come.
What you'll get
All tools and materials included. You’ll leave with your very own handmade metal clay jewellery.

title: Beginner Knitting Class – Continental Style for Crocheters
description:
If you're looking to try a new way of knitting, this two-hour Continental knitting workshop in London is the perfect place to learn a smooth and efficient technique. This activity is designed for confident knitters who want to discover how to knit in the Continental style, where the yarn is held in the left hand.
You’ll be introduced to the fundamentals of this 'picking' method, with plenty of time to practise, ask questions, and build your confidence with expert support.
In this workshop, you will learn:
How to knit and purl using the Continental technique
To practise holding and tensioning yarn in your left hand
How to work decreases, stitch combinations, and seamless transitions
Tips for switching between English and Continental methods
You'll leave this session with a brilliant new skill that can enhance the speed and comfort of your knitting, providing you with a different approach for all your future projects.
We keep our workshops small, for 1–8 people. You can “Book into a public class” on a listed date, or click “Request a class” and tell us when you’d like to meet.

title: Gelato Making Workshop
description:
In this three-hour workshop, Lorenzo invites attendees to discover the craft of ice cream making.
The session begins with a comprehensive tour of Lorenzo's kitchen, offering participants a look behind the scenes.
Throughout the workshop, Lorenzo shares his extensive knowledge about the essential ingredients and machinery used in crafting the perfect gelato and sorbet. Participants will learn the crucial differences between these two frozen desserts, enriching their understanding of the art of ice cream making.
A key highlight of the workshop is the hands-on experience in making two different types of recipes: one for gelato and another for ice cream. Lorenzo guides the attendees through the process of creating the base from scratch for both gelato and sorbet, providing insights into the techniques that define the texture and flavour of these treats.
As the ice cream churns, Lorenzo leads a tasting session, allowing participants to indulge in a variety of flavours and appreciate the nuances of each type. Alongside this sensory experience, attendees also delve into the history of gelato, exploring its origins and evolution.
To conclude the workshop, each participant gets the chance to take home 1 Tub (455ml) of ice cream in a flavour of their choice, along with the recipes they've learned.

Please note: Public dates for this class require at least 3 guests to run. In the unlikely event that we don't reach this number, we may cancel the session; if that happens, we'll inform you and let you choose between a refund or reschedule, so please watch your email/SMS one day prior to the class.

1 tub (455ml) of gelato to take home

title: BYOB Queer Throwing Taster
description:
Queer BYOB Throwing Night at Earthworks
Join us for a 2 hour Saturday night that’s all about clay, community, and creativity. Our Queer BYOB Throwing Taster Session is a relaxed, welcoming space designed especially for LGBTQ+ makers and friends to explore the potter’s wheel together.
Bring along your favourite (non-staining) drink, we love recommending our neighbours London Beer Lab, just a few arches down, with their amazing selection of craft beers and lagers. Please arrive 10 minutes early so you can get settled in before the fun begins.
Over the course of 2 hours, our friendly tutors will guide you through the fundamentals of throwing, from centring the clay to shaping your first pot. There’s no pressure to get it perfect, this is all about play, discovery, and connecting with others in a supportive queer space.
Style tip: Dress to impress, but only in clothes you don’t mind getting a little clay on! (Aprons are provided. Clay is non staining) And while it is possible to throw with long nails, you may find it easier without.
At the end of the night, you’ll select your favourite piece to be fired and glazed by our team, ready for you to collect at a later date.
Whether you’re here for the clay, the laughs, or the chance to meet new people, this class is designed to be as much about the experience as it is about the pottery. No prior experience needed, just curiosity, good vibes, and a drink in hand.
Note: Your piece will take around 5 weeks to be ready for collection, we’ll email you as soon as it’s done.

title: Tanghulu Masterclass – Traditional Chinese Candied Fruit Workshop
description:
A Warm Welcome

Welcome to our cool and friendly London kitchen! Your culinary journey begins with a fascinating introduction to the history of TangHuLu. In our small, personal classes, your experienced chef will get you settled in and excited to create the delicious Chinese treats.




Prepare the Ingredients

Get hands-on with every step: select the fruits and prepare the fruits. Not all fruits suitable for TangHuLu. We’ll guide you through the process and you will easily to make them again at home.




Cook the Sugar Syrup

The most important step, cook the sugar syrup. Your expeirenced chef tutors will guide you through carefully. Make sure you can get the perfect glaze of sugar and the crunchy texture.




Wrap and Deco TangHuLu

Unleash your creativity as you add the finishing touches. You'll learn simple but beautiful ways to decorate your TangHuLu, working with a variety of flavours to create a colourful and tempting collection of desserts.




Your Delicious Creations

Step back and admire the beautiful TangHuLu you’ve made! You’ll leave the workshop with satisfied sweet tooth, plus the skills and know-how to recreate them whenever you like.



Discover the magic behind one of China’s most iconic street desserts in this vibrant, hands-on Tanghulu workshop in London.
Learn how to transform fresh fruit into glossy, jewel-like skewers coated in a perfectly crisp sugar shell. The result? A satisfying crack, a burst of sweetness, and a beautiful treat that’s almost too pretty to eat. Almost.
What Is Tanghulu?
Tanghulu is a traditional Chinese candied fruit dessert, known for its shiny sugar coating and delightful contrast of sweet and tangy flavours.
In this interactive class, you’ll create your own handcrafted Tanghulu skewers from scratch — and take them home to impress friends and family.
In This Class You Will Learn:
How to select the best fruits for perfect Tanghulu
The science behind cooking sugar to the correct temperature
How to coat fruit evenly with a crisp, glass-like shell
Decorative techniques for beautiful presentation
You’ll work with colourful seasonal fruits and simple, high-quality ingredients — guided step-by-step by experienced tutors in a relaxed and welcoming studio.
No experience needed. This class is beginner-friendly and stress-free.

description:
Join us for a creative evening at our ceramics workshop! During this session, you will learn how to paint ceramics while enjoying the company of friends and your favourite drinks.

Once you've completed painting your ceramic piece, it will be fired and glazed and can be collected within 3-4 weeks.
Please note:
Please note: This is an adult pottery class. Participants aged 11 years and over are welcome, provided they are able to work independently in an adult-paced group class. This is not a children's class.
Your finished pieces will be fired and glazed, ready to collect 4 weeks after the class.
A materials fee of £5 per piece of pottery kept is NOT included in the class and is payable on the day of your workshop.
Pieces are ready around 4-5 weeks after the class. We will send you an email when they are ready to be collected. Please check you email and spam folder. We will keep your pots in the studio for a month. If not collected in time they may be disposed of.
It is your responsibility to arrive on time for the class. Upon arriving to your class 30 minutes or later, we have the right to reject you joining the class without any refund or rescheduling.
No cancellations or reschedules allowed.
During summer, there is no air conditioning in the studio, so please bring water and dress for the heat!
During winter, it would be a bit cold in the studio. Whilst we try our best to keep the studio warm, please prepare an extra coat or clothes to keep yourself warm during class.
Please enter and leave the studio quietly - the studio is in the middle of the neighbourhood!
** Please note that due to the nature of ceramics, final results may vary and cannot be guaranteed. This includes, but is not limited to:
Glaze colours and finishes may vary from samples and are for reference only.
Textures and fine details may appear differently after firing.
Finished pieces will shrink by approximately 15% during the drying and firing process.
Minor imperfections, such as small clay marks or uneven surfaces, may be present.
Pieces may crack, warp or break during drying or firing.
We take every care throughout the making and firing process; however, these are natural characteristics and risks of working with clay and cannot always be prevented.
If a piece is damaged beyond use during the firing process, we will reimburse the £5 materials and firing fee paid for that piece. Class fees are non-refundable.

Join us for a calming and creative embroidery workshop in London where you’ll stitch your own set of four linen napkins with personalised line drawings and words.

title: Granny Square Crochet Workshop
description:
This welcoming workshop encourages self esteem through learning a new skill. Expect a challenge! Crochet is not entirely relaxing to begin with, but by working together, we will achieve a new craft which is limitless in its possibilities. Weather its clothes, accessories, toys or homeware, crochet can transform your perception and ignite your creative brain.
To start, we cover the foundational concepts of crochet, together building knowledge to understand the craft and all its wonderful possibilities!
Each attendee will be able to choose yarn in their preferred tones to get started as we discuss colour combinations and explore yarn and hook variants. We then move on to covering three of the foundational crochet stitches with your very own new crochet hook. We cover these one by one and take it incredibly slow together as it can be the most challenging part of the lesson. After sufficient practise we move on to combining these stitches in accordance to the pattern to create the famously versatile granny square. My classes are usually small which ensures everyone gets plenty of much appreciated 1-1 time. By teaching from my home I provide a personable and relaxing learning environment where my students feel at ease looking out onto the garden. As the challenging part of the workshop eases off we can enjoy the hot drinks and sweet treats and discuss our future hopes for crochet. Finally when we finish the class you will receive reference materials to take home to remind you of everything we covered in the lesson.
By the end of the workshop, each attendee will feel happily confident in the skills needed to understand basic crochet patterns and have the ability to crochet up the work themselves.
It's always a pleasure to meet you and share my knowledge and inspiration!
Looking forward to the next class.
Bella

title: Smartphone Photography Workshop - Greenwich Park
description:
The view from Greenwich Park is a must see for any visit to south east London. The historic Queen’s House and Old Royal Naval College set the foreground, while the modern metropolis of Canary Wharf offers a starkly contrasting backdrop. To the east, the world famous O2 Arena. title: Woodworking Taster: Joinery Day Class
description:
This is a full day of hands-on joinery at POW Workshops in London. The ideal starting point if you're serious about learning woodworking but want to try it before committing to a multi-day course.
Over six hours, you'll work through the essential hand skills that underpin all traditional furniture making. You'll start with the basics of measuring and marking, move on to sawing and chiselling, and by the end of the day you'll have cut a half-lap joint with real understanding of the techniques behind it.
Here's what you'll cover:
Precision measuring and marking using traditional woodworking tools
Sawing straight lines with Japanese pull saws, learning touch, tracking, and control
Chisel techniques for waste removal and refining joint surfaces
Cutting a half-lap joint: the foundational joint that teaches you the core principles of all joinery
An introduction to tool sharpening, because sharp tools are the path to good work
Workshop safety and posture, including how body position and balance improve your cuts
This course is fast-paced and satisfying. There's a lot packed into the day, but our experienced instructor will guide you through every step, and with a maximum of 8 people per class, you'll get the individual attention you need.
No prior experience is necessary. This course is designed for complete beginners. If you've done some DIY or used hand tools before, you'll find it a great way to refine your technique with proper instruction.
What you'll get
A hand-cut half-lap joint, a solid grounding in core woodworking skills, and the knowledge to decide what comes next. All tools and materials are provided.
What's next?
Ready to go further? Beginner Joinery Workshop: Frame Joints is a two-day weekend course that takes you deeper into the joints used in tables, chairs, and frames of all kinds. It's also open to complete beginners, so if a friend wants to skip the taster and jump straight in, they can.

title: Chinese Tea and Matcha Masterclass – Brew, Taste and Create
description:
A Warm Welcome

Welcome to our fun, friendly London kitchen, where you'll discover the secrets of authentic Matcha. Your expert teacher will introduce you to this famous Chinese tea, explaining its tradition, history and development!




Whisk and Bubble Up to Be a Perfect Matcha

Next, you’ll create the amazing Matcha drink to a high standard. Learn to make either the tradtional method, whisk by bamboo brush and the modern technology, electric whisker. Best of all, you get to taste the nice tea.




Paint the Matcha

Yes, this is the stage you might not see in the UK before. The ultimate Matcha art is, to paint on the tea, with the tea. It is a premium entertainment in 10th century China. Now you can enjoy it with your creativity.




Enjoy Your Tea

This is the moment you’ve been waiting for! Your hardwork with the tasty and beautiful Matcha is ready to drink. Enjoy it with the chef tutors handmade tea desserts as well. Many of the desserts are unique in London as well. You can join other classes teaching you making the tea desserts.

Using premium tea powders and professional tools, you’ll learn how to brew properly and appreciate flavour, aroma and presentation.

title: Bubble Tea Cake Making Class: Bake and Decorate
description:
Get Comfy in the Kitchen

Slip on an apron (you can buy a brand new one after the class), meet your friendly teacher and get settled in. All your fresh, authentic ingredients are prepped and ready for you, so you can dive straight into the fun part.




Understand the Ingredients

Get on with the flour, sugar, butter etc. Your chef tutor will explain to you clearly and take you through step by step.




Prepare the Cake

It is a few steps to go through. You chef tutor will be with you and make sure you will get the best result.




Baking Cake

While baking the cake, you will make the cream topping, tapioca ball and syrup all from scratch. You can also use these ingredients to make a cup of bubble tea for yourself.




Enjoy the Cake

You can eat in the class or take home. It is enough for 8 persons to share. We have cake box for you.




Add-on Recipe Collection Booklet

This is your journey of cooking adventure.
You can get beautifully designed and printed recipe from each class once you bought the booklet (Two colours to choose).
You also will get Polaroid-style photo sticker from your class, showing your highlight in the class you attended.
Your chef tutor also will give you a stamp. It is your certificate of success.



Love bubble tea? Love cake? Now you can combine both in one unforgettable baking experience.
In this hands-on class, you’ll learn how to create a one-of-a-kind bubble tea cake — a unique recipe developed by your expert instructors and not found anywhere else.
You’ll bake a light and fluffy chiffon cake, flavour it with bubble tea-inspired ingredients, and decorate it with cheese cream and glossy brown sugar tapioca pearls.
This class is perfect for anyone looking for a fun, creative, and Instagram-worthy dessert experience.
Classes take place in a spacious, air-conditioned studio with small group sizes, ensuring personal attention. Weekday sessions are often quieter and may even become private classes.
What You’ll Learn
In this hands-on baking class, you will:
Bake a light chiffon cake from scratch
Prepare bubble tea flavour elements
Make smooth and creamy cheese cream topping
Cook tapioca pearls in brown sugar syrup
Assemble and decorate your bubble tea cake
You’ll also gain:
Essential baking skills and techniques
Confidence working with different textures and flavours
Creative presentation skills
By the end of the class, you’ll have your own beautiful cake to enjoy or take home.
Why Guests Love This Class
Create a completely unique dessert not available elsewhere
Fun, creative, and highly Instagram-worthy
Beginner-friendly with step-by-step guidance
Learn multiple skills in one class
Perfect for gifts, dates, and celebrations
This is more than a baking class — it’s a signature dessert experience.
Perfect for Special Occasions
This class is ideal for:
Birthday celebrations
Date nights & Valentine’s activities
Unique gifts
Fun group experiences

1 Ticket = 1 Person, 1 Cake

1 Ticket + Add-on Extra Cake = 1 Person, 2 Cakes
Optional Add-On Experiences
Enhance your experience with optional add-ons:
Drinks to enjoy during your class
Valentine’s special – rose-flavoured cake variation
Extra flavour options to create additional cakes

Allergy & Dietary Information
Please inform your teacher of any dietary requirements when booking.
Key ingredients include:
Gluten (cake flour)

Milk products (cheese cream)
We will do our best to accommodate dietary needs where possible.
Come along and enjoy a fun, relaxed, and creative baking environment, where you’ll learn new skills and create a truly unique dessert.
You’ll leave with a stunning handmade cake and a memorable experience.

title: Aquavit and Gin Distilling Workshop
description:
Design and distil your own personal gin or aquavit recipe in this unmissable workshop at our amazing distillery in southwest London. Regardless of whether you’re a spirits expert, an enthusiastic novice, or simply fancy a fun afternoon with friends, this unique experience is not to be missed. We’ll give you unmatched insight into the world of drinks production and provide all the tools you need to create a bottle of delicious craft spirit for you to take home and enjoy.
Relax with a perfectly mixed cocktail featuring one of our award-winning spirits as our head distiller, Sasha, guides you through the science and art of distilling, revealing the key principles and hidden secrets of flavour creation that are essential in creating great-tasting gin and aquavit. From there, you’ll move on to explore the core botanicals of each spirit and learn about their complex flavour profiles and rich history.
Next comes perhaps the most exciting part of the class – recipe creation and distillation! With expert guidance, choose from over 40 herbs, spices, and peels to create your perfect aquavit or gin. Then, put theory into practise and take on the mantle of distiller as you produce your spirit yourself on a state-of-the-art nano still. Discover the myriad of flavours that are created as your spirit slowly becomes a reality and craft something truly unique. We will even keep your recipe on file should you ever wish to order additional bottles!
With your freshly distilled aquavit or gin before you, it’s time to give it a name and blend it to bottling strength. Then all that remains is to label, stopper, and seal your new creation so it’s ready to take home and enjoy! The experience is capped off with a guided tasting of a variety of Vintersol products and perhaps even have the chance to sample a few experimental batches not yet available to the public.
As a token of our appreciation, every ticket also includes a 10% discount at our distillery shop, valid on the day of the tour.

Two cocktails over the course of the experience

title: Introduction to Steambending Course - Wall-hung Coat Rack
description:
Discover the magic moment when wood becomes pliable in this full-day steam bending workshop in London with fine furniture maker Brandon Harrison. You'll learn the science that makes it possible – understanding lignin, wood anatomy, and why there's only a brief window to work with – then put it straight into practice. Pull ash from the steambox hot and suddenly flexible, shape it onto the former before the moment passes, and experience something genuinely unlike anything else in the workshop.
Across the day, you'll master a complete range of techniques: steam bending your hooks, hand-planing the wall bar to a smooth finish, marking and cutting joints that hold everything together, drilling fixing holes, gluing and clamping your pieces, and finishing everything in hard wax oil so the grain stays open and beautiful. There's the visceral satisfaction of working fast and instinctively with the steam-bent ash, then the precision of hand tools and joinery where the construction itself becomes part of the design. Brandon brings the same depth of thinking he applies to his own heirloom-quality, internationally recognised work – trained at Sturt Craft Centre in Australia and Yacademy in Italy, with work recognised at Craft + Design Canberra, Vivid Furniture Design Melbourne, and the Clarence Furniture Prize.
You'll leave with a stunning, functional wall-hung coat hanger – three bent ash hooks hand-joined into a shaped bar, finished and ready to hang – and genuine skills you can build on. It's a day that transforms how you see wood and what's possible when you understand the craft.

description:
Join this in-depth indoor cyanotype workshop with Something Good Workshops and learn how to create magical blue prints as you explore this unique art form. title: Fused Glass Bowl Making Class
description:
1 - Introduction

The session starts with an introduction of the range of colours, techniques and design options on offer, and a brief history of Fused Glass.




2 - Examples

Examples of glass that has been fired is laid out to handle. We discuss the process of firing the glass, and how to make coasters, bowls or tea lights.




3 - Practice Cutting Glass

After a step by step demonstration you have a practice tile to perfect your glass cutting technique.




4 - Choosing Colours

You are invited to select a range of coloured glass to bring to your workspace.




5 - One on One with Nadine

Nadine will discuss any design ideas you have and offer suggestions.




6 - Create Your 1st Design

Using your new glass cutting technique you will cut and assemble glass pieces to create your first design.




7 - Mosaic Patterns

During the workshop you have 4 glass pieces to make and can choose from cutting your own glass or using the pre cut mosaic style glass pieces.




8 - Check Ins

Nadine is available to offer support throughout the session, and will regularly check in.




9 - Making the Last Pieces

You are given creative freedom with lots of guidance to support your creation of 4 designs.




10 - Session Ends

At the end of the session you get to choose if you want to have them all as bowls or have any as coasters.




11 - Post Workshop - Firing

After the session your glass is fired in a glass kiln




12 - Post Workshop - Slumping

To make bowls the fused glass is placed in moulds to create the curved shape and returned to the kiln for a second firing.




13 - Finished Glass

After its last firing (within 2 weeks) the glass is ready to be collected or posted.

title: Nalbinding Workshop: Learn an Ancient Textile Technique
description:
In this nalbinding workshop in London, you will learn how to master an ancient technique! It is a way of making fabric from a single thread, similar in purpose to knitting or crochet, but much older. You'll work on a wrist warmer, and an extra piece if time allows.
Don't worry if you're new to this technique -- you'll receive expert tuition throughout the process in a relaxed atmosphere, with plenty of opportunities for questions and support.
What to expect:
Using a needle and your thumb, you will bind the thread around itself to create interlocking loops.
This technique has been used in different ways across times and cultures; in this class, you will learn the Oslo stitch.
You will learn how to begin your work, create a starting chain, and build stitches onto it to form fabric.
We will also cover how to make increases and decreases, as nalbinding cannot be cut -- everything must be shaped as you make it!
By the end of the workshop, you'll have a completed or in progress wrist warmer, plus new skills in this ancient craft to keep practicing with at home.

title: 2-Day Wheel Throwing, Trimming and Painting Course
description:
Situated just a short stroll from Nine Elms (6 mins), Stockwell (10 mins), and Vauxhall (15 mins) stations, our cozy pottery studio is right where the creative magic happens!
Master the potter's wheel over an immersive two-day weekend intensive at our cosy London studio, designed entirely for complete beginners. You'll experience the entire ceramic journey, from preparing the clay through to throwing, trimming, painting, and finally firing, all guided by an experienced ceramicist who'll give you the personalized attention you need to truly learn the craft.
Day one is all about getting your hands on the wheel. You'll learn the core fundamentals: wedging and centering your clay, opening it up, and pulling the walls to create shape. Then you'll get hands-on practice making functional pieces: cylinders, small bowls, mugs. Keeping your best creations to finish on day two. There's no pressure to be perfect; the focus is on understanding how the wheel works and what your hands can do.
On day two, you'll trim your leather-hard pieces, flipping them back on the wheel to refine the shape and carve a professional foot ring. Then comes the fun part: using vibrant underglazes to paint your own custom designs, patterns, and colours directly onto the clay. You're not just making something; you're making something that's entirely yours.
Once the weekend is over, we'll carefully dry your creations, dip them in a glossy clear glaze, and fire them in our studio kiln. In a few weeks, you'll collect finished pieces that are food-safe, microwave-safe, and dishwasher-safe – functional art you'll actually use and treasure. You'll walk away not just with handmade keepsakes, but with real skills you can keep using.
Please note: no experience needed – complete beginners are exactly who this intensive is for. All materials, guidance, and kiln firing are included.
What you'll get
Full access to your own pottery wheel for the entire weekend.
All clay, tools, glazes, and professional kiln firings included.
2 to 3 beautifully finished, hand-painted ceramic pieces to take home.
Tea, coffee, and biscuits provided to keep the creative energy flowing.

title: Make a Knife Block: Woodworking Day Course
description:
Learn to shape by hand, rout, and finish solid wood — and leave with a piece that earns its place in any discerning kitchen.
Over a full day, you'll make a wall-mounted knife block in solid walnut or oak: a 325mm bar with a rounded cross-section, flat on the front where ten magnets hold your knives flush to the surface, and flat on the back where a sliding dovetail joint locks it invisibly to the wall. No slots, no clutter, no visible fixings — just knives on wood, held by magnets, made by you.
The form is deceptively simple. Getting there involves precision drilling, router work with a jig, a glued capping piece that seals the magnets inside the block, and an afternoon of hand-shaping — rasp, disc sander, and hand plane — that brings the rounded profile to a surface worth showing off. You'll choose your timber on the day: walnut for a darker, finer-grained result; oak for something more open and characterful.

title: Tequila Tasting and Chocolate Pairing Workshop
description:
As recommended in the Sunday Times, The New York Times and CNN:
“The best way to experience the power and pleasure of chocolate is to taste its history.”
” Crafting bonbons or chocolate bars is not just a sweet treat, but it’s like weaving my affections and memories into each delicate piece.”
Tequila Tasting, Chocolate Pairing, and Cocktails – what is not to love? A delicious combination of chocolate tasting, tequila tasting, and Melt’s original cocktails.
Tequila and Chocolate share many similarities, both originate in Mexico and Latin America, both are at their best when produced in an “artisanal” way, and both share the importance of their “terroir”. For both Chocolate and Tequila – fermentation is key for creating the flavour and complexity – which is why they make such good pairings.
Chocolate has been on an incredible journey from a “gift of the Gods” to a modern chocolate bar. We want you to experience that journey by tasting chocolate from the wild Amazon and the best single-origin estates. Melt wants people to learn about the chocolate revolution and how to put the chocolate back on its spiritual pedestal. Think of a fine wine – like a Chateau Lafite and that gives you an idea of what the best chocolate taste like – not the Ribena that most of us drink.
We want you to celebrate this amazing civilization – with chocolate, tequila, and great cocktails. Mexico has a rich history of cocktails with Tequila and Margaritas.
But Tequila, or the Spirit of Latin America, is so much more than a base for cocktails. Taste and learn about Tequila as a local. Learn the difference between Blue and White Agave and Mezqual. Melt has developed three new cocktails of our own -which feature in a new Cocktail book. The Pisco Passion, the Melt Margarita, and the Aztec Revenge. We will teach you how to make these amazing cocktails in the heart of Notting Hill, one of the world’s great urban environments. Join us on our passion with chocolate, and tequila and celebrate this rich Aztec civilization with two new and unique Cocktails – which you will love.
Indulge in the delightful pairing of chocolate and cocktails with Melt Chocolate's unique experience. Come and learn about the chocolate revolution and taste the difference!
In the same way that Ribena and the finest wine can't be compared, this tasting experience will help you understand how powerful real chocolate can be versus its cousins on the self of the shops.
This immersive journey will take you through the history of chocolate, from its origins as the "gift of the Gods" to the modern-day chocolate bars we know today. You'll be tasting this adventure through time by sampling chocolate from the Amazon and the best single-origin estates.
Melt Chocolate is inviting you to come and celebrate this amazing civilization by crafting three original cocktails inspired by the rich history of Mexican drinks featuring Tequila and Margaritas.
Come and mix up the Pisco Passion, the Melt Margarita, and the Aztec Revenge in their gorgeous urban environment in Notting Hill. You will learn how to make cocktail recipes to knock your socks off and pair them with carefully selected chocolates.
Join your talented chocolatiers in their passion to bring the rich Aztec civilization to life through cocktails and chocolate! A London experience not to be missed.
