title: Foraging Fridays: A Seasonal Creative Open-Workshop
description:
Fridays are made for slowing down a little, and I’d love for you to join me for something a bit different. Foraging Fridays: A Seasonal Creative Open-Workshop is about stepping away from the week’s busyness and letting nature guide our creations.
When the weather is kind, we’ll take a gentle walk on the common to see what the season has to offer, gathering fruits, flowers, vines, and foliage. Whatever we find, we’ll bring it back to the workshop and see where it takes us. If you’d rather skip the walk, or can't get here in time, you’re welcome to meet us at 6:30 back at the workshop...I’ll make sure there’s plenty of goodies gathered for you too.
From 6:30 back at the workshop, the evening flows quite loosely where each group can choose your own creative path. From simmering jam to preserving pickles, or botanical printing to wreath-making...all things are possible.
At the end of the evening and if the weather is kind), you are welcome to gather round the fire pit to round off the relaxing evening.
If you’d like to get a feel for the kinds of projects we might make, have a peek at my other workshop listings — you’ll see how varied and seasonal they are. Each week brings something new.
Mostly, I hope this gives you a little space to pause, make with your hands, and enjoy being part of a creative gathering.
Refreshments and some light nibbles will be available throughout.
A quick note: Our home is shared with two friendly (and sometimes diva-like) dogs. They’ll happily join us on the forage and then potter about while we’re in the workshop. They’re likely to get a bit bored once we’re busy making, but if you sit by the fire pit later, you might just find one climbs into your lap for a cuddle.

title: Chinese Calligraphy Class: Brush and Ink Art
description:
Welcome to the Class

Step into our friendly London workshop for a fascinating introduction to the world of Chinese culture. Your hosts will take you to explore the Chinese history back to when the paper was invented.




Have Some Chinese Tea and Snacks

You hosts prepared Chinese tea and handmade snacks for you. You can enjoye the delicious food while learning Chinese Calligraphy. It is not easy!




Master the Perfect Flow

Learn the deep knowledge how to write Chinese words correctly.




Practise More in the Class

Write in brush pen is not an easy way. You can try with ballpoint pen first then move on to the traditional ones.




Take the Set Home to Practise More

Yes, you will get the set, including the magic paper and the brush pen. You can practise more at home.



Step into a calm and elegant world of Chinese calligraphy in this immersive adult-only class in London.
Chinese calligraphy is more than writing — it is a centuries-old art form that combines movement, balance, and mindfulness. This class is designed as a peaceful, creative escape, allowing you to slow down and fully focus on the rhythm of brush and ink.
Guided by an experienced instructor, you’ll learn the foundations of traditional brush techniques, including how to hold the brush, control ink flow, and form strokes with confidence.
You will practise using a modern innovation — magic calligraphy paper. With just water, your writing appears like ink and gently fades as it dries, allowing you to practise freely without pressure, waste, or mess.
The session takes place in a spacious, atmospheric studio, with soft music and subtle incense creating a relaxing environment.
Throughout the class, you’ll enjoy Chinese tea and homemade snacks, making this a truly cultural and sensory experience.
By the end, you’ll leave feeling refreshed, inspired, and equipped with a calligraphy practice set to continue at home.

title: Introduction to Cyanotype Printmaking Workshop
description:
Cyanotypes: Background

You'll start by getting settled into the space and the studio, and learn about the fascinating origins of this creative and flexible printing technique.




Paper Coating

After some practice and demonstration you'll prepare for printing by mixing your Cyanotype solution and painting it onto paper.




Creating Our Artwork

During the main part of the session, you will create the images that you would like to make prints from. After making paint using binder and pigment, you will use drawing, painting, collage, or a combination to create your final design.




Exposure and Developing

After a break for lunch, you'll use the light box to expose your prints and use water to wash and reveal your finished print. I'll provide you with some blotting paper and packaging, so that you can take them and complete their drying at home!



During this in-depth printmaking workshop, we will learn how to make cyanotype prints in my home studio in Camberwell. I've practised and taught many artistic techniques professionally -- out of all of them, I think cyanotyping is one of the most fun, accessible, and enjoyable.
It can be done in a very controlled environment (as we will do in the studio) or much more simply, with sunlight. Either way, the chemical processes involved create an incredibly intense blue which is so beautiful!
Please note
This course is taught in my home studio, which is accessed via a steep loft staircase.
If you have difficulty using stairs, I’d recommend you don’t book this session, but please contact me as I will be organising dates for more accessible workshops in an alternative location.
We also have a cat, so this course may not be suitable if you have severe allergies.
Take home your own set of unique cyanotype prints and blotting paper, plus a host of new skills to try out again.

description:
Looking for creative and fun things to do in London? Come along to this enjoyable and friendly art class and learn the skill of printing whilst meeting new people and of course, enjoying a sip or two of BYOB bubbles.
What is lino printing?
Lino printing is an eye-catching form of printmaking, which involves carving into a surface block of linoleum (yes, the floor covering!). The lino is then inked before a piece of paper is placed over it. Finally, pressure is applied by hand to transfer the ink to the paper.
New to lino printing? Perfect! Your friendly teacher will be there to guide you through the whole process of creating, carving and finally printing your stunning design.
During the evening you'll enjoy the company of like-minded arty folk along with the chance to relax and unwind as you let your creativity flow.

title: Bowl Carving Woodworking Class
description:
Ever wanted to give wood carving a go but didn't know where to begin? Or maybe you want to make a unique gift for a loved one. Learn to make a beautiful wooden bowl from native green hardwood using ancient hand tools at this one-of-a-kind woodworking class in London.
Hosted at Stepney City Farm by a local expert, you'll learn the fundamentals of using traditional edge tools to carve yourself a beautiful wooden bowl. Over the course of the day you will use an axe and drawknife to shape the outside of the bowl, and a gouge and hook knife to refine the inside.
If you're looking for something a little different, you can also opt to carve a kuksa – a traditional Scandinavian style of drinking cup. The ideal tool for drinking coffee, the kuksa develops a rich patina from the coffee grounds over time. Great to use at home but also much better in a backpack than a fragile and heavy ceramic mug - a fantastic gift for any outdoorsy friends!
In addition to giving you an introduction to a variety of hand tools, the class will give you a real insight into the design and function of objects which have been used by humans for thousands of years. As you carve the object of your choice, you will learn many different carving techniques and about how green wood differs from seasoned wood.
You'll leave the class with your gorgeous handmade bowl or kuksa to cherish forever, along with the skills, knowledge and confidence to carry on this traditional, satisfying hobby.
Please note: This workshop is 18+

title: Screen Printing Workshop
description:
Make your own art! A fun day out learning how to screen print a 1 colour print. A perfect creative date, a unique east London experience - the perfect beginner workshop! At the end of the day you will leave with a set of handmade prints in your own design. No experience needed, this workshop is for everyone!
Not only will you walk away with your screen printed design, but you'll also have a brilliant understanding of the creative process — so you can continue developing your newly found passion in your own time.
Introduction to Screen printing
The workshop starts off with a brief introduction to screen printing and the Print Club London studio. You be will talked through the equipment that will used throughout the day, as well as the general theory that goes into the process. You will individually coat your own screens in preparation for use later in the day to print your own edition of prints, and will be shown some amazing examples of artwork that’s been printed in our studio by working artists.
Artworking
Our tutors will talk you through some different digital and analogue processes that will help you turn your own image into a usable Positive ready to expose on your screen. Don’t worry if you aren’t too familiar with Photoshop or using a computer, the technicians will go slowly through the techniques and ensure that the theory of what they are doing is understood by all.
Exposing
Here is where you will take your Positive and expose it onto your coated screen to make the stencil you will be printing with in the afternoon. You will be making a 1 colour print and therefore expose one image. The tutor will talk you through how our large exposure unit works and then help you wash out your screen afterwards.
Printing
Once all preparation has been done it’s time to print! The printers will show you how to get your screen set up on our printing beds and some key printing techniques. You will then be left to print your own 1 colour small edition of prints, on our workshop paper supplied by GF Smith. Our tutors will be there long the way give you a helping hand and talk you through any problems that might pop up. Once you’re finished printing you learn how to clean your screen completely, ready for use again!

title: Argentium Silver Chains - One Day Workshop
description:
This exciting in-person jewellery making class is held in Camden Town, London NW1.
You'll get to learn a new skill while having a fun day out. Whether you're a complete beginner or a jeweller with existing skills, looking to explore working with Argentium, this workshop is perfect for anyone looking to get creative and expand their range of craft skills.

You'll make each link in the bracelet from silver wire, as well as creating your own hook or toggle-style clasp to finish off the bracelet.
Argentium is a relatively new alloy of silver - purer than the traditional Sterling silver, it is also more tarnish-resistant (it will stay bright and shiny longer) and less likely to cause problems for people who may be allergic to some metals.
Argentium also has some great working properties that make it really great for fusing (joining together without soldering) and melting, which make it great for various jewellery making projects, including chain making.
Don't worry if you're new to jewellery making - this class is designed to be fun, relaxed and to provide a supportive environment for everyone. With a small group size of just 3 students, your experienced instructor will guide you through the process, ensuring you feel confident every step of the way.
All the materials you need will be provided, so simply come along on your own or with friends to enjoy a fun and creative evening. As you create your custom jewellery pieces, you'll experience the satisfaction of seeing your designs come to life. By the end of the class, you'll have a beautifully polished silver chain ready to wear.

title: Illuminated Medieval Manuscript Letter Gilding Workshop
description:
A Brief History of Illuminated Manuscripts

Begin your journey by uncovering the fascinating history of illuminated manuscripts—the intricate, gold-adorned pages that once graced the libraries of medieval monasteries and royal courts. We’ll explore the origins, symbolism, and the painstaking techniques used by scribes and artists centuries ago.




Materials, Tools & Pigments – Then & Now

We will introduce you to the traditional tools and materials used in medieval manuscript illumination, including handmade vellum, rare mineral pigments, gold leaf, and natural bonding agents. Then, we’ll guide you through their modern-day equivalents—high-quality substitutes that make this ancient craft accessible to everyone today. You’ll receive expert recommendations on materials that will help you continue practicing beyond the workshop.




Tracing & Transferring Your Letter

You’ll learn how to select and replicate a medieval-style letter, transferring it onto high-quality paper using traditional methods. We’ll provide simple samples to start, helping you build confidence before moving on to more intricate designs.




Gilding – the Magic of Gold Leaf Application

Discover the mesmerizing process of applying real gold leaf to your design. You’ll learn the art of gilding, how to use bonding agents correctly, and how to achieve a stunning, professional finish that catches the light beautifully.




Bringing Your Letter to Life with Paint

Once your gold is set, we’ll introduce gorgeous, luminous paints—inspired by the rich pigments used by medieval illuminators. You’ll explore how to layer and blend colors to create depth and brilliance, making your illuminated letter a true work of art.




Create Your Own Masterpiece

By the end of the session, you’ll have created your very own illuminated letter, complete with delicate gold leaf details and beautifully applied colors. Choose from a selection of designs or personalize your piece with your initials.



Join this medieval manuscript illumination workshop and discover the age-old art of creating shimmering, hand-decorated letters. Whether you're a first-timer or a regular maker, this uplifting session will guide you through the process of working with genuine gold leaf and vibrant pigments to bring a piece of history to life.
Throughout the workshop, you'll feel inspired by the historical significance of these beautiful documents. You'll work with high-quality materials provided on the day and receive expert advice on how to keep up your new hobby at home.
What you'll learn:
A brief overview of manuscript illumination in medieval Europe and the materials historically used
Introduction to modern equivalents: gold leaf types, adhesives, pigments, tools, and papers
Step-by-step demonstration on tracing and transferring a letterform
Application of gold leaf using professional bonding agents
Guided painting session with historically inspired colours
You'll finish the session feeling empowered by your new skills, taking home a radiant, one-of-a-kind keepsake that's ready to be framed and admired.

description:
Learn to create your own bespoke natural fragrance in a relaxed, sensory-led setting.
Guided by Lizzy, a trained aromatherapist, you’ll begin by exploring the world of natural perfumery — from the profile of individual essential oils to how scent can be layered and composed.
You’ll move through a curated selection of botanical notes, experiencing and discussing each other’s interpretations, before being guided through the process of scent layering. Using perfumery principles as a foundation, you’ll begin to shape a fragrance that feels personal to you.

title: Street Photography Workshop - Shoot London Like a Pro
description:
Join this street photography class in London and discover how to capture the beautiful chaos of the Southbank. From the rhythmic movement of skaters to the shifting river light, you'll explore one of the city's most vibrant stretches while learning to see the world through a new lens.
The session begins outside the National Theatre with a short briefing where you'll chat about what you'd like to focus on, whether that's sharpening your technique or building your confidence. Because every group is different, the class naturally shapes itself around your personal goals. You'll spend two hours wandering together, learning how to read a scene before you even raise your camera and finding perfect compositions in the middle of a busy crowd. Your teacher will guide you through the ethics of candid photography and show you how to work with available light to create images that tell a story.
During this hands-on workshop, you will explore:
Reading light and shadow outdoors – Learn to use natural light to add depth to your photos.
Composition on the move – Find balance and focus in fast-paced environments.
Ethical candid moments – Gain the confidence to approach strangers and scenes with respect.
Camera settings for street scenes – Master the technical side of capturing movement.
Developing your visual instinct – Discover how to spot unique moments that others might miss.
Whether you're a complete beginner or a curious improver, this experience is designed to be low-pressure and social. You'll finish the session with a review of your shots, giving you a chance to see what worked and how to keep growing your skills. You'll walk away with a fresh perspective on the city and the self-assurance to continue documenting life on the streets long after the class ends.
Please note: You should bring along a DSLR, mirrorless, or film camera with a fully charged battery. As we will be walking outdoors, please wear comfortable shoes and dress appropriately for the weather.
What you'll get
Two hours of personalised street photography tuition on one of London's most iconic stretches, tailored to your goals and led by a professional photographer.

title: Wrapped Zen Pebbles Class
description:
This fun in-person craft class is held in Camden Town, London NW1. You'll get to learn a new skill while having a fun afternoon or evening out or relaxing after work - not to mention with going home with your own unique decorated pebble/s to enjoy.
This course is designed for complete beginners - no previous experience in crafts making, basketry, or macrame needed.
This (and all my courses) is designed for adults. I do not currently offer classes for children and teenagers.
During the 2.5 hour session, you'll learn how to do two to three different styles of wrapping, to create your own unique wrapped pebble/s.
Add a twig, nail, or washer for added detail, or stay with just the natural rattan fibres. The rattan we will be working with is a stiff fibre, usually used for basket weaving and when wet is flexible - as it dries out it becomes strong and solid.
To wrap the rocks / pebbles, we will be weaving and winding the wet rattan firmly around them, in different patterns to create decorative, textured effects before securely tucking the ends in.
Don't worry if you're new to crafts - this class is designed for beginners. With a small group size of just 3 students, your experienced instructor will guide you through the process, ensuring you feel confident every step of the way.
All the materials you need will be provided, so simply come along on your own or with friends to enjoy a fun and creative session. As you create your custom rock/s you'll experience the satisfaction of seeing your designs come to life. By the end of the class, you'll have at least one (probably 2) gorgeous decorative pebble to take home and enjoy.
Don't miss out on this opportunity to learn, create, and have a memorable afternoon / evening!
The workshop space is down stairs (lower ground floor), so unfortunately is difficult to access for anyone with mobility problems - apologies for any inconvenience.
What you'll get
Have a fun few hours and leave with your own handmade wrapped decorative pebble/s to enjoy or to gift...
Drinks and snacks are available throughout, and you will also get detailed printed (or emailed) notes to remind you of the processes we've covered if you choose to do more at home.

title: Floral Paper Marbling (ebru) Workshop
description:
The class will begin with an introduction to sprinkling the paint for the background on the solution and using a biz (needle) to drop the paint. Then, you will learn how to shape the drops into various floral patterns, such as Hatip Ebru, Battal Ebru (Stone Abstract), and Tulip Flower.
Ebru Art is dated back to 13rd centuries where you can see the rare examples in 700 years old manuscripts. Each artwork is unique and can never be copied or done twice.
This workshops aims to follow a traditional technique, where your own hands are tracing the pattern and rhythm that have been followed by centuries of makers. It is a great example to ensure that these skills are handed down, but for our own mindset. It will truly still your mind and give you a sense of wellbeing, continuity and calmness.
If you have attended this workshop, please message us so that we can work on different flowers -
Throughout the workshop, you will create at least three unique artworks. These pieces can be proudly displayed in your own space or gifted to your loved ones as beautiful presents.
To ensure that each participant has the opportunity to get the most out of the workshop, the number of participants is limited to 5. Please book in advance to avoid disappointment.
Please note:
You do not have to bring any materials.
We will provide an apron.
You will roll your artwork to carry with you. We recommend you have a suitable place to put them like a bag.
What you'll get
You will learn how to shape the drops into Hatip Ebru (various floral patterns), Battal (Abstract Stone) and Tulip Flower.
During the workshop, you will complete at least 3 artworks. You may decorate your place or give them to your loved ones as presents!

FAQ

What safety gear do you provide?
On our UV resin workshops we provide a full safety kit for every student, including nitrile gloves and a P2V charcoal-valved mask. Our studio is also equipped with a Resiners PurAir filtration system, which is SGS-certified to remove 83% of resin-specific VOCs from the air.
Are the gloves provided in resin workshops safe for allergies?
We use nitrile gloves because they are the gold standard for those with latex allergies. While true nitrile allergies are extremely rare (less than 1% of the population), some people may experience minor skin redness from the "accelerators" used to make the gloves stretchy. If you have extremely sensitive skin, please let us know.
Is the resin "non-toxic"?
We use "Low VOC" resins, which are much safer and have a milder scent than industrial resins. However, all liquid resin requires respect. By using our specialized air purifiers and wearing your provided charcoal mask and gloves, your exposure is kept to a minimum.

Korean panax ginseng – "the root of youth"

Fermented rice water/rice extract – "the brightening beauty secret"

title: Dairy Fermenting Class
description:
Join The Fermentarium for this mouthwatering dairy fermentation class in London.
In this special class, you'll be delving into the extensive world of fermented dairy products. guided by a friendly teacher, you will learn the core tenets of fermentation, safety practices, and health benefits of fermentation, followed by demonstrations of how to make certain fermented dairy products.
The range of fermented dairy products we’ll touch upon is wide and culturally diverse. Our tutor will demonstrate how to make cottage cheese, and you’ll get to taste a variety of goods such as sour cream, butter, cottage cheese, and clabbered milk. We’ll also discuss how to make and use whey, a natural by-product of cheese production, as well as different variations of labneh.
We’ll finish off with a discussion of yoghurts, explaining the difference between mesophilic and thermophilic yoghurt varieties and sampling those too. You’ll get to make your own fermented butter as well as milk kefir using kefir cultures provided during the class. We’ll then go over how to maintain those cultures and how to ensure your ferments stay alive and healthy (even when you’re away).
Quality of ingredients will be emphasized, and differences between different types of dairy and milk - i.e. raw vs. pasteurized - will be explained in detail.

FAQ

What safety gear do you provide?
On our UV resin workshops we provide a full safety kit for every student, including nitrile gloves and a P2V charcoal-valved mask. Our studio is also equipped with a Resiners PurAir filtration system, which is SGS-certified to remove 83% of resin-specific VOCs from the air.
Are the gloves provided in resin workshops safe for allergies?
We use nitrile gloves because they are the gold standard for those with latex allergies. While true nitrile allergies are extremely rare (less than 1% of the population), some people may experience minor skin redness from the "accelerators" used to make the gloves stretchy. If you have extremely sensitive skin, please let us know.
Is the resin "non-toxic"?
We use "Low VOC" resins, which are much safer and have a milder scent than industrial resins. However, all liquid resin requires respect. By using our specialized air purifiers and wearing your provided charcoal mask and gloves, your exposure is kept to a minimum.

FAQ

What safety gear do you provide?
On our UV resin workshops we provide a full safety kit for every student, including nitrile gloves and a P2V charcoal-valved mask. Our studio is also equipped with a Resiners PurAir filtration system, which is SGS-certified to remove 83% of resin-specific VOCs from the air.
Are the gloves provided in resin workshops safe for allergies?
We use nitrile gloves because they are the gold standard for those with latex allergies. While true nitrile allergies are extremely rare (less than 1% of the population), some people may experience minor skin redness from the "accelerators" used to make the gloves stretchy. If you have extremely sensitive skin, please let us know.
Is the resin "non-toxic"?
We use "Low VOC" resins, which are much safer and have a milder scent than industrial resins. However, all liquid resin requires respect. By using our specialized air purifiers and wearing your provided charcoal mask and gloves, your exposure is kept to a minimum.

title: 2-Day Wheel Throwing Workshop: Throw, Trim and Handle Your Own Pot
description:
There is a craft to making a pot on the wheel, and this wheel throwing workshop in Homerton gives you the time and space to actually learn it. Over two consecutive sessions at our Hackney studio, you will work through the complete process of wheel throwing from beginning to end — centring, pulling, trimming, handling, and finishing. Not a condensed version of the process, but the real thing, done properly, with two glazed and fired pieces to take home.
Day 1: Wheel throwing
You will spend two hours at your own wheel, learning to centre the clay, open it, and draw the walls upward. Our potters will work closely with you throughout, teaching you to read the clay and develop control over the form. By the close of the session, you will have two pieces resting overnight, ready for the work that transforms a thrown form into a finished pot.
Day 2: Trimming handles and finishing
Returning to your leather-hard pots, you will learn to trim the foot ring on the wheel — the detail that gives a piece its proper base and balance — before pulling a handle from fresh clay and attaching it cleanly. Once the finishing touches are in place, you will select a glaze from our studio collection. We take care of the bisque firing, glaze application, and kiln firing, and contact you when your ceramics are ready for collection.
A dedicated wheel per student for both sessions
Continuous guidance from our studio potters throughout
All clay, tools, and equipment provided
Bisque firing, choice of glaze, and kiln firing included
Available Wednesday + Thursday or Saturday + Sunday
Suitable for complete beginners and those returning after an introductory session. Our potters work with each student individually and adapt their teaching accordingly.

What you'll get
Two beautiful handmade high-firing ceramics to take home.
Bisque firing, white glaze, and kiln firing for both pieces — fully included.

FAQ

Will I definitely make a pot that survives?
Our potters do everything they can to give you the best chance of success and have an excellent track record with first-timers. That said, pottery is a natural material and very occasionally pieces crack during firing due to factors outside our control — uneven thickness, air bubbles or rapid temperature changes. If this happens we'll let you know immediately. Making a pot is part of the learning process and firing costs cannot be refunded in these cases, but we will always discuss options with you.
What happens to my pots between Day 1 and Day 2?
Your pots stay safely in our studio overnight to firm up to a leather-hard consistency — this is essential before they can be trimmed. Please do not take your pots home between sessions. We look after them carefully and they'll be exactly where you left them when you return.
Is this good for a hen or stag do?
It's one of our most popular group activities. Whether it's 4 people or 12, we can accommodate your group and make it a proper event. Email us to discuss a private booking — we can arrange drinks, flexible timing and anything else to make the day work for your group.

FAQ

What safety gear do you provide?
On our UV resin workshops we provide a full safety kit for every student, including nitrile gloves and a P2V charcoal-valved mask. Our studio is also equipped with a Resiners PurAir filtration system, which is SGS-certified to remove 83% of resin-specific VOCs from the air.
Are the gloves provided in resin workshops safe for allergies?
We use nitrile gloves because they are the gold standard for those with latex allergies. While true nitrile allergies are extremely rare (less than 1% of the population), some people may experience minor skin redness from the "accelerators" used to make the gloves stretchy. If you have extremely sensitive skin, please let us know.
Is the resin "non-toxic"?
We use "Low VOC" resins, which are much safer and have a milder scent than industrial resins. However, all liquid resin requires respect. By using our specialized air purifiers and wearing your provided charcoal mask and gloves, your exposure is kept to a minimum.

title: Adults Beginners Ballet Class
description:
Join these adult ballet classes in London and develop proper classical ballet technique in a structured, progressive environment. Whether you're a former dancer returning to the art form or an adult starting formal ballet training for the first time, these classes welcome all levels and focus on the foundations that matter: correct body alignment, strength, flexibility, and the principles of classical ballet.
The classes use the Vaganova method – a Russian technique developed by Agrippina Vaganova that's known worldwide for its softness and fluidity. It uniquely draws from French, Italian, and Russian practices, and we predominantly teach this style whilst occasionally incorporating Italian and American approaches. You'll follow a precise, progressive syllabus designed specifically for adult learners, moving through formal training from September through to June each academic year.
This is a course where consistent attendance really matters. If you want to learn ballet technique properly, we recommend keeping your attendance as regular as you can manage. Each class builds on the last, and that progression – developing strength, refining alignment, understanding the principles more deeply – is what transforms your dancing over time.
What you're investing in is proper training with structure and purpose: a chance to move with awareness, build genuine strength and grace, and experience the discipline and satisfaction of learning a classical art form.

title: National Gallery Walk Through Experience
description:
Have a memorable day out in central London at the National Gallery! In this two to three hour experience, you will be guided through one of the world's top museums by a professional artist.

Located at Trafalgar Square, it is the geographic and cultural center of London. Spending a day viewing this amazing collection of art is an experience not to be missed.
From Leonardo Da Vinci to Claude Monet, you will gain insight into the lives, work, and importance of many of the greatest names in art history. Beyond the trivia of art history, your guide will use his personal knowledge and experience as an artist to give you an artist's perspective on these amazing works of art, a perspective that may change your view of art and its importance to our lives.
This experience is designed to take you through the highlights of the collection in such a way as to show you the best of the gallery without overwhelming you. The tour gives you time to step out afterwards and enjoy some of the other local attractions close by.

title: Kimchi Workshop
description:
Introduction to Kimchi

To start the class, you will be given a brief introduction on kimchi from its history to interesting facts and how it relates to modern kimchi that we love.




Ingredients

You will be shown all the essential ingredients, where you can get them and how to use them. I will also teach you which ingredients can be replaced or omitted in certain situations.




Cutting the Cabbage

You will learn different methods of cutting your cabbage and I will explain how each method differs.




Salting of the Cabbage

Salting is one of the most important stages of kimchi making. I will explain step by step how to do it and how to avoid mistakes.




Making the Kimchi Paste

While the cabbage is salting we make the kimchi paste. You will be given clear instruction what to put in the paste and how to adjust the amount of the key ingredients according to your preference.




Cucumber Kimchi Salad

As a second kimchi, you will learn to make quick cucumber kimchi salad which can be eaten straight away and makes a great side dish to many meaty dishes.




Mixing the Cabbage in Kimchi Paste

When the cabbage is salted enough, we wash it and mix in the kimchi paste.




How to Look After Your Kimchi

I will show you how to keep you kimchi and things to be careful with when storing kimchi for best taste. I also explain the maturing process of kimchi and what to expect at each stage.




Kimchi Tasting

You will have fun with kimchi tasting. I keep 6 months' samples of my homemade kimchi. Tasting kimchi at every month of maturity really lets you see and taste how the kimchi magic is developed over time.




Korean Home Meal

We finish off the class with a sit down at the table of authentic homemade Korean dishes that pair perfectly with kimchi, including Korean BBQ grilled chicken. A real insight of how Korean people enjoy our food and what food means in our daily lives.



Join this small, hands-on kimchi workshop in London and discover a one-of-a-kind tasting and making experience that will help you switch off and immerse yourself in Korea's biggest culinary culture.
As well as learning to make your own kimchi, we offer a unique guided kimchi tasting session, where you will sample homemade kimchi across five to seven different stages of fermentation – from a freshly tossed batch to a richly aged six-month version. It's a friendly, flavour-packed way to experience how Korea's most iconic dish develops over time.
Don't worry if you've never fermented anything before; the class is carefully designed to suit anyone who is interested in making kimchi. Your teacher will guide you step-by-step through an incredibly simple recipe designed for consistent, delicious results. You'll get hands-on experience crafting two of the most popular styles from scratch:
Cut-cabbage kimchi (Mak-Kimchi) – Learn the simple method of prepping, salting, and seasoning cabbage.
Cucumber kimchi salad – Whip up a fresh, crunchy side dish packed with instant flavour.
After mastering your mixes, you'll learn how to use matured kimchi to cook crisp, savoury kimchi pancakes. They're wonderfully easy to make and completely addictive!
To celebrate your new skills together, you'll finish the session with a comforting, delicious set meal featuring everything that goes perfectly with kimchi:
Your handmade kimchi – Taste your fresh creations alongside classic seasoned sides.
Korean BBQ grilled chicken – Savour perfectly grilled, smoky chicken.
Steamed rice and beansprouts – Complete your plate with traditional accompaniments.
Nourishing broth – Sip a warm, comforting soup that balances the meal beautifully.
By the time you finish, you'll have experienced a wonderful kitchen breakthrough, leaving you with the absolute confidence to recreate perfect fermentation loops at home. You'll head away ready to upgrade your everyday cooking, carrying your freshly made jars of cabbage and cucumber kimchi, alongside printed recipe cards covering every single step. Everything you need on the day is fully provided, so just show up and enjoy the fun!

title: Weekend Mahjong Workshop for Newbies
description:
Beginner to Mahjong?
Mahjong is a timeless tile-based game that has been played across Asia for over 300 years and is now gaining global popularity. Unlike poker, where you recognise the cards instantly, Mahjong requires learning the tiles and rules before you can play—and that’s where many beginners struggle.
We’ve often heard how friends and family don’t always have the patience to teach every detail, and after hours of trying, beginners still feel confused about the game.
That’s why Dear Asia Mahjong Workshops are here to help!
Why Learn With Us?
We’re Professional Teachers – We understand how people learn best and have designed two step-by-step workshops that makes Mahjong easy and engaging.Mahjong is More Than a Game – It’s a vital part of Asian social culture, and Dear Asia London, as a language and culture school, is passionate about sharing these traditions with you.
Ready to Play Guaranteed!
In this Newbie workshop, you’ll start playing right away! We’ll introduce you to the tiles, sets, and winning hands while guiding you through the basic rules and game rhythm. By the end of this session, we can guarantee that everyone who comes will learn how to play, and feel confident and ready to play Mahjong with others.
What’s Included:
Mahjong Instructor – Our experienced instructor will guide you in learning and playing.Mahjong Worksheets – Specially designed materials to help players of all levels learn and level up!Free Tea & Coffee – Enjoy a warm drink while you play.Occasional Festive Treats – Depending on the monthly theme, we might treat you to some special Asian delights!
A Social Game in a Social Space
Mahjong isn’t just about strategy—it’s about bringing people together. Our workshop offers a fun, welcoming space where you can meet new people, have a great time and maybe even organise future game nights together! We love seeing friendships blossom over Mahjong.
Small note that there may be times when we don’t have four players equally per table. In such cases, we’ll combine players across the tables to ensure a full game, with guidance from our instructor of course.
Details of the Event
Where: Aldgate Tower just outside of Aldgate East Station Exit 1
Who: New beginners to Mahjong, come alone or come with your friends / family
What is included: worksheets, expert guidance, free tea and coffee, unbeatable vibes
Visiting Us
Each attendee must be registered to our building in addition to the ClassBento ticketing. If you book two tickets, we will need both individuals’ full names and email addresses for registration.
The week before your workshop, you will receive an email from "Aldgate Tower"with your building entry invitation. This email includes a unique visitor QR code, which you’ll need to scan at the ground floor speed gates. Then, head straight up to the 6th floor, where we’ll be ready to welcome you.
Please check your spam or junk folder if you don’t see the email. Still nothing? Send us a message / whatsapp us on +44 7423 755734, and we’ll assist you promptly.

title: Nature Blueprint - Cyanotype Taster Workshop
description:
Slow down for a few hours of creativity, shades of blue, and nature at this cyanotype taster workshop at Trinity Buoy Wharf.
Join BE KA Art Studio, Elena’s riverside atelier at Trinity Buoy Wharf, for a hands-on cyanotype taster session. Cyanotype is one of the oldest photographic printing processes – and one of the most satisfying and sustainable. Using sunlight, water, and natural materials, you'll arrange botanicals, feathers, shells, and found objects onto coated paper, expose them to light, then rinse your print and watch the image bloom in that distinctive, deep, luminous blue. No cameras, no screens, no prior experience needed. Just you, some plants, and the light drawing shapes for you.
If the weather's overcast, UV light has you covered.
You’ll leave with your own original cyanotype artworks.
What You'll Do:
* Arrange botanicals, wooden letters, and other objects to compose your own cyanotype prints
* You're welcome to bring small objects, lace, flowers or negative film of your own if you'd like
* Expose your work in sunlight — or UV light
* Develop your prints in water and watch the images appear
Duration: Allow approximately 1.5–2 hours, depending on the group size.
Good to Know
This is an introductory session using pre-coated paper — solution and paper preparation and advanced techniques are covered in separate, dedicated workshops.
Step-free access and disabled toilets available
The studio is close to local favourites such as The Orchard Café and Layers Bakery, if you'd like a drink or snack before or after (both open daily until 4 pm). There's also our local pub, The Lockdown Room, near Canning Town station, for food and drinks until late.
Location — Trinity Buoy Wharf, London E14 0FP
The workshop takes place at Trinity Buoy Wharf, a historic 19th-century site in London's Docklands, now home to one of London's most vibrant creative communities, a sculpture park, event venues, and the iconic Container City™ buildings.
Privacy & Consent
By attending this event, you agree that photos and videos may be taken and used for promotional purposes, including on the BE KA website and social media channels. If you'd prefer not to appear, simply let me know, and I'll make sure to respect your wishes.
What you'll get
2 x A5 pre-coated paper sheets in your choice of colour, or small square coated paper
Botanicals, feathers, shells, and natural materials (feel free to bring your own if you'd like)
Small wooden craft letters
Aprons
Your original cyanotype artworks

title: Design and Build Your Own Crystal Geode Candle Pillar
description:
Choose Your Design

Begin by selecting your pillar candle, then explore a range of inspiring geode, stone and rustic designs. You'll decide on your own style, colour palette and overall composition before sketching out your ideas and planning your unique candle pillar.




Build the Plaster Structure

Learn how to create the mould that forms the decorative candle pillar around your candle. You'll mix and pour plaster using professional techniques to achieve a strong, durable structure before learning how to sculpt, carve and distress the surface to create the appearance of aged stone, weathered concrete and fractured rock.




Create the Geode Design

While your plaster cures, browse our extensive collection of semi-precious stones, crystals, decorative glass, beads and mixed-media embellishments. You'll experiment with different layouts and carefully design the geode cavity that will become the focal point of your piece.




Paint and Add Special Effects

Bring your candle pillar to life using a variety of decorative painting techniques to create realistic stone, concrete, metallic and antique finishes. If you'd like, you'll also learn optional gilding techniques to highlight details and add a luxurious finishing touch.




Build the Crystal Geode

Secure your chosen stones and decorative materials to create a stunning crystal geode effect. You'll also have the option of learning how to work with UV resin to encapsulate semi-precious stones and decorative elements, creating beautiful crystal-clear depth and sparkle.




Seal & Take Home Your Creation

Complete your candle pillar by applying a protective varnish for a durable, professional-quality finish. Your finished piece is ready to display—simply place your favourite pillar candle inside and enjoy a completely unique handcrafted centrepiece that you've designed and built yourself.



Transform an ordinary pillar candle into a striking sculptural centrepiece inspired by weathered stone, ancient ruins, natural crystal geodes and steampunk design in this hands-on candle making workshop in London.
You'll build a handcrafted plaster shell around a pre-made pillar candle before transforming it into a unique decorative piece using paints, semi-precious stones, mixed media and optional UV resin. The result is a beautiful candle pillar that looks carved from aged stone and broken open to reveal a sparkling crystal geode hidden within.
Whether you're drawn to dramatic monochrome finishes, shimmering metallic details, vibrant resin geodes or rustic industrial textures, you'll have complete creative freedom to design a piece that's uniquely yours – no two candle pillars are ever the same.
This workshop is made for complete beginners as well as anyone who enjoys mixed-media crafts, home décor or learning new creative techniques.

title: Necklace Making Workshop
description:
Step 1: Warm Welcome & Introduction

Guests are welcomed and can choose where they'd like to sit and get comfortable for the class. Emma will then do an introduction into what the workshop will entail and what guests will learn and take home by the end of it.




Step 2: Preparation & Setup

Guests will be introduced to materials, design boards and tools. Emma will explain how to use a design board to measure the length of your desired necklace and answer any questions about the materials and tools.




Step 3: Design Process

Choosing colours, patterns, textures and designs comes more naturally to some than others but Emma is on hand to help as much or as little as you like. There will also be lots of example necklaces on display if you'd like some inspiration. Emma can also help you with explaining some basics necklace design principles. Your design board is there to allow you to have a play around before committing to final design.




Step 4: Beading

Once you're happy with your design, Emma will show you how to attach bead ends to your wire and how to bead.




Step 5: Securing Your Necklace

Once all your beads are in place, Emma will show you how to securely close off your necklace using pilers, clam shell bead ends and crimp tubes.




Step 6: Finishing Your Necklace

Once all your beads are secured, it's time to choose your clasp and finish your necklace. There will be a range of Sterling Silver or Gold Plated clasps to choose from.

title: 4 Week Textile Art Course in Appliqué and Hand Embroidery
description:
Join this four-week appliqué and hand embroidery course and discover the joy of turning words and images that matter to you into a stitched, one-of-a-kind piece of textile art. Over four relaxed weekly sessions, you'll learn traditional hand sewing techniques while designing a fabric collage.
This course is about slowing down and trusting your own creativity to make something deeply personal. Alongside learning appliqué and embroidery stitches, you'll discover how imagery, fabric and stitch come together to tell a story – think of it as your own modern sampler, a piece to treasure long after the final stitch. No previous sewing experience is needed; you'll be guided through every stage at your own pace, from your very first stitches to the finishing touches.
Week One: Learning the language of stitch
Get to know the materials and techniques you'll use throughout the course, learning a handful of simple but beautiful appliqué and embroidery stitches and experimenting with fabrics and textures to build your confidence.
Week Two: Finding your words
Through gentle creative prompts, you'll reflect on the words you'd like your piece to carry – from poetry and music to family sayings or your own philosophy. Once you've settled on a phrase or idea, you'll explore the imagery it evokes, sketch your composition and start building your appliqué design in fabric.
Week Three: Bringing your artwork to life
With your composition assembled, you'll start stitching your design and adding embroidered detail and texture, working at your own pace with plenty of one-to-one guidance. You're welcome to take your piece home to keep stitching between sessions.
Week Four: Finishing your piece
Bring your artwork back to the studio for a final session of stitching and finishing, where you'll explore ways to complete and present it – whether that's framing, turning it into a wall hanging, stretching it, or continuing to add to it afterwards.
Please note: optional additional studio sessions are available if you'd like more time and support to keep stitching your project.

Join this brass rubbing workshop in the magnificent, atmospheric Crypt of St Martin-in-the-Fields and spend a relaxed evening discovering a fascinating, historic hobby. title: Korean Feast Cooking Class
description:
Get Ready to Get Busy

This is a action packed busy class where we make 3 classic Korean dishes: Bibimbap, Japchae and Seafood pancake




Introduction to Ingredients

You will be shown all the fresh ingredients to make all the the items in this class. You will learn how to prep the vegetables and season the meat.




Cooking the Toppings for Bibimbap

You will get to prepare some of the bibimbap toppings from scratch and some will be pre-prepped by the instructor but will be explained




Assembling Your Bibimbap

Once all the toppings are prepared you will learn how to arrange a perfect looking bibimbap with homemade bibimbap sauce.




Admire You Creation

Making a beautiful bowl of bibimbap is not difficult if you know how to. Such a nutritionally balanced healthy Korean food to know how to make!




Japchae

You will also learn to make delicious vegetarian japchae. This part will be mostly demonstration but you will learn how to prepare all the ingredients too.




Best Korean Seafood Pancake

You will learn to whip up the best Korean pancake you will ever taste. This is one dish I never order at restaurants because it's so easy and quick to make at home with the best ingredients. Restaurant pancakes hardly ever have much fillings. I will show you how to prep the ingredients and how to make the crispiest Korean pancake ever!




Have a Korean Feast Together

At the end of the class, you will have a sit down to enjoy all the dishes you have created in the class. You will all go home with extra portion of bibimbap to take home.



Learn to make two of Korea's most iconic dishes – bibimbap and japchae – at Kimchi Club W5. These crowd-pleasing favourites are perfect for impressing friends and family at your next dinner party, and you'll be surprised at how achievable they are to make.
In this hands-on class, you'll discover how to prepare bulgogi bibimbap with all five toppings – each one a delicious Korean side dish called banchan. So really, you're learning five separate dishes that come together into one beautiful, flavourful bowl. Japchae, one of Korea's most beloved noodle dishes and a party staple, shares some common vegetables with bibimbap, so together these two dishes make perfect sense to learn in one session. You'll master savoury, sweet, flavour-packed cooking that feels impressive but is genuinely accessible.
Whether you're a complete beginner or a confident cook, this class is designed to build your skills and confidence in the kitchen. Throughout the session, you'll work hands-on with all the ingredients, learning techniques you'll keep using long after the class ends. Just as real Korean families do, we'll prepare a lovely soup to accompany the food, and everyone gathers together for a proper feast at the end of the class – it's the perfect way to celebrate what you've just created and taste the results of your work.
You'll also take some food home for your family, and printed recipe cards covering everything you've learned, so you can confidently recreate these dishes and get perfect results every time.
What you'll get

description:
At Dalston Clay we get very excited about the possibilities of glaze and so we encourage you to take your ceramics practice further by returning to glaze your work to see for yourself!
Glaze is a slurry of glass-forming chemicals that, when applied to bisque ware (bisque fired) and then fired a second time (glaze fired), produces a glassy, food-safe surface; often with funky effects!
Our glazing tutorial is a guided session that begins half an hour (6 pm) before the evening session (6.30 pm). description:
A Warm Welcome

Welcome to our cool and friendly London kitchen! Your culinary journey begins with a fascinating introduction to the history of TangHuLu. In our small, personal classes, your experienced chef will get you settled in and excited to create the delicious Chinese treats.




Prepare the Ingredients

Get hands-on with every step: select the fruits and prepare the fruits. Not all fruits suitable for TangHuLu. We’ll guide you through the process and you will easily to make them again at home.




Cook the Sugar Syrup

The most important step, cook the sugar syrup. Your expeirenced chef tutors will guide you through carefully. Make sure you can get the perfect glaze of sugar and the crunchy texture.




Wrap and Deco TangHuLu

Unleash your creativity as you add the finishing touches. You'll learn simple but beautiful ways to decorate your TangHuLu, working with a variety of flavours to create a colourful and tempting collection of desserts.




Your Delicious Creations

Step back and admire the beautiful TangHuLu you’ve made! You’ll leave the workshop with satisfied sweet tooth, plus the skills and know-how to recreate them whenever you like.



Discover the magic behind one of China’s most iconic street desserts in this colourful Parent & Child Tanghulu workshop in London.
Tanghulu is famous for its beautiful glossy appearance and satisfying crack when you bite into the crisp sugar shell. In this hands-on class, you and your child will transform fresh fruit into sparkling candied skewers that look like edible jewels.
This class turns dessert-making into a fun family experience, where adults and children work side by side to create delicious treats together.
Our workshops are small and relaxed in a spacious, air-conditioned London studio, giving each family plenty of guidance from our friendly tutors. Weekday sessions are often quieter and can sometimes feel like a private class.
No experience is needed — just bring your curiosity and sweet tooth.
What Is Tanghulu?
Tanghulu is a traditional Chinese candied fruit dessert made by coating fresh fruit in a thin, crisp sugar shell.
The result is a delightful contrast of sweet, tangy, and crunchy flavours — and a treat that looks almost too beautiful to eat.
In this class, you and your child will create your own handcrafted Tanghulu skewers from scratch.
Children especially love watching the sugar transform into a shiny shell and decorating their colourful fruit creations.
In this family workshop, you and your child will learn to:
Choose the best fruits for perfect Tanghulu
Understand the science of cooking sugar to the right temperature
Coat fruit evenly with a crisp, glass-like sugar shell
Create colourful and beautifully presented Tanghulu skewers
Safely handle and cool sugar to achieve the perfect crack
You’ll work with seasonal fruits and simple, high-quality ingredients while being guided step by step by our experienced tutors.
Why Families Love This Workshop

title: Introduction to Kintsugi Workshop
description:
Traditional kintsugi (‘gold joining’) is an ancient Japanese repair technique which uses lacquer (urushi) dusted with powdered precious metals to restore broken ceramic pieces. The process illustrates the wabi-sabi philosophy of finding beauty in the flawed or imperfect. Rather than hiding flaws, kintsugi highlights them to show the object’s history.
During this two hour workshop, your tutor will guide you through every stage of the process of fixing a broken ceramic item using a micro metal mix with ureshi resin to create your gold solution. You'll then use this solution, along with a special putty, to fix together your broken pottery, creating a beautiful piece of perfectly imperfect art.
The workshop is ‘easy’ kintsugi: an accessible introduction to kintsugi principles and techniques. Traditional kintsugi uses materials that take far longer to cure and harden, and pure gold powder is best used by more experienced practitioners.
This workshop assumes no experience of kintsugi, and will give everyone the knowledge they need to repair their own broken ceramics at home. We only work with small groups, so you will each get plenty of support and guidance throughout.
You are welcome to bring your own piece of broken ceramic but due to time constraints please ensure it only has one break at most. Otherwise we will supply pretty small broken pots to choose from. Guests will take away their finished pieces on the day - please bring a box with you to safely take your piece home.
Book as an individual, or gather a group for a fun activity together.

There is a minimum of 3 participants required before the class can take place.

title: Facial Massage Class
description:
Preparing Face

this first step, we gently place our hands on the face to begin connecting with the facial muscles and skin. Using light lifting and warming movements, we stimulate circulation, encourage lymphatic flow, and prepare the face for the massage techniques that follow.

This moment is about slowing down, relaxing, and allowing the skin to wake up naturally. By learning the correct hand placement and pressure, you’ll start to feel how facial massage can instantly lift, soften tension, and bring a healthy glow to the skin.




Lifting & Sculpting Face

In this step, we begin the lifting massage movements that help tone and sculpt the facial muscles. Using gentle upward strokes and controlled pressure, we work along the cheeks, jawline, and facial contours to encourage circulation and natural lifting of the skin.

These techniques help to release tension in the face, improve blood flow, and support the skin’s natural firmness. You’ll learn how simple lifting movements can make the face feel refreshed, energised.




Natural Glow

After completing the lifting massage techniques, the skin begins to look brighter, refreshed and naturally glowing. The circulation has been stimulated and the facial muscles have been gently activated, helping the skin appear more lifted and radiant.

At this stage, you’ll start to notice how facial massage can bring an instant healthy glow to the complexion. It’s a lovely moment in the treatment where the skin looks revived, the face feels relaxed, and the benefits of the lifting techniques really begin to show. ✨




The Glow Mask

At this stage, a glow mask or collagen mask is applied to deeply nourish and hydrate the skin. After the lifting massage techniques, the skin is warm and receptive, allowing the mask ingredients to absorb more effectively.

This step helps to calm the skin, lock in moisture, and enhance the radiant glow created by the massage. While the mask rests, the face can fully relax, leaving the skin feeling soft, refreshed, and beautifully revitalised. ✨



Discover the benefits of facial massage in this relaxing and interactive massage workshop in London, where you’ll learn techniques designed to support healthy, glowing skin. Through gentle movements and guided practice, you’ll explore how facial massage can help release tension, boost circulation, and create a natural lifting effect.

title: Weekend Just Play Mahjong Club - Chinese Styles and Richii
description:
Event Details
Where: Aldgate Tower (just outside Aldgate East Station, Exit 1)
Who: Players who already know how to play with scores (not suitable for beginners)
Included: Instructor help, free tea, coffee, and unbeatable vibes
Want to play mahjong regularly?
Mahjong is still a niche board game in London — and since it needs 4 players, it can be hard to organise regular games with just your own friends or family.
In many parts of Asia, Mahjong parlours bring people together to play. While we’re not running a commercial Mahjong club, we are here to build a community.
Many of our players started as complete beginners in our workshops — and now they’re hooked! That’s why we created our ️ Just Play tickets.
Different Mahjong Style Welcome
Hong Kong Style (Main Style)
Our main style is Hong Kong Mahjong, with a 3 fan minimum to win.
If you know how to play other Chinese styles like Taiwanese, Sichuan, or British Mahjong, you’re still welcome! We’ll provide scoring cards to help you adapt.
️ However, these tables are not suitable for beginners. If you haven’t yet graduated from Level 1 or Level 2 of our workshops, or if you don’t know how to score, please join our learner workshops first to build confidence.
Japanese Riichi
Riichi Mahjong is new to our community, but we love its fast pace and strategic complexity!If you already know how to play Riichi — amazing! Please join us.If you play Chinese Mahjong and want to try Riichi, one of our instructors or friendly regulars might help, but we can’t guarantee full teaching support yet. You're welcome to learn by playing alongside others.
American Mahjong (New Community in 2026)
We’re excited to add American Mahjong to our offerings. It’s quite different from Chinese Mahjong, so we’ll run newbie workshops and regular Just Play sessions from 2026. Note: Just Play bookings require solid prior knowledge of American rules. However, we encourage cross‑style learning, so if you already know one style of Mahjong, learn another with us, so you can play at any table.
Our best price promise
We’re doing our best to keep Just Play tickets affordable at £15 for a 2-hour session — that’s our best price promise.
Unlike clubs that charge entry or venues that require a minimum spend, our ticket price covers only what’s needed: venue, staff, admin cost.
And yes — with a booked ticket, you are guaranteed a seat at the table, and we also provide free tea, coffee, and the occasional festive treat.
We're not a charity, but we are deeply committed to creating a welcoming Mahjong community. Your support helps us keep the tiles clicking, and we love seeing familiar faces return week after week!
Visiting Us
Each attendee must be registered to our building in addition to the ClassBento ticketing. If you book two tickets, we will need both individuals’ full names and email addresses for registration.
On the same week, you will receive an email from "Aldgate Tower" with your building entry invitation. This email includes a unique visitor QR code, which you’ll need to scan at the ground floor speed gates. Then, head straight up to the 6th floor, where we’ll be ready to welcome you.
Please check your spam or junk folder if you don’t see the email. Still nothing? Send us a message on ClassBento, and we’ll assist you promptly.

Free tea and coffee, occasional festive treats.

title: Kusudama Origami Workshop
description:

description:
Discover how to capture striking architectural images in this hands-on walk/workshop. Exploring Composition – Utilising leading lines, framing, and perspective for dynamic and engaging images

Optimal Camera Settings – Essential settings for architectural photography
Location
This workshop takes place along the Thames, beginning at Tate Modern, and follows a thoughtfully designed route showcasing notable architectural landmarks. Kevin will be in a café (LEON) near Tate Modern from 9:45am. The workshop starts promptly at 10:00am.

Bad Weather Policy

Crispiest Korean Fried Chicken

It's not as difficult to make the delicious Korean friend chicken if you know how to!




Two Types of Fried Chicken

Two Types of Fried Chicken

2 Types of Glaze

You will learn to make 2 of the most popular Korean chicken glaze: Honey butter garlic glaze and sweet gochujang yangnyum glaze.




Chicken Pickle

Introduction to Bibim-myeon

Bibim-myeon is a refreshing Korean cold noodle dish tossed in a sweet, tangy and spicy gochujang sauce. Served with crisp vegetables and a perfectly cooked egg, it's the perfect balance of bold flavours and satisfying textures-especially especially to pair with fried food.

title: Nigerian Jollof Cookery Class
description:
Join us for a Nigerian cooking class in London. Jollof rice is the centrepiece of every celebration, every gathering, and every argument about whose version in West Africa is the best. In this class, you will learn to make it properly, alongside grilled chicken, creamy coleslaw with a sharp salad cream tang, and sweet, caramelised fried plantain.
No experience is needed. Whether you’re a curious beginner or a confident home cook, this class offers a welcoming introduction to the bold flavours and techniques of Nigerian cuisine.
What to expect:
Build a smoky tomato base -- learn how to attain the signature smoky flavour to transform the taste of the finished rice.
Master your grains -- understand the different grains that can be used, learn the perfect rice-to-liquid ratio, and the method that gives you perfectly cooked grains every single time.
Explore regional variations -- understand what makes Nigerian jollof different from Ghanaian jollof, Sierra Leonean jollof, and Senegalese jollof, and learn tips from across West Africa.
Picking the perfect plantain -- learn how to read ripeness, control the heat, and get that deep amber caramelisation without burning.
Enjoy complimentary drinks, including zobo, Chapman, water, and tea.
By the end of the class, you’ll have prepared a full Nigerian feast and gained the skills and confidence to recreate these vibrant West African dishes at home.

All ingredients, equipment, and aprons will be provided.

title: Succession Planting Workshop for Resilient Gardens
description:
This new workshop is designed as an opportunity to enhance your plant knowledge and grow your confidence to successfully plan and maintain the succession of your planting within your garden.
In this workshop, you'll learn to create year-round garden interest through strategic succession planting. You'll develop skills in planning seasonal displays that combine flowering periods, foliage textures, and colours for continuous visual appeal.
The session combines classroom theory, garden walks, and practical exercises. You'll analyse real garden examples, participate in group discussions, and create your own succession planting plan to take home.
Together we will cover:
Planning and evaluating
Seasonal interest
Layered planting
Long-term vision
Biodiversity & wildlife
We will share our tips on how to create and maintain a successional, biodiverse, and resilient garden with minimal use of resources to achieve maximum output for wildlife, wellbeing, and enjoyment by welcoming life and colour into your space through a design and installation that works for you.
You'll leave equipped to create resilient, biodiverse gardens that provide year-round interest while supporting local wildlife.
Please note this workshop refers to ornamental succession planting in a garden, not the succession planting of vegetable gardening, which is used to ensure a constant supply of fresh produce.

title: British Scones, Crumpets and Lemon Curd Baking Experience
description:
Welcome to the Good Crumb

Settle into our welcoming London home with a refreshing drink. Meet your hosts and fellow bakers as we share the stories behind Britain's best-loved teatime treats before tying on our aprons.




Whip Up Your Crumpet Batter

Whisk together a traditional crumpet batter and learn how to work with yeast. Discover the secrets to the bread’s famous little holes that give crumpets their remarkable texture




Craft Your Lemon Curd

Whip up your own silky lemon curd—the delightful British cousin of jam that's wonderfully smooth and bursting with citrus flavour. We'll share our favourite tips for getting the texture just right.




Mix, Shape and Bake Your Scones

Mix, shape and bake classic British scones using our tips that keep them beautifully light every time.




Crumpet Cooking on the Stovetop

Cook your crumpets until crisp and golden outside, with the perfect soft springy finish that makes them ideal for soaking up butter.

Celebrate your baking together, enjoying everything you’ve made with jam and cream and a pot of tea. Leave with new baking skills, recipes and warm memories to take home.



Hosted by sisters Claudia and Giselle, you'll join us in one of our welcoming North London homes to discover three of Britain's best-loved afternoon tea classics using the family recipes we grew up with.
No baking experience is needed! Whether you're travelling solo, as a couple, with friends, or family, this is a warm, sociable experience where you'll meet fellow travellers, share great conversation, and enjoy genuine British hospitality.

Create homemade lemon curd -- a silky, intensely lemony spread that's been a beloved part of British teatime for generations.
Discover the stories behind these iconic bakes, plenty of baking tips, and the little techniques that help you recreate them with confidence at home.
Once everything is ready, we'll gather around the kitchen table to enjoy your freshly baked scones and warm crumpets with homemade lemon curd, jams, clotted cream, and a pot of English tea.
Whether it's your first time baking or you're bringing a young baker along, we'll provide as much guidance and encouragement as you need, making sure everyone feels confident and included. title: Gua Sha Facial Massage Class
description:
In this intimate and interactive 60-minute class, you'll learn the basics of gua sha massage, for you to build your practise upon at home. You'll be guided each step of the way through a full face massage routine that will leave your skin toned, sculpted, smoothed, and radiant.
Gua sha facial massage is rooted in Traditional Chinese Medicine. The Gua sha tool is designed to be pulled across the skin to help stimulate microcirculation, increase blood flow to the skin, and aid lymphatic drainage. This can help to tone the skin, help it feel firmer and lifted, smooth out the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, and drain away puffiness.

The correct pressure and movement to apply to each section of your face
Different techniques to tackle specific skincare concerns

title: Family Omurice Cooking Class: Japanese Omelette Rice Workshop
description:
Settle in and Get Cooking

We'll welcome you into our kitchen and introduce you to the Japanese dishes of the day. First up, learn how to make delicious egg fried rice.




Make Traditional Omurice

Learn how to make the traditional version of omurice, popularised in the 1970s and earlier. We'll be there to guide you every step of the way.




Make Whirlpool Omurice

Learn how to make another version -- this one popular from the 2000s. Get equipped with new cooking skills and knowledge on both versions of the dish!




Taste the Success

Reflect on your new Japanese cooking skills as you sit down, relax, and enjoy your omurice dishes. Take home your leftovers to savour the taste!




Add-on Yakitori

Learn this famous Japanese chicken sticks.




Add-on Mini Japanese Curry Class

Cook a portion of Japanese curry to serve with your omurice.



Discover one of Japan’s most comforting and beloved dishes in this fun Parent & Child Japanese cooking class in London.
Omurice — short for “omelette rice” — is a famous Japanese café dish where fluffy eggs wrap around savoury fried rice and are finished with a drizzle of ketchup.
In this hands-on workshop, you and your child will learn to cook this iconic dish together while enjoying a relaxed and creative family cooking experience.
Children especially love the final step: decorating their Omurice with ketchup drawings — smiley faces, animals, or their own creative designs.
Our small-group classes take place in a spacious, air-conditioned cooking studio in London, where families can cook side by side with guidance from our friendly chef tutors.
Weekday sessions are often quieter and may feel like a private class, giving you even more time to ask questions and enjoy the experience.
No experience is required — just bring your curiosity and appetite.
What Is Omurice?
Omurice is a classic Japanese comfort food loved in cafés and home kitchens across Japan.
It combines flavourful Japanese fried rice with a soft, fluffy omelette, creating a dish that is both simple and satisfying.
In Japan, it’s also famous for its playful presentation — many chefs decorate the omelette with ketchup drawings or messages.
In this class, you and your child will learn how to create your own beautifully presented Omurice from scratch.
During This Family Cooking Class You Will Learn To:
Understand the best rice for Japanese fried rice
Cook savoury Japanese-style fried rice with balanced seasoning
Make a soft, fluffy omelette
Wrap the omelette neatly around the rice
Decorate your Omurice with creative ketchup designs
Our chef tutors guide each step so both adults and children can cook confidently.

title: Pearl Knotting Workshop
description:
This short day class will introduce how to string jewellery using traditional knotting skills, learning from an experienced jeweller who has been teaching jewellery making since 2009.
Knotted necklaces / bracelets give a different feel to regular stringing and this technique is traditional for more expensive pearls and gemstones, for added strength and protection for the beads. This knotting (as in this class) is a different technique from more standard bead stringing.
If you are interested in this course, some basic bead jewellery / basic bead stringing skills are useful first before attempting knotting, as this is a more complex technique.
Students will each create a pair of fully knotted pearl / gemstone bracelets - you will learn how to choose and plan out their beads, then select the appropriate thread, how to create and tighten their knots, and of course how to securely attach clasps and finish the jewellery to a professional standard.
We make two bracelets during the session, rather than a necklace, as this gives more practise in starting and finishing the process - the overall process is the same for both bracelets and necklaces.
Class size - maximum of just 2 people
Class runs from 10am to 2.30pm (with a half-hour break)
Great for a girls' day out or a special treat for a celebration for a crafty or bead-loving friend, but also great for hobby or professional jewellers looking to expand their range of skills - the small class size allows a flexible approach and plenty of time for individual questions and support.
Unfortunately, the workshop space is not fully accessible, so if you have mobility issues, do get in touch before booking.
What you'll get
You will leave with a pair of bracelets made to your own design with your choice of gemstone or pearl beads and sterling silver clasps.

title: Furniture Upcycling Workshop
description:
Join this beginner furniture painting and upcycling workshop in London and learn how to breathe new life into tired furniture using proper preparation and painting techniques.
This session focuses on the core skills you need to feel confident upcycling furniture: preparing, sanding, cleaning and painting a chair or small piece, all guided step by step in a relaxed, supportive setting with plenty of room to practise and ask questions.
You'll work on a practice piece provided for the day, so you're free to focus entirely on learning the process rather than worrying about how the final result turns out. It's ideal if you're completely new to upcycling, or simply want to build your confidence before taking on a project of your own at home.
This workshop also forms the first half of the full-day "Upcycle Your Own Chair" experience – if you fancy carrying on into upholstery and finishing a whole piece in a single day, you can book the combined workshop instead.
Whether you're a beginner, a keen DIYer, or just curious about sustainable living, you'll come away with hands-on skills you can put to use on your own furniture straight away – proof that a tired piece is often better restored than replaced.
Here's what to expect:
Beginner-friendly, with no experience required
All tools and materials provided – just bring yourself, and clothes you don't mind getting messy
Small groups, with plenty of one-to-one guidance
A sustainable, feel-good day out, learning how to save furniture from landfill
Take-home skills you'll keep using long after the workshop ends
You'll be introduced to the key stages of furniture upcycling – including how to properly prepare a surface, sand it to a smooth finish, and apply paint for a clean, durable result – with individual support on hand throughout.
By the end, you'll have a completely different feel for what's possible with a little sanding, prep and paint – and you might be surprised by just how much you can transform in one session.
