title: Silver Clay Jewellery Taster Class
description:
This exciting in-person jewellery making class is held in Camden Town, London NW1.
You'll get to learn a new skill while having a fun evening out and relaxing after work. Whether you're a complete beginner or a jeweller working in different media, this workshop is perfect for anyone looking to get creative and expand their range of craft skills.
This course (and all my courses) is designed for adults. I do not currently offer classes for children and teenagers.
During the three-hour session, you'll learn how to create your very own silver pendant, or a pair of earrings from Silver Clay - this is a modern material made from particles of pure silver metal, mixed with a water based binder that holds them together as a workable clay.
Silver Clay - is real alchemy! You model the clay to create your basic forms, then dry it out and further refine it, join elements together and then finally fire the clay to burn away the binder and sinter the silver particles together to form a solid metal. Clay to solid shiny, wearable silver in just 3 hours!
Don't worry if you're new to jewellery making - this class is designed to alleviate any fears and provide a supportive environment for beginners. With a small group size of just 3 students, your experienced instructor will guide you through the process, ensuring you feel confident every step of the way.
All the materials you need will be provided, so simply come along on your own or with friends to enjoy a fun and creative evening. As you create your custom jewellery pieces, you'll experience the satisfaction of seeing your designs come to life. By the end of the class, you'll have beautifully polished jewellery ready to wear.
Join us for this relaxing jewellery making class and take home not just your new skills, but also a beautiful solid silver pendant or pair of earrings that you can proudly wear or give as a thoughtful gift. Don't miss out on this opportunity to learn, create, and have a memorable evening!
The workshop space is downstairs, so unfortunately difficult to access for anyone with mobility problems - apologies for any inconvenience.
What you'll get
Have a fun few hours and leave with your own custom designed solid silver pendant or earrings, ready to wear or to gift...
Drinks and snacks are available throughout, and you will also get detailed printed (or emailed) notes to remind you of the processes we've covered if you decide to do more creating after the class.

title: Power Tools Course: Table Saw Mastery
description:
Power Tools Course: Table Saw Mastery
Duration: 4 hrs
This power tools course is a hands-on introduction to one of the most important and versatile machines in woodworking — the table saw. Designed for both beginners and experienced makers, this practical session will help you build confidence using advanced tools safely and effectively. You’ll learn how to select, set up, and operate a table saw with precision, discovering its many uses for cutting, joining, and fine woodworking projects.
With access to four different table saw models, you’ll gain valuable insight into how each one functions and where it excels. By the end of the power tools course, you’ll leave with a handmade wooden box built entirely on the table saw — a tangible piece that showcases your new skills and craftsmanship.
 Experience Level: Suitable for all skill levels — beginners welcome
1. Understanding the Table Saw
We begin by exploring the anatomy of the table saw — blades, fences, mitre gauges, and riving knives — and how each part affects performance and precision. You’ll learn the key differences between contractor, cabinet, and portable models, giving you the knowledge to choose the right one for your workspace. As part of this power tools course, you’ll also understand how these variations impact accuracy, power, and ease of use, preparing you to make informed decisions for your own workshop setup.
2. Safety and Setup
Table saws demand respect and proper technique. This section focuses on safety — correct stance, hand placement, push-stick use, and blade height adjustment — ensuring that you feel confident and in control. You’ll learn how to change blades, calibrate fences, and align guides for perfect results every time.
Participants must wear appropriate clothing, closed-toe shoes, and ensure long hair is tied up. Please bring a bottle of water and any refreshments you might like during the break — woodworking can be surprisingly energetic!
Safety and setup are the foundation of every power tools course, and by mastering these skills early, you’ll reduce risk and improve accuracy throughout your woodworking journey.
3. Making Accurate Cuts
In this segment, you’ll practice rip cuts, crosscuts, bevels, and mitres — the essential techniques that make the table saw such a powerful tool. You’ll learn to set up fences, measure efficiently, and ensure every cut is straight, clean, and consistent. This practical part of the power tools course focuses on control, precision, and efficiency, helping you achieve professional results in any woodworking project.
4. Tips, Tricks, and Common Pitfalls
Every experienced woodworker has their go-to tricks for getting the best from their tools. Here you’ll learn proven methods to reduce tear-out, improve cut quality, and maintain a safe, clutter-free workspace. We’ll also explore common pitfalls — from kickback to poor alignment — and how to avoid them. This is where the power tools course brings everything together, giving you real-world techniques that save time and materials while improving craftsmanship.
5. Hands-On Project: Build a Box Using Only the Table Saw
Finally, you’ll put your new skills into action by building a small box entirely on the table saw. This project reinforces everything you’ve learned — from safety and setup to cutting and assembly — allowing you to leave with a completed piece you can be proud of.
By the end of this power tools course, you’ll have a strong understanding of how to safely and confidently use a table saw, along with the practical knowledge to integrate it into your future woodworking projects.
Ready to take your woodworking further? Explore more at Power Tools Course — including advanced sessions covering routers, planers, drills, and other essential workshop tools.

This intensive two-hour coffee making course in London takes you through the full journey of coffee -- from raw green beans to the finished cup. Roast theory, including drying, Maillard reactions, first crack, development time, and roast levels.

Hands-on brewing using a V60 or cafetière.
Comparative tasting to explore how origin, processing, roasting, and brewing influence flavour.

By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to identify the major green coffee origins and processing methods, recognise common green defects, describe the key stages and chemistry of a roast, explain the core variables of extraction, and brew a balanced cup using at least one manual method.

title: English Hardwood Trinket Box Workshop
description:
Join us for a hands-on carpentry workshop in South East London, where you will assemble and finish a beautifully crafted trinket box using premium English hardwood. This engaging 4-hour session is ideal for beginners and also suitable for intermediate woodworkers who want to gain experience in fine woodworking techniques while creating a functional and personalised piece. With all timber precut, your focus will be on assembly, finishing, and customisation using professional woodworking tools.
What you'll learn:
Assembling a trinket box using precision-cut English hardwood
Proper clamping and gluing techniques for secure joints
Using sanders to achieve a smooth, professional finish
Inserting and trimming spines with a saw for added strength and detail
Personalising your trinket box with a laser engraver for a custom message or image
Applying Odie’s Oil in a variety of colours to enhance the wood’s natural beauty
Tools and materials you'll use:
Precut English hardwood: Each participant will receive high-quality, precut timber to assemble their trinket box
Clamps and glue: Learn how to properly secure joints for a strong and lasting bond
Sanding tools: Smooth out edges and surfaces for a refined finish
Saw for spine trimming: Learn to trim and refine spines for durability and aesthetics
Laser engraver: Personalise your project with a unique message or image
Odie's Oil: Choose from a range of colours to enhance and protect your finished piece
Workshop schedule:
Introduction & Assembly
Welcome and overview of the carpentry course
Introduction to English hardwood and its characteristics
Step-by-step guided assembly of the trinket box using clamps and glue-up techniques
Spine Insertion & Refinement
Explanation of spine reinforcement for durability and design
Hands-on experience inserting spines and trimming them using a saw
Ensuring precision and a clean finish
Sanding & Personalisation
Using sanders to smooth surfaces and edges
Introduction to the laser engraver for customisation
Participants will engrave their trinket box with a personal message or design
Finishing & Preservation
Choosing from a selection of Odie’s Oil colours to enhance the wood grain
Proper application and buffing techniques for a professional finish
Final quality check and group showcase

Beginners interested in fine woodworking and hands-on projects
Intermediate woodworkers looking to refine their skills in assembly and finishing

Anyone looking for a creative, hands-on experience in a guided carpentry course

title: Printmaking Workshop: Hand-Carved Rubber Stamps
description:
Discover the quiet, meditative craft of rubber stamp carving at this unique printmaking workshop in London. Unlike traditional lino printing, which uses harder linoleum for larger, bolder prints, rubber stamp carving uses softer rubber and a precision knife to capture fine, illustrative linework, perfect for small marks on cards, journals, envelopes, gift wrapping, or anywhere you'd like to leave a personal imprint.
Never tried carving before? No worries! In this 2.5-hour session, you'll work in a small group of up to three under the close, hands-on guidance of an artist with 12 years of rubber stamp carving experience -- so you'll never be stuck or unsure what to do next.
What to expect:
Choose your design from a printed sheet of starter designs (Art Nouveau, vintage botanical, scientific line art) -- or bring one of your own.
Learn about the unique qualities of rubber stamp carving and how it differs from lino printing.
Transfer your chosen design onto the rubber and carve your very own stamp with hands-on guidance throughout.
Test, refine and finish your stamp, then ink and print it onto cards or paper to take home.
Pick up key skills along the way: basic stamp design principles, positive vs negative space, safe knife handling, carving techniques, and inking and test-printing.
By the end of the workshop, you'll leave with a beautifully hand-carved stamp, a complete take-home starter toolkit worth around £18 and the tools and confidence to keep carving at home.
Please note: The studio is located up a flight of stairs and is not currently wheelchair accessible.

Please note: Public dates for this class require at least 2 guests to run. In the unlikely event that we don't reach this number, we may cancel the session; if that happens, we'll inform you and let you choose between a refund or reschedule, so please watch your email/SMS one day prior to the class.

description:
Welcome

On arrival, you’ll be greeted by a glass of wine, which will be free-flowing throughout the course of the evening

The class will start with a demonstration that will cover 7 different fish. You will of course get the chance to try all of the delicious dishes that are demonstrated

Fancy some fish? Come along to this cookery class in London and learn to whip up some delicious fish dishes like a pro! Whether you're looking to expand your culinary horizons, are treating a foodie friend to a unique gift or just want to find new things to do in London, this course is quite the catch.

You will of course get the chance to try all of the delicious dishes that are demonstrated before shooting off to your station to give it a go yourself, as you prepare for the evening's two fish courses (due to the nature of the class being fish focussed, the chefs will prepare all the non-fish/seafood elements of the menu).

title: Introduction to Airbrushing Workshop
description:
Step - 1 Meet the Airbrush

Here you will be introduced to the airbrush and understand how things work and take a look inside one!




Step - 2 Learn to Mix Colour

Next you will learn how colour works with the airbrush, how to mix it and keep it flowing.




Step 3 - Start Using the Airbrush

Here you will begin to practice spraying with the airbrush, how to create lines and tones, and how to understand why things don’t always work first time. You will be introduced to some fun practice exercises to give you different ways of controlling the marks you can make.




Step 4 - Cleaning and Maintenance

Soon after you start spraying you’ll need to learn how to clean the brush and to avoid the problems that will inevitably arise.




Step 5 - Introduction to Masking

Now you have a basic understanding of how to get the airbrush to spray, its time to play with masking, where you control how and where the spray goes, and how y0u can create exact shapes and patterns.




Step 6 - Final Project

With all the skills and understanding you have gained its time to put it all together on the creation of a final project. You will be making a sunset painting which will let you test out all that you have learnt and will offer you the chance of challenging yourself at the same time! The project has been designed to work on many levels and is guaranteed to get you to reach a painting you will be happy to take home (or give to someone truly deserving as a gift!)



Ever wondered how an airbrush actually works? This hands-on airbrushing workshop in South East London is made for complete beginners – no previous experience needed – and takes you from first spray to a finished piece of your own to take home. Working with professional equipment in a relaxed, supportive setting, you'll build the fundamentals of airbrushing from scratch.
Airbrushing is a wonderfully versatile medium, used across fine art, illustration, scale modelling, custom painting and design, and this workshop gives you a solid, practical foundation in the techniques that underpin all of them.
You'll learn:
How an airbrush works
Basic trigger control
How to create dots, lines and smooth gradients
Simple masking techniques
How to build form and depth with tone
Basic cleaning and maintenance
Putting these new skills straight into practice, you'll finish the session by creating your own airbrushed artwork, complete with shading, masking and atmospheric effects.
This workshop is a warm welcome for complete beginners, curious artists, model makers and hobbyists, or anyone keen to pick up a new creative skill – all equipment and materials are provided, so just show up ready to spray.
You're in expert hands with tutor Bruce Atherton, a professional artist with more than 35 years of airbrushing experience across commercial work, fine art and specialist creative projects, and the former owner of his own professional airbrush studio. With Bruce's guidance, the focus is firmly on practical skills, creative exploration, and helping you build real confidence with this unique medium.

Understanding light, mood, and realism in photography.

title: Router 101: Skills and Safety Workshop
description:
Spend a full day mastering the trim router and the handheld router on this hands-on router skills course, built for makers ready to add a transferable skill to their toolkit.
This is a skills course rather than a single-project class, so instead of walking away with just one finished piece, you'll build real, lasting confidence with two of woodworking's most useful tools. You'll learn how each router works, when to reach for which, and how to keep things safe while still getting a clean, accurate cut – then move on to jigs, learning how to design, build, and use them to guide a router through your material with precision.
Across the day, you'll:
Understand router mechanics – how the motor, collet, and bit work together, and why feed direction is the single biggest factor in a safe, clean cut
Choose the right tool for the job – the trade-offs between a trim router, a handheld router, and a router table
Set up a router for repeatable results – dialling in material position, fence, and bit height
Read and choose router bits – straight, profile, and spiral, and how each changes your result
Get to grips with jig design – registration faces, clamping, and guide bushing offsets
Build a straight-edge guide jig from scratch – a simple, reusable jig you'll make during the session
Cut a template-guided recess – using a guide bushing and template to reproduce an identical cut safely
Bring it all together on a sample board – combining trim router, handheld, and jig-guided cuts in one piece
By the end of the day, you'll take home a shop-made straight-edge guide jig ready for your next project, plus a router skills sample board that shows off everything you've learned.

title: Sourdough Bread Class
description:
Learn the basics of sourdough fermentation and bread baking in this intro to sourdough class with a local, talented teacher from The Fermentarium.
To kick off this bread-making class, you'll learn the fundamentals of fermentation, and specifically, sourdough, interweaving these core principles with baking techniques throughout the class.
We’ll cover topics comparing sourdough to other types of fermentation, the health benefits of sourdough, the role of different ingredients in baking, and concepts like gluten development and hydration levels. Special attention will also be given to decoding different flour varieties and grains.
You'll try shaping a rye loaf which will be baked later in the class. Then we’ll make a wholewheat loaf from scratch, which we’ll shape at the end of the course so you can take and bake it at home as per our instructions. Finally, we’ll make a rye starter which you’ll also take home to be cared for and watch come to life. In addition to a fresh rye loaf, wholewheat dough, and rye starter, so please bring a tote bag to carry home your goodies!
This class is designed to provide you with the fermentation and baking skills to build your sourdough and baking intuition, so you can adapt recipes to your particular environments and flour preferences.
The class includes a selection of fermented snacks midway through.
What you'll get
A rye loaf baked in the class.
Wholewheat dough to bake at home as per our instructions.
A rye starter which you’ll also take home to be cared for and watch come to life.
A dough scraper
Detailed course notes and recipes
On going support on our dedicated Facebook support group.

title: Necklace Pendant Making Workshop
description:
In this 2.5-hour hands-on workshop, you will learn all the skills required to design and create y0ur own bespoke pendant using ancient wax carving techniques!
This workshop is a perfect opportunity to free your mind, get creative, and connect with other like-minded people whilst making a special heirloom.
We hold a lot of sentiment in the jewellery we wear. It has the power to transport us, to bring back memories of loved ones and experiences. Hand-making a special heirloom only amplifies this. You can use this time to make the perfect present for a loved one or make a special pendant to celebrate yourself.

The techniques in wax carving and what you can create in wax are endless! I will tailor a portion of the workshop to each individual's design but will also cover all the different methods and techniques used in wax carving for lost wax casting.
There will be some exciting optional upgrades available in class, including a pendant chain, gemstone setting, gold plating, or engraving to make your pendant even more special (available for pre-purchase or to add on the day).
By the end of the class, your piece will be completed, ready for casting which takes about 3 weeks.

title: 1:1 Restorative Aerial Yin Yoga Class
description:
Join this aerial yin yoga class in London and discover a nurturing space for deep restoration.
These private sessions are carefully curated to offer a collection of slow, supportive experiences that help restore your nervous system and soften your body. Rather than a continuous flow, your practice will unfold in distinct, harmonious segments – each with its own intention, rhythm, and focus to help you switch off from the outside world.
What your session includes:
Arrival and grounding – Begin seated or gently swaying in the hammock. Through breath awareness and subtle rocking, you'll allow your body to arrive fully and establish a sense of safety and support.
Lower body release – Experience supported folds and hip openers held for several minutes. The hammock carries your weight so your muscles can genuinely let go. Before movement begins, you'll connect with your current physical and emotional landscape so the practice responds to where you are today.
Spinal decompression – Enjoy gentle traction or an optional supported inversion. Slow, rhythmic movement invites your spine to lengthen and your nervous system to reset, providing a moment of total lightness without effort.
Heart and rib opening – Settle into supported backbends and side-body openings. Your breath is guided into the ribs and chest, encouraging expansion and helping you soften any protective holding patterns.
Cocoon integration – Rest in a fully wrapped savasana in the hammock. This final stage of stillness and containment supports grounding before you return to your day.
Each part of the class is intentionally portioned to balance gravity and suspension, effort and surrender. You'll finish the session feeling completely recalibrated, walking away with a profound sense of inner calm and a body that feels lighter and more spacious.

title: Signet Ring Wax Carving Workshop
description:
In this 2.5-hour hands-on workshop, you will learn all the skills required to create your perfect one-of-a-kind signet using ancient wax carving techniques! You can choose to keep the signet blank, add a fingerprint, paw print, hand engrave letters or a design yourself, or have it laser engraved professionally after casting.
This workshop is the perfect opportunity to free your mind, get creative, and connect with other like-minded people whilst making a special heirloom.
You'll be guided each step of the way by jeweller, Natasha Kutrovacz of Anonoma Jewellery. Natasha trained in NYC and creates custom jewellery for film and TV, alongside her own designs. The workshop is kept small so you will also receive 1:1 guidance on how to create your specific signet.
No need to come with an exact design in mind, the creative process will allow some time to brainstorm with inspiring materials to help you come up with your very own and unique piece of jewellery.
All materials will be provided, and no prior experience is necessary. However, if you would like to deepen your existing skill set, that is possible too. The techniques in wax carving and what you can create in wax are endless! I will tailor a portion of the workshop to each individual's design but will also cover all the different methods and techniques used in wax carving for lost wax casting.
There will be some exciting optional upgrades available in-class, including gemstone setting, gold plating, or engraving to make your ring even more special (available for pre-purchase or to add on the day).
By the end of the class, your piece will be completed, ready for casting. The casting, finishing, and polishing take about 2-3 weeks. If you have opted for gold plating, this will take an additional 5-7 working days.

title: Boob Pot Pottery Class
description:
You’ve seen them all over Instagram, now you can make your own! Join an expert teacher and a group of like-minded pottery newbies for this two-hour masterclass in making your own boob pot.
At this fun London pottery class, you’ll be shown how to work with clay, how to construct your own pot and then you'll focus on the art of adding boobs! Your pots will then be left to dry and then kiln fired.
If you'd like to paint your pot, you have a couple of options:
For a shiny, waterproof pot, you can join one of your teacher's painted ceramics sessions. Once your pot is painted, your teacher will glaze and kiln-fire it again. After this process, it will be completely waterproof – perfect for a cup, plant pot or anything else you'd like to use it for!
Alternatively, you can take your pot home and paint it with acrylic paint. If painted with acrylics, your pot will look great, but it will not be waterproof or food safe. It will still look super cute on a shelf and would work for a cactus pot!
However you decide to finish your pot off, you'll come away from this pottery workshop with a unique boob pot to use in your home or gift to a friend. If you're looking for fun things to do in London, this beginners' ceramics class is a quirky and creative activity to go for.
Join in with your friends (great fun if you're looking for birthday party ideas or hen party ideas!) or head along with family or colleagues to learn pottery making together. Alternatively, have a go solo and meet other crafty beginners in the neighbourhood.
By the end of your boob pottery class in London, you'll have your own ceramic pot to keep, a fun new experience under your belt, and some fresh pottery making skills to inspire you for future projects! You can also just play with clay if you like and build what you like with the clay provided.

title: Beginners Photography Workshop
description:
Would you like to learn how to capture the beauty of the world around you? Come along to this fun and friendly beginners photography class in London and discover how to harness the power of your camera!
Ideal for complete photography beginners, during this workshop you will learn the fundamentals and basics of photography whilst out and about with your teacher, allowing you to practise and experiment with newly learned techniques while photographing some of London’s most iconic locations.
Subjects covered:
ISO, aperture and shutter speed.
Shooting in aperture priority mode.
Shooting in manual when using a tripod.
Experimenting with panning in shutter speed priority mode.
Histogram and the importance of exposing to the right.
Tips and tricks for eye-catching compositions.
The importance of light and shooting at the best time of day.
Conveying stories in your photographs.
Focus modes and capturing sharp photos.
Metering.
Selecting the most appropriate equipment (although it is not about what equipment you have, it is how you use it!).
As well as learning the technical side of photography, you will also explore composition and the thought process behind creating (not just taking) breathtaking photos.
Typical itinerary (subject to change):
You will begin the day by meeting your teacher and group close to the London Eye. Your teacher will then give you a brief overview of the day before the group sets off to explore London with a camera in hand.
During the first half of the day, you will learn the basics of ISO, aperture, shutter speed, shooting modes and focusing all whilst exploring the stunning South Bank and London Eye area. Once you are comfortable with this, you will start to experiment with slow shutter speeds while photographing interesting subjects such as the Thames, Leake Street Graffiti Tunnels, buskers, markets and South Bank’s famous skate park.
After a short break to re-charge and fuel up, your teacher will explore with you the art of photographic storytelling, discussing tricks to create eye-catching compositions and how to make the best of whatever lighting situation you find yourself in.
As the day draws to an end, you will enjoy a sunset and blue hour/night shoot over-looking the Thames near Millennium Bridge – you're sure to go home with a selection of beautiful photographs.

title: Beginner Crochet - 3-Week Fundamentals Course
description:
Week 1 - Getting Comfortable

We'll start right at the beginning. You'll learn how to hold your hook and yarn in a way that feels comfortable for you, make your first slip knot and crochet chain, and begin making your first stitches.

This is often the trickiest part of learning to crochet, so we spend plenty of time practising together. There's no rushing and no expectation to "get it" immediately – we'll help you build confidence one stitch at a time.




Week 2 – Making Your First 3D Project

This week your crochet starts to become something! You'll learn the double crochet stitch (called single crochet in US patterns), and discover how increasing and decreasing stitches changes the shape of your work.

Using these new skills, you'll make a simple crochet bowl while learning how three-dimensional crochet is created.




Week 3 - the Famous Granny Square

Now it's time to make one of crochet's most recognisable projects. You'll learn how granny squares are constructed, how to turn neat corners, and how to change colours with confidence.

By the end of the session you'll understand how granny squares are made and have the skills to continue making them at home.



Never picked up a crochet hook before? You're in exactly the right place.
Learning to crochet can feel overwhelming when you're trying to follow YouTube videos on your own. In this three-week course, we'll guide you through everything step by step in a small group, with plenty of individual help whenever you need it.
Over the three weeks you'll learn how to hold your hook comfortably, make your first stitches, understand how crochet fabric is created, shape simple 3D projects, and finish by making the classic granny square with colour changes.
More importantly, you'll leave understanding how crochet works, so you can continue learning with confidence instead of relying on someone showing you every step.
What you'll get
6 hours of expert tuition over 3 sessions
All materials provided (hook, yarn, stitch markers, and handouts)
A granny square and amigurumi sample to take home
Printed guides for crochet charts and written patterns

title: Chisel Sharpening Course
description:
This half-day course will teach you to maintain and sharpen your woodcarving chisels and gouges and explore the different types of sharpening equipment and techniques that can be used to keep chisels razor sharp.
This course is perfect for those who have already purchased woodcarving chisels and want to gain experience in sharpening their own tools. Sharp chisels are a joy to use, easily cutting through even very hard timbers. However, without a good understanding of how to maintain a sharp edge, they can quickly become blunt and frustrating to use. In this half-day course, we will cover the different types of sharpening stones, slip stones, and strops, how to sharpen flat chisels and gouges, and the theory behind sharpening more complex shapes, such as V chisels and bent chisels.
This course is specifically designed for people who already own carving chisels and want to learn to maintain them. During the day, you will be learning how to sharpen your own chisels, so please bring a small selection with you (3-5 chisels is ideal).
Please note: chisels will not be provided for practice - you must bring your own.

Please note: Public dates for this class require at least 3 guests to run. In the unlikely event that we don't reach this number, we may cancel the session; if that happens, we'll inform you and let you choose between a refund or reschedule, so please watch your email/SMS one day prior to the class.

title: Chinese Seal Carving Workshop (篆刻)
description:
Turning Your Name Into Art

Don't worry if you're a complete beginner! Our tutor will work with you one-on-one to transform your name (in Chinese or English) into a beautiful and balanced Seal Script design.




Tracing the Design Onto the Stone

This is the key step where your idea on paper becomes a blueprint in stone. We'll show you the professional technique to accurately trace your design onto the smooth surface of the seal stone.




Bringing the Stone to Life

Now, it's your turn to take the carving tools in hand! From the very first cut to the final, clean lines, you'll experience a deep sense of focus and the pure joy of creation. Our tutor will be right there to guide you every step of the way.




Making Your First Impression

Once the final cut is made, your seal is born, carrying with it your effort and story. Now, dip it in the traditional red ink paste to make your very first, one-of-a-kind impression on paper.




An Inspiring, Intimate Workshop

Escape the everyday in our real artist's studio. We keep our workshops intimate with six or fewer guests, ensuring everyone receives personal attention.



What is Chinese Seal Carving?
Chinese Seal Carving, known as Zhuànkè (篆刻), is a traditional Chinese art form that involves carving a design into the bottom of a seal. It is a unique craft that combines the beauty of ancient Seal Script calligraphy (篆书) with the skill of sculpture.
In East Asian tradition, the ultimate way to sign your name is not with a pen, but with a personal seal.
For centuries, this one-of-a-kind, hand-carved mark has been the artist's ultimate signature. It acts as the artwork's passport—the highest proof of authenticity used to verify priceless paintings and calligraphy. A seal is so unique that its impression becomes an inseparable part of the art itself.
In this workshop, we invite you to rediscover your name in this ancient and focused way. From designing the beautiful Seal Script characters to carving the cool stone by hand, you will transform your name into something more than just a symbol. It becomes a beautiful, functional piece of art, imbued with your spirit and your time.
————————————————————————————————
In this workshop, you will:
Learn the History: Explore the deep cultural meaning of seals in Chinese tradition.
· Design Your Seal: Create a unique design with your name (in English or Chinese) or a personal symbol.
·Learn Seal Script: Grasp the basics of ancient Seal Script for a balanced composition.
·Carve on Stone: Use traditional tools to bring your design to life on a beautiful seal stone.
·Take Home Your Work: Leave with a finished, ready-to-use seal to stamp your art, letters, or books.
Perfect for beginners and anyone interested in calligraphy, design, or a unique creative experience. You'll leave with a beautiful, functional piece of art you made yourself.
Also interested in calligraphy? Check out our Calligraphy Lantern Workshop on our homepage!

title: Print Four Ways – Printmaking Taster Course (6 Weeks)
description:
Week 1 - Mixed Media Cyanotype

Cyanotype is a method of printing via exposure. Blocking out elements of pre-coated paper with elements of different opacities, you can achieve beautiful results using lots of different materials to compose an image. You'll be invited to create and expose an A6 and A3 image of your own, getting to grips with the materials. In the evening, we'll use UV light as part of the exposure process.




Week 2 - Gelli Print

Gelli printing uses blocks of latex to create mono prints, by coating the surface with thin layers of acrylic paint and using absorbent mediums or paint brushes to remove and impress images on the block. Using little plates, you'll be encourage to use the plates in different ways, creating a series of monoprints.




Week 3 - Lino Print

Lino printing is a relief method which can be used to creat striking graphic images. We'll cover the basics of carving safely and how to use the tools in a standard set, then you'll be invited to design, carve and print your own series of prints using the process.




Week 4 - Tetrapak

Tetrapak cartons can be used to create an effective intaglio-style print utilising collagraph style printing methods and a printing press. You'll be stepped through the process and the invited to design, etch and print your own series of prints with our printing press.




Week 5-6 Personal Project

Freestyle! You've learned the methods and tried the tools, now it's your chance to go back to the processes the inspired you most and give them another try with support.



Discover the joy of printmaking in this six-week guided course, meeting once a week. You’ll get a broad introduction to four different print methods, followed by the chance to create a personal project of your own.
Across the first four weeks, you’ll learn the fundamentals of:
Gelli printing for playful, colourful monoprints
Tetrapak printing, using upcycled packaging for intaglio-style prints
Lino printing for bold, graphic relief designs
Cyanotype printing, a photographic sun-printing process
In the final two weeks, you’ll be supported to design and develop your own project using any combination of the techniques you’ve learned. Whether you’d like to create a series of prints, experiment with layering methods, or refine a single approach, you’ll have access to our tools and plenty of guidance.
This course is designed to give you both structure and creative freedom — learn the essentials, then put them into practice in your own way.

What shall I wear?
Pottery making is messy - especially on the wheel. Please wear clothes that you don't mind getting dirty. If you like you can bring your own apron, however we also have some in the studio. If you can bear it, please trim your nails, otherwise long nails will get in the way and mark the clay.

description:
Learn the basics of Itajime Shibori, a Japanese resist-dyeing technique (aka a sophisticated tie dye) that transforms simple folds into bold, geometric patterns. In this hands-on 2-hour workshop, you’ll experiment with folding, clamping, and dyeing fabric using indigo dye, revealing beautiful, one-of-a-kind designs when your work is unwrapped. Perfect for beginners and curious creatives alike, this relaxed and playful session focuses on process over perfection. You’ll leave with your own indigo-dyed textile pieces, a solid basic understanding of Itajime techniques, how an indigo dye bath works, and the confidence to continue experimenting at home. No prior experience needed, just come ready to fold, dye, and get -just- a little messy.
You’ll learn how precise folding and clamping techniques create striking, repeatable patterns, then bring them to life using an indigo dye bath. This workshop demystifies the process while leaving plenty of room for creative play and experimentation.
Designed for beginners but rich enough for experienced makers, the session balances clear demonstrations with hands-on making. By the end, you’ll have a collection of unique dyed textiles and a deeper understanding of how fold, pressure, and this very particular pigment interact — plus plenty of inspiration for applying Shibori to future projects.
This is a family-friendly workshop, and beginners as well as more experienced natural dyers are welcome to join.

title: Stained Glass Painting Workshop: Create Your Own Glass Roundel
description:
Create Your Design

Choose a design that you would like to translate onto glass. Work with tracing paper to develop and refine your design, thinking about how your image can be translated into line, shape and pattern on the round glass.




Mix and Blend Your Glass Paints

Experiment with specialist glass paints to build your own custom color palette. Practice blending, layering, and creating smooth color transitions on sample pieces with expert guidance from Helen before painting your final glass roundel.




Paint Your Glass Roundel

Paint your design onto your glass roundel using fine brushes and your custom glass paints. Helen will guide you through controlling paint on smooth glass, from fine lines and intricate details to layered, expressive brushwork.




Finished Glass Roundel

Helen will kiln-fire your piece in her studio to permanently set the paints and enhance their depth and color. Complete with a pre-drilled hanging hole, your glass artwork will be ready to collect and display the following week!



Create your own glass roundel in this creative stained glass painting workshop in London! Bring an image or design you'd like to translate into glass, or create your own design during the session using tracing paper.
Never tried this craft before? No worries! You'll be guided through each stage of the process, from transferring your design and experimenting with colour to painting your roundel and preparing it for firing.
What to expect:
Create or bring an image, pattern, or drawing to turn into a stained glass painting.
Learn how to transfer your design onto glass using specialist glass paint.
Experiment with different types of line and mark-making.
Learn how to mix and blend colours directly on the glass.
Explore how different colours interact to create subtle transitions, depth, and luminosity.
Build up your design by adding colour and detail to the glass.
Prepare your finished roundel for the kiln.
Learn what happens during firing and how heat transforms the glass paint.
By the end of the workshop, you'll have created your own unique piece of hand-painted glass art from your own design. Your finished roundel will be ready for you to collect the following week after firing!

title: Wax Carving for Jewellery Making Workshop
description:
Learn wax carving for jewellery in this one-day beginner's workshop held at a dedicated studio in Camden Town, London NW1. You'll discover how to create your own unique ring or pendant design in wax, explore different wax types, and experiment with various tools and techniques. Wax carving is ideal for creating master models for casting sculptural jewellery shapes that can be difficult to make directly from metal.
This intensive one-day activity covers the key skills needed to carve your own design. You'll have the opportunity to create a ring (or pendant if preferred) and potentially make test pieces to try different ideas. The focus is on providing a thorough grounding so you can continue developing your wax carving skills independently. While simple ring designs are often the most straightforward starting point, if you have a specific, more complex design in mind, it's advisable to discuss its feasibility for a one-day introduction with the tutor beforehand.
This workshop welcomes anyone over 18, whether you are a complete beginner or already have some jewellery making or craft skills. The class size is kept small, with a maximum of 3 participants, ensuring personalised attention.
You'll leave this comprehensive session feeling knowledgeable, with your own completed wax model(s) and a solid foundation in wax carving techniques.

title: City of London Ghost Story Exploration Class
description:
Join this ghost tour in the City of London area for an experience with a difference.
This tour will guide you through some of the most historic areas of London, recounting the paranormal activities that are reported to have occurred there. But it also discusses the nature of these 'ghost stories' – what makes them so compelling, what makes them scary, and what makes them uncanny?
You will get an introduction to the ideas which have been put forward throughout the centuries about these phenomena, using concepts from such luminaries as Sigmund Freud, Henry James, and even Charles Babbage – inventor of the mechanical computer, and, perhaps surprisingly, the 'stone tapes' theory. As an exercise, at least five of the stories you hear will be made up, applying these very principles. But can you tell which of the ghost stories are real and which are fabricated by your guide?
You'll finish this thought-provoking tour not just with a new appreciation for the city's tales, but with an exercise in thinking about the nature of ghost stories generally and a new perspective on what makes them so haunting.

Please note: Public dates for this class require at least 3 guests to run. In the unlikely event that we don't reach this number, we may cancel the session; if that happens, we'll inform you and let you choose between a refund or reschedule, so please watch your email/SMS one day prior to the class.
What you'll get
A ghost tour of the City of London area, an introduction to the ideas which have been put forward throughout the centuries about these phenomena, and an exercise in thinking on the nature of ghost stories generally.

title: Punch Needle Embroidery Class
description:
Feel like getting creative? Come along and discover a new hobby at this fun and friendly punch needle class.
Punch needling is a cross between embroidery and rag rug latch hooking.
It's ideal for beginner crafters as it's an easy skill to learn – perfect if you need fun things to make and want a DIY craft to keep your hands busy at home.
In this class, you will learn how to punch needle and create two different effects at the same time with your tool. One side is flat stitches, and the other side has a loopy shaggy look. You can mix and match these effects on the same side for added dimension and texture. 
Throughout the class, you'll be encouraged to enjoy this craft as mindful meditation so that you can relax and let your worries melt away.
This punch needle class is also suitable for all ages – you can easily do it with children as the tool is not too sharp and it's a wonderful craft for children to take part in. 
By the end of this craft class, you'll have a beautiful punch needle creation to call your own!

title: Fire and Breath Bowl Making Experience
description:
In this captivating workshop, you'll be delving into the mesmerising art of fire-making at The Clearing. No prior experience necessary. You'll journey through the fundamentals of fire safety, the intricacies of using ferro rods and tinder, creating char cloth, mastering flint and steel, and the challenge of lighting wet wood fires. Not to mention the fascinating process of making charcoal in a fire, as well as carving with fire to make fire breath bowls. Don't worry if you're new to this – we'll guide you through every step, ensuring a safe and enriching experience.
You'll work with a variety of materials, all provided for you, creating a take home craft by the end. Exploring the creation of fire bowls, you will be using small pieces of seasoned wood and manipulating embers on the wood to create a bowl. These are formed using your breath and the wind. This process is a beautiful, meditative experience that helps embed the fire making knowledge.
Immerse yourself in our magical outdoor learning space, The Clearing, nestled in the ancient woodland of Lesnes Abbey Woods in South East London. Embrace the transformative nature of this workshop as you learn new skills and techniques. And best of all, you'll leave with your own handmade creations to treasure. Remember to dress warmly for this outdoor adventure!
This is a beginner-friendly introduction workshop, you’ll get a knowledge and experience around open fires, plus take home some willow charcoal and char cloth.
Please wear weather appropriate clothing, bring a packed lunch and something to share if you’d like to. We all love biscuits! We will have warm tea available.
This workshop is suitable for adults and children 8 years and older. An adult must accompany an attending child and pay for a separate ticket.

title: Silver Jewellery Casting Workshop
description:
Join this silversmithing class in London where you will learn various techniques for melting and casting with silver to create your own unique jewellery. Ideal for those with some jewellery (metal working) experience.
This (and all my courses) is designed for adults. I do not currently offer classes for children and teenagers.
During this fun and creative day out, you will have the opportunity to play with fire and explore different ways of melting and casting silver. We will cover sand (delft clay) casting, and water (drop) casting, allowing you to create a diverse range of shapes and forms. Once you've experimented with these techniques, you will have the chance to transform your favourite shapes into wearable solid silver jewellery.
You can expect to create either a series of test pieces or one or more completed pieces. We will be creating abstract, organic forms with the water / drop casting, or replicating pre-prepared forms using the sand casting process - the most successful forms for this are chunky rings, medallions and relatively simple forms - you will have a selection of shapes to choose from on the day.
This class does not include wax carving or creating your own unique master model for the sand casting - that is a separate class / technique - for the sand casting, you will be able to choose from a wide range of pre-made rings, shells and other shapes and forms to cast from.
Throughout the class, your experienced instructor will guide you through the process and provide all the necessary materials. You can expect a supportive and uplifting atmosphere where you can freely explore your creativity.
By the end of the workshop, you will leave with your own stunning piece of solid silver jewellery, made entirely by you. So why not join us for this exciting silversmithing class in London and discover the joy of creating your own beautiful jewellery through the art of melting and casting with silver.
Please note that the workshop is located down stairs and metal working can be fairly physical, so it may not be suitable for individuals with mobility or dexterity issues – we apologise for any inconvenience.

description:

title: Chinese Calligraphy and Lantern Making Workshop
description:
Merge the ancient art of Chinese calligraphy with the timeless craft of lantern making in this unique, hands-on workshop.
With step-by-step guidance from your tutor, you'll learn how to use traditional Chinese brushes to write Chinese characters and gain insight into the history and beauty of this ancient art form.
For beginners, we usually teach the character Fu (福), one of the most beloved Chinese characters, meaning good fortune, blessings, and happiness. Its balanced structure makes it ideal for first-time calligraphy learners while introducing essential brush techniques.
If you'd like an extra challenge, you're welcome to try our pre-selected classical Chinese poems. Please note that these options are significantly more difficult and may require additional guidance during the workshop.
Afterwards, you'll assemble your very own traditional Chinese lantern and decorate it with your newly learned calligraphy. (Bonus: it lights up!) Whether it's a meaningful gift or a unique decoration for your home, you'll leave with a beautiful handmade lantern full of personal significance.
If you'd like to write a custom phrase or have a specific theme in mind, please contact us before the workshop so we can prepare suitable reference materials for you.

title: Cultured Condiments Making Class
description:
Give your condiment an extra kick with cultures and fermentation. In this cultured condiments class with local experts at The Fermentarium, you will learn all about fermentation and its health benefits, distinguishing fermentation from other methods of preservation like pickling or canning, and the main principles behind safe fermentation from start to finish.
This is the perfect gift experience for any foodie out there who wants to take their dishes to the next level or fermentation fans on the hunt for fun things to do in London.
We’ll start by laying out the main fermentation technique which will serve as a base for our recipes before diving into production. In this class, you'll make fermented ketchup, fermented Mexican salsa, and a fermented Caribbean chutney for you to take home and ferment according to our specific instructions. We’ll also discuss other recipes such as fermented sriracha, probiotic mayonnaise, fermented mustard, salad dressing, and much more.
Throughout the class, we’ll suggest all sorts of ingredient substitutions and recipe variations to encourage you to get creative with your ferments based on what you have at home, as well as how to use them in dishes. The course includes a variety of fermented snacks for you to have a point of reference for the recipes we’ll be sharing with you.
Suitable for both newcomers to fermentation and experienced fermenters looking to try out new recipes.
We kindly ask participants to bring 2 glass jars and a carrier bag or other suitable bag (Kilner or Fido type jars are best but you can use any jar), as this helps us to keep the cost of the course down and encourages the re-use of old jars. We will be making 300-400g recipes but you need to leave some head space between the jar contents and the lid, but not bigger than 500ml. Also you will probably want to use the jars after the initial batch to make your own ferments at home so you may want to buy jars big enough to suit you and your family needs. It is always better to have a jar that is too big rather than too small.
What you'll get
Two condiments to ferment at home.
Course notes including additional recipes to try.
On-going support through our dedicated Facebook support group

title: Beginner Joinery Workshop: Frame Joints (2-Day Course)
description:
This is where your woodworking journey gets serious. Over two full days at POW Workshops in London, you'll learn the core joints used in tables, chairs, frames, and carpentry structures of all kinds. The same joints that have been the backbone of furniture making for centuries.
No experience needed. You'll start from the basics of measuring and marking, and by the end of the weekend you'll be cutting mortice and tenon joints, the single most important joint in woodworking. Along the way, you'll develop your sawing, chiselling, and marking skills to a level where you can execute joints with real precision. You'll put it all together by building a trivet that incorporates the joints you've learned.
Here's what you'll cover:
Halving joints (half-lap joints): the foundation, and a joint you'll use again and again
Bridle joints: an elegant frame joint used in table and chair construction
Mortice and tenon joints: the single most important joint in furniture making
Tool sharpening, learning to maintain a sharp edge on your chisels and plane irons
Precision marking and layout, the skills that separate good work from rough work
Posture and body mechanics: how balance and positioning give you more control than brute force
This course is modelled on the structured approach used by London's best furniture-making schools, adapted for a weekend format so you don't need to take time off work. With a maximum of 8 people per class, you'll have plenty of time with your instructor.
Whether you're a complete beginner or you've done our Joinery Taster and want to go deeper, this course is for you. If you've already got some experience with hand tools, you'll find the structured approach fills in the gaps and sharpens your technique.
What you'll get
A completed trivet built with joints you've cut yourself, plus the core skills to take on Intermediate Joinery Workshop: Dovetail Joints and more ambitious woodworking projects. All tools and materials are provided.
What's next?
Intermediate Joinery Workshop: Dovetail Joints. You'll learn the joint that every woodworker wants to master: through dovetails, half-lap dovetails, and mitred dovetails. Together with Joinery 1, these two courses give you the complete foundation for furniture making.
Build a Stool: Using the theory of mortice and tenon joinery you've learnt in the Frame course, you will learn how wedges make the joint incredibly strong and why they are often used in chair construction. You will leave the course with a three-legged stool crafted from English Ash: the classic chair-making timber.

title: Basic Tiling DIY Workshop
description:
If you're facing down a home DIY job in the kitchen or bathroom and you want to learn some skills from the experts, join The Great British Woodshop for an introductory class to uncover the mysteries of tiling.
Learn basic skills including setting out tiling work, different adhesives, tools, cutting tiles, tiling around difficult areas etc.
As they say, it’s all in the prep, in this case, prep is not just getting your tools ready. If your walls or floor are not square or level then laying your tiles requires much more thought. Cutting the tile is the easy part and mixing the adhesive or grout is no more difficult than baking a cake.
Adding trim to tile edges, creating tile joints with symmetry to the surroundings and making sure all your tiles are level with each other make the difference between a botched job and one you are proud to show off.
This is a skills-based class where students cut tiles and learn cutting equipment and techniques. We do not mix adhesive and lay any tiles in this class.
Learn the basics such as:
Preparing the room for tiling
Laying out your tiles and working out how many you need
Levelling the floor
How to cope with tiling difficult areas such as uneven walls
Explaining adhesives used for different surfaces
Demonstrating and examining all the tools required
Cut in straight & curved lines, notching, removing the centre of a tile
Explaining tiling involving Borders, Diamonds, and Patterns
Spacers and Wedges
The use of edge trim around sills and corners
How to cut around windows and reveals
How to tile around sockets and switches
How to tile splash-backs
How to tile around pipes, showers, cabinets etc.
Please Note: Minimum of 3 bookings for this course to run.

title: Itajime Shibori with Botanical Dyes Workshop
description:
Shibori (しぼり/絞り) (from the verb root "shiboru" – "to wring, squeeze or press") is a Japanese manual resist dyeing technique that produces a number of different repetitive patterns on fabric. In this session, we will learn about Itajime Shibori exploring different ways of tying, pinching, and folding fabrics to get a range of exciting geometric patterns.
We will also learn how to extract pigments from food and garden waste by making a dye bath to dye our shiboris in them.
I will be showing some samples, giving some natural dye and shibori tips, and sharing some basic - and not so much! - information regarding natural dyes, including how to prepare fabrics for dyeing and what fibres best take natural pigments.
This is a family-friendly workshop, and beginners as well as more experienced natural dyers are welcome to join.
Experience creative wellbeing through hands-on making and sensory engagement with natural materials
Strengthen collaboration and connection through shared creative exploration
Develop awareness of sustainable materials and textile reuse

Leave with handmade textile pieces and inspiration for sustainable creative practices

title: Shibori - Stitch Resist Indigo Dye Workshop
description:
In this hands-on shibori dyeing workshop, you'll learn the ancient art of Bai shibori indigo dyeing, mastering four distinctive stitching techniques to create your own beautifully patterned scarf or bag. You'll develop skills in this traditional resist-dyeing craft that dates back over 1000 years in Southwestern China.
Curious about working with traditional dyeing methods? This activity welcomes beginners while honoring the rich cultural heritage of the Bai ethnic minority. The step-by-step approach ensures everyone creates something beautiful regardless of prior experience.
Throughout this one-day session, you'll begin by exploring the fascinating cultural history of Bai shibori and its connection to indigo dyeing traditions. After gaining this contextual understanding, you'll learn four different shibori stitching techniques that create distinctive patterns when the fabric is dyed. Drawing inspiration from the natural world around you, you'll apply these techniques to create your own unique design. The magical transformation that occurs when the bound fabric enters the indigo vat creates a memorable and almost magical experience.
By the end of this how-to workshop, you'll connect with an ancient textile tradition while creating something both beautiful and functional.

title: Introduction to Hand Building Clay Class
description:
Welcome to My Studio

We will be working in my lovely pottery studio with studio grade materials and tools. You will have your own work bench, plenty or room and be able to understand how your work fits within the overall ceramic process, see the glazes, kiln, references and tools.




There Will Be Demonstrations and Follow Along

I’ll explain the projects and show samples. You may have ideas of how you’d like to approach each one and we can discuss any additional tools I might find for you. They’ll be a demonstration of even rolling, shaping, and cutting before I guide you whilst you prepare your own clay.




Learning Cutting, Joins and Construction

We’ll make the small dish first and then the mug. You’ll look through the stamps [there are masses] to find your own style. Bring your own if you like!




Fast Marks on Your Plate

We’ll move to a different way of using slabs, as a pre-dried surface [plate] that can be scratched with the traditional sgraffito technique. We’ll discuss the best techniques for achieving strong positive and negatives in a rotational design.




Collect Fully Glazed Work After Four Weeks

No additional charge, this is included. Your beautiful work will be ready to use or gift. Collect from my studio or one of my markets.



Arrange your own small group of up to 4 people, and confirm a date and a time that suits. An ideal activity for couples or friends.
Come to my cosy and easily accessed studio and learn hand-building slab techniques for clay with plenty of space while building your own mug, dish, and plate.
Working with studio-grade stoneware, I promise your finished work will be satisfying and functional (as well as highly original) and food and dishwasher safe. I’ll explain the nature of clay as a material and how we work harmoniously with elements of shrinkage, clay memory, and moisture to construct with strength and durability. I’ll draw attention to the well-being benefits of using smooth, repetitive movements with this earthy and calming material.
Learn slab rolling, and create accurate cutting and strong mitred joins. We’ll explore how to harness stamping with an effective release agent as a decorative technique. No difficult blankness here; I will have loads of stamps, rollers, and letters to choose from to make your work really personal. Suitable for all levels of experience.
When you have completed your dish and mug, we will end with moving to a black stoneware plate, already made and prepared with white slip ready for the application of one of the most satisfying decorative techniques: sgraffito. This involves scratching through the top white layer to create black line work as the clay beneath is revealed. I’ll give an idea of how best to construct your design and encourage speedy, spontaneous mark-making; this is the time to let loose and create quick, fun images.
Collect your fired and glazed work around four weeks later (firing and glazing are included in the price).

title: Children's Splatter Painting Class
description:
Children’s Splatter Painting Experience
Big Colour. Brilliant Mess. Their Own Artwork to Keep.
Give your child the freedom to splash, drip, flick and throw paint inside a real working artist’s studio—without having to clean up the mess at home.
During this energetic one-hour experience, children create their own colourful splatter painting on a 30 × 40 cm stretched canvas. A DBS-checked practising professional artist will help them choose a personalised colour palette, demonstrate exciting techniques and guide them as they turn every splash into an artwork they’ll be proud of.
No previous art experience is needed. Children can simply enjoy experimenting, expressing themselves and seeing their ideas come to life.
£39 per child
One-hour artist-led experience
Suitable for ages 7–16
Small, supervised groups
All materials and protective equipment included
Spaces are limited to keep the experience comfortable, supportive and enjoyable for every child.
Why Children Love It
This isn’t an ordinary sit-down painting class. Children are encouraged to move, experiment and enjoy the excitement of creating with paint.
They can:
Choose colours that reflect their personality
Try pouring, dripping, flicking and splashing techniques
Build layers, patterns and bold colour combinations
Create freely with guidance available whenever they need it
Take home an original artwork made entirely by them
It’s colourful, energetic and wonderfully messy—but still carefully supervised from beginning to end.
Why Parents Love It
Your child enjoys the kind of creative mess you probably don’t want happening in your living room, while we provide the materials, guidance, protective clothing and clean-up.
The experience is ideal for:
A memorable weekend treat
School holiday activities
Creative birthday gifts
Siblings or friends attending together
Children who love art and trying something different
Young people who enjoy active, hands-on activities
Parents looking for a supervised drop-off activity in Wimbledon
They leave with more than a painting: they gain a sense of achievement from creating something completely their own.
Everything Is Included
All they need to bring is their imagination—and clothes that can handle the occasional colourful splash.
What Happens During the Experience?
1. Get Ready
Children are welcomed into the studio and helped into their protective clothing and safety equipment.
2. Choose Their Colours
The artist helps each child create a personalised palette using colours they genuinely love.
3. Learn the Techniques
Children are shown how to pour, drip, flick, splash and layer paint to create different marks and effects.
4.Create Their Artwork
It’s time to experiment. Children create their own individual painting while the artist offers encouragement and guidance throughout.
5. Admire the Finished Piece
At the end, there is time to look at their creation and take photographs before the painting is left to dry.
A Supervised Drop-Off Experience
This is a children-only class, so parents do not need to remain in the studio.
You may relax in our communal waiting area or leave and return at collection time. Please make sure we have your correct contact details before the experience begins.
If you would like to paint alongside your child, please choose one of our Private or our 1-hour splatter Experience instead.
What Should My Child Wear?
We provide protective overalls, gloves, shoe covers and safety glasses.
Splatter painting is naturally messy, so children should arrive in comfortable older clothes and shoes. Small amounts of paint may occasionally reach clothing or personal belongings.
Taking the Artwork Home
Splatter paintings normally need approximately three days to dry fully.
You can:
Collect the artwork from the studio once it is dry after 3 days
Arrange your own courier
Ask us about delivery
Purchase a £5 takeaway box and take the canvas home on the day
Artwork must be collected within 14 days of the experience.

Paperdoll Art Studio
Wimbledon Art Studios
10 Riverside Yard
London SW17 0BB
Parking
Free on-site parking is available when your vehicle registration is entered during checkout. For weekend experiences, parking must be registered in advance because the Wimbledon Art Studios office is closed at weekends.
After passing through the black gate, turn left and wait by the yellow studio entrance. Your artist will meet you there shortly before the class begins.
Arrival Information
Please arrive 10 minutes before the scheduled start time. This gives us enough time to complete the required forms and help your child put on their protective equipment.
Classes begin promptly. Children arriving 10 minutes or more after the start time may not be admitted, as late entry can disrupt the experience for the rest of the group.
Ready for a Colourful Adventure?
Treat your child to an exciting creative experience where making a mess is encouraged—and leave the cleaning to us.
They’ll have a brilliant time experimenting with colour and create an original painting they’ll be excited to show everyone.
Book your child’s place today. Small-group spaces are limited.

description:

You’ll also explore colour theory and painting techniques, learning to mix realistic colours and use expressive brushwork.

Discover the art of observation, learning to see and capture every detail of your subject.
Harness the power of light and shadow, transforming flat objects into three-dimensional works of art.
Refine skills in composition, arranging objects thoughtfully to create harmonious and engaging still life scenes.
Experiment with different mediums, from graphite to charcoal to watercolour, finding the perfect tools to bring your vision to life.
Develop a personal artistic voice, learning how to inject emotion and storytelling into every still life you create.
Complete a beautiful final painting, showcasing your growth and mastery of the still life art form.

By the end of the class, you’ll have completed a beautiful final painting, showcasing your new skills and unique style. You’ll leave with a newfound appreciation for the beauty of everyday objects, and the skills to transform them into captivating works of art in a single session.

title: Enamel Jewellery Workshop
description:
A Colourful Welcome

Step into our welcoming London studio and discover the enchanting art of enamelling. You’ll be greeted by trays of jewel-like colours and introduced to this historic craft, ready to create your own vibrant, wearable masterpiece from scratch.




Choose Your Design

This is where your unique design begins. Select your favourite shape from over 40 beautiful fine silver blanks, from classic circles to intricate patterns. With friendly one-on-one guidance, you’ll sketch your ideas and prepare your silver for a perfect finish.




Paint with Powder

Experience the most magical part of the process – applying the enamel. You’ll learn how to handle the fine, colourful powder, carefully layering and blending shades to bring your unique design to life. It's a wonderfully mindful and creative technique, perfect for beginners.




Transform in the Kiln

Watch in amazement as your piece goes into the kiln. In a matter of moments, the heat works its magic, fusing the powder into a smooth, glossy, and durable glass surface. It’s an exciting reveal that never fails to delight.




Enjoy Your Vibrant Creation

Give your new treasure a final polish to make the colours pop and the silver shine. You'll leave the workshop wearing a stunning piece of enamel jewellery that is completely unique to you – a beautiful testament to your newfound silversmithing skills.



Learning the stunning art of enamel jewellery making with zero experience at this exciting Enamel Jewellery Workshop in London. Discover the historical significance of enamel jewellery and gain practical knowledge of various enamel techniques and styles like cloisonné and plique-à-jour. In this hands-on workshop, you will immerse yourself in the process of creating unique enamel jewellery pieces using fine silver blanks and a range of tools and materials.
During the workshop, you will have the opportunity to choose from 40 different designs of blanks and learn how to file them to perfection. Design and sketch your ideas before getting one-on-one guidance from experienced instructors. They will demonstrate the proper application of enamel powder and guide you in colour blending, layering, and achieving desired effects. With personalized assistance, explore design concepts and bring your unique enamel jewellery project to life.
Once you have created your masterpiece, it will be baked to perfection for durability. Then, learn the finishing techniques to enhance and polish your enamel jewellery, ensuring its timeless beauty. Demonstrations on cleaning and adding final touches will leave you with a finished piece that you can proudly wear or gift.

title: Nigerian Street Food Cookery Class
description:
Toast and Grind Your Own Yaji Spice Blend

Discover the aromatic spices that give Nigerian street food its distinctive flavour, then create your own spice mix.




Master the Art of Suya

Learn to skewer and grill thin cut beef like a suya masters in Nigeria. Plenty of help will be on hand if you need it!




Get Hands-On with Fermentation

Work with tangy fermented rice batter to create sinasir, traditional Northern Nigerian pancakes with a unique sour flavour.




Caramelise Onions and Mash Beans to Perfection

Create a Crunchy Cassava Salad

Take a Seat at the Table

Fiery, smoky, and bursting with spice, Nigerian street food is a feast for the senses and one of Africa's best-kept culinary secrets. Transport yourself to the vibrant streets of Lagos, Kano, and Enugu by getting to grips with four Nigerian dishes in this class. From grinding aromatic spice blends to mastering the art of caramelisation and fermentation, you'll gain hands-on skills and cultural insight whilst learning how to make traditional recipes in a modern kitchen.
This class is welcoming and suitable for all skill levels. You don't need experience with Nigerian cooking; everything is explained step by step, with plenty of guidance, storytelling, and practical tips along the way. You'll leave with the skills to recreate a complete traditional breakfast at home, plus tips on ingredient sourcing and storage.
What to expect:
Learning about Nigerian street food culture and the hot spots in Nigeria.
Smoky beef suya – thinly sliced, heavily spiced, and grilled.
Sinasir – tangy fermented rice pancakes.
Ewa agoyin – rich mashed beans with caramelised pepper sauce.
Abacha salad – cassava salad with red palm oil dressing, smoked fish (or smoked mushrooms), and fresh herbs.

Water and tea are available throughout the class.

title: Collage Workshop in an Artist's Studio
description:
Discover Collage

You’ll be introduced to a short history of collage as a form of expression. Discover how 19th-century English women used collage albums to gossip, joke, and imagine other lives; how Surrealist artists used collage to make familiar things appear strange; and how collage can be used to transform images, explore identities, communicate ideas, and excite the senses.




Gather Inspiration

Look at a few examples of collage approaches, from playful combinations to more thoughtful image disruptions, to spark ideas for your own work. This draws on my 25 years as an artist and university teacher, but designed to be relaxed, hands-on, and suitable for complete beginners.




Cut, Collect, and Compose

Using magazines, printed images, coloured papers, and found materials, you’ll begin selecting, cutting, tearing, and collecting fragments that catch your attention. You’ll experiment with combining images in unexpected ways, discovering how collage can transform familiar pictures into something playful, surreal, poetic, abstract, or entirely new.




Arrange and Reimagine

As your collage develops, you’ll play with layering, scale, and unexpected image combinations to create something entirely your own. Often the most exciting moments happen through experimentation — when unrelated fragments suddenly connect and a new image or story begins to emerge.




Refine, Glue, and Take Home Your Collages

You’ll have time to make final adjustments, glue your works into place, and continue exploring different compositions. At the end of the workshop, you’ll leave with collages to take home, along with new ideas for working creatively with images, materials, and visual storytelling.



Join this collage workshop in East London and step into an inspiring artist's studio for a relaxed, hands-on morning of visual storytelling. It's a completely low-pressure environment where you'll discover the rich history of collage as an expressive art form. You'll explore how 19th-century English women used collage albums to share gossip, trade jokes, and imagine other lives, as well as how Surrealist artists used the medium to make the familiar look beautifully strange. Guided by a local artist with 25 years experience and 10+ years of teaching fine art the university level, you'll view captivating examples of collage approaches – from playful combinations to thoughtful image disruptions – to spark ideas and ease any creative anxiety before you begin.
Using a hand-picked array of magazines, printed images, coloured papers, and interesting found materials, you'll learn how to select, cut, tear, and collect fragments that catch your attention. This casual, friendly session encourages pure experimentation, meaning there's absolutely no need for prior skills or a background in drawing. As your piece develops, you'll play with layering, scale, and unexpected image combinations to craft a composition that is entirely your own. Your teacher will show you how unrelated fragments can suddenly connect to tell a brand-new story. You'll have plenty of time to refine your layout, make final adjustments, and securely glue your pieces into place.
This revitalising workshop is a fantastic way to switch off from screen time, slow down, and enjoy a mindful break in a welcoming social setting. Whether you come along with your friends for a feel-good catch-up or arrive on your own to connect with a warm community of makers, you'll pick up new ideas for working creatively with imagery. You'll leave the studio feeling deeply inspired, carrying a collection of personal, story-rich keepsakes that are ready to show off at home.

Expert, step-by-step guidance from a local studio artist.
Inspiring examples and reference materials to guide your ideas.

Each session brings new surprises and designs, making every workshop a unique cultural experience.
