title: Thai Cookery Class
description:
Explore Thai cuisine and add some authentic Thai recipes to your repertoire as you learn to cook with chef Yui at this deliciously creative cooking class in London.
Your chef teacher Yui comes from a Thai-Chinese family where cooking and eating have always been a focal point of family life. From a young age, Yui found her passion for cooking from her family with traditional Thai recipes passed on from her Grandmother.
Yui moved to the UK in 2001, where she began to learn to cook more Western food, adding her own Asian twist to classic recipes. In recent years, Yui has showcased her passion for authentic Asian cuisine on BBC’s MasterChef UK 2019 as a quarter-finalist and Channel 4’s Beat the Chef.
At this Thai cooking class, you'll learn to cook:
Thai Spring Rolls
Som Tam Salad
Thai green chicken curry - an authentic, spicy curry paste cooked with chicken and simmered in coconut milk, seasoned with palm sugar and fish sauce.
Thai Sticky Glutinous Rice
As part of your class, you'll learn the basics of cutting, slicing and chopping using a Chinese cleaver. You’ll also be taught how to fill, fold and season your pork dumplings to make them extra delicious.
With chef Yui as your guide, you'll gain the basics of Thai seasoning with herbs and spices and you'll learn what kind of seasoning to use to make delicious Thai dishes independently.
By the end of your cooking class, you'll have a selection of tasty Thai dishes to enjoy. Sit down with your fellow chefs and enjoy your meal!
Please note:
The menu for this class contains allergens such as nuts, shellfish, gluten and egg. Your teacher can cater for those who have allergens by providing alternative recipes or ingredients. Please contact your teacher at the time of booking to let them know. Halal alternatives are available where possible - please let your teacher know if you'd like to request this.

title: Woodworking Class: Router
description:
Learn how to use a woodworking router with confidence during this one-day intensive class. You'll cover all the important and useful capabilities of this versatile woodworking tool!
Guided by expert craftsman David, this class will cover the basics, accessories, bits and tables of a woodworking router. Router basics:
Features of the router.
Depth setting and adjustments.
Shank sizes and inserts.
Speed control and why you need it.
Router direction and safety.
Router joinery.
Dust extraction.
Looking after your router and cutters.
Router accessories:
The fence and how to use it.
Router bases.
Collars and bushes.
Collet extensions and sleeves.
Plates and trammels.
Making jigs and jig accessories.
Straight edge guides.

Straight cutting bits.
Profiling bits.
Bearing guided cutters.
Speciality bits.

Safe working practices particular to tables.
Mounting the router on a table.
Mounting plates, fences and mitre slots.

title: Nigerian Cookery Class: Iyan and Efo Elegusi
description:
Discover Specialist Ingredients

From the ingredients responsible for Nigerians signature umami taste to the cuisine's spicy reputation, you'll connect with authentic Nigerian ingredients and learn how to use traditional Nigerian cooking tools!




Cook the Perfect Efo Elegusi

Learn how to work with melon gourd seeds and transform them into a stew that's both comforting and protein-rich then work with spinach leaves and learn the best way to maintain the vibrant green leaves.




Master the Art of Iyan

Learn the technique of pounding fresh yam, working quickly to achieve that signature smooth, stretchy texture without lumps.




Balance the Duo

Understand how iyan and efo elegusi complement each other and learn the traditional way of serving them together on one plate.




Take a Seat at the Table

Enjoy your feast served in the traditional style with cookbook author Lopè Ariyo.



Smootħ and pillowy soft pounded yam served with efo elegusi is the ultimate Nigerian comfort food. It's the dish that is supposedly responsible for giving Nigerians the highest twin rate in the world! In this immersive class, you'll learn to make the perfect pounded yam (iyan) alongside the classic stew, efo elegusi, discovering the techniques that transform simple ingredients into a harmonious feast.
This class is welcoming and suitable for all skill levels. You don’t need experience with Nigerian cooking, everything is explained step by step, with plenty of guidance, storytelling, and practical tips along the way. You’ll gain both confidence in the techniques and a deeper understanding of the food’s cultural significance.
What to expect:
Learning what iyan is and how to prepare it in its different forms.
Making a traditional soups:
Efo elegusi – nutty egusi seed soup decorated with vibrant spinach
Enjoying complimentary soft drinks:
Zobo (hibiscus, ginger, pineapple)

By the end of the session, you’ll leave with practical skills, cultural insight, and the confidence to recreate this comforting Nigerian classic at home. More than just a cooking class, it’s a chance to connect with food, tradition, and flavour and to enjoy a generous, nourishing meal made by your own hands!

title: Wooden Jewellery Workshop with Silver and Pearls
description:
This workshop explores how to use wood to create contemporary jewellery designs. You will learn how to decorate wood with silver pique dots and pearls, creating unique jewellery with your own decorative design. You will also discover techniques to incorporate wood into your work using standard jewellery hand tools, without requiring extensive specialised equipment. Guidance on sustainability and material sourcing, as well as innovative uses of wood by designers, will also be covered. Handouts will be provided, and you will have the opportunity to purchase Sarah’s book, Creating Jewellery in Wood.
You will create either two wooden pendants or a pair of earrings, decorated with silver pique dots and pearls to your own design. These intricate details will showcase the techniques you’ll learn during the workshop, resulting in stunning, personalised creations.
The day will begin with an introduction to working with wood in jewellery design, including a look at the tools and techniques required. You’ll learn how to adapt standard jewellery hand tools for use with wood, making this approach accessible even if you don’t have a fully equipped workshop. The instructor will demonstrate the process of inlaying silver pique dots into wood, guiding you step by step so you can practise this method on your own pieces.
In the next stage, you will explore techniques for attaching pearls to wood, adding an elegant touch to your designs. Alongside this hands-on work, there will be discussions on sustainability, covering how to source wood responsibly and choose materials that align with your values. You’ll explore a range of cold connection techniques to create completed jewellery pieces, as well as gain knowledge about different types of wood and their suitability for various designs.
Throughout the workshop, you’ll receive individual guidance to develop your own jewellery designs. By the end of the day, you’ll leave with completed pendants or other jewellery pieces that reflect your personal style and newly acquired skills. To support your learning, you’ll receive handouts summarising the techniques covered and additional resources for further exploration. There will also be an opportunity to purchase Sarah’s book, Creating Jewellery in Wood, as a valuable reference for future projects.

title: 8 Week Pottery Course
description:
Situated just a short stroll from Nine Elms (6 mins), Stockwell (10 mins), and Vauxhall (15 mins) stations, our cozy pottery studio is right where the creative magic happens!
Discover the joy of working with clay in our hands-on, 8-week comprehensive ceramic course! Designed for complete beginners as well as those looking to refine their foundational skills, this programme covers the full lifecycle of pottery-making, starting with the tactile art of handbuilding and moving into wheel throwing.
Course Highlights
Handbuilding Techniques: Explore pinch pots, coil construction, and slab building to create unique, sculptural pieces.
Wheel Throwing Mastery: Learn the fundamentals of centring, opening, pulling walls, and shaping cylinders on the potter's wheel.
Trimming and Finishing: Master the art of refining your pieces, adding handles, and carving textures once the clay reaches the leather-hard stage.
Glazing and Surface Design: Experiment with various glazing techniques, dipping, brushing, and texture applications to bring your pieces to life.
Firing Processes: Gain an understanding of how kilns work, including bisqueware and glazeware firings.
Weekly Breakdown
Week 1: Introduction to clay, wedge preparation, and mastering pinch pots to understand clay behaviour.
Week 2: Handbuilding basics—expanding your skills using the coil and slab methods.
Week 3: Introduction to basic wheel-throwing (centring, opening, and pulling your first walls).
Week 4: Refining cylinders and practising consistency on the wheel.
Week 5: Trimming bottoms, refining shapes, and adding handles or custom details to leather-hard pieces.
Week 6: Finishing up foundational projects and preparing pieces for the bisque firing.
Week 7: Introduction to glazes, colour theory, and testing surface decoration techniques on test tiles.
Week 8: Glazing bisqued pieces using dipping, pouring, and layering methods, followed by final loading for the glaze firing.
What you'll get
Access to studio pottery wheel, work tables, and professional tools
All necessary clay (up to a specified weight limit per student)
A curated selection of studio glazes
Bisque and glaze firings for your finished pieces

You'll explore simple and spontaneous brushstrokes to bring your paintings to life in a beautiful and expressive way and attempt some Chinese calligraphy.
By the end of the workshop, you'll have not only learned new techniques in Chinese Brush Painting but also created your own masterpiece to cherish. Join this activity for a fun and enriching experience in the world of art!
About The Tutor – Angela Reich
I love Chinese Brush Painting! I paint in both the freehand and meticulous styles, and also practise Chinese calligraphy. The freehand style is simple and spontaneous, using only a few brush strokes to evoke the subject, or the season. The meticulous court style is elegant and realistic, using subtle washes.
I have studied Chinese Brush Painting (CBP) for over 30 years, learning from many Chinese artists in the UK and in China, visiting China several times to sketch the landscape and flowers.
I love sharing my enthusiasm for this unique art form. I teach individuals and groups at my home studio in Surrey and also give workshops to various CBP groups.
I am Chair of the Chinese Brush Painting Society, the UK national network for this fascinating art.

title: Chanhua Workshop
description:
Join us for a fascinating paper craft and ink class in London where you will delve into the intricate art of Chánhuā. Discover the traditional techniques of making artificial flowers using silk thread, cardboard, and metal wire. In this workshop, you will learn how to design the shape and colour of a beautiful flower blossom brooch to take home.
Chánhuā, also known as "Twining Flower, " is a traditional craft of making artificial flowers using materials such as silk thread, cardboard, and metal wire. It is mainly popular in regions like Taiwan and Fujian, and there are similar intangible cultural heritage projects in Hubei as well. Traditional chánhuā is often used for ancestral worship, weddings, and home decorations, with different patterns and styles reflecting local customs and traditions. Today, chánhuā is experiencing a revitalisation with efforts from various parties. It is a suitable choice for handicraft enthusiasts who want to explore the world of traditional flower making, although mastering the technique can be challenging. Learning chánhuā allows one to appreciate the beauty of handicraft art and experience the charm of traditional culture. By preserving and developing the skill of chánhuā, we can protect and pass down this essential intangible cultural heritage, while also contributing to creating unique artistic pieces.
Here's what to expect in the workshop:
Learn about the background and development of Chánhuā.
Explore the different materials and tools used in traditional flower making.
Receive a DIY kit for £20 to enhance your hands-on experience.
Immerse yourself in the world of handicraft art and traditional culture as you craft your unique Chánhuā creation. By the end of the workshop, you'll not only have a beautiful flower blossom brooch to cherish but also a newfound appreciation for this essential intangible cultural heritage.
What you'll get
All materials and tools to make a gorgeous Chánhuā brooch to take home with you.

title: Cloisonné Enamel Jewellery Workshop
description:
In this class you will learn how to use vitreous enamelling techniques and cloisonné wires to create a unique, colourful silver pendant. Cloisonné is a technique which is effective for a wide variety of designs ranging from simple to intricate, and therefore this workshop is suitable for all levels and experiences.
What will I make?
You will make a sterling silver cloisonné enamel pendant.
What will happen on the day?
In this class you will be guided through making a silver cloisonné vitreous enamel pendant using a sterling silver disc.
You will be introduced to a range of methods and techniques which will give you the skills to translate your design from paper to metal. Beginners will be able to make something simple, whilst those with more experience can develop their skills.
You will learn how to form the wires for your chosen design and transfer them to the metal. Layers of enamel will be added, and you will learn how to graduate and blend the colours into one another.
Having created your piece, you will then be guided through finishing, learning how to grind the surface flat and achieve a smooth polished enamel surface.
You will finish with a piece that is unique to you, and have a greater understanding of enamelling techniques that you can take forward into further projects. You are also welcome to bring any pieces you have started at home for advice, and to work on alongside this project.
Who is my instructor?
Linda Connelly is an award-winning enamel artist and jeweller who has been making enamelled jewellery for over thirty years from her studio in Surrey. She is an experienced tutor who spent nearly twenty years teaching enamelling and jewellery making in adult education, most recently teaching her own private classes up until the pandemic.

title: Korean Street Food Class
description:
Introduction to Ingredients

Settle in and get familiar with the ingredients for kimbap and seafood pancakes! Some will be prepared in advance and some you will get to make from scratch.




Prepare the Fillings

You will be shown how to prepare all the ingredients and how to cook it for making kimbap. Plenty of help on hand if you need it!




Rolling the Kimbap

Next up, you'll learn how to season the rice and how to lay down the fillings like a prop.




Learn the Techniques

Then we'll show you how to roll the perfect kimbap, including how to avoid some of the common mistakes.




Experiment with Fillings

We will try 3 different popular combination of the fillings. You will get good amount of practice in the class so you can recreate it at home!




Make Spicy Tteokbokki

You will learn how to make Korea's most popular street food, tteokbokki. This rice cake sticks in savoury spicy sauce is one addictive dish that every Korean loves! Perfectly pairs with Kimbap and usually served together.




Make Seafood Pancakes

You will also learnt to make one of the most loved traditional street food -- seafood pancakes from scratch. We'll show you how to make the batter from simple ingredients.




Take Home Your Creation

We always have a sit down meal at the end of the class to share the food. We usually make more than enough in the class so whatever is left is for you to take home!



Get ready for a fun, hands-on, authentic Korean street food cooking class in London at Kimchi Club W5! You'll learn to make two of the most iconic street foods of all time: Kimbap and seafood pancake.
No experience is needed! You’ll be guided step-by-step through each recipe, learning about the essential ingredients, techniques, and how to recreate these favourites easily in your own kitchen. You will have plenty to take home for your family to try all the dishes you create in the class.

Make three rolls of kimbap, including classic and tuna varieties.
Learn how to prepare seasoned rice and work with roasted seaweed.
Experiment with a variety of colourful and flavourful fillings.
Master the techniques for rolling perfect kimbap every time.
Learn how to make a traditional Korean seafood pancake from scratch.
Create a delicious dipping sauce to accompany your pancake.
Discover authentic home-cooking techniques and ingredient tips.
As with all our classes, all ingredients and cooking materials are provided and ready for you on the day. You’ll also take home printed recipe cards covering everything you learned, so you can confidently recreate the dishes at home and get perfect results every time.

description:

Shaping

Boiling

Join this hands-on workshop and learn the secrets to creating the perfect chewy bagel from scratch. You'll be guided through the sourdough process to achieve a fantastic texture and digestibility, resulting in a beautiful, mild, and creamy flavour rather than a sour one.
It's a wonderful way to switch off and get stuck into a new skill as you're guided through every step of the process. You'll learn how to work with a sourdough starter specifically for sweet and mild baking, as well as how to maintain it for your future kitchen adventures.
During this session, you will:
Levain and maintenance – Learn about the sourdough starter used for sweet and mild baking and how to maintain it.
Hand-kneading – Knead the dough by hand to build essential bagel strength; it's a low-hydration dough, so you'll get a bit of a workout.

title: Ultimate Tamales Mexican Cooking Class
description:
Join me for a Mexican cooking class focused on the art of making tamales – a traditional activity for celebrating special occasions in Mexico. Tamales are delightful parcels filled with corn dough and a rich stew, wrapped in banana or corn husk leaves and steamed to perfection. Working with authentic Mexican ingredients will transport you to the vibrant streets of Mexico, evoking a sense of excitement and cultural immersion.
As you work your way through the class, you'll not only learn the ins and outs of tamal making but also gain valuable tips and tricks from an experienced cook. Once the cooking is done, you and your fellow participants can savour the fruits of your labour by enjoying a delightful meal together.
Take home the knowledge and expertise to recreate this festive dish in your own kitchen, along with the satisfaction of mastering a quintessential Mexican culinary tradition. Plus, you'll leave with a belly full of delicious tamales and a heart brimming with the joy of shared culinary experience.
Learn to make the perfect tamale dough
Create two different fillings: corn husk chicken tamales and banana leaves mushroom tamales
Prepare complementary side dishes like refried beans and Mexican pasta salad

description:

title: Sushi Master Experience - Beginner to Advanced
description:
Welcome and History

Arrive at a relaxed kitchen setting and meet your instructors. Begin with an easy introduction to sushi history -- fascinating stories that set the scene for what you’ll be creating.




Make Beginner Level Sushi

Start with a basic Sushi and Maki to learn the beginner level skills. This is to prepare your skills for the next steps.




Make the Chef's Signature Dragon Rolls

Learn how to craft the signature dragon roll, with a variety of fillings to suit every taste. Big group? No worries -- everyone gets to personalise their own roll while picking up expert tips along the way.




Make Many Other Types of Sushi

Discover playful sushi styles that took shape after the 1990s. These contemporary twists are as fun to make as they are to eat, and you’ll see how innovation has kept sushi evolving.




Taste the Success

Finish by arranging your colourful rolls, snapping a few photos, and then sitting down to enjoy a shared feast. You’ll leave with new skills, a full stomach, and memories worth savouring.




Add-on Sake Tasting

Enjoy a few Sake while you eat your handmade Sushi.




Add-on Knife Sharpening

Learn essential knife skills before the class.




Add-on Recipe Collection Booklet

This is your journey of cooking adventure.

You also will get Polaroid-style photo sticker from your class, showing your highlight in the class you attended.
Your chef tutor also will give you a stamp. It is your certificate of success.



Ready to go beyond the basics?
This immersive Sushi Masterclass is designed for food lovers who want more than a beginner workshop. Whether you’ve taken a sushi class before or simply want a deeper experience, this session will elevate your skills, confidence and presentation.
Welcome to the next level of sushi making.
What Makes This a Masterclass?
This class includes everything from our beginner workshop — plus premium techniques, signature rolls and professional presentation skills.
We begin with a short but engaging introduction to sushi’s evolution — from traditional Japanese origins to modern creative rolls found in today’s restaurants.
Then you’ll step into the role of sushi chef.
During this Masterclass you will:
Understand and season sushi rice properly
Create a perfectly structured classic sushi roll
Master our Chef’s Signature Dragon Roll
Learn modern sushi styles developed in recent decades
Refine rolling control and shaping techniques

The course length is 2 hours a session, beginning at 6.30pm and ending at 8.30pm, on Wednesdays every week for four weeks.
The class takes place in Central London in a working carving studio with ongoing projects and commissions, giving you the opportunity to see the working practise of a professional carver.
Course Structure:
Week 1: The first evening will focus on the basics of woodcarving with an introduction to the tools, how to use them safely and effectively, the properties of timber including understanding grain direction, and a practical project focusing on chip carving.
Week 2: The second evening will build on the skills you’ve already learned. Having practised chip carving during the previous week, you will move on to shallow relief carving. During this session, you’ll work on drawing out a design suitable for shallow relief and begin creating a background.
Week 3: The third evening will focus on creating the surface and understanding the forms of the carving.
Week 4: The final evening will focus on finishing your shallow relief carving. During this session, you will move on from working on the forms and begin working on the finishing touches of your carving, which you can then take home to display or work on further in your own time.
What will I achieve? By the end of the course you will have covered:
Identifying suitable timber species for future carving projects
The correct way to safely use chisels and mallet
How to secure your work
How to lay out your design on timber
How to create a carving in relief
An introduction to historic ornament

title: Black and White Photography Class
description:
If you've been looking for some unique things to do in London and you want to expand on your skills with the camera, why not join this class and learn how to capture images in black and white.

Software. Explore different software and plugins for professional photo colour conversions.

title: Ceramics Handbuilding Course
description:
Important venue update: All workshops will take place at our new studio at 377 Station Road, Forest Gate.
In this ceramic four week course, you will learn the three fundamental hand-building techniques: pinching, coiling, and slab-building. By the end of the course, you will understand all the most important elements of design and construction with clay so you can create original pottery of your own. These foundational practices are the basis for almost all ceramics made by hand-building.
You can expect to leave with 1-2 larger detailed pieces or a collection of smaller items.
No prior experience in the craft is necessary for this course. It is suited to anyone who is curious to work with clay for the first time as well as those who already have a good knowledge and experience. Our smaller class sizes allow the tutor to spend a higher proportion of their time with individuals who would like deeper insights and to further their skills/understanding.
If you don't know what you want to make, don't worry! We have a range of ideas and objects to inspire the design, and we have excellent assistance on hand for the building of your final piece. Think coffee mugs, teacups, pasta bowls, decorative vases, planters, table jugs, wine carafes, candlestick holders, wall hangings, the list goes on.
We also welcome anyone who already has decided on a design or idea of what they want to achieve for their final piece - the tutor will help configure the session plans to that idea and ensure the course material is relevant! We will all create in a communal space with support and instruction.
Throughout the course, you will learn through discussion, doing, and testing the boundaries to understand the limits of clay - making you a truly resilient potter!
The class atmosphere is friendly and supportive, and you should expect to chat and get to know each other as you work - ideas and encouragement are shared throughout. We can’t wait for you to join!
Course Itinerary
Week 1 Introduction to Ceramics
Learn about types of clay and how they differ.
Learn the three hand-building techniques (Pinching/coiling/slab-building) and try to push them to their limits.
Understand how clay can be reclaimed.
Week 2 Finessing Ceramics
Learn about decorating techniques including but not limited to; mark-making, burnishing, simple marbling, inlay.
Learn how to attach ceramic pieces together.
Understand how to calculate clay shrinkage.
Understand what happens as clay dries and why/how it is fired.
Share and discuss inspirations.
Start prototyping and experimenting for your final pieces.
Week 3 Developing an Idea
Fast sculpting mini-project, test your hand-building skills with a fun warm-up exercise.
Start working on your final pieces, with guidance and discussion from Sorrel and the group.
Week 4 Finishing Your Vision
Finish building your final pieces ready to be fired.
Use decoration techniques on your final pieces.
Choose your glaze colours to be applied by Sorrel.
There is also an optional addition to join a glazing class for £30* (date to be confirmed with the tutor following each course). During this, you can glaze your works yourself before they are fired.
Please note: We strive to help you create something amazing during your pottery class. Because each piece is handmade and involves many variables (such as clay handling, glaze, and firing conditions), we’re unable to offer refunds or replacements for defects or damages that occur in items you’ve made.

title: Tutored Life Drawing Course London
description:
Join a relaxed and friendly life drawing and painting class in the heart of Covent Garden, guided by a professional tutor each week. Whether you're completely new or already have some experience, this class helps you enjoy the process, build confidence, and steadily improve your skills.
Unlike most public life drawing sessions, our classes run in a unique 8-week figure study cycle, working with the same professional model and a longer pose across multiple weeks. This gives you the rare opportunity to develop your drawing or painting gradually, improve proportions and anatomy, and see real progress — while still being able to drop in at any point.
Each session begins with short warm-up poses to loosen up and sharpen observation, followed by a longer pose where you can take your time developing your work. You’re welcome to work at your own pace and in your preferred medium.
You can choose to work with:
Charcoal and pencil for drawing
Acrylic or watercolour for painting
Classes are kept small (maximum 10 students), so everyone receives personal guidance in a calm and welcoming studio atmosphere. Many students come for relaxation, creative focus, and the joy of learning in a supportive environment.
You’re welcome to join for a single drop-in session, or continue attending to follow the full 8-week cycle if you’d like deeper progress. Longer study options are also available — just ask us in the studio.
What you'll get
The experience of being in an atelier style life drawing class. Materials can be included depending on your ticket, and you can take home anything you create during the class.

FAQ

Do I have to start at the beginning of the 8-week block?
No. Students are welcome to join at any point in the 8-week cycle. Because the class is fully tutored with individual instruction, the tutor will guide you based on your current level and help you integrate into the ongoing pose study.
What if I miss a class?
That’s absolutely fine. You can simply continue the following week and progress at your own pace. There is no penalty for missing a session, and the tutor will help you refocus when you return.
Why do you use the same model and pose for 8 weeks?
This is part of our classical atelier-style training approach. Working from the same pose over several weeks allows students to: Improve proportion and structure Refine anatomy and form Develop more finished drawings or paintings Correct mistakes over time This method is commonly used in professional art academies and is rare in public life drawing classes in London.

title: Weaving Taster Workshop: Ready, Sett, Weave
description:
Join this one-day weaving 'tasting menu' at Weavers Works and discover the creative possibilities of the loom. Whether you are an absolute beginner hungry to try a new craft or an experienced weaver looking to play with texture and pattern without the prep, this workshop is the perfect fit.
You don't need to worry about complex setup or planning; every 8-shaft table loom is dressed and ready for you. With guidance throughout the day, you'll feel supported as you move from loom to loom, sampling a range of structures.
Your five courses will include:
Twills and crepes – Explore a range of basic to fancy twills and crepes on a varied gamp
Colour and weave – Play with the effects of colour in the warp and weft
Huck weaves – Create lacy weaves and textures with warp and weft floats
Deflected double weave – Discover the magic of layered interlocking structures
Waffles – Experience three-dimensional weaving in awe
By the end of the session, you'll have a deeper appreciation for the craft and a 'takeaway' of five woven samples, one from each course, to keep as a record of your textile adventure.
Please note: the class runs from 10 am to 4.30 pm. An hour-long lunch break is included, with tea and coffee provided. There are plenty of cafés nearby, or you are welcome to bring your own lunch.

title: Adventurous Beginners Sewing Course: Make a Jumpsuit
description:
This is one of our personal favourite patterns! The Paper Theory Zadie Jumpsuit is a stylish, relaxed wrap-over jumpsuit. There are no fastenings, just a tie, but this means it’s a great pattern to leap into the world of adapting and adjusting a pattern to suit your preferences. You can make a long or short sleeve version.
You’ll learn how to make your own binding or create your own facing. We’ll be sewing pleats and adding slanted trouser pockets.
If you’re thinking, "Jumpsuits never fit me, " we can help! We’ve chosen this pattern to run as one of our courses as the genius Tara over at Paper Theory has designed it in a way that makes it easy to adapt the fit.
We'll spend dedicated time teaching you how to adapt the pattern for your body. We’ll discuss the importance of body rise and making sure you’ve got good coverage in the bodice.
This course is suitable for adventurous beginners. We do ask that you can thread and use a sewing machine to take part in this course, even if you have very basic knowledge! If you think you’ll just need a quick reminder, that’s fine. If you want to take on this challenge but can’t use a sewing machine yet, book onto our beginners' "Learn to Sew a Cushion or a Tote" before you start.
You can work at your own pace. You will have 7 weeks to complete the Jumpsuit during our Sew Your Own Way sessesions where everyone is working on their own project.
We have plenty to keep you occupied, whatever your level. We know clothes making can seem like a daunting prospect at first, but it's easy when you know how! It gives you the opportunity to be unique and creative with your style. It's a great way to relax and unwind, make new creative friends, and you can become part of the growing Make Mee Community.

Get hands-on with the most important step: making the signature mochi pastry. We’ll guide you through the process of creating that famously soft, smooth, and chewy texture, ensuring you master this key technique with confidence.

Discover the satisfying skill of filling and sealing your mochi. You’ll learn the traditional technique to neatly encase delicious fillings, creating the perfect little parcels of flavour. It’s a wonderfully mindful and fun part of the class.

title: Taster Sewing Course
description:
In this exciting sewing class in Northolt, West London you will learn the ins and outs of domestic sewing. If you've always wanted to explore the world of fashion but have been apprehensive about the cost, this is the perfect opportunity for you.
Over the course of two 3-hour sessions, held on Saturdays once a month, you will be guided through various sewing techniques that will help you gain confidence in your skills. You will learn how to thread up a machine, including the bobbin, and discover how to inset an invisible zip using finishing techniques such as the French seam.
This workshop is designed to alleviate any fears you may have as a beginner, and you will be amazed at just how much you can achieve. The friendly atmosphere will make you feel at ease as you navigate your way through simple sewing tasks to hone your abilities. By the end of the course, you will even be able to create your very own simple tote bag or cushion.
Throughout the workshop, you will work with a variety of materials, allowing you to experiment and find your own unique style. The supportive instructor will provide step-by-step instructions, ensuring that you feel comfortable every step of the way.
Not only will this workshop introduce you to the world of fashion and sewing, but it will also provide you with a transformative experience. As your skills grow, you will gain a sense of accomplishment and the confidence to tackle more complex projects in the future. And the best part? You get to take home your creations, a tangible reminder of your journey into the exciting world of sewing.

title: Stool Making: 2-Day Woodworking Course
description:
Join us on this two-day furniture making workshop in London and create a solid ash stool built to endure for generations. This isn't a kit and there are no screws involved; instead, you'll master the traditional techniques of wedged joinery, working from raw timber blanks to a finished piece. Under the expert guidance of furniture designer Brandon Harrison, you'll gain hands-on experience with hand planes and spokeshaves as you shape each component of your stool.
You'll work with English ash, a resilient timber with a rich heritage in British craft. Throughout the two days, you'll learn how to read grain direction, drill compound-angle mortises, and secure your joints permanently using wedged tenons. This process focuses on the deeply rewarding joy of creating something with your own hands, ensuring you leave with a piece of furniture where the construction itself is a beautiful part of the design.
Across the two days, you'll learn to:
Read and mark out timber – Understand grain direction, mark mortise positions and splay angles, and transfer seat profiles from a template.
Drill compound-angle mortises – Use a drill press jig to bore the angled holes that ensure your stool stands perfectly true.
Shape octagonal legs – Mark eight faces on a square blank before planing each one flat and tapering them with a spokeshave.
Refine the seat profile – Use a jigsaw and spokeshave to create a comfortable D-profile seat ready for finishing.
Cut round tenons – Fit each tenon to its specific mortise and saw the kerfs required for the locking wedges.
Assemble and wedge – Master the sequence of gluing and driving wedges home to lock your joints forever.
Customise your finish – Choose between a chamfered, rounded, or square seat edge using hand tools.
Apply hard wax oil – Protect the wood with a finish that highlights the natural ash grain and makes it ready for daily use.
By the time you've sliced your tenons flush and applied the final coat of oil, you'll have gained a fresh challenge to inspire your future projects. You'll head home with a functional masterpiece and the enduring skills to kickstart your next creative obsession.

title: Five Week Silver Jewellery Course
description:
Ready to go beyond a one-off taster and really learn silversmithing? Our beginner silver jewellery course is your chance to discover the fundamentals of jewellery making over five weeks of evening classes – building genuine skills and real confidence as you go.
This isn't a quick intro; it's a proper hands-on journey into traditional silversmithing. Week by week, you'll learn how to transform silver and other metals into beautiful handmade pieces guided step-by-step by experienced instructors. You'll work with professional tools, master traditional techniques, and create projects that matter – silver rings, bracelets, pendants, and charms – each one with your own creative flair woven right through it.
Over the five weeks, you'll build a solid toolkit of skills: soldering, annealing, piercing and sawing metal, forming, adding texture, filing, finishing, and polishing. By the end, you won't just have made jewellery – you'll have the confidence and know-how to keep creating long after the course finishes.
Whether you're a complete beginner or you've dabbled before and want to develop your skills properly, this course is made for you. You'll leave with finished pieces you've crafted with your own hands, a genuine understanding of the craft, and the spark to keep making.

title: Sourdough Class for Beginners
description:

You don't need any experience to join. Whether you're a complete beginner or looking to troubleshoot your current sourdough making process, this class is for you!

A loaf will be provided to score and bake, which will be enjoyed at lunch, and then we’ll start the process again.
The first part of the class will be theoretical, exploring flours, their properties, how to choose the right one for the right bake, and then we’ll move onto the practical, so that you’ll see the steps more than once.
There will be a light lunch, and the class will end with everyone bringing home a loaf ready to score and bake later that evening or the next day.
You'll take away a finished loaf to bake, plus a goody bag and handy new skills to perfect your future sourdough loaves.

title: Acrylic Pouring Workshop
description:
Discover the mesmerising world of acrylic pouring and create your own vibrant fluid art masterpiece in this relaxing, beginner-friendly workshop.
Acrylic pouring is a playful and expressive art form where colours flow, blend, and transform into completely unique abstract designs. No experience is needed — this class is all about experimentation, creativity, and letting go of perfection.
During the workshop, you’ll learn professional acrylic pouring techniques including dirty pours, flip cups, swipes, layering, and how to create beautiful cells and lacing effects. You’ll also discover how to mix paints to the perfect consistency, choose colour palettes that work beautifully together, and use different pouring methods to achieve stunning results.
This experience is designed to be fun, mindful, and deeply therapeutic. Watching the paint move across the canvas is incredibly calming, making this class perfect for anyone looking to relax, reconnect with creativity, and enjoy a unique artistic experience.
You’ll be guided step-by-step throughout the session and will create your own one-of-a-kind artwork to take home. Every piece is completely different, making acrylic pouring one of the most exciting and surprising forms of modern abstract art.
Perfect for:
Complete beginners
Creative date nights
Team building activities
Birthday celebrations & hen parties
Mindful solo experiences
Anyone wanting to explore fluid art and colour therapy
All materials are provided, including canvases, acrylic paints, pouring mediums, gloves, and protective equipment. Just bring clothes you don’t mind getting a little paint on and get ready to pour, play, and create.
Come and experience the magic of fluid art — where every pour becomes a surprise masterpiece.

title: Album Cover Collage Art Class
description:
Create Your Own Album Cover Art Session
Have you ever created with collage? If so, you already know how much fun it is, but if you try my style, you’re in for a whole new experience.
These immersive, hands-on sessions are a deep dive into a unique mash up of punk-inspired collage and street art style I've developed over the years. We aren't here to make things look neat or perfect; we are here to tear down and layer up.
Inspired by my late mum's love for punk and her own artwork on album sleeves, we'll be using authentic copies of her old music magazines, song sheets, stickers, books, tape, embellishments, and a spray paints and more. We'll even rip up pieces of my own artwork that has been sat in my studio for years to build up those layers. And right at the end, I’ll introduce you to the pièce de résistance - going in with the spray paint to bring the whole artwork together.
Whether you're a musician looking to design your next vinyl sleeve or someone who just wants to get their hands messy, these sessions are designed to pump your creativity, break the rules, and make you completely lose track of time. Whether you’re looking for a speak of inspiration or just want to do something different. With the radio playing the background, it’s a unique experience and a direct dive into my world.
Drop the overthinking, leave the perfectionism at the door, and come create something raw.
We are becoming a collective now. Come join us.
Looking for a Group Experience?
I also offer tailored corporate workshops and private group sessions. Whether it’s team building or a creative get-together, please get in touch to discuss what you're looking for and let's make it happen.
What you'll get
The Studio Experience
More than just an art class, these sessions are held in my own personal art studio - a space to be inspired, reignite your spark, or get those creative juices flowing as you slow down, connect, and create something entirely your own.

The Takeaway: You’ll design a unique album sleeve, fully finished and ready to take home to display on your wall.

By the end of this enlightening activity, you'll have gained a solid foundation in weaving techniques and created your own distinctive textile piece - opening the door to a whole new world of creative possibilities.

title: Sip and Paint: Cake Decorating Experience - the Arding Rooms
description:
STEP 1: Blank Canvas

We start with a blank cake canvas and our paints




STEP 2: Initial Outline

Next, we use our brush to create an initial outline of our painting




STEP 3: Palette Details

Next, we use both our paintbrushes and palette knives to add depth and dimension to our paintings




STEP 4: Eat Your Painting

The best bit! You get to eat your cake when you get home.



Swap the canvas for cake and the paintbrush for buttercream at this one-of-a-kind cake decorating experience in Battersea – a joyful, creative afternoon from Good Cake Day, hosted at one of South West London's most beautiful new venues, The Arding Rooms.
You've heard of sip and paint. Sip & Cake is exactly what it sounds like – and yes, you get to eat your artwork at the end.
Your blank canvas arrives presented on a food-safe artist's palette, complete with wells of buttercream "paint" in a range of colours, brushes, and a small palette knife. An expert instructor will guide you through the strokes, swirls, and palette-knife techniques that bring a cake to life, and an inspiration image is provided to get you started – though where you take it from there is entirely up to you. No experience needed, just a willingness to have fun with it.
A complimentary drink is included from the off, with both alcoholic and non-alcoholic options, so whether you're reaching for fizz or a fruity mocktail, you'll have something to sip while you create.
Every Good Cake Day experience is rooted in the BLUSH philosophy – the belief that everyone is beautiful, loved, unique, special, and human – and the afternoon reflects that from the very first moment. Before the painting begins, you'll take part in a guided mindfulness activity: a quiet few minutes to write a letter to your future self, sealed up and posted back to you three months later. A small, lovely thing to look forward to.
The venue itself is worth the trip. The Arding Rooms sits within the lovingly restored Arding & Hobbs building at Clapham Junction – a landmark former department store where Arts and Crafts-inspired interiors meet original preserved features, including a magnificent domed stained glass window. You'll be painting your cake in a space that's a work of art in its own right, just eight minutes by train from Victoria or Waterloo.
Here's how the afternoon unfolds:
2:00–2:15pm – Arrival, welcome drinks, and meeting your fellow artists
2:15–2:30pm – Guided mindful letter writing to your future self
2:30–4:15pm – Painting your cake, with expert guidance throughout
4:15–4:30pm – Group photos, boxing up your masterpiece, and farewells
Everything is provided – all materials, a box to carry your cake home safely, and a carrier bag. All you need to do is turn up.

title: Advanced Dessert - Dubai Chocolate Mochi Making Workshop
description:
A Warm Welcome

Welcome to our cool and friendly London kitchen! Your culinary journey begins with a fascinating introduction to the history of mochi. In our small, personal classes, your experienced chef will get you settled in and excited to create these delicious Japanese treats.




Create the Perfect Dough

Get hands-on with the most important step: making the signature mochi pastry. We’ll guide you through the process of creating that famously soft, smooth, and chewy texture, ensuring you master this key technique with confidence.




Make the Dubai Chocolate Filling

Learn to make the popular Dubi chocolate filling from scratch. Catch up the trendy food fashion and adjust the taste to your favourite.




Wrap the Mochi

Discover the satisfying skill of filling and sealing your mochi. You’ll learn the traditional technique to neatly encase delicious fillings, creating the perfect little parcels of flavour. It’s a wonderfully mindful and fun part of the class.




Your Delicious Creations

Step back and admire the beautiful mochi you’ve made! You’ll leave the workshop with a box full of your own multi-flavoured Japanese desserts to take home and share, plus the skills and know-how to recreate them whenever you like.



Dubai chocolate mochi is more than just a dessert — it’s a luxurious fusion of Chinese ancient dessert technique and Middle Eastern-inspired indulgence, combining soft, delicate mochi with rich, decadent chocolate flavours.
In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn how to create these elegant treats from scratch, blending texture, flavour, and presentation into a truly premium dessert experience.
Perfect for team building, client events, or special celebrations, this session is designed to be creative, interactive, and visually impressive. Whether you’re a beginner or a dessert lover, our expert instructors will guide you every step of the way.

description:

title: Traditional Chinese Tea Ceremony at the Fan Museum
description:

Guided fan talk – Discover the rich history and cultural significance of China export fans.

Tea and pastry tasting – Enjoy the delicate flavours of hand-picked premium teas and artisanal treats.
Gongfu brewing techniques – Master the foundational steps of this mindful brewing style.
Museum exhibition tour – Wander through the latest display of British royal fans, noticing the intricate details of pieces once owned by figures like Queen Victoria.
By the end of the afternoon, you'll feel completely refreshed and inspired by these ancient traditions. You'll leave with a newfound appreciation for tea philosophy and the rewarding sense of peace that comes from a quiet, creative escape.

title: Watercolour Painting Improvers Course
description:
If you have a basic understanding of watercolour techniques, this intermediate course is the perfect activity to build upon your skills and refine your artistic practice.
In this supportive and inspiring workshop environment, you will learn how to achieve greater control and explore more advanced skills. Each week builds on key principles, guiding you through exercises designed to improve your technique in working wet-on-dry, wet-on-wet, and glazing. You'll also explore how to capture light, shadow, and atmosphere effectively, adding new subtlety and complexity to your work.
With a combination of quick studio exercises and more challenging compositions, such as portraiture and botanicals, this course is structured to offer both technical instruction and creative exploration. You’ll be encouraged to experiment with new approaches and make intentional artistic choices to help develop your own personal style.
Throughout the course, you'll cover a variety of techniques and focus areas, including:
Advanced brushwork and control – Refine your line, stroke, and pressure for precision and expression while using different brushes for varied effects.
Layering and glazing – Understand the timing between layers and learn to build depth and vibrancy through transparent washes.
Colour mixing and harmonies – Refine your palette with more nuanced tones and use colour to create mood and emotion.
Light and shadow – Create realistic or dramatic lighting effects by understanding light sources and shadow placement.
Wet-on-wet and texture techniques – Make soft blends and atmospheric transitions, using salt, sponges, and resist for visual interest.
Composition and subject variety – Compose strong, balanced images by working from references and observation on landscapes, florals, and portraits.
Personal style and self-expression – Identify and develop your artistic voice by choosing subjects and techniques that reflect your personality.
Final projects and portfolio building – Plan and complete finished watercolour artworks and prepare a mini-portfolio of your best work.
By the end of the course, you'll have a folio of accomplished paintings and an enriching new understanding of the watercolour medium, giving you the confidence to continue your artistic practice.

description:

title: Metalsmithing Class: Foldform
description:
This small-scale metalworking taster workshop focuses on the contemporary metalsmithing technique called Foldforming.
Essentially, foldforming involves taking flat sheet metal and folding it. Through hammering or passing it through a rolling mill, the metal will be stretched and curved. When opened up using your hands, interesting and unique three-dimensional forms are created.
Worried about being a complete beginner? Don't worry, this is perfect class to learn all the basics and try something new.
What will I make?
Using copper sheet, you will create a selection of 6-10 foldforming samples, trying out many different types of folds and using the foldforming ‘bible’ by Charles Lewton-Brain as a reference.
There will also be samples made by the tutor on display to inspire you. You will learn fundamental metalsmithing techniques, such as annealing copper, hammer forging, filing, and saw piercing.
You will also use finishing processes to give your samples the wow factor and turn them into art to display in your home, including cleaning and polishing, burnishing, and flame patination.
What will happen on the day?
The tutor will demonstrate a technique, and then the class will create that sample. This will allow the tutor time to help guide everyone individually as they work and ensure good hammering technique is used and that there is good health and safety when using a hot flame.
After the set of samples are made, students can tailor the designs to their plan, whether it is working at a smaller scale for potential jewellery projects or imagining how the foldforming samples could be integrated with other materials and practices. There will then be time in the afternoon to finish and burnish some of the more successful samples to elevate them from a plain sample to a decorative item to be displayed in the home.
Earplugs will be provided for protection as it does get noisy when hammering begins.
Who is my instructor?
Emma-Jane Rule is an award-winning Contemporary Metalsmith, with a workshop at StudionAme in Leicester. She is a member of Design-Nation and has exhibited nationally at contemporary art, craft, and design events.
Her handcrafted contemporary metalwork is created using traditional silversmithing skills as well as the metalworking technique of foldforming, creating unique and collectible metal art.
Taking inspiration from the rhythms and patterns found in nature, Emma-Jane’s portfolio includes decorative vessels and wall art in silver and base metals, lighting, and jewellery.

description:

Practical life drawing

title: Metalsmithing Class: Score and Fold
description:
Join this exclusive MasterMaker metalsmithing workshop at FORGE in London, led by renowned makers Paul Wells and Anastasia Young during London Craft Week. As authors of "New Jewellery Techniques" and pioneers of the innovative curved score and fold technique, they offer a unique opportunity to explore the exciting possibilities of creating beautiful three-dimensional forms from sheet metal using wire-scoring methods.

Starting with paper maquettes to grasp the principles, you'll then progress to creating several copper samples. The focus is on exploring the process and discovering the design potential this technique unlocks. You'll receive expert advice, troubleshoot ideas, and discuss how you might incorporate these methods into your own creative practice.
The day concludes perfectly with a relaxed chat, allowing you to mingle with the instructors and fellow participants over complimentary wine and delicious sushi. You'll leave this insightful session not only with your sample creations but also with fresh inspiration and a deeper understanding of this unique metalworking technique.

title: Two Day Traditional Indigo Resist Dyeing Course
description:
Join this weekend indigo resist dyeing textile course in North West London and connect with one of the most ancient dyeing methods in the world. This hands-on workshop is a wonderful opportunity to learn about the rich history of traditional indigo-dyed textiles from China.
This creative activity will teach you how to master three different traditional resist dyeing methods from China: stitch-resist (扎染), wax-resist (蜡染), and soy paste-resist (型糊染). You will not only learn the techniques but also discover the fascinating cultural stories behind these crafts.
On the first day of the course, you will have the chance to learn and practise all three traditional techniques. On the second day, you can choose the method you enjoyed the most to create a larger, more detailed project. We will provide some sample fabric, one square scarf, and one t-shirt for you to work with. You are also welcome to bring your own natural fibre items to dye and create with during the session.
You will leave this immersive experience with a collection of beautifully patterned textiles, equipped with the skills and inspiration to continue your indigo dyeing journey.

title: Chinese Calligraphy Class
description:
Ever been drawn to the beauty of Chinese characters, ink paintings or traditional Chinese culture? Join Iris for a year-long journey into Chinese calligraphy, discovering how brush, ink and movement come together in expressive, meaningful artworks.
You'll explore Chinese regular script, inspired by the disciplined elegance of Ouyang Xun, one of the most influential calligraphers in Chinese history. Through guided practice, demonstrations and personalised feedback, you'll learn how individual brushstrokes build balance, rhythm and harmony within each character – no previous experience required, whether you're completely new to calligraphy or simply curious about Chinese culture.
Through monthly in-person classes, you'll cover brush techniques and essential strokes, the structure and balance of characters, and the rhythm and beauty of regular script, completing a finished calligraphy artwork in every class to take home, display or gift.
The course includes:
10 in-person Chinese calligraphy classes
A final student exhibition celebrating everyone's progress
A finished calligraphy piece from each class
Take-home practice copy sheets
Ongoing online guidance and feedback between classes
Chinese calligraphy isn't about writing quickly or perfectly – it's an invitation to slow down, observe closely, and discover the beauty that comes through patient practice. As brush, ink and movement come together, many find a quiet, meditative rhythm, making this as much a gentle space for inner exploration as it is a traditional art form to learn.
About your teacher: born and raised in Taiwan, Iris began learning Chinese calligraphy at nine, training under experienced calligraphers alongside her art education before working alongside artists and calligraphers to deepen her craft. She later moved to London to study Art Management and has been based there since 2019, now sharing traditional Chinese calligraphy with students from all backgrounds.

title: Colourful Anodising Workshop
description:
We are delighted Alice Fry is returning to teach this popular workshop!
You will be guided through the theory and science behind anodising niobium. You will experiment and play with niobium and titanium to create a spectrum of colours and finishes on the metal, before creating your finished piece.
There will be plenty of time for discussions and relaxed, playful making.
What will I make?
You will create a 3” x 3” colourful niobium wall tile for your home, which you can either mount straight to your wall or in a frame. You will have experimented with anodising smaller pieces of niobium and titanium before starting your finished design.
What will happen on the day?
We will start the day with an introduction to refractory metals, with a presentation by Alice focusing on the theory and applications of niobium anodising. Following this, you will be shown demonstrations in dip, sponge, brush, masked and relief anodising techniques. Alice will also guide you through setting up the equipment.
You will then have the opportunity to practise these techniques and experiment on small pieces of titanium and niobium to create colour samples. You will also be supplied with tape (to mask off sections of your designs), scalpels, pencils, and various finishing materials and brushes. Following your experiments, you will be supplied with a 3” x 3” sheet of 0.51mm thick niobium for your design. Alice will help you with your designs and guide you through anodising your finished piece.
If you finish your piece and would like to try more, there will be the opportunity to buy additional niobium to try out.

title: Leatherworking Class: Handstitched Small Leather Goods
description:
Discover the craft of traditional hand-stitched leatherwork in this beginner-friendly workshop in London. This hands-on class is ideal for anyone who wants to learn how leather goods are made using classic saddle stitching techniques, while creating a beautifully finished leather piece to take home.
The class takes place in a real working leather studio, where guests will be introduced to different types of leather, their main features, and the tools and methods commonly used in the field. With expert guidance throughout, participants will learn how to prepare, mark, cut, punch, edge finish and hand stitch leather, as well as how to use simple fastening hardware.
Guests will be able to choose their project from a selection of small leather goods such as passport holders, glasses cases, purses, card holders and similar accessories. Informative handouts and supplier lists are also included, making this a valuable introduction for complete beginners as well as those looking to deepen their leathercraft knowledge.
Materials are included.
If you are interested in booking a private class, please note that sessions are usually scheduled 4 to 8 weeks from the booking date.
This tuition may take up to 6 hours to complete, although the exact timing may vary depending on group size, the chosen project and the pace of the session.

A hand-stitched leather item to take home, practical experience with saddle stitching and core leatherworking techniques, plus useful handouts and supplier information for continuing their leathercraft journey

title: Intensive One Week Pottery Course
description:
Dedicate five mornings to developing your throwing skills in this intensive one-week course. Running Monday to Friday from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm, this activity offers a structured approach while allowing space for your own self-directed projects.
Throughout the week, you will explore various ceramic throwing techniques:
Monday: Learn how to centre clay focusing on how to pull up the walls evenly. You will make a cylinder shapes, bowl shapes, bottle shapes.
Tuesday & Wednesday: Practice wheel throwing further with larger quantities of clay, make a jug form and make handles.
Thursday: Working with leather-hard clay, you will learn how to attach handles and use turning tools to refine your work and make a footring if required, you can carve patterns and details into the clay.
Friday: Decorate and further refine the shapes of your thrown items, and learn how to apply coloured slips for decoration.
Please be aware that the glazing session for your finished work is scheduled separately, approximately two weeks after this activity concludes (the specific date and time will be confirmed later).
This course provides a valuable opportunity to gain hands-on experience with key pottery processes in a condensed timeframe, resulting in several pieces ready for the final glazing stage and a broader understanding of working with clay.

Please note: Public dates for this class require at least 4 guests to run. In the unlikely event that we don't reach this number, we may cancel the session; if that happens, we'll inform you and let you choose between a refund or reschedule, so please watch your email/SMS one day prior to the class.
What you'll get
All materials, aprons, glazes, and firings are included in the price and provided by the studio. At the end of the course, the attendees will make at least 4-8 pieces of pottery ready for collection after 4 weeks.

title: Advanced Colourwork Knitting Workshop – Master Fair Isle
description:
In this advanced colourwork knitting class in London, you’ll build the skills and confidence needed to tackle bold, beautiful multi-colour projects. The focus is on understanding how colourwork works, so you can knit with intention, improve your finish, and enjoy the process rather than wrestling with tangled yarn.
This class is best suited to confident knitters who are already comfortable with knit and purl stitches and have completed a few small projects. While it isn’t suitable for complete beginners, everything is explained clearly and supported step by step, with plenty of time to ask questions and troubleshoot as you go.
What to expect:
Learn how to confidently read and interpret colourwork charts.
Understand yarn dominance and how it affects your finished fabric.
Manage floats on the back of your work for neat, even tension.
Explore techniques for knitting with two colours, including one-handed and two-handed styles.
Knit a stranded colourwork sample with expert guidance throughout.
Tips for fixing common colourwork issues and refining your technique.
By the end of the class, you’ll feel confident starting stranded colourwork projects such as Fair Isle hats, Nordic mittens, or Icelandic yoke sweaters, with a solid understanding of charts, yarn control, and tension that will support your knitting for years to come.

title: CMYK Screen Printing Course
description:
Get to grips with the ins and outs of CMYK screen printing in this two-part workshop in Peckham, where you'll first learn the rules of colour separation inside out, then spend a full day breaking them to create something genuinely unconventional.
In Part 1, you'll build a solid understanding of CMYK's limitations, potential and underlying logic – the theory that makes everything in Part 2 possible. Then in Part 2, you'll explore playful ways to subvert CMYK norms and push your prints toward more exciting, unexpected outcomes.
Level: beginner to intermediate.
Dates & times:
Part 1 – Theory and separations: Wednesday, 24th September 2026, 7pm–9pm
Part 2 – Exposing and printing: Saturday, 26th September 2026, 10am–4pm
What's covered:
Digital art-working CMYK separations, bitmapping, LPI–DPI, angles and frequency, stochastic dots
Printing techniques, including printing a square on a square on a square on a square, and working with inks
Moiré mitigation and exposing
Led by Giorgia Boller, a visual artist whose practice centres on screen printing and collage. After completing a master's degree in printmaking, she now shares the joys of screen printing with anyone keen to learn the process, guiding you from first principles right through to confident, creative experimentation.

title: Create Your Own Fantasy World: Drawing and Worldbuilding
description:
Are you interested in a captivating drawing class in London where you'll unlock your imagination and create your own fantastical world? Join us to learn how to craft intricate maps, invent unique creatures, design engaging characters, and construct immersive environments. This workshop blends drawing skills with storytelling and worldbuilding, empowering budding artists to bring their visions to life.
Don't worry if you're new to drawing or world creation, as this course is designed for beginners, offering guidance and creative prompts every step of the way. Over six weeks, with one class per week lasting two hours, you'll delve deep into your creativity and develop a complete mini-world to take home.
Discover your world's concept and sketch a detailed map, from continents to hidden kingdoms, adding imaginative elements like floating islands and volcanoes.
Learn to sketch various environments like forests, mountains, and underwater areas, bringing them to life with shading and colour pencils.
Let your imagination run wild as you invent fantasy creatures inspired by real animals, focusing on anatomy, texture, and expressive features.
Design a range of characters from heroes to villains, adding personality through facial expressions, poses, and costume designs.
Create intricate structures like castles and temples, alongside objects such as weapons and relics, experimenting with shapes and materials.
By the end of the course, you'll consolidate all your creations into a final project, showcasing your world map, key locations, creatures, and characters. Whether you create a poster, booklet, or large illustrated sheet, you'll leave with a tangible memento of your imaginative journey.
Weekly Breakdown:
Week 1: World Concept & Map Making
Brainstorm: What kind of world is it? (magical, futuristic, natural, etc.)
Draw a simple map (continents, islands, cities, landmarks)
Add creative details (floating islands, volcanoes, hidden kingdoms)
Week 2: Environments & Landscapes
Learn how to sketch forests, mountains, deserts, underwater areas, etc.
Choose 2–3 environments from their map and draw detailed scenes
Introduce atmosphere and mood through shading and colour pencils (optional)
Week 3: Fantasy Creatures & Animals
Invent creatures that live in the world (dragons, hybrids, mythical beasts)
Study real animals to mix features
Focus on anatomy, texture, and expressive features
Week 4: People & Characters
Design inhabitants (heroes, villains, royalty, villagers)
Learn simple character drawing and costume design
Add personality through facial expressions and poses
Week 5: Structures & Artifacts
Create architecture (castles, towers, temples) and objects (weapons, relics)
Explore shapes and materials
Optional intro to perspective drawing for buildings
Week 6: Final World Showcase Project
Combine all elements into a presentation: world map, key places, creatures, and characters
Create a poster, booklet, or large illustrated sheet
Group share and celebration of each student’s world

title: Intro to Drawing Course: Foundations
description:
Join this six-week drawing course in London and discover the essentials of creating art! Perfect for beginners, this comprehensive workshop will guide you through the fundamental techniques of drawing, step-by-step, allowing you to build confidence and skill over time.
This activity is a 6-week course, with 1 class per week, each lasting 1.5 hours, giving you a total of 9 hours of dedicated learning time. It's suitable for ages 13 and up.
Here’s a peek at what you'll learn how to do each week:
Week 1: Introduction to Drawing Tools & Line Work – You'll get an overview of essential materials like pencils, erasers, and sketchbooks. Learn basic line types such as contour and gesture, and loosen up with fun warm-up exercises like blind contour drawings.
Week 2: Shapes and Forms – Explore how to draw using basic geometric shapes and understand how to transform 2D shapes into 3D forms like cubes, cylinders, and spheres. You'll practise drawing simple objects from observation.
Week 3: Shading and Texture – Get to grips with the basics of light and shadow. You'll learn different shading techniques, including hatching and blending, to add depth, and discover how to create various textures such as wood and fabric.
Week 4: Proportion and Composition – Work from reference materials, focusing on objects and still life. You'll be introduced to basic measuring techniques for proportion and learn tips for framing your subjects and composing your drawings effectively.
Week 5: Perspective Basics – An introduction to one-point perspective will show you how to draw simple spaces like rooms or streets. You’ll learn how to combine form and depth to create more realistic scenes.
Week 6: Creative Project & Review – Apply all the techniques you've learned throughout the course to create a final drawing. There's an optional theme, such as a fantasy scene or your favourite object, to inspire you. The class concludes with a review session offering positive feedback on your progress.
All materials needed for the course will be provided, so you just need to bring your enthusiasm! You'll gain not just technical skills but also a fresh outlook on the world around you, culminating in a finished drawing (or more!) to proudly take home.

description:

You'll also leave with a stronger technical foundation and the confidence to continue recycling and working with silver independently.

title: Intermediate Jewellery Workshop: Keum Boo Masterclass
description:
This exciting in-person jewellery making class is held in Camden Town, London NW1.
Some previous experience of making silver jewellery is required so that there is also time for the key part of the day - adding the gold highlights using the technique of Keum Boo.
Keum Boo is an ancient Korean technique that uses a combination of pressure and heat to fuse pure gold into the surface of a piece of silver. The gold foil can be cut into shapes and is applied to the surface of a finished piece of jewellery.
Add to your existing silver or silver clay jewellery making skills, while having a fun day out. Recommended for those who have completed at least one beginners level silver jewellery making course or silver clay jewellery course, or similar.
This course (and all my courses) is designed for adults. I do not currently offer classes for children and teenagers.
During this full-day class, you'll spend the morning creating one or more simple pendant or earring designs in sheet silver or in silver clay, then in the afternoon we will prepare these pieces and use them to add the pure 24ct gold foil details and then give the pieces a final polish and / or apply patination to give a greater contrast to the designs.
Depending on the size of your designs, you will end the day with at least two pendants or pairs of earrings in solid silver, with decorative highlights in gold - to ensure we have time in the afternoon for the Keum Boo - these designs cannot be too large or complex in design - we need to get the basic piece/s finished before lunch!
There will also be a limited selection of previously made blanks to practice the Keum Boo technique on, or you are also welcome to bring your own previously made items that you would like to decorate.
With a small group size of just 3 students, your experienced instructor will guide you through the process, ensuring you feel confident every step of the way.
All the materials you need will be provided, so simply come along on your own or with friends to enjoy a fun and creative day. As you create your custom silver pieces, you'll experience the satisfaction of seeing your designs come to life. By the end of the class, you'll have at least two beautifully polished silver pendants with gold details ready to wear.
Join this relaxing jewellery making class and take home not just your new skills, but also beautiful solid silver jewellery that you can proudly wear or give as a gift. Don't miss out on this opportunity to learn, create, and have a memorable day!

title: Jesmonite Sculpture Course
description:
Whether you want to create unique gifts for the ladies in your life this Mother's Day or you're after a new hobby to let your creativity soar, this two-day sculpture course in London will see you getting hands-on experience working with Jesmonite — a uniquely versatile material.
Jesmonite can be used to replicate the appearance and texture of any surface finish, and even the finest of detail. It can mimic the appearance of materials such as stone, wood, leather and fabric. It is strong and durable, can be pigmented to any colour and used to create decorative surface effects.
It is often used as a lightweight alternative to stone and concrete, and has become an increasingly popular material widely used by artists, designers and prop-makers.
This two-day course will explore the different applications of Jesmonite under the tutelage of an experienced maker. Through a combination of live demonstrations and hands-on activities, you'll be constructing geometric and curved forms, creating decorative effects using pigment, and learning how to replicate other materials and textures using Jesmonite.
During the course you'll learn:
Day one
Introduction to the material, experimentation with mould making techniques using Polypropylene sheets that can be cut, scored and folded to make geometric and curved moulds relatively quickly that you will cast into.
You will learn how use Jesmonite pigments, create decorative effects such as Terrazzo and mar- bling, join objects together using Jesmonite and finishing processes.
Day 2
You will learn how to make a simple Silicone mould to mimic another material such as leather, fabric or wood and will learn how to laminate hollow castings with Jesmonite using Thixotrope and Quadaxial glass reinforcement.
You'll leave the class with a finished piece to keep forever or give as a one-of-a-kind gift, as well as the skills to continue casting to your heart's content. Whether you're making practical objects or expressive sculptures, you'll love discovering this fantastic material in a fun, relaxed environment.

title: Private Tambour Beading Embroidery Class
description:
Embroidery hooks originated in India and China before being used in France, in the 19th century. Today, the delicate work of tambour beading can be seen on most luxury catwalks such as Chanel, Dior and Louis Vuitton.
During this class, you will be introduced to the intricate art that is tambour beading. Tambour beading is a special embroidery technique which consists of using a small hook to create chain stitches and neatly applying beads and sequins to fabric.
Along the way, you will learn how to set up a see-through silk organza fabric on a slate frame. Then, you will practise the chain stitch with the hook in every direction. You will use fine couture materials such as glass beads, bugles and sequins and learn how to attach them to your delicate fabric.
You will be shown couture samples to get inspired and see how this beautiful and rewarding technique can be used. Tambour beading is a challenging technique to learn but the results are highly rewarding!
What you'll get
The fabric, beads, sequins and thread are included and are yours to keep.
The frame, tambour and scissors are not to be taken away but they will be provided during the class if needed.

title: Glass Fusing and Slumping Course
description:
Are you looking for creative things to do in London? Come and spend the weekend discovering a new skill at this hands-on glass fusing course in Camberwell!
Glass fusing is the technique used to bond colourful glass pieces together by melting the glass at a high temperature in a kiln. While slumping involves moulding the heated glass into beautiful shapes in the kiln.
During this two-day fused glass course, you'll have fun learning the ins and outs of these two methods and unleash your creativity on your own DIY projects.
Whether you're a beginner or more experienced in fused glass art, this workshop is a brilliant first step into the rewarding and accessible activities of glass fusing and slumping. With guidance from an expert teacher, you'll be amazed at the pieces you create!
In this course, you'll cover:
How to cut glass.
Using glass powders, frits and stringers.
Making textures.
Fusing at different temperatures.
Fusing in layers.
Fusing insertions.
Slumping as part of the fusing process.
Slumping after fusing into moulds.
Kiln firing and preparation.
By the end of this fused glass course, you'll have a beautiful creation to call your own and all the skills needed to continue your new favourite hobby!
This course is suitable for over 16s only.
