title: Intermediate Joinery: Dovetail Joints (2-Day Weekend Course)
description:
The dovetail is the signature joint of fine woodworking: strong, beautiful, and unmistakably handmade. In this two-day weekend course at POW Workshops in London, you'll learn to cut dovetails by hand with real precision.
Where Beginner Joinery Workshop: Frame Joints covered the joints used in frames and structures (halving, bridle, mortice and tenon), Joinery 2 focuses on the joints used to make containers of all kinds: boxes, drawers, cabinets, and chests. These are the joints that let you start building real furniture.
Here's what you'll cover:
Through dovetails: the classic, with its distinctive interlocking pins and tails
Half-lap dovetails: a refined variation used in drawer construction
Mitred dovetails: the most challenging, where the joint is completely hidden from view
Precision layout and marking, because dovetails demand accuracy
Sawing and chiselling to tight tolerances, developing the fine motor control that makes hand-cut joints fit perfectly
Understanding grain direction, and why it matters for joint strength and appearance
This course builds directly on the skills from Joinery 1. You'll be expected to be comfortable with basic sawing, chiselling, and marking before you arrive. If you've completed Joinery 1 or have equivalent experience, you're ready.
Taken together, Joinery 1 and Joinery 2 give you the complete foundation for furniture making. Frame joints for structures, dovetails for containers. From here, you can start building real pieces.
What you'll get
A set of beautifully hand-cut dovetail joints and the skills to incorporate them into your own projects. All tools and materials are provided.
What's next?
If you want to put your new skills into a real project, try Woodworking Workshop: Build a Three-Legged Stool, a two-day weekend build using traditional wedged through tenons. Or continue developing your skills with our workspace memberships, where you'll have access to the full workshop to work on your own projects.

title: Digital Photography Course - Level 2
description:
If you're looking to become more proficient behind the camera, this digital photography level 2 course is the perfect workshop for you. This two-day activity combines complex theory with practical exercises – such as location shooting and equipment demonstrations – to give you the advanced tools you need. You will learn the photography techniques required to create the professional and creative photographs you’ve dreamed of capturing.

Throughout this photography course, you will learn:

Light – Understand the colour and behaviour of light, including natural, artificial, direction, shape, form and quality.

Camera settings – Explore multiple settings and commands on DSLR cameras.

Lenses – Learn about lens selection, accessories and the fine adjustment of your lens and focusing.

Advanced focus – Learn about hyperfocal distance and how to take sharp images of still or moving objects.

Light meter – Metering your subject and metering modes explained in depth.

White balance – Understand how to achieve correctly colour-balanced images.

Exposure – All intermediate-level exposure photography techniques are covered, including exposure bracketing, exposure compensation and the magic triangle dynamics.

Histograms – Learn how to read histograms and benefit from this info to achieve better-balanced exposures.

Flash – Discover how to achieve greater images using your flashgun or speedlite.

Accessories – Learn about camera accessories that can enhance photographs, including reflectors, diffusers and light shapers.

Above all, this course will show you the importance of ‘making’ rather than ‘taking’ a photograph. You'll leave with a renewed perspective, equipped with the knowledge of how to confidently create beautifully composed images.

title: Introduction to Oil Painting Course
description:
Step into the rich world of colour, texture, and light with this inspiring 10-week introduction to oil painting. Designed for beginners and improvers alike, this course offers a friendly, structured journey into one of the most expressive and rewarding mediums. Drawing on classical foundations of observation, tone, and composition, each session will gently guide you through the building blocks of painting – from preparing your surface and mixing harmonious colours to capturing light, depth, and atmosphere on canvas. You’ll discover timeless techniques used by the masters while learning how to bring your own fresh, modern energy to them.
Through a blend of short demonstrations, guided exercises, and personal exploration, you’ll learn to:
Set up your materials and workspace with confidence
Mix luminous colours using a limited palette
Understand tone and value to create form and depth
Experiment with brushwork, layering, and texture
Build your own visual language rooted in classical technique
With small class sizes and individual guidance, there’s plenty of space to explore at your own pace and ask questions along the way. By the end of the course, you’ll have developed the skills, insight, and confidence to continue your oil painting journey, with a strong foundation and the beginnings of your own portfolio.

title: Direct Method Mosaic Workshop: Full Day
description:
If you're looking to develop your creativity with fun activities in London, look no further than this hands-on mosaic class in Holborn!
Guided by an expert mosaicist, this one-day workshop will provide an in-depth introduction to the beautiful world of mosaic, covering basic history, the evolution of mosaic over the centuries and most importantly — making!
You'll create a stunning piece using the direct technique, where the tesserae (individual tiles) are glued directly onto wooden support following a pre-made design from your teacher using long-lasting adhesive.
In this workshop, you'll cover:
Introduction to the course and the technique.
Selection of the design and materials.
How to transfer/ draw an image to prepare the creation of a mosaic.
How to cut and shape tiles to create your own mosaic using mosaic nippers.
How to create a mosaic using Andamento (layout) technique.
The direct method: glueing your tesserae directly onto the wooden support.
How to complete and grout your mosaic.

title: Hand Stitched Leather Bag Course
description:
This is a practical two-day group tuition during which you will receive an overview of basic leather craft and hand sewing skills and techniques and create your own hand-sewn leather bag to take home with you.
The class will take place in our London workshop, where you will see how a leather craft studio is equipped and receive practical demonstrations of common leather and bag-making methods.

Gained an understanding of leather types and tanning methods
Been instructed on the use of common fastenings and closure techniques

Learned how to saddle stitch leather and understood the different tools and materials used in the technique
Understood and practised leather craft techniques such as beveling and burnishing
Created your own hand-stitched leather bag to take home with you

description:

title: Pewter Casting Sculpture Course
description:
If you've ever wanted to try your hand at metal sculpture but weren't sure if it was right for you, this four-day course in London will let you get to grips with the ancient art of pewter casting. Under the expert tutelage of an experienced sculptor, you'll be making your own design in wax or clay before learning how to cast it in beautiful pewter to create a stunning work of art.
Pewter is a brilliant metal to use for beginners, as it's lightweight, soft enough to sculpt and has a relatively low melting point, so no need to set up any complicated equipment. Over the course of four sessions, you'll learn how to harness these qualities for yourself as you're guided through the complete process of making your sculpture to keep forever or give as a one-of-a-kind gift for someone special.
The course will cover the following:
Day one
You'll experiment with different waxes to make a small sculpture to cast. (You may also bring in a wax you have already made to cast if you have one.)
Day two
You'll add casting ‘runners’ and ‘risers’ to your wax sculptures in preparation for casting, then make plaster mould burn out in an oven.
Day three
You'll cast your design in pewter and clean it up afterwards.
Day four
You'll finish your piece with polishing, patination and working cold pewter. You'll also pick up some tips on setting up at home.
Whether you're coming along yourself or treating the artist in your life to a unique birthday gift, this course is a brilliant opportunity to learn some time-honoured techniques for beginners and experienced sculptors alike.
Please note:
The cost of this course includes 1 kilo of pewter, any additional will be charged at £70 per kilo.
Each session includes a one-hour break for lunch; this is included in the stated class duration.

Finish off wax.

Wax gating.

Second dip.

Burnout bronze moulds.
Puttying up shells.

Breakout moulds.
Fettling and chasing.

Patination.
Final finishing.
Pop up exhibition.

title: Cyanotype Printmaking Class: Botanical Blueprinting
description:
Make your own cyanotype prints using historical printmaking processes and create some unique images of plants at this interesting craft class in London.
This hands-on printing workshop introduces you to the basics of the cyanotype printmaking process discovered in 1842, using watercolour paper, cyanotype paint and UV light to create your very own botanical images.
Explore the history of early photography and make some interesting blueprints from dried botanical specimens in this unique printmaking class. You'll be guided throughout the making process by your talented teacher and you'll learn lots of interesting facts about historical printmaking as you craft.
The cyanotype printing process allows you to create beautiful floral Prussian blueprints - join this craft workshop and learn about the history and chemistry of this method and make some unique pieces of botanical art to take home with you.
Come with your friends or kids to experience an enjoyable creative craft and learn new skills. It's a fun workshop to try if you're looking for things to do in London. By the end of the session, you'll have a new appreciation for printmaking and you'll go away with the basic knowledge of this crafting process, allowing you to continue cyanotype printmaking on your own. You'll also have some great botanical images to keep or share with loved ones!

Everything you need to create some lovely botanical prints to keep, hang on your wall or gift to a friend!

description:

Course schedule:
Day one - street photography
Walk the streets of London and learn about Documentary and street photography. In this class, you will learn to shoot on the move in different environments and capture moments that tell a story.
Day two - portrait photography
Working with a portrait photographer, you'll develop your own style and practice techniques. This is a great chance to experiment with aperture to capture emotion, change the lighting to give your portraits a different feel, and play with composition and framing. You'll also learn how to work with a model.
Day three - food/product photography
In this class, you will learn how to take striking images and learn about the commercial side of product photography. There will be hands-on experience with creative set-ups and arrangements for close-ups, you'll get to grips with aperture to create texture and interesting backdrops, and you'll learn how to light your subject.
Day four - wildlife photography
In the fourth class, you'll be observing and photographing wild animals. This is a great way to develop your staking and timing skills for effective images. Plus you'll experiment with different camera modes.
Day five
The final class will involve examining your portfolio and workflow. You'll pick up some basic editing principles on how to enhance your images and receive critique from your teacher.

description:

What is Powertex? It’s used in mixed media projects of all kinds from garden fairy houses and figure sculptures to paintings and jewellery. But what exactly is it?
Here’s some things you should know about Powertex:
It’s water-based
It’s non-toxic
It’s environmentally friendly
A universal medium that can be used to sculpt fabric
A liquid that can be used to harden natural fibres including textiles, paper, card, and leather.
It can be combined with Stone Art powder to make an air-drying clay
It comes in a variety of colours as well as transparent
It’s adhesive for use with sand, stone, plaster, wood and metal (for example) in mixed media projects, canvases, sculptures, jewellery making and much more
It’s a brilliant way to upcycle old fabrics and just about anything else
It can be used to create weatherproof art such as garden ornaments and signs, glasses and more! Glasses will be hand washable.

Eco-friendly lifestyle: Take your newfound knowledge and passion for upcycling beyond the workshop. Embrace a more sustainable way of living by incorporating eco-conscious practices into your daily routine.
Join the movement: Be a part of a community that cares about the environment and believes in the power of crafting to make a difference. Share your creations, inspire others, and celebrate the journey to a greener planet together!

During this workshop, you will learn the fundamentals of working with wool fibres, including how to blend and lay them out to create stunning textures and patterns. Lesley will guide you through the process of using a resist for 3D work, allowing you to create unique and intricate designs for your felt flower.
Through hands-on practice, you will acquire the skills to make and fuse three individual felt components, which will come together to form your very own 3D flower. Lesley will be there every step of the way, providing demonstrations and offering personalized help and advice to ensure your success.
The workshop fee includes a pack of high-quality wool fibres and all the necessary feltmaking equipment. Additionally, light refreshments will be provided to keep you energized throughout the class.

title: 3D Felted Vessel Workshop
description:
In this immersive workshop, you will embark on a journey into the ancient art of feltmaking. Discover the rich history of this craft that has been utilized for centuries by nomadic cultures to create essential items such as carpets, clothing, and even portable homes called yurts. With the guidance of experienced artist Lesley, you will dive into the world of 3D vessel making using the wet felting technique.
Under Lesley's expert instruction, you will learn the essential skills needed to create stunning 3D vessels. From blending and laying out wool fibres to incorporating other fibres for surface decoration, every step will be carefully demonstrated and explained. You will also explore the use of a resist for 3D work and the techniques required to manipulate your creation, giving it shape and intricate detail.
Worried about materials? Rest assured, the workshop fee includes a pack of wool fibres, as well as other fibres for decoration. Additionally, you will have access to all the necessary feltmaking equipment during the workshop. If you prefer, you are welcome to bring your own fibres, as long as they are suitable quality wool unspun roving or tops in a medium micron weight.
Lesley recommends breeds such as Shetland, Finn, Swedish or Swiss, Gotland, Bergshaf, but Merino can also be used with extra layers for added sturdiness. Don't have the right fibres? Not to worry, Lesley will have a selection of extra fibres available for purchase on the day.
This class is an amazing opportunity to not only learn a traditional craft but also unleash your creativity in a supportive and friendly environment. Take home a beautiful and unique 3D vessel that showcases your newfound skills and artistic flair. Let the transformative power of feltmaking guide you on a creative journey like no other.

title: Framed Felted Memory Sampler Workshop
description:
Feltmaking is one of the oldest textile crafts in the world, used in nomadic cultures for centuries as a way to make carpets, boots, clothes and portable homes known as yurts. Today it is also a popular textile craft that allows you to create unique practical and artistic items from 2D art to sumptuous wearables.
In this workshop you will learn how to make a 2D wet felted memory sampler to create your own unique reminder of a significant life event, special holiday or another treasured memory. For example, the sampler could capture the colours of the landscape after a once-in-a-lifetime trip, or mark a wedding or anniversary.
The workshop fee includes a box frame, wool fibres, silk fibres and other materials but you are encouraged to bring something of your own to incorporate, such as fabric scraps, a piece of lace, knitting yarns or even buttons. It could be a piece of a favourite item of clothing that you no longer wear e.g scarf, jumper, blouse; a piece of a wedding dress or baby’s first outfit; or the buttons or trimming off a loved but now unworn item of clothing. Almost any fabric can be used, but natural fabrics such as silk, linen, wool or cotton work best. As the sampler will shrink as it is felted it is best to bring pieces that are A5 – A4 size that you don’t mind cutting up.
During the workshop you will learn how to:
Blend and lay out wool fibres, - How to apply fabrics, lace, knitting yarns etc
How to manipulate the wool and other items into a finished piece using the wet felting technique
How to further embellish and mount your sampler into a box frame that will be supplied as part of the workshop fee.
Lesley will demonstrate each step and give students individual help and advice.

title: Brush Lettering Workshop: Create Your Own Framed Print
description:
Join this brush lettering class in London and discover the calming art of modern calligraphy at Arch 61 in New Covent Garden Market.
Perfect for first-timers, this hands-on workshop provides a gentle introduction to lettering, helping you create personalised artwork that’s ideal for your home or as a heartfelt gift. You'll find a friendly vibe waiting for you as you settle in to explore this beautiful craft.
Throughout this relaxed and supportive session, you'll be guided through every step – from initial pen control to finishing your very own masterpiece. You'll start by mastering basic strokes and letterforms before moving on to layout and composition. By the time you're finished, you'll have designed a framed piece featuring a word, name, or quote that carries your own unique signature.
During the workshop, you will:
Learn brush pen techniques and lettering fundamentals – Get to grips with the basics of using a brush pen.
Practice strokes, letterforms, and word building – Build your confidence as you see your style develop.
Explore layout and composition for your final design – Learn how to balance your artwork for a professional look.
Create a personalised hand-lettered artwork – Express yourself through your chosen words.
Take home a framed piece ready to display – Walk away with a handmade keepsake you'll be proud to show off.
There's no need to worry if you've never tried this before. This class is all about low-pressure fun, offering a mindful break from the daily grind in a creative London setting.
This experience is a wonderful way to switch off and find your spark. You'll leave the session feeling revitalised, with a custom piece of art and the skills to continue your new favourite hobby at home.
What you'll get
Tombow black dual brush pen.
Pencil.
Guided practice sheets – Includes pen techniques, mark making, full alphabet, and word guides.
5 sheets of practice paper.
High-quality smooth card for your final artwork.
Frame for your finished piece.

title: Lace Bowl Machine Embroidery Workshop
description:
If you're the proud owner of a new sewing machine and would love to discover some of the amazing things you can do with it, learn how to use free machine embroidery to create a beautiful stitched bowl at this fun sewing class in Thames Ditton.
Under the tutelage of an experienced teacher, you'll have fun learning how to use water-soluble fabric, trap threads inside it and stitch on top of it to create a wonderfully lacey effect. Enjoy the fascinating process as you wash away the fabric to leave your delicate stitching in place. Experiment using different colours to create a multicoloured bowl that is strong and sturdy once dry. With this technique the possibilities are endless!
Don't worry if you're a complete beginner, as you'll have all the help you need from your friendly, knowledgeable teacher. You'll leave with your beautiful bowl in hand, as well as a head full of new knowledge about your sewing machine that you can put to good use in the future.

title: Collage Workshop: Make a Memory Book for Special Celebrations
description:
Pre-personalise Your Session

Once you've booked we'll send you a Google form for key information like colour preferences, playlist preferences, the favourite things of the special hen/birthday person so that we can source and create collage materials specific to them. At this stage you can also organise any special touches like custom cocktails or treats for the day.




Send Us Your Treasured Photos

We'll provide your group a link to a photo drive where people can drop as many photos as they like. We'll print these in various sizes for the day.




Settle in on the Day

Join us in our space in Deptford, grab a drink from the bar, get settled in your seats and we'll do a round of introductions - even if you all know each other, it's a good way to settle into the space




Make Your Collage

To loosen up and get familiar with the materials available we'll prepare a prompt that everyone can have a go at collaging. Whether it's collaging a dress for the bride-to-be, a cake for the birthday person or something specific to the person and group in question - these are great things to have in the book and also a nice way to get started




Enjoy a Trip Down Memory Lane

Now it's time to get your hands on the photos! We'll lay them all out on a table and you can fight over them with the other people in the group to compose your pages.




Your Completed Collage

At the end we'll take some time to look at everyone's pages before popping them all in the album to take away as a brand new bumper book to treasure and look back to



Celebrate a big milestone with creativity and connection. In this collage workshop, you and your group will transform cherished photos into a collaborative keepsake album. Perfect for hen dos, birthdays, or any special occasion, this experience combines laughter, creativity, and meaningful memories.
We’ll begin with a playful warm-up collage that gets everyone familiar with the materials and sparks conversation – for example, collaging the bride a one-of-a-kind wedding dress or creating a whimsical birthday cake for the guest of honour.
From there, each participant will create two unique pages for a beautiful 30x30 photo album with removable pages. Using the photos you’ve provided in advance (which we’ll print for you), along with our carefully curated materials, guests can collage, decorate, and add personal notes. This collaborative process gives everyone the chance to contribute their creativity and stories, resulting in a heartfelt book that captures the spirit of the celebration.
The final album is a truly special keepsake, brimming with laughter, love, and personal touches – something to treasure long after the party ends.
A selection of teas, coffees, and biscuits is included during the class. We also have a licensed bar with drinks and snacks available to purchase and can arrange drinks packages, special treats, cakes, or decorations on request to make your celebration extra special.
What you'll get
A 30x30 photo album with removable pages
Two collage pages designed by each guest
All materials provided, including scissors, glue, papers, magazines, and embellishments
Printed photos (from images sent in by participants before the workshop)
Guidance and prompts throughout to inspire ideas and make the process easy and fun

No knowledge or skill required.

In this two-hour workshop, you will discover and play using a variety of tie-dye techniques and natural indigo dye - the ultimate in instant gratification!

title: Mosaic Workshop in South West London
description:
Join this immersive mosaic lamp workshop in South West London and learn how to create your very own stunning piece of Turkish art. In this creative activity, you'll discover the time-honoured technique of how to arrange hand-cut glass and decorative beads into a beautiful, functional lamp that will bring warmth and character to any space.
Your experienced instructor will guide you every step of the way, making this workshop perfect for complete beginners. You can choose to follow classic Turkish patterns or create a unique design that expresses your own artistic vision.
The whole experience is designed to be a peaceful escape. You'll be crafting in an authentically decorated studio, with gentle Turkish instrumental music creating a serene atmosphere. As you work, you'll enjoy traditional Turkish hospitality, sipping on aromatic tea and sampling delicate rose delight.
Here's what you can expect from your session:
Settle into the atmospheric studio environment a few moments before the class starts
Select your preferred design approach – traditional or contemporary
Learn the careful art of arranging glass pieces and beads to create your unique pattern
Experience Turkish customs and refreshments whilst you craft
Receive clear instruction on the final steps to complete at home

description:
If you've got a new sewing machine and want to learn how to make the most of it, improve your sewing skills and have a fun time doing it with this foundation paper piecing workshop in Worcester Park.
Foundation paper piecing is used to create fabric designs accurately. It is sometimes used in making quilt patterns to help to get really accurate shapes but it is also often used for creating pictures from fabric. Come along and learn how it works and have a go yourself by making a lovely design to take home as a piece of fabric art.
Don't worry if you've never tried anything like this before, as you'll have the full support of your friendly teacher throughout the class, who'll make sure everything goes smoothly as you create your design. description:
Successful patchworking and quilting is part knowing what to do, and part practice.
Come along as and when you have a question, need help, want some time out to actually get some patchworking done, or want to have a go at a new technique. Each session will have a demonstration at the beginning and then you can practice that technique or seek help with your own project as needed. title: Music Notes Patchwork Workshop
description:
In this charming patchworking class, you will learn the art of creating beautiful music notes through patchwork. Not only will you get to make a pair of patchwork semi-quavers or quavers, but you'll also receive a kit and detailed instructions that will enable you to make more notes at your own pace. Whether you're a seasoned quilter or a complete beginner, this workshop is designed to cater to all skill levels.
Joining this workshop alleviates any fears or concerns you may have about creating music notes. The instructor will guide you through the process, ensuring that you understand the specific proportions and orientation rules that apply to these delightful symbols. Even if you don't read music yourself, you can rest assured knowing that the instructor will help you achieve a perfect representation of these notes.
Throughout the class, you'll work with various materials and fabrics to create your patchwork semi-quavers or quavers. With each step, you'll gain confidence and develop new skills in patchwork and quilting. The experience may be both exciting and fulfilling as you see your musical notes come to life under your fingertips.

The possibilities are endless, and this patchwork can be utilized for any project of your choice in your own time.

description:

You'll learn how to create beautiful, lasting prints using seasonal leaves and petals on specially treated textiles. Focus on composition, shape, and colour palettes as you craft your own unique pieces to take home.
If you're a first-timer, you'll fit right in. Your teacher will guide you through the process step by step, encouraging you to experiment and play with your designs in a supportive, friendly environment. Expect a hands-on experience with practical demonstrations and help whenever you need it.
Working with an array of plant-based materials is a wonderful way to switch off, and the process is quite cathartic as you watch the natural pigments unfold before you. You'll work with an experienced artist and tutor who will help you feel at ease throughout the session.
Learn how to transfer fresh flowers and leaves – Master the technique of hapazome on fabric.
Explore visual compositions and plant pigments – Discover how to arrange your foliage for the best results.
Create your own designs and play with different patterns – Experiment with different botanical shapes.
Develop visually rich textures and colour combinations – Mix and match seasonal flora.
Use specially treated fabric to make your prints last longer – Ensure your handmade keepsake stays vibrant.
You'll leave the class with a fresh set of skills and your own stunning botanical creations. It's a feel-good way to spend a few hours, leaving you feeling inspired and proud of what you've made.

Children

Cook and store fresh pasta.

title: Tagliatelle, Ravioli and Tortellini Pasta Making Class
description:
For real Italian pasta that blows you away, you need a real Italian “sfoglina” showing you how to make it! Join this tasty in-person London cooking class and master authentic, fresh pasta making with help from an expert.
In this hands-on workshop, you will learn the secrets to making pasta dough from scratch and shaping the perfect tagliatelle, ravioli, tortellini and other filled pasta. Immerse yourself in real Italian cooking culture and pick up all the secrets to successful fresh egg pasta making!
Learning how to make pasta is easier than you think. Even beginners can pick it up! You'll get plenty of advice from your teacher Valeria as you unwind and have fun in her home kitchen. Your Italian cooking session will be a mix of individual work, work in pairs and demonstrations from your chef.
Throughout your cooking class, you'll learn:
How to choose the right ingredients for perfect pasta dough and how to make variations of it.
The technique to get a smooth and silky texture.
How to use a pasta machine to roll out and shape fresh pasta.
How to shape tagliatelle by hand and with a pasta machine.
How to handle pasta dough to make different shapes out of it.
Some great ideas on different fillings and sauces to pair with them.
How to cook and store fresh-filled pasta.
If you're looking for team building activities or fun things to do in London with your foodie friends, come and learn all about Italian cooking together. At the end of the class, you'll sit down to enjoy your delicious homemade pasta.

Fresh egg pasta dough from scratch.
Tagliatelle, ravioli, tortellini and other filled pasta shapes.
Spinach and ricotta filling for stuffed pasta (other fillings available on request).
Brown butter, sage and parmesan shaves sauce to dress your pasta (other sauces available on request).

title: Moss Wall Terrarium Workshop
description:
Make the Base of the Wall

You will use a clay putty to create a structured wall that you can fix moss and hardscaping onto.




Add Moss and Hardscaping

Using mosses, driftwood and lava rock create the base of your wall




Continue to Build

Continue to add mosses and small ferns



Join this moss wall terrarium workshop in Bow and learn how to create your own lush, vertical landscape. Whether you’re a regular at our studio looking to level up your skills or a complete beginner eager for a fresh challenge, you’ll be guided through every step of this hands-on experience.
You'll start by discovering the fascinating history and science that makes these self-sustaining ecosystems work. After a helpful demonstration, it’s your turn to get stuck in. You’ll begin by crafting a clay wall within your glass cylinder vessel, which serves as the foundation for your living art. From there, you can add moss, bark, and even slate to design your own miniature steps, before standing the vessel upright to plant the base layer. While the focus is on mastering hardscaping with moss and ferns, you’ll also have plenty of other vibrant plants like Fittonia to choose from.
Everything you need is provided, including a 20cm x 15cm glass cylinder and a circular perspex lid to keep your greenery thriving. It’s a low-pressure environment where you can switch off, enjoy the tactile process, and connect with fellow plant lovers.
You'll finish the session with a sense of pride and a unique keepsake to display at home. This class is a wonderful way to rekindle your creativity and walk away with a flourishing piece of nature that'll continue to grow and inspire you.
Learn the science behind closed ecosystems – Understand how your terrarium breathes and thrives.
Build a vertical clay wall – Master the techniques of creating a stable, living backdrop.
Design with hardscape materials – Use bark and slate to add depth and texture to your scene.
Plant your base layer – Selection and placement of mosses, ferns, and tropical plants.
Take home your creation – A completed 20cm x 15cm glass terrarium with a lid.
Please note: The workshop lasts approximately 2 hours. If two people wish to make one terrarium together, please select the 'bring a plus one' ticket. Please arrive on time and let us know if you're running late!
What you'll get
A finished Moss Wall Terrarium to take away and watch it grow.

title: Eco Resin Tray Making Workshop
description:
STEP 1 —CREATIVE DECISIONS

Decide which tray to make and choose the base tray colour and terrazzo colours.




STEP 2 — MIX, COLOUR & ADD CHIPS

Mix your Jesmonite liquid and powder until smooth; the consistency should resemble thick double cream
Add your chosen pigment and stir until the colour is completely even
 Add your chosen terrazzo chips ✨




STEP 3 — POUR & CURE

Pour your mixture slowly and evenly into the mould
Tap the sides gently to release any air bubbles
Leave it completely undisturbed to cure.




STEP 4 — MINI BREAK

While we wait for the curing process, we’ll have a mini break.




STEP 5 — DEMOULD & SAND

Gently flex the mould and ease your tray out carefully
Sand progressively from coarse to fine grit sandpaper 🎨




STEP 6 — RINSE, DRY & SEAL

Rinse thoroughly under clean water and pat dry
 Once completely dry, apply a thin layer of finishing wax
Buff gently with a soft cloth for a beautiful, lasting finish.




STEP 7 — ADMIRE YOUR WORK!

Your one-of-a-kind terrazzo Jesmonite tray is complete — no two trays ever look the same. Yours is uniquely yours. 🖤

Artichoke and cumin dip – Mix a creamy, spiced dip that's perfect for sharing.

title: Ceramic Painting Workshop - the Classic Blue and White
description:
In this intimate workshop, you'll discover the timeless art of blue and white porcelain painting, learning three classic Chinese techniques to create your own decorated earthenware plate. You'll master traditional methods including Fengshui - shading, Pingtu - flat painting, and Gouxian -outlining, taking home a unique piece that showcases your newfound skills.
For those who might feel daunted by this ancient art form, rest assured that this activity is specifically designed for beginners. With only four participants per class, you'll receive plenty of personal guidance as you explore each technique at a comfortable pace.
What you'll learn:
Fengshui-shading techniques for creating depth and dimension
Pingtu-flat painting methods for solid areas of colour
Gouxian-outlining skills for precise decoration
Traditional composition principles
Throughout the session, you'll work on a generous 24cm earthenware plate, learning how to apply these time-honoured decorative methods. Your instructor will guide you through each distinctive technique: the subtle gradations of Fengshui-shading, the smooth application of Pingtu-flat painting, and the precise art of Gouxian-outlining.
This focused workshop will connect you with centuries of artistic tradition, while helping you develop your own creative expression. You'll leave with not only your finished plate but also an appreciation for the refined techniques that have made blue and white porcelain so cherished throughout history.
What you'll get
All necessary tools and materials, as well as firing and glazing One plate. When booked with ClassBento, it also includes shipping your plate to your address once they are fired.

Beginner-friendly.

title: Still Life and Nature Drawing Intensive Course
description:
Build strong drawing foundations through focused observation of natural forms in this six-session drawing course in London or online. If you've ever wanted to seriously strengthen your ability to capture the world around you, this technical intensive offers a supportive yet rigorous environment to develop your skills. Over six weeks, you'll move beyond casual sketching to master the core principles that underpin all fine art.
Working with beautiful natural subjects like plants, shells, and organic forms, you'll find a calming space to switch off from the daily grind and focus on the rewarding challenge of deep creation. This course is designed as a deliberate mission to gain tangible skills, offering guided correction and a structured progression that makes even complex techniques feel accessible.
Throughout the six sessions, you'll cover:
Observational accuracy – Learn how to train your eye to see like an artist.
Structural drawing methods – Master the art of breaking objects down into simple volumes.
Light and shadow – Understand tonal rendering, from highlights to deep cast shadows.
Proportion and spatial relationships – Discover how to translate 3D forms onto a 2D surface with confidence.
Texture rendering – Explore techniques for capturing bark, leaf surfaces, and organic irregularities.
Compositional still life – Learn to arrange and draw natural object groupings effectively.
By the final session, you'll have moved from seeing to truly observing, finishing the course with a sustained drawing that combines all your new competencies. You'll walk away with a solid technical grounding and a renewed sense of confidence in your creative practice.
Please note: Complete beginners are very welcome, though this course requires a higher level of concentration and practice than a casual one-off workshop.
What you'll get
Technical drawing instruction across 6 structured sessions
Demonstrations of each stage of the drawing process
Individual feedback and correction
Progressive exercises
Reference guidance for continued practice

title: Real Silver Gintsugi Workshop
description:
In this beginner's gintsugi workshop, you'll have the opportunity to experience the captivating art of mending broken ceramics with silver. Gain an understanding of the ancient Japanese technique that beautifully repairs pottery while enhancing its aesthetic appeal. Gintsugi is the silver cousin of kintsugi, gold repair. Genuine 23k gold can be added to your experience upon request, but the tools and techniques do differ depending on the metal choice.
Important note: This repair is not food safe, and only for decorative purposes.
Upon entering the workshop, any fears or worries will instantly melt away as you embark on this exciting creative journey. Led by our experienced instructor, you'll be guided through a step-by-step process that demystifies the art of gintsugi.
Throughout the workshop, you'll work with a variety of materials to create your own one-of-a-kind gintsugi pieces. This includes genuine silver, handcrafted tools specifically designed for this art form, as well as salvaged ceramics from local studios. Don't worry if you've never attempted this technique before – this class is designed specifically for beginners. You'll be amazed at the sense of accomplishment you'll feel as you witness your broken ceramics transform into unique, beautiful artworks.
This hands-on experience will not only teach you the art of gintsugi, but it will also provide you with a newfound appreciation for the beauty of imperfections through the philosophy of wabi-sabi. By the end of the workshop, you'll have your own gintsugi creations to take home and proudly display.
Don't miss out on this opportunity to learn a fascinating new skill and explore your creativity. Join us for an unforgettable workshop where you'll discover the art of gintsugi and create stunning pieces that celebrate the beauty of imperfection.

title: 3-Month Oil Techniques Painting Class
description:
In this engaging oil painting class in London, you will embark on a creative journey to discover the art of oil painting. Over a delightful span of 3 months and 12 sessions, each lasting 3 hours, you will delve into the world of colours, brushstrokes, and canvases while honing your artistic skills in a relaxed and supportive environment.
During the initial month, you will master the fundamentals and foundations of oil painting, including an introduction to oil painting techniques and materials. You will create intriguing monochrome paintings, explore colour theory, and have the opportunity to paint still life compositions - all while fostering your creativity and gaining confidence in your abilities.
As the workshop progresses into traditional techniques and developing styles, you will have the chance to replicate works by famous artists such as Monet, Van Gogh, and Matisse. By learning their distinctive styles and brushwork, you will further refine your own artistic expression and develop a deeper appreciation for different artistic approaches.
The final month of the workshop offers an opportunity for advanced techniques and personal projects. You can choose to focus on portraiture, landscapes, or a personal painting project, receiving expert guidance and feedback along the way. At the end of the workshop, you will proudly take home your completed personal work, equipped with newfound skills and knowledge in the art of oil painting.

Take home your completed personal painting and newfound skills in oil painting

You will be guided through each step of the process, from setting up your palette to varnishing and caring for your finished oil paintings. Get ready to unleash your creativity and immerse yourself in the wonderful world of oil painting in this inspiring workshop.

description:

title: Christmas Ceramic Making Class
description:
Lantern House

We begin by rolling out a smooth, even slab of clay. Using templates, cut out the front, back, sides, and roof pieces. We score and slip the edges, then carefully join each wall together. You’ll smooth the seams with tools and your fingers to make the structure strong. Add textures, tiles, chimneys, stars, patterns, or any details you like using stamps or sculpting tools. You’ll shape and attach the roof pieces, and you’ll paint them with underglaze colours. Leave it with us to bisque fire it and glaze it.




Angel Tea Light Holder

We begin by rolling out a smooth, even slab of clay. Using templates, you’ll cut the main body shape for your angel. We then gently curve and form it into a standing shape that can hold a tea light at the base. We score and slip the pieces, then attach the wings to the body. Smooth the joins with tools and your fingers so everything stays secure during firing. Now use underglaze paint, leave the piece with us to get fired, then glaze it ready for collection.

title: Hand Fan Painting Workshop
description:
Learn the art of painting your own Spanish hand fan in this hands-on workshop, led by a tutor who grew up in southern Spain, where hand fans are part of everyday life. They're not just used to keep cool in summer – they're gifted at weddings, birthdays, hen parties and Christmas too, often becoming treasured keepsakes passed down through families.
In this session, you'll design and paint your own Spanish hand fan using acrylic paint pens, in a workshop made to feel accessible for everyone. Whether you arrive with a clear idea, want to go completely freestyle, or have no idea where to start, you'll find plenty of stencils, inspiration and guidance on hand to help you feel confident – there's absolutely no pressure to be "good at art".
Choose your fan:
Classic fabric fan (£46) – made with plastic ribs and white fabric, with a matching protective cover included; the plain white finish is the perfect canvas for your design, and these fans are hugely popular in Spain for weddings, birthdays and celebrations
Traditional wooden fan (£52) – a beautifully compact wooden fan that's perfect for everyday use, with that iconic Spanish clack when you open it and a wonderfully traditional feel
Handmade artisan fan from Spain (£69) – crafted by local artisans in your tutor's hometown using wood and fabric, these are truly special pieces and ideal for a meaningful gift or keepsake; they can feel a little stiff when brand new but loosen beautifully with use over time
Whichever fan you choose, you'll leave with a beautifully painted piece that's entirely your own – a fun, hands-on keepsake to treasure, gift or add to a growing collection of personalised presents for future celebrations.
This workshop is also available as a private session for birthdays, hen parties, work socials and other celebrations – just send a message beforehand to check availability.
Please note: as all hand fans are brought over from Spain, certain styles are limited in number and can sell out.

description:

Sculpt cool details by hand

title: Three Course Italian Cooking Class for Private Groups
description:
Celebrate your next team building event, hens party or other private event in London with a delicious three-course Italian meal—made by you! In this Italian cooking class, you and your group will learn how to cook pasta, mains and desserts under the guidance of a qualified chef.
This is our most popular class as groups will gain a fantastic insight into the world of Italian cuisine. Everyone gets stuck in and has fun but also achieves a great sense of satisfaction seeing what they have prepared under the guidance of our Head Chef.
The cooking class begins with focaccia, olives and a chilled glass of Prosecco (or cappuccino, depending on the time of day), and then the fun part begins! You will start to prepare antipasti or fresh pasta. This will be followed by making a delicious main course with vegetable sides and a classic Italian dessert. Combining demonstrations with hands-on cooking, this beginner-friendly class is the perfect opportunity to learn some exciting new cooking skills while bonding with your group.
Once everything is cooked and ready, sit down at the table and enjoy your three-course meal with a glass of wine or a cold beer. Upon leaving the school we are happy to provide you with takeaway boxes should you wish to take home some of the food, and a full recipe booklet will be emailed to you within 48 hours of the class.
Dishes selection (select each of the following from our menu after booking):
One starter or pasta
One main or pasta
One vegetable side
One dessert
Team building and competitive cooking:
Any of our group classes can be given a fun, competitive edge. Teams will be judged not just on the flavour of the food but on presentation, timing and communication.
The chef will present a prize, chosen by you, to the winners. Ask for a list of prizes, such as signed cookbooks, homemade Italian biscuits and wine, when requesting your class or communicating with La Cucina Caldesi.

description:

You'll be guided by your talented teacher Camilla in her new garden pottery studio. Camilla will teach you the basics of working with clay for DIY pottery as you cover simple techniques, different types of clay, and how to build your very own pot, mug, or planter.

title: Botanical Dyeing Class for Children and Families
description:
Join this bundle dyeing workshop in London, a fun and beginner-friendly environment where children and families will each create a cotton bandana using flowers, leaves, seeds, and other botanicals. You'll learn the art of bundle dyeing in an atmosphere designed to be gentle, safe and enjoyable for all levels of experience.
During the workshop, you'll be guided on how to select natural materials and explore different techniques to create unique and unexpected patterns. Working with vibrant dyes and eco-friendly materials, you'll see stunning results as you engage in a process that's both soothing and meditative. It's a lovely way to unwind and enjoy some quality time together while getting hands-on with nature.
In this class, you'll:
Select your botanicals – Choose from a variety of flowers, leaves, and seeds to create your palette.
Master bundle dyeing – Learn the specific techniques required to transfer natural pigments onto fabric.
Create your patterns – Explore how to fold and tie your bandana for different visual effects.
By the end of the session, you'll have gained a wonderful new skill and a bespoke bandana imbued with your personal touch. You'll leave with a beautiful, wearable memory that serves as a heartfelt keepsake of your day together.

title: Valentine's Needle Felting Workshop
description:

In this hands-on workshop, you'll discover the techniques to create charming cartoon designs or personal artistic expressions on your clothing, transforming everyday items into wearable works of art.
Needle felting might sound technical, but it's a wonderfully accessible activity that requires no previous experience—just your enthusiasm and willingness to explore. You'll be amazed at how this simple technique can add character and whimsy to your wardrobe pieces.
Throughout this creative session, you'll work with soft wool fibres and special felting needles, learning how to blend colours and build texture as you bring your chosen design to life. The gentle, repetitive motion of needle felting creates a relaxing atmosphere where your artistic vision can flourish naturally.
By the end of the workshop, you'll have rejuvenated a beloved piece of clothing into something entirely personal and distinctive—a brilliant example of sustainable fashion with your own artistic stamp.

title: Dried Flower Bauble Making Workshop
description:
Join us for a beautifully festive Christmas workshop at the welcoming Admiral Hardy in Greenwich, where you’ll learn how to create elegant dried flower Christmas baubles using real flowers that we grow, harvest, and preserve ourselves. This hands-on bauble-making workshop is designed as a calm and creative escape during the busy festive season - perfect for slowing down, making something meaningful, and enjoying time around a shared table.
All of the flowers used in this workshop are grown by us and carefully dried using traditional preservation techniques. We work with seasonal blooms such as statice and dahlias, chosen for their colour, texture, and longevity once dried. During the session, we’ll share insight into our growing and drying process, explaining how flowers are preserved specifically for decorative use and how this affects colour, shape, and durability.
You’ll be guided step by step through the bauble-making process, starting with choosing a colour palette before learning how to carefully layer dried flowers inside clear baubles. Each guest will create a set of 2 Christmas baubles, thoughtfully designed to work beautifully together while still allowing room for individuality. Every bauble is completely unique, making each finished set a truly personal keepsake.
This bauble-making workshop is suitable for complete beginners - no previous experience is needed. The focus is on enjoyment, creativity, and gentle guidance rather than perfection. We provide a relaxed, supportive environment where you can take your time, ask questions, and enjoy the process as much as the finished result.
Your completed baubles will be finished with luxurious velvet ribbon, ready to hang on your Christmas tree or give as beautifully handmade gifts. Designed to last for years, these decorations become a cherished part of your festive traditions and a reminder of a slow, creative moment.
Hosted in the warm and welcoming setting of the Admiral Hardy in Greenwich, London, this Christmas workshop is also a lovely social evening out. Guests are welcome to arrive early or order drinks and food from the bar during the workshop, making it the perfect combination of creativity and relaxed festive indulgence. Whether you’re coming solo, with friends, or as a family group, you’ll be warmly welcomed.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll leave with your finished set of 2 dried flower baubles, new creative skills, and a deeper understanding of how flowers can be grown, preserved, and transformed into long-lasting decorative pieces. This workshop is ideal as a festive treat, a thoughtful gift experience, or a unique alternative to traditional Christmas activities.
We also offer private bauble-making workshops for groups, celebrations, and team events. Please get in touch to discuss bespoke quotes and dates.

title: Lino Print Christmas Cards Workshop
description:
Settle In

Grab a seat, get your tea or coffee order in or order something for yourself from the bar. We'll let you relax into the space before we get started with the class.




Learn the Basics of Carving

We'll cover the basics of safe carving with linoprint tools, advising on what it's useful to think about when approaching your design and familiarising you with the process




Get Designing

The fun part! Start drawing, googling and browsing our collage books to find inspiration for your card. Design on paper, transfer it to your block and carve ready for printing




Print Your Piece

Print your new design onto card blanks in colours of your choice – go as bold as you like or choose something more subtle; your call!




Fancy Some Glitter?

The cards will take a little time to dry, but that doesn't mean you can't decorate over them! Use our paints, glitters, gems and sequins to add little sparkly touches to your cards if you wish




Admire Your Creations

Your beautiful lino-printed Christmas cards are ready for you to give to your favourite people this festive season.



In this festive lino printing workshop in London, you’ll learn the basics of lino cutting and printing while creating your own Christmas cards. Starting with a 6x4" lino block, you’ll carve a design of your choice with expert guidance, before inking and printing onto blank cards. By the end of the session, you’ll have a small set of unique hand-printed cards ready to share with loved ones.
The atmosphere in our workshop space is warm, welcoming, and relaxed, making it the perfect setting to unwind and get creative. Tea and coffee are included, and if you’d like to make the session feel extra special, our bar is open with a selection of drinks available to purchase.
If you’d like to expand your creativity even further, you can add an extra piece of lino for just £1 to make two designs, or take home a full set of lino cutting tools for £10 so you can continue printing at home.
This workshop is beginner-friendly – no prior experience is needed. You’ll be guided through safe cutting techniques, how to transfer designs onto lino, and how to print cleanly onto card using simple methods.
Everything you need is provided, including a 6x4" lino block, carving tools, inks, and blank cards. You’ll also get to keep your lino block so you can continue printing at home.
You’ll leave the session not just with a set of gorgeous, hand-printed cards to share with loved ones, but with a newfound confidence in your creative skills.
At Something Good Workshops, we have a fully stocked bar with a great mix of drinks - from craft beers and cocktails to soft drinks and tea and coffee - so you can sip, snack, and have a proper good time! Got any special requests or dietary needs? Just let us know, we’ve got you covered!

title: Beginner's Guide to Crocheting a Granny Square
description:
Fall in love with crochet by creating a classic granny square! You’ll be able to combine beautiful colours to stitch this traditional crochet design, perfect for setting you up for so many other projects. Granny squares can be used to make blankets, garments and more – we’re here to help you get started with your first one.  

With the help of an Hobbycraft Artisan, you’ll learn how to crochet a granny square by using all the key techniques. You’ll use double and treble stitches, as well as learning how to decipher a granny square pattern and how to change yarn colours. 

There’s a kit included with the workshop to give you everything you need for the project. Within the 90-minute session, you’ll be able to create one granny square, though you can continue to practice making more once you’ve got to grips with all the skills. The kit even features a pattern for a granny square blanket to help you continue your adventure in crochet!  

This workshop is the perfect way to grow your crochet confidence, with tips and support from a pro! It’s ideal if you already have basic knowledge of the stitches but are looking to refresh yourself or develop further.

title: Felted Collage and Word Art Class
description:
Learn to make your own felted artwork at this creative textile art class in London.
Be inspired by the masters: Matisse cutouts, Braque birds or contemporary word artists, and create your very own felt painting. Or use clever wordplay and the graphic quality of text to create some felted slogan art.
You'll use pre-felt – a partially processed form of felt – to create your designs. This type of felt is perfect for collage-style imagery because of its propensity to be cut into clean crisp shapes. After you've prepped your collage, you'll use wet felt making techniques to bring the layers together into your finished work of art. Once dry, it can be embellished with stitches or beads.
The final stages of wet felting can be quite vigorous. If you have arthritis or a similar condition in your hands you may find parts of this process challenging. This does not mean you will not be able to undertake this workshop, just that it may take you a little longer to fully felt your work.
This London art class is suitable for all ages and skill levels, everyone can be creative with colourful felt and have fun making textile art even if you've never tried it before. Your expert teacher will guide you through the making process every step of the way.
As this is an in person class you'll be able to choose from a wide selection of pre-felt colours to create your artwork including your A4 backing piece. All the equipment you'll need will be provided by Tabletop Workshops and whilst Covid remains active participants will not share equipment.
A fun class to enjoy solo, with friends, colleagues or loved ones, or a great option to enjoy with larger groups for a team-building activity.
This class can only run with a minimum of three people. If the minimum number of makers isn't reached, you may be asked to reschedule to another date.
By the end of your craft class, you'll have your very own piece of felted textile art to take home with you. You'll also have a range of new felting and collaging skills to enjoy using for future projects.

title: Etching and Printmaking Course
description:
Embark on an immersive two-day etching workshop in London with Art Hub Studios to inspire your mind with new printmaking techniques.
This hands-on and intensive craft course is designed to introduce you to the essential aspects of the craft, providing you with the necessary skills to incorporate the techniques you learn into your own artistic endeavours.
Etching is a time-honoured printmaking method that involves engraving lines or marks into a metal plate's surface using an acid, known as mordant. This technique originated in the sixteenth century and has been extensively evolved ever since, allowing for a variety of both gestural and controlled marks.
To kick off day one of this workshop, you will focus on hard and soft grounds, allowing you to experiment with generating either precise, clear lines or softer, textured imprints. The second day delves into how different tones can be achieved through aquatints.
In this etching and printing course, you will:
Prepare plates including filing edges, degreasing, polishing, and applying ground.
Learn soft and hard ground etching for creating linear or textural marks.
Discover how to achieve tones through etching with aquatint.
Prepare paper for printing.
Learn to safely use oil-based inks and the etching press.
Finish your prints and sign an edition.
Please note:
Participants must be over the age of 18.
This course requires a minimum number of participants to run. If the minimum number of participants is not reached, we unfortunately have to cancel. We will notify you seven days before the start date and you will receive a full refund or we can transfer over to another date.

title: Landscape Painting Class
description:
Explore the beauty of nature in this landscape painting course in London. This inspiring activity is perfect for anyone, from complete beginners to more experienced painters, who wants to learn how to capture the great outdoors through art.
This course combines studio-based classes with fantastic outdoor field trips to iconic locations like Hampstead Heath – famously captured by the painter John Constable. You'll learn how to work confidently with a range of mediums, including oil, acrylic, watercolour, and mixed media. Your teacher will guide you through the key principles of landscape painting, from composition and colour theory to capturing the changing light and atmosphere of your surroundings. You will discover how to paint from both photographs and direct observation, developing your skills in plein air (outdoor) painting.
Throughout the workshop, you will receive one-on-one guidance and constructive feedback in a supportive group setting, helping you to develop your personal style and creative interpretation of the world around you.
In this landscape painting class, you will learn:
The foundations of landscape painting, from choosing materials to preparing your surface
How to work with different mediums like oil, watercolour, and acrylic
Techniques to capture light, shadow, and natural atmosphere
Composition skills for framing and balancing your scene
How to develop your sketching and observation abilities
The fundamentals of painting en plein air (outdoors)
How to explore different artistic styles to find your personal voice
Ways to use texture, layering, and mixed media to add depth
The process of taking a piece from initial sketch to a finished painting
How to receive constructive one-to-one and group feedback
You will finish this course with a newly honed set of artistic skills and the confidence to paint landscapes with authenticity, leaving with a portfolio of vibrant works that reflect your unique connection to the natural world.

With hands-on sessions at iconic London locations like Waterloo Station, Covent Garden, and the South Bank, you’ll learn how to quickly capture the essence of bustling urban life, from architecture to people in motion. By the end of the course, you will have a diverse sketchbook of urban scenes, improved skills in rapid sketching and visual storytelling, and the confidence to sketch the world around you with energy and clarity.

You will develop skills in:

- Master the fundamentals of quick urban sketching in real-time
- Learn to simplify complex architecture into basic shapes using perspective
- Develop your gesture drawing skills for capturing movement and energy
- Experiment with line weight and shading techniques to create depth and dimension
- Gain confidence in using colour and watercolour washes to bring life to your sketches
- Create contrast through light and shadow in cityscapes
- Produce a diverse sketchbook of on-location drawings from iconic London landmarks

description:

title: Tea Tasting Experience
description:
Orientation to Tea

We'll start with a quick orientation about tea. Where does it come from? What gives tea it's distinct flavour?




From Leaf to Cup

We'll learn about tea production and you'll experience the shape, texture and aroma of different dry tea leaves, before they're brewed.




Tea Tasting and Sensory Experience

We'll spend the majority of the course here, brewing and tasting 4 types of tea. From observing the aroma of the wet leaf and tea liquor to tasting the tea and noting the flavour profile, you'll learn the unique differences between each tea type. We'll also pair the teas with light bites to further amplify the tasting experience



Step into the rich, multicultural world of tea in this immersive tasting experience in London from Anaré - where tea, culture, and connection come together.
Hosted by a certified Tea Sommelier, in this welcoming class you’ll discover the essentials of tea: where it comes from, how it’s grown and produced, what shapes its flavour, and why the “perfect cup” depends on the tea you’re brewing.
Together, we’ll taste four distinctive teas from some of the world’s great tea cultures, including India, China, Taiwan, and Japan. You’ll explore black, green, white, and oolong teas through a full sensory experience — observing the dry leaf, noticing the aroma, tasting the infusion, and learning how each tea expresses its own character, craft, and story. We'll also sample a few bites that pair well with the teas and further amplify the flavours.
Along the way, you’ll gain practical brewing tips, cultural insights, and a deeper appreciation for the incredible variety within the world of tea. Whether you’re a curious beginner, a devoted tea drinker, or simply looking for a calming and memorable experience, this class is designed to be relaxed, engaging, and deliciously eye-opening.
You’ll leave with a new appreciation for tea, simple brewing guidance to use at home, and a selection of tea samples so you can continue your tasting journey after the class.
What you'll get
A gift pack of tea samples, along with brewing instructions to take home, is included.

title: Italian Through Words: Italian Practice
description:
Join us for an Italian speaking experience in London! Imagine spending a Saturday morning immersed in the Italian language -- writing postcards from imaginary cities, conjuring the smell of a market in Naples, inventing characters and stories, and sharing them with others. That's exactly what this workshop is!
Perfect for learners at A2 level and above, Italy Through Words is a creative, cultural half-day experience where Italian is not just studied -- it's lived. Through writing, conversation and storytelling, you'll explore the language from the inside, guided by the richness of Italian places, food, art and everyday life.
What to expect:
Writing from images, keywords and cultural prompts.
Describing Italian places, markets, piazzas and bars.
Writing a postcard from an imaginary Italian city.
Inventing short characters, dialogues and narrative scenes.
Guided conversation around Italian cities, food, music and cinema.
Sharing and reading your texts aloud with the group.
Grammar is not taught explicitly -- key structures are reinforced naturally through context and creative use.
You'll leave with new vocabulary, sharper communication skills, and your very own taccuino italiano -- a small personal collection of the texts you created during the day.

Three guided activities: writing, conversation and culture, and storytelling.
Visual and cultural prompts for every activity.
Pair and small group work throughout.
Collective sharing and reading of your texts.
A collection of everything you write on the day!

title: Adobe Lightroom Editing Class for Photographers
description:
Learn how to edit your images efficiently and creatively in this comprehensive Adobe Lightroom workshop in London. With the unique ability to process multiple images quickly, Lightroom is the perfect tool to help your photographs truly shine, whether you're making small adjustments or developing your own individual style.
In this six-hour class, you will learn the fundamental principles of editing and gain knowledge on an effective digital workflow. This hands-on activity will demystify the challenges of editing and make you a much more efficient photographer, enhancing both your creative and organisational skills. Using the latest version of Lightroom CC, you will be guided through each module, giving you a solid foundation and a deeper knowledge of digital imaging.
You will learn how to:
Navigate the Lightroom interface with confidence.
Use the ‘Library’ module for importing, using keywords, adding metadata, and tagging.
Master the ‘Develop’ module to make exposure, tonal, colour, and composition adjustments.
Export your images correctly for various uses.
Understand different file formats like RAW and JPEG.
Get to grips with image resolution and sizes.
Prepare your images perfectly for posting online or for print.
This class will completely reshape your post-production process. You will leave with the confidence and skills to manage and edit your images effectively, giving you more time behind the camera and the ability to produce consistently impressive results.

description:

title: Family Clay Workshop, Christmas Light Setting
description:
Welcome to My Studio

Settle into my pottery studio which is level access from the pavement alongside a big free and unrestricted car park.




Sit Together, Work Together

I set up a special space for this class with sat bench space so children are safe and at a appropriate height to work. You will be next to your child so as to encourage and work together.




Start with Pre Rolled Clay and a Simple Template

I will prepare even slabs on boards so the simple shapes can be cut quickly and we can progress to the creative bit!




Use a Template to Cut Your Base Shape

Easy to use card templates will guide cutting of the base shape which we will build onto.




Select Your Clay Tools

My collection of festive cutters can make simple shapes quickly and I’ll have lots of tools that we can use to print or stamp with too. Print, cut, model and shape, the more marks made the better the glaze will be!




Add Shapes and Modelling

Build up a border of festive elements which will decorate your light setting. I have lots of tools to hand.




Your Finished Work

I will guide your finished work through the firing and glazing processes and it will be ready to collect three to four weeks later.



A clay class for all the family, making festive light settings that can be a joyful part of your family celebrations for many years to come. The session is specially designed to include children under 12 in a seated space and is appropriately timed at an hour. [See Q&A to determine if this class is right for your children.]
Introduce all the family to working with studio-grade clay in a cosy and welcoming pottery studio with studio-grade materials and tools. All classes include full firing and glazing too, so the work will be functional and durable, preserving the outcome of your family’s creativity. Adults sit next to children so assistance can be offered alongside my instruction and demonstration.
Pre-rolled clay slabs are presented for cutting around a template. [We use entirely safe wooden knives.] Festive shapes can be cut with cutters or by hand, stamped or impressed, and applied to the surface. The more marks and texture, the better! title: Professional Accessory Pattern Making Course
description:
This pattern-making course teaches the fundamentals of creating patterns for bags and accessories, distinct from clothing.
Over four consecutive classes, you will develop key skills for expanding industry knowledge or starting your projects. You’ll learn pattern-making terminology, how to cut and prepare materials, and how to develop patterns based on shape and finishing techniques. You will also create glued prototypes using reinforcement materials to verify the accuracy of the patterns you have drafted.
The course covers simple gusset patterns, linings, seam allowances, cutting margins, and details like zippers, tabs, and straps. You will gain insights into related techniques such as marking, cutting, gluing, and reinforcing, along with an overview of leathers, vegan alternatives, reinforcements, and hardware.
By the end, you will have a set of patterns, simple prototypes, and a curated list of leather suppliers and tools, plus handouts for ongoing reference.
Summary of topics covered in the class:
Principles of pattern making and vocabulary for bags and accessories
Analysis of main bag and accessory constructions
Pattern making and development for two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes
Pattern making for simple linings, pockets, zip panels, handles, and other essential features
Material cutting using patterns
Assembling bag and accessory prototypes/mock-ups using reinforcement materials
By the end of the tuition, you will have:
Understood the principles of pattern drafting for accessory construction and created finished patterns to take home with you.
Learned how to use patterns to accurately cut materials.
Constructed and completed reinforcement prototypes to verify pattern accuracy.
Gained a basic understanding of the differences and best uses of leathers, vegan leathers, reinforcements, and hardware.

title: Introduction to Patchwork and Quilting Course
description:
If you've always wanted to try patchwork or quilting and you'd like to build your skills, try this beginner's course into basic patchwork and quilting. Working in a group environment with other like-minded budding quilters, you will work on a project of your choice with guidance and support in a sunny, relaxed environment.
Over a period of 5 courses, you will learn the various stages of patchwork: design, piecing, construction, stitching and bindings.
Concept: picking a design, colours, and size.
Piecing: sewing together fabric shapes to make the quilt top design.
Construction: attachment of backing fabric, wadding/batting to make a fabric sandwich.
Quilt stitching: decorative sewing to hold the layers together and form a design
Binding: the fabric strip that holds the three layers together at the edge.
Squares are the most basic shape in quilting. Each side of the square is the same size; cut on the straight grain; and the design is easily adapted by changing the size of the square.
Quilting is a creative, skilful, resourceful and relaxing talent to enjoy with new and old friends. The more you do it, the more ideas you generate, new pieces get created and the more exhilarating you feel losing yourself in the creative process.

This two-day course gives an in-depth approach to tambour beading and couture embellishments practised in the Couture houses of Paris today. It will cover the tambour beading technique using silk organza, seed beads, and bugle beads to cover the basic chain stitch and a vermicelli design. The second day will cover couture embellishments including ribbonwork, three-dimensional beadwork, and flowers.
18th-19th May 2-DAY COURSE 10am-4pm
Course outline:
Day one:
Learn how to create a solid framework for beading using silk organza on a rotating frame. This technique can be applied to larger frames to bead panels for a garment.
The main focus is on the basic chain stitch using a tambour hook correctly set up for silk organza.
Learn how to create a secure knot and change direction.
Seed beads and bugle beads are used to start tambour beading with a variety of techniques including vermicelli.
Day two:
Couture embellishments including ribbonwork are taught using a beading needle and thread to create a variety of texture and dimension with three-dimensional beadwork, clusters, raised beadwork, and brickwork for trims and edging.
Please remember although you will be learning in a mixed technique group, your class is tailored specifically to your progress.

description:

Everyone will have their own pottery wheel, and there is a maximum of 6 people per class.
Week 1 will be an intro to clay and handbuilding, looking into how to make a pinch pot.
Week 2 will see the wheel come into play! It begin with the teacher giving a demonstration, then students will start with the very basics - weighing the clay, centering, pulling up the walls and using your tools. You’ll have a go at both bowl and cylinder forms.
Week 3 will teach trimming and finishing your pots, using a different set of tools and refining your pieces before they go through the kiln.
Week 4 is glazing week - you’ll learn the basics of glaze and what it is, how to apply it and what to expect when your pieces go through the kiln.

Choose Your Book

Begin by choosing the book that will sit at the centre of your bouquet, along with a selection of flowers and foliage to build around it. This is where your bouquet starts to feel personal, whether you’re drawn to something soft and romantic or a little more simple and understated.




Build Your Bouquet

With clear guidance from your teacher, you’ll start arranging stems around the book to create the shape of your bouquet.
This part is relaxed and hands on, with simple techniques that make the process feel approachable even if you’ve never worked with flowers before.




Add Floral Details

As your bouquet begins to take shape, you’ll add more flowers and greenery to create depth, softness and balance. This is often the moment it all starts coming together, as the book becomes framed by the arrangement and your design begins to feel complete.




Wrap Your Bouquet

Once your bouquet is arranged, you’ll learn how to wrap it neatly using florist style paper. This stage gives the piece its finished look and transforms it from an arrangement on the table into something that feels thoughtful, polished and ready to gift.




Tie the Ribbon

Add the final details with ribbon and any last adjustments to the flowers or wrapping. Your teacher will be there to help refine the shape, so even the finishing touches feel easy and enjoyable.




Leave with Something Beautifuk

At the end of the workshop, you’ll head home with a finished flower bouquet with your next read inside. Alongside your bouquet, you’ll take away a lovely couple of hours spent making something by hand in a warm, book filled space.
