title: Columbia Road Floristry Class
description:
Enjoy Your Intro

Step into our bright studio near Columbia Road and let the scent of fresh flowers greet you. Settle in, meet your fellow budding florists, and get inspired by the vibrant colours and textures of the beautiful blooms waiting for you.




Pick Your Palette

This is where your unique creation begins. We’ll introduce you to our stunning selection of seasonal flowers and foliage. You’ll have plenty of time to explore the textures and scents, choosing the perfect stems to match your personal style.




Learn Floristry Secrets

Ever wondered how professionals create that perfect structure? We’ll guide you step-by-step through the classic hand-tying technique to build a balanced and beautiful bouquet. It’s a fun skill to learn, and we’ll be right there to help you master it.




Shape Your Design

Now you can let your creativity flow! Arrange your chosen stems, playing with height, texture, and colour to bring your floral vision to life. This is a wonderfully relaxed and mindful part of the workshop, perfect for enjoying the moment.




Wrap It Beautifully

Add the finishing touch by learning how to wrap your bouquet like a pro using our lovely, sustainable paper and string. It’s the perfect way to protect your creation for the journey home and make it truly gift-worthy.




Your Finished Bouquet

Step back and admire your gorgeous handiwork! You’ll head home with not only a stunning bouquet to brighten your space but also the skills and confidence to keep creating long after the class ends.



Just around the corner from the iconic Columbia Road Flower Market, our floristry workshops are inspired by the colour, abundance and ever-changing selection of flowers that fill the area each week.
At Studio Two Point, we love working with seasonal flowers and foliage, embracing what’s naturally at its best rather than following a fixed formula. You’ll be introduced to a carefully curated selection of stems before learning the foundations of floristry and hand-tying — from preparing and conditioning your flowers to creating shape, balance and movement within your bouquet.
From there, we encourage you to experiment. Play with unexpected colour combinations, different textures, heights and forms to create something that feels completely your own. There’s no single finished bouquet we’re all trying to recreate — everyone will leave with their own dreamt-up floral creation.
Along the way, we’ll share plenty of practical floristry knowledge too, including how to make your flowers last longer, which varieties dry beautifully, how to care for your bouquet at home, and some of the tips and tricks we use when working with flowers ourselves.
Designed to be relaxed, social and beginner-friendly, the workshop is as much about enjoying the creative process as it is learning a new skill.
What you'll get
All materials and tools to make a hand tied bouquet to take home with you.

title: Acrylic Painting Class - Aerial Seascapes Study
description:
Birds Eye View Seascapes Painting Class
Step into the world of contemporary seascapes and discover the beauty of painting from a birds-eye view perspective. This beginner-friendly class invites you to explore your creative side using a variety of materials, including acrylics, inks, Posca pens, and metallics, to craft a vibrant and captivating masterpiece you’ll be proud to take home.
What to Expect
This hands-on workshop is designed to be fun, inspiring, and accessible, even if you’ve never painted before. You’ll be guided through the process step-by-step, learning how to work with acrylics and inks to bring your seascape vision to life. From understanding colour combinations and adding shimmering metallic accents, every moment of the class is an opportunity to learn and express yourself.
Alma Tipon, founder of Paperdoll Art Studio and a professional artist based at Wimbledon Art Studios in London, will lead the session. With years of experience in painting birds-eye view seascapes, Alma will share her passion and expertise, helping you approach your work with confidence and creativity. Her seascapes are known for their dynamic blues, turquoise and touches of metallics that evoke both depth and elegance—a style you’ll explore and make your own.
Why Book This Class?
Explore: Learn to paint with fluid acrylic ink for flowing effects, use Posca pens for bold details, and add depth with gouache. These mediums combine to create dazzling, eye-catching seascapes.
Learn from Professional Artists: Practicing artists bring real-world experience to the class. You’ll benefit from expert insights and techniques, elevating this beyond your average painting class.
Fun & Supportive Environment: Whether you’re a seasoned artist or a complete beginner, this class offers a stress-free environment. You’ll feel inspired as you experiment with different mediums and styles, creating your own interpretation of a birds-eye seascape.
Take Home a Finished Artwork: By the end of the class, you’ll have a beautiful, completed artwork to proudly display, made with high-quality materials (time may vary depending on individual speed).
Great Value for Your Investment: You’ll get expert guidance, top-quality materials, and a relaxed, inspiring studio atmosphere. It’s more than just a class—it’s a personal investment in your artistic journey!
Important Note:
Please arrive 10 minutes early to ensure a smooth start. Unfortunately, late arrivals exceeding 10 minutes cannot be accommodated, as it would disrupt the ongoing class.
Fun Fact:
Alma’s artwork has been featured in prestigious exhibitions and publications, and her mini Birds Eye View Seascapes, valued at £485, are highly sought after. This class offers a rare chance to create a piece of significant value and beauty!
We look forward to welcoming you for a truly unique and enriching painting experience!
What you'll get
All professional-grade materials included
Tea & Biscuits/Chocolates
Complimentary glass of Rosé

title: Unique Extrusion Pottery Class
description:
Welcome & Get Settled

Come in, get cosy, and grab your apron. Pick your spot in the studio and get ready for a fun, hands-on pottery session.




Choose Your Piece

Decide whether you’d like to make a mug or a vase. This will guide how we prep your clay and plan your design.




Prep the Clay

We’ll get your clay ready and show you how to prepare it for extrusion, so it’s smooth and easy to work with.




Extrude Your “Sticker” Shapes

Use our signature extrusion equipment to create fun, pasta-like shapes—your sticker-style decorations/ charms for your mug or vase. Get creative with textures and patterns!




Build Your Piece

Learn how to assemble and construct your mug or vase using your extruded shapes. We’ll guide you step by step to make a piece that’s uniquely yours.




Paint & Personalise

Once your piece is built, choose from a range of colours and paint your creation. Add any final touches to make it truly personal.




Capture the Moment

Snap a photo with your masterpiece to remember your creative session.




Keep or Gift

You can choose the pieces you like to keep we’ll fire and glaze it for you (1 mug per person is included any extra firing & glazing fee: £10 for mug-size, £30 for vase-size), creating a beautiful finished piece perfect for keeping or gifting.



Discover the art of personalisation with extrusion.
Step into the creative world of Maison S. Sommet Pottery Studio and try your hand at our signature extrusion technique. This beginner-friendly workshop is a fun, hands-on experience – think of it like making pasta or sausages with clay! You’ll use the clay guns to create playful shapes, which you can turn into decorations and patterns for your mugs or vase.

A mug-sized container – perfect as a coffee mug, pen holder, planter, or toothbrush holder
A vase-sized piece – ideal for flowers or as a statement art object

Our relaxed and welcoming studio atmosphere makes it easy to experiment, unwind, and enjoy the creative process. It’s also a lovely activity for a date, a family outing, or a fun catch-up with friends.
Once your piece is shaped, you can decorate and paint it to make it truly personal. If you choose to keep your creation, we’ll fire and glaze it for you all included! (Firing of 1 mug per person is included - Extra piece firing & glazing fee: £10 for mug-size, £30 for vase-size), creating a beautiful finished piece perfect for keeping or gifting.

title: Speed Drawing Course
description:
Master fast, expressive drawing techniques to capture movement, form, and scenes with confidence.

Develop the skill of fast, expressive drawing in our engaging Speed Drawing classes. You’ll learn to capture movement, simplify complex subjects, and cultivate a unique style with speed and confidence. This art course progresses by building upon fundamental techniques, beginning with gesture and rhythm to infuse energy into your sketches. You’ll learn to break down objects into simple shapes, explore rapid figure and portrait drawing, and practise quick scene composition, encompassing environments and architecture.

By the end of the course, you’ll have a folio of dynamic drawings and a revitalised approach to sketching. You’ll acquire the skills and confidence to draw anytime, anywhere, transforming everyday moments into vivid, imaginative artworks. This drawing class will help you develop a unique style that blends speed with expressive details and experimental mark-making.

Speed Drawing Classes Content

You will develop skills in:

- Master the basics of gesture drawing, capturing movement and energy quickly
- Improve your ability to simplify complex subjects into basic shapes and forms
- Learn rapid figure drawing techniques, capturing human form efficiently in short poses.
- Explore different mediums such as pencil, charcoal, ink, and brush pens.
- Draw everyday objects rapidly, focusing on form and structure.
- Build a sketchbook full of dynamic and expressive quick drawings showcasing your progress.

title: Abstract Art Course - Colour, Texture, and Form
description:
This engaging abstract art course in London is the perfect activity for anyone wanting to explore the expressive potential of form, colour, and texture.
In a supportive and practical workshop environment, you will learn how to move beyond realism and develop your own unique visual language. Each week builds on the last, helping you expand your creative repertoire through a combination of artist studies and personal experimentation. You'll discover how to use mixed media, create compelling compositions, and translate emotions into abstract work. This course offers both structured guidance and the space for creative play, making it ideal for complete beginners and those looking to refine their abstract practice.
Throughout the course, you will cover a wide range of techniques and focus areas, including:
Introduction to abstract thinking – Learn how to move beyond realism and understand how abstract art communicates through shape, gesture, and mark-making.
Exploring colour theory – Discover the emotional power of colour and how to use it effectively in your work, experimenting with palettes to create mood and harmony.
Developing texture and surface – Use thick and thin layers of media to build up rich, varied surfaces with tools like brushes, palette knives, and sponges.
Composition and visual impact – Understand the building blocks of composition such as space, rhythm, balance, and contrast to shape your visual narrative.
Mixed media techniques – Combine various materials like collage and stencils to generate unexpected and dynamic results.
Intuitive and expressive process – Use intuition and spontaneity as creative tools, engaging in gestural drawing to loosen up and trust your instincts.
History and inspiration – Gain inspiration from key figures in abstraction and understand its development through major art movements.
Personal voice and reflection – Identify recurring themes in your work to develop a personal style and take part in reflective exercises to deepen your understanding.
You’ll finish the course with a portfolio of work that reflects your unique style, a strong foundation in key abstract techniques, and a freeing new confidence to trust your artistic intuition.

title: Still Life Drawing and Painting Course
description:
Be inspired by the enduring art of still life, and learn how to capture light, texture, and form using pencil, charcoal, and paint in this engaging workshop.

You'll immerse yourself in the timeless practice of still life, developing your skills in observation, composition, and rendering. From simple objects to complex arrangements, you'll learn how to capture the essence of form, light, texture, and colour. Throughout this drawing lesson, you'll be introduced to new techniques: mastering basic shapes and proportions, exploring shading and tonal values, and experimenting with textures like glass, metal, and fabric. You’ll also explore colour theory and painting techniques, learning to mix realistic colours and use expressive brushwork.

This activity will enable you to:

Discover the art of observation, learning to see and capture every detail of your subject.
Harness the power of light and shadow, transforming flat objects into three-dimensional works of art.
Refine skills in composition, arranging objects thoughtfully to create harmonious and engaging still life scenes.
Experiment with different mediums, from graphite to charcoal to watercolour, finding the perfect tools to bring your vision to life.
Develop a personal artistic voice, learning how to inject emotion and storytelling into every still life you create.
Complete a beautiful final painting, showcasing your growth and mastery of the still life art form.

By the end of the course, you’ll have a comprehensive portfolio of studies charting your artistic development, and a final piece that showcases your unique style. You’ll leave with a newfound appreciation for the beauty of everyday objects, and the skills to transform them into captivating works of art.

title: Bookbinding Workshop: Coptic Binding and Slipcase
description:
In this workshop you will learn how to make a Coptic bound book and a protective slipcase. The Coptic binding is a historical, non- adhesive structure, still popular today for its flexible and beautiful format. It has hard covers and exposed sewing on the spine and opens perfectly flat which makes it ideal to use as a notebook, sketchbook, photo album or to incorporate your own artwork or writing.
You will learn how to prepare the covers and sections and sew the book together. In the second half of the workshop, we will be making a bookcloth covered slipcase designed to fit the Coptic book. The slipcase is an open-edged box that leaves the spine visible while protecting the book. This workshop is suitable for complete beginners as well as those with some experience in bookbinding.

title: Life Drawing Class
description:
Join this life drawing class in London and discover how capturing the human form is one of the most effective ways to develop your hand-eye coordination. These sessions offer a wonderful way to switch off and clear your head after a busy day, providing a mindful break through the simple act of putting pencil to paper. Even established painters and illustrators return to these workshops throughout their careers to keep their skills sharp, making it a supportive environment for everyone to learn.

If you're a budding fashion designer, illustrator, or fine artist, these lessons are a fantastic place to start. You'll gain a deeper understanding of human anatomy and structure before moving on to more complex compositions. Your friendly teacher will guide you through a variety of techniques in a relaxed, low-pressure setting, ensuring you feel comfortable whether you're a complete beginner or looking for a creative refresh.

Throughout the session, you'll explore:

An introduction to artists using the figure – gain inspiration from historical and contemporary works.

Experimenting with drawing mediums – get hands-on with charcoal and pencil drawing.

Mark making – find your unique style through different strokes and textures.

Exploring basic anatomy – understand the shapes, silhouettes, and proportions within the body's structure.

Line and creating tone – learn how to add depth and dimension to your sketches.

Movement of the body – capture the fluid energy of different poses.

Expression by the model and artist – focus on the emotional connection and character of the subject.

To ensure you can truly master the art of drawing the human form, these classes use professional nude life models. There's no need to bring anything along with you as all materials, including high-quality paper, are provided. You'll finish the session with a newfound sense of artistic confidence and a collection of sketches that showcase your evolving talent.

Please note: these classes use nude models.

title: Abstract Painting Class
description:

Imagine painting in an artist’s studio, surrounded by inspiring artworks, flowers on the table, and relaxing background music — all while being guided by a practising artist to complete your piece.
This isn’t your typical paint and sip session. In our studio, you’ll actually pick up a few abstract painting techniques along the way.
What Is Abstract Art?
Abstract art focuses on expression, emotion, and experimentation rather than realistic representation. It’s all about colour, form, texture, and movement. Inspired by artists like Kandinsky, Rothko, and contemporary creators, this workshop explores the freedom and boldness of abstract composition. There’s no right or wrong — just pure creativity on canvas. You don't need to be good at drawing at all.
What You’ll Learn:
How to create expressive abstract artwork using acrylics, gouache, chalk, pastels & gold foil
Layering techniques, mark-making, and composition
How to use colour and shapes to evoke emotion and movement
What to Expect:
You’ll work from curated references and prompts, but with plenty of freedom to experiment. We recommend to bring a photo abstract rference - choose something simple easpeacially if your a biginner withabstracttion. There’s no pressure to draw or follow strict lines — we provide everything ready for you, so you can focus on layering and flow. This class encourages exploration and bold choices, helping you build confidence and find your personal style.
This 2.5-hour creative workshop in London includes hands-on use of professional art materials in a supportive, energised space. Whether you’re planning a team building activity, a fun day out, or a gift experience, this session is designed to inspire and refresh.

title: Nature-Inspired Animal Illustration Workshop
description:
Join us for a relaxed Sip & Draw experience and explore the art of Animal Illustration in this welcoming, creative workshop hosted at The Oyster Catcher. Set in the heart of Greenwich, this beautiful riverside venue provides the perfect backdrop for a mindful, hands-on session combining drawing, nature, and gentle creativity. Drinks are available to order from the bar throughout the workshop, allowing you to settle in and enjoy the process at your own pace.
This workshop is designed for beginners and those looking to build confidence in drawing animals in a supportive, informal setting. You’ll be guided step by step through the foundations of Animal Illustration, learning how to observe and capture shape, proportion, texture, and expression. No prior drawing experience is needed, just curiosity and a willingness to experiment.
We’ll begin with gentle warm-up exercises, giving you time to familiarise yourself with soft pastels and green-toned art paper. You’ll explore blending techniques, layering colour, and creating depth, essential skills for successful Animal Illustration. These early exercises remove pressure and encourage play, helping you understand how pastels behave before moving into your main piece.
You’ll then be guided through illustrating a wildlife subject, such as an owl or fox, using a carefully selected reference image. The focus is on building your drawing gradually rather than striving for perfection. You’ll learn how to suggest feather or fur texture, work with light and shadow, and bring character into your artwork. This approach makes Animal Illustration feel accessible and enjoyable, even if you’ve never drawn animals before.
Once your illustration is established, you’ll be introduced to a small selection of pressed leaves and botanicals. These are used sparingly, as subtle accents to complement your drawing rather than overwhelm it. You’ll learn how to place them thoughtfully so they enhance the composition and connect your artwork back to the natural world, while keeping the focus firmly on Animal Illustration.
Throughout the session, there is plenty of one-to-one guidance, live demonstrations, and encouragement. The atmosphere is calm, social, and unhurried—ideal for a Sip & Draw experience. The Oyster Catcher’s relaxed setting allows you to work comfortably, enjoy a drink from the bar, and ease into creativity without pressure.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll have a finished nature-inspired artwork to take home—a piece that reflects your own hand and interpretation. More importantly, you’ll leave with new skills, techniques, and confidence to continue exploring Animal Illustration in your own time.
All materials are provided, including soft pastels, specialist paper, pressed botanicals, and reference images. This workshop is perfect for anyone looking for a restorative creative experience, a thoughtful gift, or a relaxed evening of art, drinks, and inspiration in Greenwich.

title: Real Flower Jewellery Workshop
description:
Transform real flowers into stunning wearable jewellery in this relaxing creative workshop in London. You'll design and create your own piece – earrings, a necklace, bracelet, pendant, or another botanical accessory – using professional UV resin techniques to preserve the beauty of real blooms. What makes it special is that many of the flowers you'll work with are grown on our family farm in Suffolk, carefully cultivated, harvested, and preserved before coming to our London studio. You're creating with flowers that have been lovingly prepared by us.
This is a hands-on, beginner-friendly experience where you'll be guided every step of the way. You'll learn how to design your piece, select botanical elements that work beautifully together, and master the UV resin technique that transforms delicate flowers into lasting keepsakes. There's no previous jewellery-making experience needed – just bring yourself and your ideas. As you work, you'll discover how colour, composition, and real flowers combine to create something that's both beautiful and wearable.
By the end, you'll leave with a piece of jewellery you've designed and made yourself – something completely unique that reflects your personal style. Whether you're treating yourself, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying a creative afternoon with friends, you'll walk away with a wearable keepsake and the satisfaction of having made something meaningful with your own hands.

title: Whipped Drink Candle Making Workshop
description:
Join our Valentine's Day Candle Making Workshop at Three Colts Tavern (near Bethnal Green Tube Station), where you'll get to design and decorate your own soy wax candle!
Please note, there are 2 options for your candle.
1) Standard Soy Wax Candle (no whipped cream) - where you spend the first half of the class painting the jar and then filling the candle and choosing your scent & colour the second half.
2) Whipped Drink Candle (with whipped cream/wax) - where you have less time to paint the jar as you'll be whipping the candle instead. There will still be some time for painting but definitely not as much as the first option. (Please also note, it is not possible to scent or change the colour of the whipped cream wax, but you are able to add fragrance/colour to the candle drink part underneath the wax.)
For both options, you'll choose your Valentine's Day themed scent (or a normal scent!) and favourite colour wax - and even decorate your candle with themed wax melts too!
Whether you keep it for yourself or gift it to someone special, this workshop is all about self-expression, community, and empowerment. title: Kintsugi Ornament Workshop
description:
* Please note that this is a seasonal workshop only. It will return in December of 2026, so feel free to pop onto the waitlist to be informed when new dates are released.
Join us for this festive twist on our signature Beginners Kintsugi repair workshop!
Celebrate the season with a calming and mindful workshop introducing you to the practise of Kintsugi repair. You will learn the fundamentals of traditional repair and materials and practise your skills on a piece of hand-made stoneware. Then moving on to repair your very own ceramic ornaments using hand-blended French bronze powder. Perfect as gifts, or to adorn your own tree.
We keep our workshop sizes small and cosy so that you get the opportunity for plenty of guidance. Because of this, spaces are limited, so booking ahead is recommended!
What is Kintsugi?
This Japanese ceramic repair technique using gold and bronze powders to create stunning repair lines originated during the 15th century and has evolved to become a beloved art form adopted by modern artists and restoration specialists alike. Kintsugi means 'to join with gold' and is the artistic embodiment of the Wabi-sabi philosophy which emphasises the beauty of imperfection. In our Beginners Kintsugi Workshop, we practise modern-hybrid repair methods, providing each attendee with all the materials and guidance they need to leave the session with a beautiful repaired piece of their own. If you have ever wondered about the history, philosophy and techniques behind this fascinating practise, this workshop is for you!
Your Instructor:
The workshop will be led by a trained historic conservator ready to answer all of your questions about traditional and modern kintsugi repair. Our goal for this session is to leave you with the confidence to execute your repairs at home, in addition to taking away a beautiful completed repair at the end.
The most perfectly 'imperfect' festive activity to ease you into the holidays!
Please note that while our studio is located on the ground floor, with no stairs, there are several narrow doorways to navigate. Please message ahead so that we can be sure to accommodate any special needs you might have.
What you'll get
2 ceramic ornaments to repair and take home
1 small stoneware piece to practice repair
Tea and mulled wine
A copy of The Salvage Company Brief Kintsugi Repair Guide

title: Kintsugi Pottery Class - Groups and Team Building - London
description:
Join this kintsugi workshop in London and celebrate the beauty of flaws, where broken pottery becomes even more stunning for having been repaired. Guided by a seasoned kintsugi master, you'll learn the traditional Japanese art of mending cracks and chips with gold resin to highlight, rather than hide, each piece’s unique story.
This mindful, hands-on experience is about more than just fixing ceramics; it's about embracing imperfections and finding value in the unexpected. You'll work through the process of carefully breaking and then re-creating a one-of-a-kind piece that's both beautiful and deeply meaningful. We'll provide all the materials and tools you need, ensuring a low-pressure environment where you can focus on the creative process.
Kintsugi dates back to the late 15th century and is rooted in the philosophy of wabi-sabi – finding beauty in the imperfect. By the end of the session, you'll have mastered the techniques of:
Preparing your ceramic vessel – Understand how to safely break your piece to create the best canvas for repair.
Mixing gold resin – Learn the art of combining lacquer with powdered gold to create a shimmering adhesive.
Precise application – Master the steady hand required to fill cracks and join pieces back together.
Polishing and finishing – Discover how to smooth the gold lines to make them a standout feature of your work.
You'll walk away with a newfound sense of resilience and a bespoke keepsake that proves wonky is beautiful. This workshop offers a life-changing perspective on how damage can be reimagined as art.

title: Mandala Rangoli Workshop
description:

You will be guided through the process step by step from understanding the traditional patterns to mastering the technique of layering colours with finesse.
Rangoli is a traditional Indian art form that involves creating colourful patterns on the floor or tabletop. The word "rangoli" comes from the Sanskrit word rangavalli, which means "rows of colours".
Rangoli is often made during Indian traditional festivals and other important celebrations, such as Diwali, Tihar, Onam, and Pongal.
Rangoli is made to welcome Lakshmi, the Hindu goddess of wealth and good luck, into homes.
Don't worry if you're a complete beginner – our experienced instructor will make sure you feel comfortable and confident throughout the class. You'll work with a variety of materials, including coloured powders and chalk, to bring your mandala rangoli to life.

By the end of the workshop, you'll have a beautiful mandala rangoli to take home – a tangible reminder of your creativity and something to light up your homes this festive season!

title: Decal Transfer Ceramic Workshop
description:
No experience is necessary; just bring your imagination.
Working with transfers onto ceramic, also known as decals, involves applying pre-printed designs onto the surface of the ceramic plates/bowls. We have a vast selection to choose from!
To apply the decals, they are soaked in water to release the design from the paper backing, allowing it to be carefully placed onto the ceramic surface. We have a choice of crockery – plates and bowls.
Once positioned correctly, the decal is gently pressed to remove any air bubbles and ensure adhesion. The ceramic piece is then fired again to permanently fuse the decal onto the surface, creating a durable and decorative finish. Working with decals on ceramic allows for intricate designs and detailed imagery to be easily transferred onto the surface, adding a unique and personalised touch to the finished piece.
Leave with us to fire in the kiln and we will post back to you within 6 weeks.

description:
When creating hand-built relief or indented tiles, the process typically involves shaping the clay by hand to create the desired relief or indented patterns. This can be achieved by pressing objects or tools into the clay to create texture and depth or by building up the clay through relief work.
Once the tiles are formed, they are left to dry before being fired in our kiln. After firing, the tiles will be dip-glazed (the colour of your choice) and posted to your door within 4-8 weeks. Teaching this process involves demonstrating hand-building techniques, creating patterns, and/or incorporating pictures into the design.
By providing step-by-step guidance and hands-on practise, you can learn to create your own unique set of 4 tiles with intricate patterns and images, all taught by our experienced tutors.

Choose your favourite Italian adventure! Each package is designed for hands-on fun, laughter, and celebration.

Cocktails and Italian Street Food Making
Dive into the vibrant spirit of an Italian street festival! You’ll learn to make iconic Italian cocktails and create delicious, easy-to-eat street food classics (frittini). A dynamic, hands-on class packed with flavour.

For a more sophisticated festa, embark on a guided tour of Italy’s finest wines. Our expert sommelier will introduce you to a selection of exquisite wines, perfectly paired with a board of authentic Italian delicacies.

description:

Choose your personal colour palette – From bold, vibrant tones to soft, earthy hues.
Work with acrylic paints – Build your base composition on a 30cm canvas.
Experiment with professional textured mediums – Use black lava, glass beads, resin sand, and texture paste.
Apply gold leaf – Elevate your artwork with a refined, shimmering finish.

We provide everything you need to get stuck in, including all paints, gels, and aprons. To keep the atmosphere social and uplifting, you'll also enjoy a selection of antipasto snacks while you work. title: Shutter Speed Photography Workshop
description:
Want to take more creative and unique photographs? Come along and broaden your photography skills with this creative shutter speed and night photography workshop.
During this walking photography workshop in London, you will discover different types of panning, light trails and long exposure photography techniques through out-in-the-field tutorials and demonstrations. Throughout the workshop, you will have opportunities to practise and experiment with newly learned techniques while snapping iconic sights such as St Pauls Cathedral, Leadenhall Market and Tower Bridge.
Subjects covered:
Panning.
Using shutter speeds creatively.
Light trails with moving traffic.
Shooting in manual mode, shutter speed priority and aperture priority mode.
Histogram and the importance of exposing to the right.
Intentional camera movement (ICM).
Using filters (if you have them).
Try out tips and tricks for eye-catching compositions.
The importance of light and shooting at the best time of day.
Conveying stories in your photographs.
Selecting the most appropriate equipment (although it is not about what equipment you have, it is how you use it!).
As well as learning the technical side of using longer shutter speeds, we will talk a lot about the thought process of creating (not just taking) photos. Your teacher, who is an experienced professional photographer, will offer up their top tips on composition to guide your photographic eye and help you develop a keen eye for exceptional imagery.
Itinerary (subject to slight change):
To begin, your group will meet close to St Paul's tube station. Your teacher will then offer a brief overview of the day, before setting straight out to explore London with our cameras.
After that, we will head to Leadenhall Market and Tower Bridge, ending with a night shoot and light trails.
Please note:
You will be given a specific meet-up point upon booking.

title: Ikebana Arrangement Workshop
description:
A Brief History of Ikebana

Learn how this centuries-old Japanese art began as temple offerings and grew into a meditative practice that values balance, simplicity, and space.




Meet Your Materials

Get to know the seasonal flowers, branches, and foliage you’ll be working with, each chosen for its natural line and form.




Prepare the Stems

Trim, strip, and hydrate your stems so they’re ready to shine.




Create the Three Lines

Arrange the guiding stems — Shin (heaven), Soe (human), and Hikae (earth) — to set the structure.



Discover the timeless beauty of Ikebana, the traditional Japanese art of flower arrangement. Rooted in centuries of history, Ikebana emphasises the harmony of nature, seasonality, and simplicity to create sculptural, meaningful designs. Today, this elegant art form continues to inspire modern floral styles around the world.
In this hands-on workshop in London, you’ll learn to craft stunning arrangements using a kenzan (pin frog) as your base, allowing for structure and creative expression. All materials are provided, and you’ll get to take home your arrangement, including the vase, kenzan, and seasonal flowers.
Perfect for individuals or small groups, this workshop offers a relaxing and therapeutic experience. Whether you’re new to floral design or simply seeking a creative outlet, come join us and explore the serene beauty of Ikebana.

title: Fine Wine Tasting and Handmade Pasta Workshop
description:
Join this luxury wine tasting and pasta making class in London for a hands-on culinary experience that combines the elegance of Italian viticulture with the timeless craft of traditional cooking.
This immersive event is hosted by two passionate experts, Carl and Luca, who bring together years of knowledge to create a wonderfully relaxed atmosphere. Your evening begins with Carl, a wine educator who makes discovering new grapes feel like a chat with a friend. You’ll start with a glass of Prosecco on arrival, followed by a fascinating comparison with Franciacorta – Italy’s refined answer to Champagne. Carl will guide you through a journey across Northern Italy, introducing:
Soave (100% garganega) – a vibrant white wine from volcanic hills, celebrated for its fresh citrus and floral character
Valpolicella ripasso – a rich yet elegant red wine, layered with deep cherry fruit and silky texture
Recioto della valpolicella – a historic sweet wine offering luxurious flavours of dark fruit and cocoa
Alongside the tasting, Luca will show you how to create fresh pasta from scratch using traditional techniques. These workshops are designed to feel like an evening among friends in Italy – social, uplifting, and full of flavour. After a warm welcome with premium antipasti, you'll get stuck into the dough, rolling and shaping it into two beautiful handmade styles: tagliatelle and farfalle.
As you work, Luca will share stories about Italian food culture and the secrets behind the perfect bite. Once your creations are ready, he'll cook them up and serve them with two delicious sauces: a rich traditional meat ragù and a creamy courgette and double cream sauce topped with crispy pancetta. You’ll then sit down to enjoy your meal as more wine is poured and the garden fills with conversation and laughter.
You’ll leave with a refreshed sense of culinary confidence, wonderful memories, and the spark of inspiration to recreate these authentic flavours in your own kitchen.

title: Introduction to Linocut Printing Workshop
description:
The workshop is about learning the use of traditional Japanese hand tools, the process of inking Lino blocks, printing on different types of handmade printing paper, and developing a new understanding of various techniques in Linocut printing. All of these enable you to make numerous fine art prints to take away at the end of the session!
Printing Class Structure
Intro - Cups of tea, coffee, or soft drinks followed by some words from me on my printmaking career and a round-the-table 'meet and greet' from everyone to begin the workshop.
Stage one - Getting to know the hand tools in order to design, draw, and cut the Lino. Next up is the inking of blocks and the process of hand printing by use of traditional Japanese barens (circular discs wrapped in bamboo) on three types of paper: these include Japansese Hosho, newsprint and coloured papers.
Stage two - Delve a little deeper, showing you how to use multiple blocks and reduction-cutting techniques to create more complex multi-colour prints.
Stage three - This is a perfect opportunity to make multiple prints through editions, ending the final part of the session by experimenting with your favourite design or playing with various colours.
Stage four - I'll be collecting everyone's individual prints, wrapping them in sheets of tissue paper and rolling them up into tubes for safe passage home.
Please feel free to leave your email addresses at the end of our workshop so I can forward a tools and materials list from my suppliers I use for the studio.
My studio is on floor 6 at Regent Studios: if you’re not taking the stairs, please take the right-hand lift and depart on floor 6 for studio 64B. For evening sessions, there will be plenty of snacks and refreshments. Day workshops include a homemade veggie soup for autumn and winter with a light plant-based lunch the rest of the year.
What you'll get
1 x A4 size Lino block - both sides can be used/cut
1 x set of 5 Japanese cutting tools: 7mm Aisuki (flat chisel), 7mm Hangito (knife), 4mm V, 5mm U and 3mm U
Water-based inks: blue, black, red, green, yellow and white + new colours can be made/mixed
3 types of paper - including a fine Japanese Hosho
Tubes to away prints at the end of the session

description:

You will join our fixer-maker movement to fix, improve and reimagine the things we already have. Avoid the misery of landfill! Learn together.

Your teacher will guide you through the process of working with mixed media, helping you feel at ease even if it's your first time picking up a palette knife. You'll spend a few hours in a cosy atmosphere, enjoying tea and sweet treats while you focus on the tactile joy of building your masterpiece. It's a low-pressure environment where you can switch off from the outside world and simply enjoy the feel-good process of making something beautiful.
During this workshop, you'll:
Create a beautiful 3D lemon textured canvas – Use figurines and paste to bring your art to life.
Learn layering and texture techniques – Master the skills needed to add depth and dimension to your work.
Enjoy tea and sweet treats – Relax in a warm and welcoming setting.
Leave with a unique handmade interior piece – A one-of-a-kind keepsake for your home.
Everything you need is provided for you, so you can just show up and let your imagination take the lead. You'll finish the session with a gorgeous lemon artwork that's ready to display, having enjoyed an uplifting experience that leaves you feeling inspired and refreshed.

You will take home your finished textured lemon artwork, ready to decorate your space.

title: Lino Print Coaster Making Workshop
description:
Design & Draw

Choose your theme and sketch your design onto the lino block.




Carve

Carefully carve away the areas you want to stay unprinted.




Ink the Lino

Roll a thin, even layer of ink over the carved lino surface.




Print

Lift the coaster slowly to reveal your design.



In this hands-on lino printing workshop in London, we explore the process of lino printmaking to design and produce your own set of unique coasters. This session is all about creativity, experimentation, and turning everyday ideas into tactile, functional art pieces.

Learn how to safely and confidently carve your design into lino!

Print your design onto coasters, experimenting with composition, layering, and ink to achieve your final pieces.
By the end of the workshop, you will leave with your own carved lino block and two finished printed coasters. Each one a small piece of functional art, made entirely by you.

title: Private Authentic Chinese Dumplings Cooking Class
description:
If you're keen to broaden your culinary horizons, come along to this hands-on cooking class, where you'll learn how to create delicious homemade-style Chinese dumplings completely from scratch!
Not the same as dumplings from Chinatown or other Dim Sum takeaways, these are the real ones that Chinese families enjoy at home, especially in Northern China, the birthplace of the dumplings, where they're part of the staple diet.
During this dumpling class, you'll learn how to make dumplings from expert Chinese cooking teacher Pan. You'll be shown how to make your dishes using authentic methods. With class sizes kept small and intimate, you will get full attention from Pan, who'll be around to make sure all your questions are answered.
This class begins with a short introduction to the world of dumplings and Asian cuisine — you will learn all about the history of dumpling making and how dumplings fit into modern trends of cooking.
During this dumplings class, you will learn how to do:
three types of fillings:
1. pork minces with Chinese chives optional prawns
2.sweet corn with minces
3. Courgettes with eggs optional add prawn.
Make dumpling pastry from dough.
Three ways to fold dumplings.
Cook your dumplings in Chinese ways.
This class is designed for beginners, and will focus on wrapping, the most important stage. You'll also learn how to knead dough and chop your ingredients by hand for the best results.
At the end of this dumpling cooking class in London, you can sit down and enjoy what you've made, or take it all home for later. Recipe will send via email after lesson.
Allergy Information
Gluten is not avoidable.
Soy and Sesame seeds can be avoided.
Egg is used in this class for Veg option fillings.
Pork is the authentic filling in Chinese dumplings. If you don't eat pork, don't worry. Our vegetable filling is the second best to the pork filling. It is suitable for vegans.
Vegan option please notify me in advance. If you don't eat prawns pls notify me too.
This class could be held online as well as at client site. Please send us a message to discuss the details.
What you'll get
All the ingredients and tools to make some Chinese dumplings to enjoy after the class.
Complimentary tea during the whole class.
two sides provided with dumplings
Recipe sent to you after the class.

title: Yin Yoga with Sound Bath Class
description:
Join us for a calming and rejuvenating 75-minute workshop where you can learn how stillness meets sound in a truly restorative activity. Guided by me (Tiffany), you’ll be gently supported through a sequence of long-held Yin yoga poses, expertly designed to softly open the body, increase flexibility, and foster a deep release.
As you soften into each posture, Emma will subtly match the moment with harmonious healing sounds from crystal bowls, chimes, and other instruments. This unique combination helps to balance your nervous system and quiet your thoughts, effortlessly guiding you into a meditative state.
The blending of Yin Yoga and Sound Healing is incredibly powerful. The long, passive holds of Yin promote physical release, and the vibrational frequencies of the sound bath amplify the experience. The soothing tones help to:
Deepen your stretches – The sound encourages your nervous system to relax, allowing your body to release tension more effectively.
Quiet the mind – The immersive soundscape provides a focal point, making it easier to surrender to the present moment.
Enhance emotional release – Vibrational healing can help to unblock stagnant energy, fostering a sense of lightness and clarity.
Promote deep renewal – The sound waves resonate within the body, encouraging a profound sense of well-being.
The session concludes in gentle silence, providing a sacred space for integration and inner peace. This class is perfect for anyone seeking stress relief, an emotional reset, or simply a nurturing moment to reconnect.
You’ll leave with a renewed sense of peace and resilience, feeling wonderfully calm and profoundly relaxed after discovering the transformative power of stillness through sound.
Please note Sound baths are not advised for:
Those in the first three months of pregnancy
Children
Those with pacemakers or metal implants
Anyone experiencing severe mental health problems
Those with a history of epilepsy or seizures should consult their doctor for suitability

Do I need any prior experience in jewellery making to join this class?

description:
Join our Correll Garden Club for a relaxed, open session designed for anyone who enjoys being outdoors, getting their hands in the soil, and connecting with others along the way.

title: Photoshop for Beginners: Professional Retouching Class
description:
Ready to transform your photos with confidence, even if you've never touched Photoshop before?
In this beginner-friendly class, you'll learn the essential tools and techniques used by professional photographers and creatives around the world. Whether you're a content creator, aspiring photographer, artist, or just curious about editing, this course will help you take your visuals to the next level.
Led by a professional photographer and retoucher, this course is perfect for complete beginners. We'll start with the basics—navigating the interface, working with layers, and understanding file types. From there, you'll learn how to clean up images, adjust colours, retouch skin, and bring out the best in every photo.
This is not just a technical class—it's creative and supportive. You'll be encouraged to explore your own visual voice and develop editing skills you can truly use. Expect a warm, inspiring environment with room for questions, mistakes, and growth.

title: Kollabo: A Cultural Pottery Painting Experience
description:
Join us for one of London's most unique Mother's Day experiences, an afternoon of pottery painting that celebrates heritage, identity, and the power of collaboration. One afternoon, three African-owned businesses, a creative experience unlike anything else in the UK.
This Mother's Day weekend, Revyvely, Tobi's Tales, and Kloza are coming together for Kollabo, a pottery painting experience that celebrates who we are, where we come from, and the power of what we can build together.
Here's what you'll do: Pick up a brush and paint whatever feels like you, words from your mother tongue, patterns rooted in your culture, a proverb your grandmother used to say. There are no rules, no pressure, and no artistic experience required. Just you, your heritage, and a piece of art you'll actually want to keep.
While you create, you'll be surrounded by great food, great energy, and a room full of people who get it.
This experience is perfect for you if:
You love the idea of using language as a form of art
You want a creative experience that actually means something
Are looking for a thoughtful way to celebrate Mum, a sister, girlfriend, or any woman who deserves more than flowers
You'd rather spend your afternoon making something unique than scrolling on your phone
You want to celebrate your cultural identity through hands-on expression
By the end of the workshop, you'll feel a renewed sense of connection to your heritage and pride in your creative abilities. You'll head home with a one-of-a-kind cultural keepsake that serves as a beautiful reminder of your personal story.
Kollabo was ideated and executed end-to-end through Kloza, a platform built for structured African business collaboration, proof that when we come together with intention, we build something worth showing up for.
What you'll get
A range of pottery pieces to paint and personalise
All painting materials (glazes, brushes, etc.) and firing included
Complimentary drinks and snacks to keep the vibes flowing (BYOB welcome)
Guided instruction and freedom to create
A fun, relaxing space to connect and create
See booking options
Knowledge required
Beginner-friendly, no experience needed.

title: Learn to Dance to Any Song – Feel Confident on Any Dance Floor
description:
Ever been at a party, wedding or night out when a great song comes on – and had absolutely no idea what to do? Maybe dancing feels awkward, you're a bit rusty, or you keep falling back on the same two moves.
Learn to Dance to Any Song is here to change that. This fun, beginner-friendly session isn't about memorising a complicated routine or mastering one particular style. Instead, you'll pick up the skills that help you understand music, move naturally, and feel more confident whenever you dance.
You'll explore rhythm, musicality, timing and different ways of moving your body, then put it all into practice across a mix of music and dance styles – Latin one moment, a party classic, pop song or 80s/90s favourite the next.
You'll discover how to:
Find and follow the beat of a song
Recognise when the music changes
Move without needing choreography
Adapt simple movements to different types of music
Dance confidently on your own
Dance and interact with another person
Add your own personality and style
Avoid freezing when someone says, "Come on, let's dance!"
Along the way, you'll pick up simple movements inspired by different dance styles, building a collection of easy moves you can mix, match and adapt depending on what's playing.
There's no pressure to perform and no dance experience required. This isn't about turning you into a professional dancer – it's about reaching the point where a song comes on and, instead of wondering what you're supposed to do, you can just feel the music and dance.
The perfect bit of preparation for parties, weddings, holidays and nights out, or simply for feeling more comfortable and confident on the dance floor.
What you'll get
You will learn practical dance skills you can use in real-life social situations, including:
How to find the beat and stay in time with music.
Basic musicality and rhythm.
Easy movements that work with different songs.
An introduction to several styles of dancing.
Solo dancing techniques.
Simple partner dancing.
How to transition between different movements.
How to improvise rather than rely on choreography.
Tips for looking and feeling more natural when dancing.
Greater confidence for parties, weddings and nights out.
Most importantly, you'll leave with moves you can actually use the next time somebody puts on some music.
See booking options
Knowledge required
Absolutely none!
This experience has been created specifically for beginners, people who haven't danced for years, and anyone who simply doesn't feel confident on the dance floor.
You don't need rhythm, previous dance lessons, or a dance partner.
Come on your own, with a partner, or with friends.
If you've ever thought, “I can't dance, ” this class is for you.
What to bring
Wear comfortable clothes that allow you to move freely and comfortable shoes suitable for dancing.

Comfortable footwear
An open mind
Plenty of energy!
No specialist dancewear or equipment is required.

description:
Join us for a cosy evening of creativity and flavour as we explore the art of infused liqueurs.
In this relaxed home workshop, you’ll learn how to blend fruits, herbs, and spices to create your own beautifully bottled infusions — the perfect handmade gift (or personal treat!).
We’ll start the evening by talking through the basics of infusion: how to choose your base spirit, balance flavours, and layer ingredients to create something completely your own. You’ll then make your own small-batch liqueurs using a range of seasonal ingredients — from citrus peels and warming spices to herbs and berries freshly foraged from the garden.

Once your bottles are sealed, you’re welcome to stay by the fire pit (weather permitting) or gather around the kitchen table for some refreshments and conversation. title: Kokedama Hanging Planter Workshop for Beginners
description:
Join this kokedama class in London and discover the serene, hands-on art of Japanese moss ball gardening. This workshop offers a peaceful escape from the daily grind, where you'll learn to create your own sustainable hanging planters using traditional techniques.
Guided by an expert teacher, you'll master the delicate process of crafting a moss ball, from selecting the right greenery to carefully binding it with string. This low-pressure environment is perfect for first-timers, ensuring you feel supported as you explore this elegant aesthetic. You'll gain a deep understanding of plant care and the unique needs of your new botanical companion, making it easy to keep your creation thriving at home.
Kokedama technique – Learn how to create a moss ball, wrap it with string, and bind it with care
Plant care – Understand the needs of your chosen plant and how to care for your hanging planter
Japanese aesthetics – Experience the calming beauty of Japanese design through a simple, yet elegant plant display
By the end of the session, you'll have gained the confidence to continue your green-fingered obsession independently. You'll leave with a beautiful, handmade kokedama that brings a fresh spark of nature into your living space.

title: Natural Deodorant Workshop
description:
Natural deodorants offer a gentle alternative to many commercial products by using simple, non-toxic ingredients that allow the skin to breathe naturally. They can help minimize body odour without the use of synthetic fragrances, preservatives, or harsh chemicals often found in commercial deodorants. Many conventional deodorants contain aluminium compounds, parabens, and other additives that some people prefer to avoid in daily use. By opting for natural ingredients like coconut oil, baking soda, and essential oils, you reduce exposure to these substances while still feeling fresh.

title: 4 Week Beginners Pottery Course
description:

We will introduce you to a range of handbuilding techniques and practices. This workshop covers all the fundamentals of how to work with clay, along with basic decorating techniques and simple glazing.
The January schedule is:
Week 1: Kurinuki pot – You will start with a solid block of clay and carve it out to create an interior.
Week 2: Vase – Slab-built vessel, you can choose from a cylindrical or rectangle design.
Week 3: Plate – Using a mould, you can decorate this using coloured slips.
Week 4: Glazing – Glazing your pieces.
The February schedule is:
Week 1: Mug – Pinch pot mug with a handle.
Week 2: Coiled planter – Using crank clay which will be suitable for outdoor use.
Week 3: Bowl – Using a mould, you can decorate this with sgraffito using slips.
Week 4: Glazing – Glazing your pieces.
These workshops run for consecutive weeks on the same day at the same time. Sorry, but if you’re unable to make a week, we’re not able to offer any alternative sessions.
Please be aware that this listing does not include wheel throwing; we offer that as a separate listing.
You'll finish the course with a fantastic new set of skills and a wonderful sense of achievement, taking home a collection of beautifully glazed, hand-built pottery items that you made yourself.
What you'll get
We provide a set amount of clay to be used each week. This has been calculated to ensure that your pieces will have enough time to dry (and be fired once) before the final week of glazing.

title: Natural Morning Routine Body Products Workshop
description:
Embrace a refreshing start with our Natural Products Morning Routine. Enjoy a delicious coffee and pastry and learn the benefits of natural products and essential oils while we create natural shave cream, deodorant, face scrub, and daily moisturising sunscreen. Perfect for preparing your own natural essentials or thoughtful gifts.
Our workshop will be held at The Ministry, a private members' club with a café, bar, and garden. Upon arrival, you will be warmly welcomed by our friendly reception team to a designated space in the bar where your host will greet everyone and welcome them to the private workshop space. You can relax and enjoy the space before or after your session.
Come solo, bring a friend, or schedule a private group workshop of your choice. Let's craft, chat, and create lasting memories together. If you have any dietary constraints, please let us know in advance of the workshop or contact us with any questions.

title: Sterling Silver Leaf Jewellery Experience
description:
Join us for a relaxed and creative jewellery-making workshop in London, where you'll have the opportunity to create your own sterling silver earrings, bracelet, or both.
No previous experience is required. You'll be guided through the entire process in a relaxed and supportive environment, learning at your own pace within a small, friendly group.
Whether you choose the full-day experience or attend a single earring or bracelet workshop, you'll learn traditional jewellery-making techniques and create beautiful handmade pieces to take home.
What to expect:
Learn metalworking and jewellery making techniques.
Explore fold-forming on copper and create a decorative copper pendant while learning the fundamentals.
Develop essential jewellery-making skills, including cutting, forming, folding, texturing, and hammering metal.
Create your final piece in sterling silver, transforming your new skills into a beautiful pair of earrings, a bracelet, or both.
Enjoy complimentary hot or cold drinks and biscuits during a break in the middle of the workshop.
By the end of the session, you'll leave not only with new skills and a memorable experience, but also with beautiful handmade jewellery that you can wear with pride, knowing you created it yourself.

At the end of the workshop, you'll leave with beautiful handmade jewellery and the skills used to create it.

description:
Retreat to a relaxed creative workshop at Chill 'N' Paint. Treat yourself or a buddy to a laid-back event where you'll meet possible new friends, uncover artistic abilities, and bring home an incredible gift. title: Expressive Interior Sketching Workshop
description:
If you love drawing interiors but feel held back by perspective, straight lines and scale, this relaxed 2½-hour workshop is all about letting go of technical perfection and finding your own expressive style instead.
It's suitable for beginners, hobby artists, experienced sketchers, interior designers, and anyone keen to capture the charm of a room in a freer, more personal way. Rather than chasing strict accuracy, you'll focus on mood, atmosphere and character – the things that make a space feel like itself.
Over the session, you'll learn how to:
Loosen up, overcoming the fear of the blank page and embracing "imperfect" lines
Prioritise style over scale, capturing texture and atmosphere rather than exact measurements
Build engaging compositions and vignettes, choosing views that frame the details worth telling
Develop expressive mark-making, using simple pen and pencil techniques to give your drawings personality
By the end, you'll have a collection of expressive interior sketches, a fresh sense of confidence in your drawing, and a new way of seeing the spaces around you. Best of all, you'll leave with practical techniques to keep exploring in your own sketchbook, ready to keep developing your style long after the workshop ends.
What you'll get
A finished artwork - your interior sketch you may even want to frame.

title: Sketchbook Journalling Workshop: Travel and Everyday
description:
Would you like a more personal and creative way to remember your day-to-day adventures, trips, and holidays? In this relaxed sketching workshop in London, you’ll learn how to turn everyday moments and travels into a sketchbook full of lively, memorable pages.
No drawing experience is needed -- this workshop is open to complete beginners as well as anyone wanting a more relaxed, enjoyable approach to sketching. You’ll be encouraged to work loosely and intuitively, combining sketching, handwriting, colour, and playful layouts in a way that feels personal rather than perfect.
What to expect:
Focus on capturing the feel of a place through key moments -- a walk in nature, a holiday vista, a café table or anything else that captures your eye.
Explore easy sketching techniques anyone can do.
Figure out how to choose the key moments to capture and get creative with.
Experiment with simple, effective page layouts.
Adding notes, colour, and details to tell your story and make it truly yours.
Use inspiration from your own images, plus our provided images.
By the end, you’ll have the confidence and ideas to start your own sketchbook practice -- a creative way to relive your adventures, big or small.

The first chapter in your sketchbook journal -- filled with colourful memories.
A set of sketching techniques suited for quick and atmospheric sketching.
More eye for storytelling and choosing moments.
Creative confidence to work loosely and intuitively, moving past the fear of making mistakes.
Inspiration to continue your sketching journey.

description:

Focusing on drawing an array of objects within the inspirational surroundings of the V&A museum, you will create loose freestyle sketches. Participants will be encouraged to develop their own style - tuning in to their unique creative side.

Join us for an enjoyable sketching experience. Let go, tune in to your creative side, and hopefully surprise yourself with what you can achieve.

title: Authentic South Indian Cooking Class
description:
If you're keen to learn something new to update your home cooking, come along to this cooking class and dining experience in London.
Learn to make traditional South Indian dishes with your host, a home cook who has been cooking throughout her life. You might learn to make dishes like a traditional tomato or coconut chutney, a meat or vegetable curry dish, as well as dosas or idlys, for your South Indian meal together.
Please note that for some of the dishes such as dosas components will be prepared in advance, as dosa batter needs to sit for several days before cooking. Jemima is excited to share her culture through food and offer an authentic/traditional cooking class in London. She can also accommodate vegetarian diets in her South Indian cooking class.
The cooking portion of your experience lasts 1-1.5 hours depending on the size of your group, after which you will enjoy the meal you prepared together.

title: Fused-Glass Jewellery Workshop
description:
Create Your Pieces

Let your creativity flow under the guidance of Jessie to help make your ideas a reality as you start making your fused glass pieces.




Load Your Shelf

Carefully assemble your pieces on the shelf, ready to go in the kiln! Plenty of help will be on hand if you need it.




Fire in the Kiln

All pieces are carefully fired on their own shelf in our kilns -- watch as your project comes to life!




Reveal Your Work

Results are carefully pulled from our kiln to reveal your beautiful work -- almost ready for the final step.




Attach the Findings

We have an array of findings to complete your pendants, earrings, bracelets, rings or charms. Fine metals available upon request on the day for an extra cost.




Jewellery Posted to You

We will carefully package your jewellery and post it to you, ready to wear, gift or cherish for years to come.



Dive into the colourful world of fused glass in London in this hands-on, 2-hour workshop with Jessie at Medora Studios. Whether you’re a complete beginner or just looking to try something creative, you’ll be guided step-by-step to make your own unique glass pieces.
This beginner-friendly session is perfect for anyone curious about glass art, jewellery-making, or personal creative projects. All materials and equipment are provided, so you can focus on experimenting, learning and having fun!
What to expect:
Introduction to fused glass tools, equipment, and techniques.
Step-by-step guidance on creating your own designs, cutting, layering, and arranging glass for firing..
Kiln firing and finishing of your pieces.
Jewellery fixings attached (for wearable items) and your creations packaged and posted free of charge.
A supportive environment encouraging creativity, experimentation, and fun.
You’ll leave with your very own handmade fused glass pieces and the skills to continue exploring this vibrant craft!
What you'll get
Introduction to glass fusing.
Tutorial on the tools and techniques needed.
All materials and tools needed.
You can make up to 6 ready-to-wear pieces of jewellery or small decorative items (sun catchers, nightlights, etc.)
We attach the jewellery fixings to make your design into a necklace, ring, etc.
Items are gift-wrapped after firing and returned to you!

title: Private Birthday Party Jewellery Making Workshop with Drinks
description:
A birthday is always worth celebrating, so this isn't any ordinary workshop, this is a party workshop!
You'll be guided on how to create your own easy beaded jewellery to take home or wear on the special day/week. Choose between making earrings, bracelets, or necklaces, whilst listening to your choice of music. No need to fret if you're new to this craft - it's perfect for beginners and celebrations!
During this workshop, you'll be working with a variety of colourful beads and materials, allowing your creativity to flow freely. There are a range of good-quality materials, most of which are hypoallergenic. Hypoallergenic supplies have been treated to make the risk of having an allergic reaction almost 0. In terms of the beads, I mostly use gemstone and crystal pave beads, love a bit of sparkle. I have other types of beads as well, such as letter beads, so I'm hopeful you'll find something you like!
If you have a specific colour or type of bead you'd like to use, please do let me know when booking, and I'll try my best to source it (no extra cost). If this is the case, please book at least 1 week in advance so I receive everything in time.
Drinks:
You'll be greeted with a choice of water, prosecco, a mimosa, or a nimosa (non-alcoholic), and will be able to top up throughout the workshop. You can also bring your bottle (BYOB).
As the workshop progresses, you'll find yourself immersed in the joy of creating something beautiful with your own hands. Walk away feeling accomplished and proud, adorned with unique jewellery that reflects your personal style.
Location:
I can travel to you or help source a location. Sadly I don't have a private venue. There are loads of free venues we could potentially use, such as a park (if the weather permits) or a pub/café.
Celebrate a special occasion, learn a new skill, and create something beautiful!

title: Clay Hand Building Class: Green Man Pottery Wall Plaque
description:
Prepare Slab Work

You’ll use guides to keep the clay slab level and roll out under instruction and care to minimise warping and uneven shrinkage.




Examine the Green Man Legend and Natural Resources

I’ll have lots of resource available to use for planning your design. We’ll reference everything seasonal, which might include leaves, berries, nuts, seed pods, mushrooms & stems. You are very welcome to bring your own references or natural forms along too.




Create the Basics of the Face

With the help of a template to position features we’ll cut out evenly and then create the basic structure of a face.




Impress, Stamp, Model & Create

Using soft clay and some impressions, stamps, tools and ingenuity we’ll create the natural elements, let your imagination run wild!




Fill Every Space

They’ll be lots of studio tools and stamps to fill all the gaps and make a rich textured surface that will hold a glossy green glaze.




Collect Your Richly Glazed Work Ready to Hang After Four Weeks

I will carefully dry, kiln fire and glaze your work, ready for collection four weeks after your class.



Learn about the rich and varied legend of the 'green man' (or woman!), how this mythical figure peeping from the natural world protects and celebrates the natural environment and is ever-present in the wheel of the year. Then create your own representation in a relief-modelled plaque that will hang in your garden or on an interior wall.
There'll be loads of resources ready to examine for inspiration in this small but companionable class, and you are welcome to bring your own natural finds, drawings, and ideas along. This is a legend that has changed a lot over centuries, so new interpretations and ideas are always welcome.
We’ll create a slab of clay and a template for the basic facial features, and then test out the mark-making possibilities of natural materials to create in clay a face peeping from leaves, stems, berries—everything from a rich seasonal natural world. I’ll show you how to select the right tools, create these pieces, and stick them down securely without cracking.
This is an immersive but friendly activity in a working pottery studio with a max group size of four. Expect quiet moments of thinking and experimentation but also kind exchanges of ideas and encouragement. Suitable for any level of starting skill.
I’ll show you the glaze and kiln process to come and will then tuck your work away to dry before twice firing and glazing for you. You will collect fully glazed and ready-to-hang work four weeks later (or postage can be organised).
It’s not hugely messy, but bring your own apron if required. Free and very easy parking on site or bus links from the Elizabeth line in Woolwich or Jubilee line at North Greenwich.
What you'll get
All materials and tools are provided.
See booking options



FAQ

Is your studio easy to get to?
Yes and there are lots of options including buses and a train station within 15 mins walk. Or masses of free parking right on site within a few metres of my studio door, with level access. Longer riverside walk in’s from Woolwich or the O2 are possible and both have Thames clipper docks.
Will I get very dirty?
No, there will be clean up available and you can borrow an apron or bring your own. Clay will dry to brushed away dust very quickly in any case.
Is there an accessible toilet?
There is a toilet within my studio with level access.

title: Wax Carving Jewellery Workshop
description:
Learn the art of lost wax carving with this London jewellery workshop, creating yourself a ring, pendant or two charms using wax to form your design.
Lost wax carving involves building a mould around a wax model. After the mould sets, the wax is melted away to create a space that metal can be poured into. This type of carving and casting can create beautiful details and it makes for unique jewellery.
Have some creative fun with friends and loved ones in this class by creating special jewellery pieces together. Working in your teacher's welcoming London studio, you'll be shown how to use jeweller's wax to create your unique accessories.
In this beginner wax carving workshop, you will be taught how to carve a ring, pendant or charms using a range of wax carving tools. The finished wax is then sent to a caster for casting into silver ready for cleaning and polishing to be picked up at a later date or posted out to you within two weeks.
During you're class you'll learn how to:
Create designs for wax carving.
Carve a jewellery design using wax tools.
Finish and clean up wax design ready for casting.
You'll make one of the following:
Ring (max 8mm wide).
Pendant (30mm by 15mm).
2 x charms or 2 x small pendants (15mm by 15mm).
This relaxing London workshop is suitable for beginners and is a wonderful creative experience to enjoy with loved ones or as a gift experience. If you're looking for birthday gifts, hen party ideas or just something extra special to do with friends, learn to make your own jewellery together using this traditional wax carving technique.
Please note:
Any piece larger than the specified dimensions will incur an extra charge on the day. Your teacher will run through your options with you before you begin.

title: 6 Week Pottery Wheel Course - Intermediates
description:
Refine your skills and take your pottery to the next level with this 6-week intermediate throwing course in Greenwich. Designed for those who feel confident centring 1kg of clay and pulling even walls, this series of workshops offers a supportive space to tackle more ambitious projects and sophisticated techniques.
Working with larger amounts of clay, you'll focus on refining your process to achieve thinner walls and bases. Under the guidance of a knowledgeable teacher, you'll explore the rewarding challenge of creating complex forms and decorative finishes. You'll have the opportunity to learn or improve on:
Throwing with more clay – Scale up your work and handle larger weights with ease.
Closed shapes and bottles – Master the art of collaring in and creating elegant, narrow necks.
Lidded vessels – Learn the precision required to craft perfectly fitting lids.
Candlesticks – Explore architectural forms and functional design.
Throwing off the hump – Build efficiency by creating multiple small items from one large piece of clay.
Surface decoration – Add a personal touch to your work with professional finishing techniques.
Everything you need is provided, including studio white or buff stoneware clay and a full range of professional tools and glazes. The course includes the glazing and firing of up to six of your favourite pieces, and you'll even receive three hours of independent, untaught studio time to practice at your own pace. You'll leave this experience feeling inspired and empowered, taking home a collection of handmade stoneware that showcases your newfound technical mastery.

This course is for intermediate students; it's recommended you complete two or three beginner courses before joining.

title: Phone Charm Workshop
description:
Learn how to design and create your very own unique beaded phone charm in this practical workshop, using professional techniques and high-quality materials. This engaging 90-minute activity is perfect for developing your design skills while crafting a beautiful, personalised accessory to take home and use.
No previous experience is needed for this hands-on workshop; it's designed for participants of all skill levels. You'll find the process approachable and enjoyable, making it ideal for creative beginners or experienced crafters looking to learn new techniques. You'll have the chance to work with a diverse selection of materials – including charms, colourful beads, glass beads, letter blocks, and pendants – giving you plenty of options to express your unique style.
Throughout the session, your tutor, Emma, will expertly guide you through the complete phone charm-making process. You'll learn how to move from initial design ideas to technical construction, mastering valuable techniques such as how to string beads effectively, tie and secure components, safely use flames to melt and seal ends, and create the essential knot for attaching the charm to your phone.
By the end of this informative workshop, you'll leave with practical phone charm-making skills to continue exploring at home, along with your wonderful handcrafted phone charm that perfectly reflects your aesthetic preferences.
Please note: Your teacher will provide instructions on how to enter the building upon arrival. It's recommended to arrive about 10 minutes before the starting time to get settled in.
