title: Spring Clay Class
description:
Rolling Out

We’ll roll out the clay we need. I’ll show you how clay moves and how it is best rolled. For very young children I can prepare this earlier.




There Are Tools to Help

I have a slab roller which can be used by me and assisted by children.




Cut with Templates

They’ll be templates to help cut the right shapes.




Impressing & Construction

Everyone enjoys using stamps with clay. It’s so immersive and we can use rollers, textured fabrics etc. Strong constructions will be created with liquid clay called slip.




Personalise Your Chicken

There are lots of ways to personalise your work. We can add elements or colour.




Full Firing & Glazing Included

Your work will be kiln fired and glazed [as part of the class cost] and ready to collect three to four weeks later.



Join this spring-themed clay class and enjoy some creative family time during the school holidays. It's a wonderful opportunity for you and your children to get hands-on in a studio space specially set up to be safe and welcoming for little makers.
Using studio-grade materials and professional tools, your kids will learn how to use templates to cut clay shapes and impress beautiful textures and patterns. They'll then construct a simple chicken shape and apply vibrant colours to their creation. If time allows, they'll also get to craft a little pinch pot basket, the perfect size for holding small chocolate eggs.
The class is designed to be low-pressure and fun, ensuring everyone feels supported throughout the making process. It's a feel-good way to switch off together and enjoy a mindful break from the usual routine.
By the end of the session, each child will have created a charming decorative chicken and a matching basket. These stoneware ceramic pieces will be professionally fired and glazed, ready for collection in three to four weeks. It's a heart-warming way to create a lasting keepsake that you can bring out and enjoy every year.
Please note: The price includes full stoneware firing and glazing. Work will be ready to collect in three to four weeks.
What you'll get
All materials and tools are provided.
See booking options
Knowledge required
Suitable for beginners. Be prepared to help young children alongside me.

You won’t get hugely messy but you may like to bring an old cover up or an apron.

FAQ

How many children can one adult bring?
One adult per group is fine as long as you are able to assist any very young children in the group. Children over 8 can generally work confidently on this project. Each person attending will have their own seat, be making and needs a booked place.
My children like to run about, is this suitable?
My studio is a working space and situated with other art workers. Whilst this is a cheerful and friendly session you’ll need to remind that this is a sat down activity and it’s dangerous for me and them if they are running around.
Is there a toilet / parking / a cafe?
Yes free unrestricted parking mere steps from my door, there is a toilet inside my studio and there is a great cafe on site [mon-fri at the moment].

title: Fern Kokedama Workshop
description:
Join this kokedama class in London and discover the serene Japanese art of creating beautiful moss-covered soil balls. Kokedama, which literally translates to 'moss ball', offers a wonderful way to display plants without the need for plastic pots, making them a sustainable and eye-catching alternative for your home.
You'll start this hands-on workshop with a friendly introduction to the world of moss art before being guided through the process of crafting your own fern kokedamas. It’s a low-pressure environment where you can switch off and enjoy the tactile experience of working with nature. You'll have plenty of lovely ferns to choose from, ensuring your creations are truly one-of-a-kind.
Everything you need is provided for a stress-free session:
Carpet moss – Use high-quality moss to wrap and protect your plants.
Kokedama twine – Learn to secure your moss ball with decorative binding.
Choice of ferns – Pick your favorite greenery from a wide selection.

title: Private Team Building Terrarium Workshop
description:
If you're planning a team-building event and want something a bit out of the ordinary, look no further than this terrarium making class in London! Whether you're an eco-conscious crew or just want to bring a bit of nature into the office, a terrarium making class might be just the activity you've been looking for.
Terrariums are incredible self-sustaining ecosystems, they can last for years without needing any care at all.
Our workshops begin with a 20-minute introduction on the history and science of terrariums, including their beginnings as an accidental victorian invention! Participants will learn how the terrarium creates it's own water cycle, and the types of plants and moss that can be used.
We will run a quick demonstration, including advice on planting techniques and how to get to grips with our specialist terrarium tools. Then it's time for everyone to get stuck in and make their own! We're on hand throughout the workshop to offer planting help where needed and answer any questions along the way.
The workshops finishes with a round-up of aftercare advice to keep the terrariums healthy, and each participant receives a care guide and bag for taking their terrariums home.
Where do the workshops take place?
We recommend that smaller workshops (up to 20 participants) take place in our Shop+Studio in Shoreditch where you'll be surrounded by beautiful terrariums and plants. Prefer a small workshop at a location of your choice? Let us know and we can discuss your options.
For larger groups (15-60 participants) we can come to a location of your choice, be that a workplace or hired venue. We're happy to suggest some great venues across London if needed. We're able to run multiple workshops per day, and can also facilitate drop-in style sessions.
If you have a bespoke event in mind just get touch with some details about your requirements and we'll plan the perfect workshop for you.
Please note:
For workshops held off-site at a venue of your choice, there is an additional cost of £100 to cover our travel, time, and parking costs.
For off-site workshops we arrive 45 minutes before the start time to begin setting up. We'll bring everything along with us on the day, all we need from the venue are table and chairs.
What you'll get
Everything you need to make a terrarium to keep:
Terrarium plants, moss, gravel, compost, activated charcoal
Glass vessel with cork
Use of special terrarium tools during the workshop
Bags and care guides

No prior knowledge of plants or terrariums is required -- we'll teach you everything you need to know.

description:
Elevate your workplace or client event with a private Chinese calligraphy experience, thoughtfully curated to bring calm, creativity, and cultural depth into a professional setting.
Blending art, mindfulness, and heritage, this session offers a rare opportunity to step away from fast-paced environments and engage in a slower, more intentional practice—ideal for fostering clarity, creativity, and connection.
Hosted at your office or chosen venue, the experience is fully adapted to your space, creating a calm, elegant atmosphere for your team or guests.
Why companies choose this experience
A distinctive alternative to traditional team-building activities
Encourages focus, mindfulness, and creative thinking
Creates meaningful shared moments in a relaxed setting
Ideal for client entertainment and premium hospitality
Fully hosted and tailored to your space and group size

title: Photograph Printing: Ceramic, Textile and Alternative Surfaces
description:
This short day course is designed for beginners curious about exploring creative techniques that bridge the digital and handmade worlds & a taster-style session featuring a number of photographic techniques and alternative surfaces to print on.
You’ll learn how to create digital negatives from your own photographs and transform them into tangible prints & objects using the Cyanotype or Van Dyke process. We’ll also experiment with Polaroid Lift, transferring images onto unusual surfaces - you will be able to choose from wood, fabric, or glass. Over an immersive day, you’ll craft unique, personal artworks while gaining insight into craft-based photographic methods.
This course is limited to 6 participants for a personal and hands-on experience.
COURSE AGENDA
Introduction to Alternative Photography Processes
Overview of Cyanotype, Van Dyke, and Polaroid Lift techniques.
Creating Digital Negatives
Step-by-step guidance to prepare negatives from existing digital images.
Printing with Light and Chemistry
Explore Cyanotype and Van Dyke processes to create unique handmade prints.
Polaroid Lift Transfers
Learn to apply your photographs onto unconventional surfaces like fabric, glass, or wood.
Personalised Projects
Hands-on time to create your own works under my guidance.
*Photographs in the listing are by previous participants of the course: Julie, Gill & Lucy.
What you'll get
A foundational understanding of historic photography processes.
Hands-on experience in creating 3–4 unique works to take home.
An intimate group setting with only 6 participants, allowing for tailored guidance.

title: Tile Pottery Painting Class: Design, Colour and Carve
description:
Apply Design Work in Pencil

I’ll show how designs can be created onto the tile surface with tracing , stencils or impressions and refer to the original method used historically.




Consider Colour

You’ll have a traditional pallet of colours to use or you can mix your own from stains that are used like water colours.




Line Work Is Added Last

Once your colours are complete the final stage is to add any line work. Carve fine lines through and around your colour blocks. These will be backfilled with a fine inlay of black glaze.



Join this pottery painting class in London and create your own design on a 15 cm handmade stoneware tile using traditional processes and motifs. Whether you're a seasoned pro or have no experience with clay, drawing, or painting, you'll find plenty of resources and tools to inspire you and make the design process easy.
During this hands-on workshop, you'll start by sketching out your ideas and transferring them onto the clay surface. You'll then use underglaze stains to create a vibrant colour base over your traced design. After painting, you'll use a traditional scratching tool to lightly score line work through the images and into the clay. These lines are then washed with a black stain to create striking detail on your finished piece.
A clear glaze will be applied to brighten your colours before your work is fired in the kiln. You'll finish the session feeling inspired by your new skills, with a beautiful, one-of-a-kind keepsake to cherish.
Sketch your ideas – Transfer your personal designs directly onto the clay surface
Paint with underglaze – Create a colourful base that will become even brighter after firing
Master line work – Use a traditional scratching tool to score details and apply a black stain wash
Glaze your work – Apply a clear coating to make your design pop
Your finished tile will be fired and ready for collection three to four weeks later, serving as a wonderful reminder of your creative breakthrough.
What you'll get
You will enjoy the benefits of an immersive creative session, learn about traditional tile decorative techniques, and make your own stoneware tile with studio-grade materials and tools. This will be fully fired and glazed.
See booking options
Knowledge required
No previous experience is necessary.
What to bring
You will receive a sheet outlining any design work you’d like to prepare beforehand. But this is not essential, and this can be created within the session. You won’t get hugely messy, but do bring an apron if required.



FAQ

Is this a pottery painting class?
We will certainly be painting as part of the process but this is a lot more. The class explains & uses traditional decorative ceramic studio techniques. You will be using image transfer, pencil drafting, painting & line work with carving.
I’m too busy to prep anything, will this matter?
No. You are welcome to work out a draft before you arrive (and you’ll have a sheet to explain the size and tips for best results) to maximise your work time with the clay but if you’d rather I have resources and templates etc for lovely designs.
Is this good for a group?
Let me know if you’d like to book for a group - I can use a much larger space at my studio for up to 12 but it needs booking. This is an ideal project for a hen or stag - create cork backed tiles to go on the tables at the wedding with a common colour theme?
See more FAQs

Even Rolling

I’ll show you how to achieve even rolling out of your clay and avoid the likelihood of warping.




Careful Cutting Out

Construction & Finishing

Firing & Glaze

Your work will be fully fired and glazed with no extra charge, and become fully functional and dish washer safe.

You can fully personalise your work using a wide range of creative stamps and letters, making your dish truly one-of-a-kind. title: Family Clay Workshop, Sgraffito [scratch Technique] on Tiles
description:
Welcome to My Studio

Let’s settle in first, with sat space for children. We’ll have a brief introduction to my studio and what I do there and what we might look at after the project is done. Children may be interested to see the kiln, how their work will become glazed and examples of additional pottery projects made by children.




Pre-prepared Tiles

I will have pre prepared black stoneware tiles ready for working on. These will be ‘leather hard’ and have a top layer of white. We will be using a traditional technique to scratch away this white to reveal line, pattern or text and create the basis for some colour to be added.




Plan Our Work

We’ll have a chat about the way that short messages can inspire us and help remind, remember, make goals, or whatever is appropriate for your family and of course you may already have your own ideas. Drawings or text are equally effective. We’ll make a quick plan on paper to use as reference.




Practice with the Tools

A quick practice with the tools helps everyone gain confidence and inspires new pattern too. Tools are pointy rather than blades, used at your own risk but my own children have used them safely.




A Border Creates the Space for Pattern and Text

You’ll all have easy and simple help to create the basics of your design




Drawing Out the Tile Design Is Clear for Everyone

Use your paper work as reference and start scratching your design onto the clay. We’ll add colour too!




Finished Work Will Dry Slowly and Be Glazed Transparent

I will guide your tile through the two firings and glazing process and your tiles will be ready for collection three to four weeks later.



Join this special pottery class in South East London, created for all the family to enjoy together in a professional studio space.
You will get to work with studio-grade clay, vibrant colours, and proper tools as you create your own unique picture tile. FAQ

Can I leave my children with you?
I am fully DBS checked and insured but you’ll need to buy a place too and be on hand to assist younger children. Your children will produce work which will truly preserve those moments of passion, drawings and hand writing so I’m sure you’ll want to help them create something meaningful for you all!
Is this suitable for very young children?
This is a professional working space and not suitable for running about but children who can sit up in a chair and make marks will love this. Children that need a breather can pop outside with your supervision to the picnic area right alongside my studio. Possibly as a guide I would say over age 4 but you be the judge, I taught an amazing 3 year old this week.
Is this a good activity for older & younger children & a grand parent?
YES, and for you too! It’s something you can all do together at your own level and with your own ideas. Make a family set of tiles [and come back next year and make another set!]

title: Paint Jam Hen Party
description:
Celebrate in style with a Paint Jam hen party, the perfect arty way to spend the day with your hen and her best friends. Set in an immersive pop-up art studio, these hen party experiences are packed with creative fun and special touches designed to make the day one to remember.
You'll enjoy an artist-led painting workshop complete with themed art projections, live DJ sets and a proper party feel, or opt for a curated music playlist if you'd prefer something a little calmer. Everyone paints their own canvas on an easel, and there's the option of a large communal canvas that the group paints together for the hen to keep, or a conjoined-canvas option where each guest takes home a piece of one bigger picture. A prosecco reception and nibbles are on offer too, with BYO or full catering and bar options available, plus a choice of fab modern art painting themes to set the tone.
Built on the belief of Art for Everyone, the Pop-Up Art Studio is a warm, fully inclusive space where total beginners are more than welcome.
The Classic Paint Jam Hen Party gives you the full Paint Jam experience over 3 hours. You'll paint your own canvases in a lively, social party atmosphere, with a DJ spinning tunes as you get creative, paint, dance and drink together. The session kicks off with a prosecco reception and nibbles on arrival (non-alcoholic parties can also be arranged), followed by intro exercises on your chosen painting theme before you paint your own themed canvas. There's also a communally painted hen canvas to create together – a special keepsake the hen gets to take home.
To make the day even more memorable, you can add on extras like afternoon tea, a prosecco brunch, delicious dining, a professional make-up artist, a life model, or fancy dress.
Please note: the base venue is in Brentford, though different locations can be arranged, and every Paint Jam hen do is created individually to suit exactly what you'd like.

A Canvas each*
A big communal HEN canvas for you to paint together*
All materials including paper, paints, brushes and other art materials.
Live DJ Music – you can also send us requests for your hens fave tunes.
Prosecco reception + nibbles (crisps, dips, olives & nuts).
Protective t-shirts.

title: Bridal Party Embroidery Experience
description:
Join this bridal party embroidery workshop in London and experience a wonderful, hands-on way to celebrate the bride-to-be with a beautiful personal touch.
Perfect for first-timers and seasoned stitchers alike, this relaxed session is a great place to start if you've never picked up a needle before. Your encouraging teacher will guide you step-by-step through simple embroidery techniques, making it incredibly easy to switch off, share stories, and craft custom pieces together without any pressure.
This experience draws inspiration from beautiful wedding traditions found across many cultures – where close friends and family come together to craft handmade embroidered items for the couple (just like Angelina Jolie's famous wedding veil, which featured drawings by her children!). It's a heartwarming alternative to the usual party plans, focusing on quality time together and slowing down to make memories.
You can choose exactly what you would like to customise to create a truly one-of-a-kind keepsake:
Veils and handkerchiefs – Add delicate patterns, meaningful dates, or sweet initials.
Scarves and garments – Stitch lovely motifs that she can wear long after the big day.
Sentimental keepsakes – Create a unique heirloom packed with love from her favourite people.
By the end of this uplifting workshop, your group will have shared a beautiful, bonding experience that turns simple threads into lasting memories. You'll all walk away with a collection of stunning, custom-stitched treasures ready to surprise the bride on her special day.
Please note: You must provide the fabric items you wish to embroider yourself (such as veils, handkerchiefs, or scarves).

Everything (except the item to be stitched on) to be able to create a piece of embroidery to gift to the bride.

Next, you will discover the graceful rhythm of brush and ink as you learn the art of calligraphy. You'll be guided through foundational strokes to create your own expressive piece. Throughout the day, you’ll enjoy gentle guidance, inspiring stories, and time to reflect and connect with others in a relaxed, welcoming space. This beautiful day of creativity and calm requires no experience, just curiosity and an open heart.
You’ll leave with your own unique artwork and a calm, inspired mind, feeling thoroughly refreshed by this day dedicated to slowing down and learning new skills.

title: Introduction to Gilding Workshop
description:
Introduction

I'll draw on my experience of working in museums and galleries, and alongside conservators, to teach you a little bit about this ancient art form.




Choose Your Shapes

There will be a range of wooden shapes to choose from - they make excellent baubles for the tree or are simply beautiful catching the light on these darker days.




Gilding

I'll talk you through the process step by step. You'll work with adhesives and different brushes to achieve the desired effect.




Experimentation

Once you've finished your wooden shape you'll have the chance to experiment with different shapes and textures - make a gorgeous golden shell or bring your own trinket!



Join me in this delightful introduction to gilding workshop. You will embark on a creative journey into the elegant world of gilding. Learn the enchanting art of applying gold leaves to various surfaces as you craft a stunning piece to adorn your home. No prior experience is needed, as you will be guided through each step with patience and experience.
During the workshop, you will become acquainted with the different tools and techniques involved in the gilding process. Working with delicate imitation gold leaf, you will experience a sense of calm and accomplishment as you transform ordinary objects into shimmering masterpieces.
We'll start with gilding a wooden shape, from flowers to celestial shapes - perfect gifts, decorations, or just adding some light to the gloomy days. I'll talk you through the process, the materials, and the ways in which you can incorporate gilding into other art practices.
Once you've got to grips with the process, you'll be able to experiment with different textures. I'll provide a gorgeous selection of shells for you to play with, or you are welcome to bring your own small trinket to turn to gold - some of my favourites include Lego bricks and dried leaves.
By the end of the session, you will take home not only a beautiful gilded creation but also a newfound appreciation for this mesmerising craft. A perfect combination of creativity, learning, and joy in this gilding activity.
I'll be hosting this session at Something Good Workshops in Deptford. There will be a range of hot drinks and alcoholic refreshments for sale at their bar so you can make your experience even more magical!
What you'll get
Expert tuition and guidance throughout.
One gilded wooden shape of their choice.
One gilded trinket - choose from shells or bring your own small object (Lego brick, dried leaf, stone, etc)

title: Indo-Oriental-French Cooking Class - Half Day
description:
Get ready for a culinary adventure in the heart of London that embraces a true fusion of flavours and cuisines! This cooking class is a vibrant melting pot, where you'll learn to create dishes that combine the best of African, French, Chinese, and Indian gastronomy into one amazing experience.
The birthplace of this incredible culinary emulsion is the island of Mauritius. With its French colonial past in the 18th century, the arrival of Chinese immigrants in the late 19th century, alongside the Indian community that lived and worked there during the same era, a deeply layered gastronomy has emerged. Each culture brought its unique cooking techniques and ingredients, creating a fusion that is as diverse as it is delicious.
Join your friendly and passionate teachers at the London Vegetarian and Vegan School as we celebrate the very essence of these flavours, blending them with the refined techniques of French culinary disciplines that continue to shine today. You'll learn to cook three to four recipes under expert guidance.
Indulge in traditional dishes like rougaille and vindaye, and let your taste buds explore innovative creations inspired by the renowned five-star restaurants of the island. From spiced tapenade to coconut risotto, this culinary journey will leave you inspired and eager to recreate these incredible flavours in your own kitchen.
Outline of the day:
Recipe review, demonstration and skill techniques.
Refresher break.
Full hands on workshop.
Take home cooked cuisine.
What you'll get
All ingredients and equipment needed to make and take home your cooked cuisine.
Aprons to wear throughout the class.

title: Italian Cooking Class: Handmade Pasta, Bruschetta, Tiramisu
description:
Cook Together with Chef Malachi

Chef Malachi will guide you through the cooking process and share simple professional techniques to help you create delicious Italian dishes. With years of experience as a London-based chef, he loves bringing people together through food and creating a relaxed, enjoyable cooking experience.

During the class you’ll cook, learn new skills and enjoy the process of preparing fresh Italian dishes together in a friendly atmosphere. 🍝

Join pastry chef Sofia to create a classic Italian tiramisu assembled in elegant glasses. During this part of the class, Sofia will guide you step by step through the technique, sharing professional pastry tips and secrets to achieve the perfect creamy texture and balanced flavour.

With over 6 years of experience in pastry and more than 1000 students taught both online and in person, Sofia will share practical tricks, common mistakes to avoid and small details that make desserts truly exceptional.

This is your chance to learn directly from a pastry chef 🍰




Create a Creative Bruschetta Trio

Start the class by preparing a delicious Italian bruschetta trio. You’ll learn how to toast the bread perfectly and combine fresh ingredients to create beautiful and flavourful toppings.

This part of the class is fun and creative — everyone will have the chance to experiment with different combinations and presentation. It’s the perfect way to begin the evening and get into the Italian cooking spirit. 🥖🇮🇹




Make Fresh Handmade Tagliatelle

In this step you’ll learn how to make fresh Italian pasta from scratch. Together we will prepare handmade tagliatelle and discover the simple techniques that give pasta its perfect texture.

Chef Malachi will guide you through each stage — from mixing the dough to shaping beautiful pasta strands. The pasta will then be served with a rich wild mushroom and truffle sauce, creating a truly authentic Italian dish. 🍝✨

By the end of this step, you’ll understand the fundamentals of fresh pasta and feel confident recreating it at home.



Join this Italian cooking class in London and master the art of traditional flavours under the expert guidance of Chef Malachi and Pastry Chef Sofia. This hands-on session is all about getting stuck in and preparing a delicious three-course menu while picking up simple professional techniques in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere.
Throughout the session, you'll work together to create:
Bruschetta trio – Experiment with different toppings to build your own delicious combinations.
Fresh handmade tagliatelle – Prepare pasta from scratch and pair it with a rich wild mushroom and truffle sauce.
Classic tiramisu – Assemble individual desserts in glasses for the perfect sweet finish.
There's no need to worry about the technical side of things, as you'll be supported every step of the way. description:

We start the evening by getting to know each other and learning a little about Ukrainian food traditions. I will share stories about Ukrainian cuisine, family recipes and the dishes we will cook together. This is a relaxed and friendly moment to meet the group before we begin cooking.




Cooking Traditional Ukrainian Borscht

Together we will cook one of the most famous Ukrainian dishes — traditional borscht. You will learn how to prepare the ingredients, balance the flavours and create a rich, comforting soup using authentic techniques. I will share tips and stories about why borscht is such an important part of Ukrainian food culture.




Making Homemade Varenyky

We will prepare traditional Ukrainian dumplings from scratch. You will learn how to make soft dough, shape the varenyky and fill them the traditional way. This is one of the most loved Ukrainian dishes, often made together with family and friends.




Golden Deruny & Sharing Dinner

We finish the cooking by making crispy golden deruny — traditional Ukrainian potato pancakes. Once everything is ready, we will sit down together and enjoy the dishes we have prepared in a warm and relaxed atmosphere.

FAQ

What safety gear do you provide?
On our UV resin workshops we provide a full safety kit for every student, including nitrile gloves and a P2V charcoal-valved mask. Our studio is also equipped with a Resiners PurAir filtration system, which is SGS-certified to remove 83% of resin-specific VOCs from the air.
Are the gloves provided in resin workshops safe for allergies?
We use nitrile gloves because they are the gold standard for those with latex allergies. While true nitrile allergies are extremely rare (less than 1% of the population), some people may experience minor skin redness from the "accelerators" used to make the gloves stretchy. If you have extremely sensitive skin, please let us know.
Is the resin "non-toxic"?
We use "Low VOC" resins, which are much safer and have a milder scent than industrial resins. However, all liquid resin requires respect. By using our specialized air purifiers and wearing your provided charcoal mask and gloves, your exposure is kept to a minimum.

title: Private Cyanotype Workshop
description:
Join this private cyanotype session at BE KA Art Studio, Elena's riverside atelier at Trinity Buoy Wharf, just moments from Canary Wharf. Set at your own pace, this tailored one-to-one (or small group) format is perfect for exploring the technique in a bit more depth.
Cyanotype is one of the oldest photographic printing processes, and one of the most satisfying – using only sunlight, water and natural materials. You'll arrange botanicals, feathers or shells onto coated paper, expose them to light, then rinse your print and watch that distinctive deep blue image bloom. No cameras, no screens, no experience needed – just you, some plants and the light doing the rest.
This private format is ideal for a special occasion, a creative day with friends or family, or simply a more personal, flexible pace than a group taster session. You'll:
Arrange botanicals and objects to compose your own prints
Explore techniques and materials in more depth, at your own pace
Add a personal touch with photo on film, wooden letters, drawings or handwritten details
Expose your work in sunlight or UV light
Develop your prints in water and watch the images appear
Sessions run for two hours as standard, though this can be adjusted to suit you, and step-free access with disabled toilets is available on site.
Please note: by attending, you agree that photos and videos may be taken for promotional use on the BE KA website and social channels. If you'd rather not appear, just let Elena know and your wishes will be respected.
What you'll get
1 A5 coated paper sheet in your choice of colour, or 2 small squared sheets.
1 A4 watercolour sheet, which you'll prime with the photosensitive solution.
1 A4 print of your photo on film — Please decide beforehand what photo you'd like printed on film to make one of your artworks.
Markers and brushes.
Cyanotype chemicals and aprons.
Botanicals, feathers, shells, and natural materials (feel free to bring your own if you'd like).
Small wooden craft letters.
More material can be purchased on site on the day. If you'd like a longer session or to explore a particular technique (including drawing and painting on film, double exposure, cyanotype toning, cyanotype and watercolour, etc.), please let me know, and I'll adjust as needed.

Meet Paint Jam: a one-of-a-kind team-building workshop with a proper party feel. It brings together an artist-led painting session with live DJ sets, themed art projections and a prosecco reception on arrival – a fresh, quirky alternative to the usual corporate event. Prefer something slower-paced? Simple painting workshops and art-and-meditation sessions are on offer too.
You can host your Paint Jam at the Pop Up Art Studio in Brentford, in your own office, or at a partner venue in Fitzrovia, Bermondsey, Soho, Covent Garden, Kings Cross or Shoreditch. Pick from a range of painting themes, and weave your brand in if you like.
Paint Jam's signature Art Tunnel is an experimental journey through modern art, built on the belief that art really is for everyone. In this warm, studio-meets-party space, you'll have canvases, easels, acrylic paints and all the tools you need at your fingertips, with a friendly artist guiding you and the DJ's music sparking inspiration throughout. Everyone keeps their own painting to take home or hang proudly on the office wall.
Art really is good for you – Paint Jam sessions bring out creative expression, play and a welcome sense of presence and relaxation. Expect your team to leave feeling refreshed and freshly connected to their creative side, having picked up new skills and bonded in ways that carry straight back into everyday teamwork.
For something extra special, try the collaborative painting workshop, where the team negotiates fun, colourful painting challenges together under the artist's guidance. It's a cathartic, uplifting experience that creates a lasting group memory – and the artworks can later be hung in your workplace as a proud, feel-good symbol of the day.
Please note: the video was filmed in our previous Soho studio – please enquire about current central London venue options.

An artist-led painting workshop.
A stretched canvas 40x50cm to paint and keep.
A large collaborative canvas experience.
Acrylic paints, drawing materials, and all brushes, palette knives, and painting equipment, including an easel each.

title: Immersive Bengali Cooking Workshop
description:
Join OITIJ-JO Kitchen for a three-part cooking workshop and explore the bold, comforting flavours of Bengali home cooking. This is a wonderful activity for anyone curious about Bengali food and culture, with no prior experience needed.
Over three Wednesday evenings, you will learn how to create traditional dishes from scratch with guidance from a woman-led social enterprise. At the end of each hands-on session, you'll sit down with your fellow classmates to enjoy the delicious meal you've all prepared.
Your weekly cooking schedule:
Session 1 – 21st August: Bhorta – Discover the art of smoky, mashed vegetables and proteins, a cornerstone of Bangladeshi comfort food.
Session 2 – 28th August: Pitha – Make sweet and savoury handmade rice cakes from scratch that are delicate, festive, and full of cultural history.
Session 3 – 4th September: Roti & Masala Curry – Create flaky, layered flatbreads paired with a rich, slow-cooked masala, cooked the traditional way.
Whether you're joining for all three sessions or just coming along to one, you’ll finish this series with a renewed sense of confidence in the kitchen and the skills to recreate these comforting meals at home, along with a deeper appreciation for Bengali culture.

title: Wildlife Gardening Workshop
description:

During the session you will gain insight into simple, achievable actions that can help you to encourage wildlife in your garden and learn to adopt a more relaxed attitude to the way you manage your space. Alongside practical demonstrations of our own radical ‘nature-first’ approach, we aim to discuss current trends in sustainable gardening, with a critical approach to their impact. The session will leave you confident in moving beyond simply ‘organic’ or ‘chemical free’, into embracing the wild, without sacrificing what is most valuable to you in your space.
‘If something is not eating your plants, then your garden is not part of the ecosystem’: alternative approaches to pest and disease management

title: Foraging Workshop: Kimchi Making and Wild Soup
description:
We’re thrilled to invite you and your team to join us for an unforgettable culinary adventure blending nature, creativity, and connection. Perfect for a friends day out or date! Our upcoming wild food foraging events are designed to foster collaboration, spark inspiration, and create delicious memories.
We will be enjoying + discover the wealth of seasonal plants and fungi of Hackney Marshes, as we forage to create seasonal lacto-ferments and tasty soup.
Please meet us by 11am at the entrance to the Middlesex Filter beds nature reserve (west side entrance), accessible on the Canal Towpath opposite Millfields park (see attached picture for entrance front).
So, to give a bit more detail, on this fun and engaging workshop, we will go out with Fergus in Hackney Marshes and identify different seasonal wild plants and herbs, learn how best to work with them (not just for soup, but in loads of different ways), as well as gather plants relevant to lacto-fermentation and the making of a delicious seasonal soup.
Commonly made foods which utilise fermentation include yoghurt, kimchi and pickles. We will discover which plants are best suited for fermentation, and each gather a unique combination, however we will all have a common base with which to start, for example: hogweed. We will then, with Fergus’ guidance, be able to customise our lacto-fermentation with the other plants collected during our forage, such as cow parsley, wild garlic, even some fungi perhaps.
We will also be foraging together to gather ingredients for a communal soup, which Fergus will prepare.
As we enjoy our soup and sourdough bread, we will also feast on any foraging questions you have for Fergus, and for Tevin and his unique Herbivore creations.
Fergus will give clear instructions on how to monitor and adjust the lactoferment you will have prepared in the weeks after taking it home from the workshop.
Feel free to bring your own wine or beer :)

title: Authentic Italian Cooking Class
description:
Ciao & Benvenuti

I’ll welcome you with a smile and a little taste of Naples as we get ready to cook together. Everything you need will be set out, so you can relax and enjoy the experience from the very start.




Fresh Flavours

We’ll begin by exploring the fresh, simple ingredients that make Italian food so special — juicy tomatoes, fragrant basil, rich olive oil. The quality of these is the secret to true flavour.




Cooking Together

Now it’s your turn! Roll up your sleeves as we chop, stir, and simmer step by step. No experience needed — I’ll guide you through every stage, just like cooking at home with family.




Secrets of the Kitchen

You’ll discover authentic Italian techniques passed down through generations — from shaping pasta by hand to layering silky aubergines for Parmigiana. These are the tips Italians grow up with but rarely write down.




Dish Comes Alive

This is the magic moment — the kitchen fills with Mediterranean aromas as your dish comes together, bubbling, golden, and ready to be enjoyed.




Buon Appetito

Finally, we sit down to enjoy the meal you’ve created. You’ll leave not just with a delicious dish, but with new skills, stories, and a taste of Italian tradition to share again and again.



Discover the joy of authentic Italian cooking at this hands-on culinary workshop. In a warm and welcoming kitchen, you will learn how to prepare classic dishes from scratch, with no prior experience needed – just an enthusiasm for delicious food!
This activity is a chance to learn traditional cooking secrets passed down through generations. Using fresh, seasonal ingredients, you will enjoy the incredible aromas of garlic, basil, and rich tomato sauce as your host guides you step-by-step.
In this class, you will:
Learn how to make an Italian favourite, such as handmade pasta, Parmigiana di Melanzane, or classic meatballs.
Cook your chosen dish from start to finish with expert guidance.
Sit down to enjoy the delicious meal you have prepared in a relaxed, friendly setting.
You will leave this session with a wonderful sense of accomplishment, armed with new skills and authentic recipes to take home so you can recreate the true taste of Italy for your friends and family.
Please note: Vegetarian or gluten-free options are available on request — just let me know in advance so we can plan the right ingredients together.

title: The Way of Matcha Workshop
description:
Join this unique, sensory tea workshop in London, designed to introduce you to the beauty of Japanese tea rituals with a contemporary and seasonal twist. This activity is rooted in the philosophy of presence, simplicity, and sensory awareness, blending traditional Japanese tea ceremony, mindful matcha preparation, and modern tea tasting, all within a calm and welcoming environment. You will learn how to slow down and connect with the present moment through this engaging workshop.
The session unfolds gently to help you feel at ease:
You will start with a mini sensory exploration to calm down and ground yourself.
This is followed by a short guided ceremony rooted in chanoyu tradition, where you’ll observe and sip matcha in stillness and learn about the cultural significance of tea as a ritual.
During this hands-on activity, you’ll be guided step-by-step in how to prepare your own bowl of matcha. You will learn to use high-quality uji tea, a traditional bamboo whisk (chasen), and thoughtful technique to create the perfect bowl. After your whisking practise, you’ll be served a chilled or warm matcha creation featuring a seasonal fruit purée – a fresh, modern twist on this traditional drink.
Each delightful drink is thoughtfully served with a small, seasonal wagashi (traditional Japanese sweet), selected to complement the flavours of the tea.
This soothing workshop offers a restorative experience, leaving you with a deeper appreciation for the art of Japanese tea. You will take home the skills to prepare matcha and a richer understanding of its cultural importance.
What you'll get
A hands-on matcha workshop in London
A better understanding of the art of Japanese matcha
Hands-on unique experience in preparing and whisking matcha & tea drinks
A delicious, seasonal wagashi treats
A calming, mindful experience in London

Spend 2 hours at the potter’s wheel learning the basics of throwing bowls and cylinders.
Create approximately 2–4 clay pieces during the session.
Receive hands-on guidance from a professional pottery tutor.
Work in a small group (maximum of 8 people) for personal support.

title: Pottery Taster Class: Wheel Throwing and Hand Building
description:
Join this pottery wheel and hand-building class in Balham and get ready to get hands-on with clay in a relaxed, friendly environment. Over two hours, you'll explore the basics of crafting bowls and cylinders, splitting your time between the potter's wheel and traditional hand-building techniques. With a maximum of eight people per session, you'll have plenty of space to learn and connect with fellow makers while a professional tutor guides you through every spin and sculpt.
During this session, you'll typically create between two and four pieces, making it a fantastic way for first-timers to spark their interest in ceramics. Whether you come with a friend or head along solo to meet some like-minded people, the focus is entirely on having fun and enjoying the tactile nature of working with clay.
What's included:
Professional instruction – Learn from a seasoned potter who will guide you through the process.
Two hours of guided making – Spend an hour at the wheel and an hour hand-building.
Two finished pieces – You'll finish the session with one wheel-thrown masterpiece and one hand-built creation.
Firing and glazing options – Choose to enjoy the making process for £50, add bisque firing for £5, or opt to decorate and glaze your work for an additional fee (£10 per hour).
Collection – Your items will be ready to pick up within 21 days, and we'll keep them for another 30 days.
This low-pressure workshop is a wonderful way to switch off from the daily grind and find your flow. You'll finish the class feeling inspired by your new skills and ready to show off your unique handmade keepsakes.
Please note: If you choose to have your items fired and glazed, you will need to return to the studio to collect them once they have been through the kiln.

title: Matcha Tasting and Pottery Workshop
description:
Come and join us for this two-hour matcha and pottery workshop in London! You’ll sip premium ceremonial-grade matcha and create your own matcha bowl to take home.
Don't worry if you've never tried your hand at pottery before -- this workshop is beginner-friendly and perfect for anyone looking to slow down, create, and connect with the art of tea. It's a perfect gift for the matcha lover in your life, and a great activity to do with friends in London.
What to Expect:
Freshly whisked matcha tasting (45 mins): your journey begins with a calming tea-tasting session. - -
Discover the art of preparing matcha the traditional way using a chawan (matcha bowl) and chasen (bamboo whisk), while enjoying two styles of matcha: usucha (thin tea), and iced oat matcha latte.
You’ll also learn more about the origins of matcha, why it is good for our health, and how to whisk your own matcha at home.
Short break (5 mins)
Make your own matcha bowl (70 mins): after a short break, you’ll be introduced to hand-building techniques under the guidance of expert instructors.
Your finished piece: after the workshop, your matcha bowl will be professionally glazed and kiln-fired to ensure it’s food-safe and ready for tea rituals at home.
Free studio pickup
UK shipping: £5
Optional painting session after firing: £5
Immerse yourself in this relaxing workshop where you can connect with the art of tea and pottery, and once it's ready, take away your handmade matcha bowl to cherish.
What you'll get
Matcha tea tasting.
Hands-on matcha-making experience.
A completed matcha bowl to use at home.

description:

​

title: Beautifully Broken: Kintsugi and Matcha Experience
description:
Break

Let go and let it break




Meditate

Analyse your pieces




Repair

Build it back together piece by piece




Heal

Remind yourself that you have the power to fix anything



Join this Kintsugi workshop in London at Craftshops and discover the meditative art of turning broken ceramics into beautiful, one-of-a-kind treasures. You'll intentionally break a ceramic piece, then slowly and thoughtfully piece it back together using gold – a hands-on process that's as calming as it is creative.
Rooted in traditional Japanese philosophy, Kintsugi teaches us to embrace imperfection and find meaning in repair. Whether you're a complete beginner or looking to try something different, this workshop is designed to feel low-pressure and welcoming. There's no rushing – you'll work at your own pace, guided by a friendly teacher every step of the way. As your hands work, you'll discover something genuinely therapeutic: the joy of slowing down, letting go of the need for perfection, and experiencing the quiet satisfaction of creating with intention.
This is as much about the journey as the finished piece. You'll find space to unwind, connect with others and enjoy a moment of calm away from everyday life. The whole experience encourages mindfulness, patience and gentle reflection – pure feel-good creativity.
By the end, you'll walk away with a beautifully restored ceramic piece that's entirely yours – a one-of-a-kind keepsake and a tangible reminder that broken things can become even more beautiful. It's the perfect way to nurture your wellbeing and create something genuinely meaningful.
What you'll get
Complimentary matcha to enjoy as you relax into the experience
A friendly, professional guide to support you every step of the way
All materials provided, including your ceramic piece and gold for restoration
Your own finished Kintsugi masterpiece to take home and proudly display

title: Floral Palette Knife Painting Workshop
description:
Join this palette knife painting class in London and discover a feel-good way to catch up with friends while exploring a new creative skill. You'll swap screen time for real-life fun as you learn how to build beautiful textures and vibrant colours on canvas in a low-pressure, welcoming environment.
Guided by a friendly teacher, you'll follow a simple process to bring your floral masterpiece to life:
Lightly sketch your design – Start with a gentle pencil outline to map out your composition.
Paint the background – Use a wide brush to sweep in your base colours and set the mood.
Shape the leaves – Get hands-on with a palette knife to create thick, expressive foliage.
Create the flowers – Use the palette knife to layer paint and add wonderful dimension to your blooms.
Add the final details – Finish your piece by using a thin brush to define the vase and delicate stems.
Your teacher will demonstrate every step on their own canvas first, so you can see exactly how it's done before you have a go. Whether you're a complete first-timer or a regular maker, there's plenty of support available if you have questions or need a little extra help.
You'll finish the session with a sense of pride and a one-of-a-kind keepsake to show off at home. This social London painting class is a wonderful way to spark your imagination and walk away with a lasting piece of art that reminds you of a joyful, mindful afternoon.

title: Notebook Bookbinding Class
description:
In this hands-on bookbinding workshop in London, you'll learn the traditional Coptic stitch binding technique, a beautiful method that creates a notebook with an exposed spine that opens completely flat. This ancient binding style is both decorative and practical, allowing the pages to lie flat -- perfect for drawing, writing, or displaying photos.
Never tried bookbinding before? No worries -- this class is completely beginner-friendly, and you'll receive expert guidance throughout as you engage with this timeless craft.
What to expect:
Work on your own A5 handmade book, choosing to make it either as a sketchbook, journal, or photo album.
You will be guided step by step through folding pages, preparing the covers, and stitching the sections together using the distinctive Coptic binding pattern.
Feel free to bring your own special papers, photographs or materials and we'll help you incorporate them into your book.
Personalise and decorate the cover using Posca markers, adding patterns, colours, or botanical motifs to make your book truly unique.
By the end of the workshop, you'll have your completed book -- completely unique and lovingly handmade by you. Plus new creative skills to keep experimenting with at home!
What you'll get
All materials provided, plus expert tutelage on this ancient bookbinding tradition.

title: Pretty Bow Sip and Stitch Embroidery Workshop
description:

Back stitch – Master this fundamental stitch for clean outlines.
Whipped back stitch – Perfect for creating smooth lines and hiding any gaps in your back stitches!
Satin stitch – An embroidery must-have stitch.
Fly stitch – Add curves and a variety of shapes with this stitch.
French knots – Perfect these classic, dainty raised dots.
3D beads – Learn the secrets to adding shimmer and dimension to your work.
You don't need to bring a thing as everything is set up for you. You'll receive a full kit containing all the high-quality materials required to complete your hoop design. It's a lovely excuse to catch up with a friend over a drink while you learn a skill that you can use to hand-craft unique gifts for your loved ones.
You'll leave the session feeling inspired and refreshed, carrying home a charming handmade keepsake that's ready to show off. This experience is a fantastic way to rekindle your creativity and walk away with newfound confidence in your making abilities.

title: Street Photography Workshop: Still-Life on the Streets
description:
Join this street photography workshop in West London and capture the city from an entirely new perspective. You'll go beyond the typical wide-angle shots and candid portraits to focus on the quiet, often overlooked details that give a street its character. Whether it's a weathered park bench, a vibrant shop-window display, or a brightly coloured door, you'll learn how to turn these everyday scenes into striking photographic subjects.
This session is perfect for beginners looking for a gentle, structured introduction to the craft, as well as more experienced photographers who want to slow down and practice intentional composition. You'll benefit from shared insights and hands-on guidance as you explore the urban landscape together.
During the class, you'll learn how to:
Spot and select compelling subjects – Find the hidden gems in plain sight.
Master core framing and composition rules – Use the rule of thirds, leading lines, and negative space to create balance.
Approach your shots creatively – Discover when to get close, when to step back, and how to use focal length to tell a story.
Create narrative focal points – Turn simple details like a rusted bike or an old sign into the star of your photo.
Refine your practical workflow – Pick up quick camera-setting checks, exposure tricks for tricky lighting, and tips for reviewing your work.
By the end of the walk, you'll have a fresh set of skills and a collection of unique images that showcase your personal vision. It's an eye-opening experience that ensures you'll never look at a simple street corner the same way again, leaving you with a newfound appreciation for the art of observation.
What you'll get
A PDF as a handout
See booking options
Knowledge required
Basic knowledge of your camera.
What to bring
Please bring along any camera you're comfortable using, whether that's a smartphone, digital SLR, mirrorless, or film camera. You'll just need a basic understanding of how your equipment works and a curiosity to walk and observe the world around you.



FAQ

Who is this workshop suitable for?
It welcomes complete beginners who want a gentle introduction to street photography, as well as experienced shooters looking to explore still‑life compositions on the street.
What equipment do I need to bring?
Any camera you’re comfortable with – a smartphone, digital SLR, mirrorless body or even a film camera – provided you know how to adjust ISO, aperture and shutter speed.
What will I walk away with after the workshop?
You’ll leave with a small portfolio of 5–10 thoughtfully composed street‑still‑life images, a personal checklist for future outings, and the confidence to spot and capture overlooked urban details.

title: Textured Art Workshop
description:
Join this textured art workshop in Sunbury-on-Thames and spend two hours playing with rich textures, beautiful colours, and raised paint as you create your own custom canvas. It's a wonderfully feel-good, low-pressure way to switch off from the busy week and discover a fun, creative outlet.
You don't need any prior art experience at all, and you don't even need to arrive with a fixed idea in mind. This hands-on class is completely made for beginners, and everything is designed to make you feel right at home. At the start of the session, you'll get a warm introduction to how the materials work. You'll have the chance to test out the modelling paste, try the different tools, and learn how to shape, layer, and build up beautiful dimensions before moving onto your main canvas.
Once you feel comfortable and ready, you'll choose your favourite colours and start building your design. Whether you want to sculpt soft textured flowers, craft a modern abstract piece, or just see where your intuition takes you, the choice is entirely yours! You'll have friendly, step-by-step guidance throughout the entire session, but there's no requirement to copy an exact template. We're here to give you plenty of support so you feel confident while leaving lots of room to experiment and make something genuinely one-of-a-kind.
Here's what you'll learn during this hands-on session:
How to apply modelling paste using palette knives and tools
How to create raised texture on canvas
Simple textured painting techniques, including floral and abstract styles
How to use colour, shape, and composition in your artwork
How to add finishing touches to complete your piece
Textured art is wonderfully tactile, a little messy, and incredibly satisfying as you press, scrape, and smooth the paste. By the time the session wraps up, you'll have experienced a delightful creative awakening, leaving you with a great basic understanding of palette knives and that lovely sense of pride that comes from making something beautiful from scratch. You'll head home with your gorgeous, personalised 20 x 25 cm textured canvas keepsake, ready to display proudly on your wall.
Please note: Your artwork may still be wet when you leave, as thick textured paste takes some time to fully set. Your teacher will show you exactly how to carry it home safely in your provided carrier and how to let it dry properly once you get back.
What you'll get
Your own 20 x 25 cm textured canvas to take home.
All materials provided, including acrylic paints, modelling paste, palette knives, tools, and aprons.
A short demonstration to help you feel confident before starting.

title: Lightbulb Terrarium Class
description:
In this uniquely inventive terrarium workshop in London, you'll learn how to create an extraordinary miniature world inside an A60 lightbulb - a technique you won't find taught anywhere else in the world.
Since 2024, we’ve been giving people the chance to roll up their sleeves and create their very own unique lightbulb terrariums. Sure, terrarium workshops have been all the rage lately, but nowhere else in the world will you find someone teaching you how to cram a miniature world into an actual lightbulb—and trust us, we’ve checked. Thoroughly.
Even if you’re a terrarium workshop veteran, this is your chance to learn a completely different technique using the most iconic of all lightbulbs: the A60. It’s like terrarium-making, but with a twist of “how on earth did they fit that in there?”
But wait, there’s more! This workshop isn’t just about getting your hands dirty—it’s a time machine. We’ll whisk you back to Victorian times, where a surgeon in London’s East End made an invention so groundbreaking, it lit the way for everything we’re doing now.
So grab your friends or rope in your team, and dive into this one-hour(-ish) lightbulb terrarium workshop. It’s crafting, storytelling, and just the right amount of quirk rolled into one.
What you'll get
All materials and tools to make a WildBulb WB60 Terrarium with its concrete stand, in an individual branded carton box packaging.
Paper bags are also available to make it easier to carry the terrarium.

Discover the sweet side of Italy in this hands-on dessert-making experience, where you'll learn to make two of Italy's most-loved treats from scratch: the original tiramisù and the traditional Sicilian cannolo.
You'll start with the tiramisù, learning the proper technique for whipping mascarpone to a light, airy consistency and layering it with espresso-soaked savoiardi biscuits, just as it's done in Italy. Then it's on to the cannoli, where you'll work with a traditional pastry dough, learn how to fry the shells to that signature crisp, and fill them with a rich, sweetened ricotta mixture, finished with your choice of toppings like chocolate chips, candied fruit or chopped pistachio.
Throughout, you'll use authentic Italian ingredients and time-honoured techniques passed down through generations, with friendly, hands-on guidance to help you get every step right, even if you've never made an Italian dessert before.
Once your creations are ready, take a seat and enjoy the fruits of your labour, paired with a thoughtfully chosen selection of Italian sweet wines to complement each dessert. It's a relaxed, indulgent way to explore Italy's rich dessert traditions, with great food, good wine and even better company. You'll leave with a full belly, new skills in your back pocket, and the know-how to recreate both desserts at home.

FAQ

This seems sociable, is it suitable for a larger group?
Yes! I have taught up to 12 in an additional space which is v close to my space at Thames-side. This allows for desk space each but also for a table for setting up drinks or snacks etc.
What’s the difference between throwing and hand building?
Throwing is on a potters wheel. You sit up to the machine and use the spinning forces to shape and lift the clay. You’ll get results at your first session but not necessarily the shape you were after.. that takes years and years of learning and practice. Hand building is a way of constructing pottery without the wheel. I use mostly slabbing, so rolling very even slabs which are compressed, rotated and lifted correctly to avoid warping and cut accurately and cleanly. Much easier to learn as a beginner and results can be a lot more functional as long as easy steps in construction and joining are followed.
I’m after a well being activity but I’m not really very arty, will this be suitable?
Of course, this session is about working with an earthy natural material with documented well being benefits when it is worked. I will guide your process and show you how best to use simple stamping devices within the functionality of the construction and design to create your own work with no blank space anxiety here! There will be time and encouragement to discover your own design by experimenting with shape & pattern flow.

Oasis base (size small or large)
Selection of flowers

What to bring
What you'll need
Scissors or secateurs

If you are sourcing your own materials:
Florals
Foliage: These are basically greenery, so any sort of leafy branches that can be used to fill space, such as eucalyptus, myrtle, or lemon leaf. I personally love working with Ruscus as it's very versatile and provides some depth.
Main flowers: I always like choosing a few "main flowers" which will be the centre of attention of your centrepiece. These tend to be larger, eye-catching flowers such as roses, dahlias, ranunculus, Lisianthus, or chrysanthemums.
Supporting flowers: As the name suggests, these are smaller flowers that take a bit of a "supporting" role. Those smaller, daintier flowers help fill the arrangement, add texture, and make the main blooms shine. Examples of these are carnations, mini roses, and a very good option is Gypsophila.
Remember to think of your colour schemes when picking your flowers. If you have any questions regarding these or types of flowers, please feel free to reach out!
Oasis base: If you are sourcing your own materials, please bring an oasis base of whatever shape or size you prefer. These can often be found at florists' shops or plant nurseries. I recommend buying one with a plastic base included already; otherwise, please think about what you can use as a base (such as a tray or plate) under the oasis.

title: Jewellery Making Taster Workshop: Create a Sterling Silver Ring
description:
Cut Out Your Silver

Get settled in and ready to create. You will begin by measuring and sawing a strip of sterling silver. This is where your ring starts to take shape!




Soldering

You will then form your silver strip into a band and solder it using a jeweller’s torch, joining the metal to create your ring. Plenty of guidance on hand if you need it!




Hand Finishing

title: Cyanotype Workshop - Archiving the Seasons
description:

You will learn all about the magical cyanotype process, a camera-less printing technique where UV-sensitive paper is exposed to light to create striking blue and white images. This workshop focuses on archiving the seasons, using a wonderful collection of pressed leaves, flowers, and plants to create your designs. It’s a fantastic chance to explore and nurture your connection with nature through art making.
In this hands-on session, you will get to:
Learn about the history of the cyanotype process, composition, and photography.
Experiment with exposing times and double exposures to create different effects.
Use a variety of natural foliage provided by Lizzie to create your motifs.
Make and take away three of your own prints on high-quality watercolour paper.
This workshop is open to all ages, though children must be over eight years old. Please get in touch with any queries, as accommodations can be made.
For your comfort and safety, please note:
The chemicals used can stain clothing, so it's a good idea to wear something you don't mind getting messy.
UV lamps will be used during the workshop.
It is advised to wash your hands if any chemicals come into contact with your skin.
Some prints may still be drying at the end and will need to continue drying at home – their beautiful blue colour will deepen over the next 24 hours.
This enriching experience will give you a new set of skills and a deeper appreciation for this historic art form, leaving you with three beautiful, personal prints to cherish.
What you'll get
3 Cyanotype prints.

title: Collage Narratives – Creative Writing Collage Workshop
description:
Join Elena at her atelier on the Thames for a creative writing collage experience. Connect with forgotten stories and uncover hidden narratives from within. Explore creative writing through text collage. Cut, rearrange, and transform found words into new narratives, shaping unexpected connections into your own original piece. This hands-on process bypasses the pressure of writing from scratch, opening space for discovery, play, and personal insight. Fragments become portals to echoes of memory, imagination, and new worlds.
In this words cloud collage workshop, you’ll be guided through a creative process that combines writing and visual composition. We begin with a short meditation and breathing practice to settle the mind. You’ll then be provided with magazines, newspapers, 30 x 30 cm white cardstock or A3 coloured paper card, scissors, and glue—everything you need. With gentle guidance, you’ll create your own collage of words, allowing meaning to emerge intuitively as you work. If you feel comfortable, at the end of the workshop, you’ll have the opportunity to share your piece with the group, if you wish, and we can enjoy a brief moment of collective reflection.

All materials included
Step-free access

title: Action Vision Board Workshop
description:
Join BE Ka Art Studio for an action vision board workshop in London — a thoughtfully curated experience blending creativity, science, and conscious personal growth.
Whether you're stepping into a new chapter, navigating a transition, or simply ready to pause and reflect, this workshop is designed to meet you wherever you are and help you move forward with clarity, intention, and a renewed sense of purpose.
And with spring already in the air, there's something quietly powerful about choosing this moment to set new intentions — the season has always been a natural prompt for fresh starts and new beginnings.
Set within Elena's spacious atelier at Trinity Buoy Wharf, this workshop is designed to help you move forward with clarity, intention, and a renewed sense of purpose. Led by Elena — a multidisciplinary artist, educator, and Hatha yoga teacher with a background spanning fine arts, art and science, Reiki, and creative health and wellbeing — this session goes well beyond collage. You'll gain a grounded understanding of the neuroscience behind vision boards themselves: how the physical act of searching through magazines, making intuitive choices, and arranging images by hand actively engages your brain's visual, emotional, and motivational pathways — not just the finished board on your wall. Drawing on Gestalt principles of visual perception, you'll also learn how to design your board with intention, so that its composition works with your brain rather than simply filling a page. A short guided meditation and breathwork practice opens the session, creating a calm, grounded space to tune into your own direction before you pick up the magazines and scissors. Working at your own pace and with Elena's individual support throughout, you're welcome to share reflections with the group or simply settle into your own quiet creative space. This is a low-pressure, inclusive environment — ideal whether you're new to this kind of work or simply looking for a moment to pause, reflect, and reconnect with what you want. You'll leave feeling refreshed and purposeful, taking home a bespoke action vision board to keep your goals in focus long after the day is done.
This is a place to slow down, tune in, and reconnect with what truly matters to you.
By attending, you agree to the possibility of being photographed for promotional purposes; please let Elena know on the day if you'd like to opt out.
The venue has step-free access throughout.

title: Home Coffee Training Class
description:

title: Rainbow Tree Art Class
description:
Searching for some creative things to do in London? Why not learn to paint our signature rainbow tree with our Homeless Made artist Guan?
Guan has been part of the Homeless Made collective for the last three years. He originally got involved after he became homeless and took up painting as a hobby. He has always found painting to be therapeutic and relaxing, allowing him to focus more and concentrate which helps with his mental health and wellbeing. Since working with Homeless Made Guan has designed many pieces of art that have gone on to be sold and showcased at exhibitions. One of his proudest pieces is his signature Rainbow Tree. Guan's Rainbow Tree is inspired from the tree he saw in the park when he was homeless. He would wake up every morning and see this tree, signifying hope for him. This beautiful design has gone on to be sold as a greetings card and also many canvas designs.
At this art class, you will be guided step-by-step as you learn how to paint The Rainbow Tree. title: Candlelit Ritual Sticky Chai Tea Workshop
description:
Arrival · the Soft Landing

We begin with a slow, sensory chai-making ritual. Whole spices are warmed, stirred, and steeped. Hands wrap around mugs as steam rises. This simple act becomes a threshold, a quiet boundary between the world you’ve left behind and the softness you’ve entered.




The Pause · Journaling & Presence

Settled on scattered cushions, you’re offered gentle prompts and blank pages. You may write, doodle, daydream, or simply sit. There is no sharing unless you wish. This is time to listen inwardly and meet yourself without expectation.




The Silly & the Sublime · Creating Your Dreamscape

With old magazines you've brought with you, textures, and images, you’re invited to play. We gently “blueprint” your own cosy corner, a dreamscape of softness, warmth, and rest. It’s light, imaginative, and grounding, reminding you that comfort is something you’re allowed to create.




The Craft · Sticky Chai Creation

You create your own bespoke sticky chai blend using our enchanted spice bar. Grinding, blending, and filling your tin becomes a meditative act. You’ll name your creation, a reminder of this feeling to take home with you. We name ours Snooze, Snug and Homely.




The Linger · Chai & Connection

Conversation, if it happens, is soft and unhurried. Warm your hands around your decorated sticky chai, and ease your way back into the world, carrying this slowness with you.



A candlelit, half-day tea-blending workshop in London for souls who need to step out of the drought and back to the kitchen table. This is not a just a tea-blending workshop, it's a small, candlelit pocket where the sticky chai stays warm, the clocks soften their grip, and you're invited, no, welcomed, to be human again.
Immerse yourself in a candlelit chai sanctuary retreat class in London at The Enchanted Chai Sanctuary where you step away from the hustle and bustle to rediscover a peaceful connection at the kitchen table.
This tea blending experience is not about self-improvement or adding more to your load. Instead, it's a place to unwind and slow down from daily life.
Embrace the gentle activities planned for the day, including chai rituals, quiet reflection, creative exercises, and moments of deep rest to help you relax and reconnect with your wild soul whispers.
Experience the alchemy of brewing sticky chai together, opening whole spices and sipping warmth that revitalises your parched spirit.
Delve into self-exploration in soft candlelight, with optional journaling prompts inviting you to embrace your unpolished, authentic self.
Engage in playful creativity, crafting your own Cosy Corner dreamscape and bespoke sticky chai blend to take home.
This retreat offers a transformative experience, leaving you feeling softer, less parched, and reconnected to your inner wild soul. Take home your crafted blend as a reminder of this sanctuary and the unhurried, comforting warmth it provided. Unwind, create, and rediscover at The Enchanted Chai Sanctuary, where you can leave feeling replenished and deeply connected to the tranquility of bygone afternoons.
What you'll get
A cosy arrival and slow tea-making ritual using whole spices
Time to journal, dream or simply rest; no sharing, no fixing
Create your own Cosy Corner Dreamscape
A playful, tactile moment of cutting, pasting and imagining a sanctuary you can return to at home

FAQ

What is Sticky Chai?
Unlike dry tea blends, our Sticky Chai is a living, botanical experience. We hand-fold organic, caffeine-free rooibos or low-caffeine, sustainability-sourced black tea with sun-warmed spices into a thick, organic coconut nectar. You'll taste no coconut but rather a sensual coconut flavour. This "wet" blend keeps the spices potent and fresh, creating a dark, glistening texture that is entirely plant-based and sustainably sourced. It is a golden alchemy of spice and earth.
Why is it called a Sanctuary?
Because we believe a cup of our sticky chai should be a boundary between you and the busy world. The Sanctuary is a space of presence, designed around the ethics of sustainability and the beauty of the pause. By using mostly organic, vegetarian-friendly ingredients, we ensure that your moment of peace is in harmony with the world around you.
Is the Sanctuary accessible?
The Sanctuary is currently hosted within a beautiful Grade II listed building. Due to its protected heritage structure, there is unfortunately no wheelchair access at this specific location.​We believe the magic of the Enchanted Chai Sanctuary should be open to everyone. We are actively seeking alternative, fully accessible venues for our future gatherings so that every guest can join us at the table. If you have any specific questions about the space, please reach out, we are here to help.

title: Thread Wrapping Textile Art Workshop for Beginners
description:
Preparing the Base and Materials

We begin by preparing the working surface and selecting the colour palette. A rigid square base is fully wrapped with cotton cord to create a clean, textured foundation.




Establishing the Structure

The first cord elements are laid and fixed along the edge of the base. This step defines the visual boundaries of the artwork and sets the structural logic for the weaving process that follows!




Introducing Linear Weaving

Long cord segments are guided across the surface, wrapped tightly and evenly. The cords are not knotted in a traditional way but layered and tensioned to create a flat, architectural texture.




Building Geometric Intersections

Additional strands are introduced and woven over and under the existing lines. This creates intersections and geometric blocks, adding depth and contrast while keeping the surface minimal and controlled. Help on hand if you need it!




Extending the White Structure

Additional white cord is used to extend the existing geometry. The weaving continues within the established structure, reinforcing rhythm, balance, and density without changing the colour palette.




Introducing Green Accent

A light green cord is carefully integrated into the composition. The new colour follows the same wrapping and layering logic, subtly shifting the visual focus while maintaining harmony with the existing white structure.




Completing the Interwoven Pattern

Dark green lines are reintroduced to frame the composition. The contrast between white, dark green, and light green is finalised through precise wrapping and tension control.




Final Adjustment and Trimming

Loose ends are tightened, aligned, and trimmed. You're all done! Take home your unique weaved artwork.



In this textile art workshop in London, we explore thread wrapping as a meditative textile process. Using cotton threads and a simple base structure, you’ll create a hand-wrapped textile panel built through repetition, rhythm, and close attention to material and texture. The emphasis is on the physical act of wrapping rather than speed or perfection!
This workshop is suitable for adults with no previous experience in textile art. It’s designed as a calm, focused practice that gently guides you into the process, making it accessible and grounding even if you’re completely new to working with textiles.
What to expect:
Working with natural cotton cords and threads.
Learning a simple but versatile thread-wrapping technique.
Layering and guiding threads to build texture and structure.
Developing a composition through balance, tension, and repetition.
A slow, mindful making process in a quiet, supportive setting!
By the end of the workshop, you’ll leave with a finished textile panel and a clear understanding of the wrapping technique, along with the confidence to continue exploring it. More than just an object, you’ll take away the experience of a calm, reflective way of making that encourages focus, patience, and presence.
What you'll get
One finished textile wall piece.
Hands-on experience with a slow, repetitive wrapping technique.
A deeper understanding of texture, rhythm, and material tension.
A calm, focused making experience.

title: Handwoven Round Wall Art Workshop for Beginners
description:
Preparing Natural Wool

We work with natural wool.
First, we gently separate the wool into a few parts.
Each part will be used step by step to create the artwork.




Creating the First Loops

We take one part of the wool and start working with it.
We carefully form soft loops and place them on the round base, one by one.




Fixing the Wool on the Back

On the back side, each piece of wool is secured with a small knot.
This helps the artwork stay strong and keeps the loops in place.




Repeating the Process

We continue making loops slowly and calmly.
This process is very relaxing and meditative, and the artwork begins to take shape.




Shaping the Final Look

As we add more loops, we can already see the finished wall art.
At this stage, we adjust the texture and shape to make it soft and balanced.
